1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 9.7% YoY and 4.8% QoQ, 2.1% below Kotak's estimate (CLSA calls it broadly in line). The shortfall came from low-teens growth in 2W OEM and mid-single-digit growth in TBR/2W replacement, and 10% YoY growth lagged peers, possibly from replacement-market share loss. (Kotak, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 8.3% YoY and 25% QoQ, 6.5% below Kotak's estimate, with margin at 11.4% (-460bps QoQ). Gross margin dropped about 560bps QoQ on a 16-18% QoQ rise in raw material costs, and other expenses (possibly marketing) were higher than expected. CLSA put the margin about 200bps below its estimate. (Kotak, CLSA)

outlook.note: Kotak expects margin pressure to continue near term as rubber prices stay elevated and crude is volatile, and sees BKT's entry into TBR/PCR adding competition. It cut FY27-29 EPS by 2-12% (FY27E by 12%) and kept SELL with a Rs125,000 fair value. CLSA says industry price hikes of 7-9% in 1QFY27, with a further 5-6% planned in 2QFY27, should help margins recover sequentially. It cut FY27CL EPS by 8% (EBITDA margin 14% from 15%), raised its target price to Rs165,238 and kept O-PF. Net, the estimate cuts outweigh the recovery view. (Kotak, CLSA)

companies.name: Ather Energy
companies.note: ASP has gone up to 161k by June (from 150k q-q) which can cover further material cost increases.  A potential entry into motorcycles offers further long-term optionality. Key upside risks: Policy support in other states like ICE ban or EV incentives, and inclusion of Ather in the PLI scheme.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs12,169m (+89% YoY, +4% QoQ) was about 1% below consensus (Rs12.3bn). Volumes rose 81% YoY to 83,173 and realization was up 5% YoY and 4% QoQ to Rs146k (JP, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA loss of Rs331m was far better than consensus of Rs811m loss. The margin of -2.7% (+320bps QoQ) beat consensus of -6.6%, helped by staff costs (flat YoY, -7% QoQ) and other expenses (+9% YoY). Gross margin of 19.7% was in line with consensus, and the QoQ margin gain came despite a 5.6% QoQ rise in raw material costs (JP, CLSA, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management cites very strong EV demand, with bookings of about 50k units/month against capacity of 35k/month. Capacity should ramp to 920k in 3QFY27 (Factory 3.0 adds 500k) and the EL platform launches in August. The c.7% price hike should help 2QFY27 margins, though commodity costs remain a headwind. CLSA raised its FY27/28 volume estimates by 27%/16% and its TP to Rs1,600. Nomura raised its TP to Rs1,714 and says margin risks are behind. JP expects positive consensus revisions (CLSA, Nomura, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs172bn (+37% YoY, +7.7% QoQ) was 1.0% above consensus, helped by 29% YoY volume growth (exports +54% YoY) and a ~3% QoQ rise in ASP to Rs119.9k, with the weaker rupee (Rs94.4/US$) lifting export realisations. (Nomura, CLSA, Bern)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs36bn (+45% YoY) was 4.4% above consensus; margin of 20.9% (+113bps YoY, +9bps QoQ) beat the 20.2% consensus despite ~4.5% commodity cost inflation, offset by the 2.3% price hike, export realisations, operating leverage and lower discretionary spend (other costs 5.5% of sales vs 6.1% expected). (Nomura, CLSA)

outlook.note: Management plans to lift exports to 250k units/month (vs 188k in FY26) from 2QFY27, expand capacity from ~7mn to 9mn units p.a., and launch a 125cc+ range refresh (10 models) with new Pulsars; it flagged more commodity cost pressure ahead. Nomura raised FY27-28F volumes by 5-6% and EPS by 8-10% (~16% ahead of consensus), and upgraded to Buy with TP Rs12,220; CLSA lifted FY27-28 EPS 5-6% and TP to Rs12,068; Bernstein stays Outperform (TP Rs11,500). (Nomura, CLSA, Bern)

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs60.8bn (+16% YoY) was 1.5% above Kotak's estimate. Volumes rose 12.3% YoY and ASPs 3.3% YoY (Kotak). JPMorgan put it 2% above JPMe and slightly ahead of consensus (JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs15.1bn (+20% YoY) was 0.6% above Kotak's estimate, helped by better gross margins and offset by higher other expenses. Margin was 24.9% (+90bps YoY, -60bps QoQ), 20bps below Kotak's estimate. JPMorgan had EBITDA 3% above JPMe (Kotak, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs66.3bn (+32% yoy) was 4-5% above consensus and estimates, led by higher ASPs (Rs200.7k/unit, +5.7% yoy, +4% qoq) on a richer mix of parts and accessories and price hikes, partly offset by weaker export pricing (Nomura, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs15.9bn (+32% yoy) was ~4% above consensus of Rs15.3bn (2.8% above Kotak), driven by better ASPs and lower other expenses (10.7% of sales vs 12% expected), partly offset by weaker gross margin (RM/sales 58.5%, +290bps qoq); EBITDA margin 24.0%, in line with consensus (Nomura, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management sees enquiries strong and expects strong growth to continue. Capacity rises from 120k to 132k units/month from July, towards 1.65mn by Oct-26 and 2mn by Mar-27. A price hike of 0.8% in July offsets 450bps of cost inflation, and margins are expected to recover gradually. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 2-4% on higher ASPs and lifted fair value to Rs8,200; Nomura left EPS largely unchanged and raised TP to Rs8,437 but flagged the 250cc launch as key upside, and competition and the ICE ban as risks (Kotak, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue was 5% above Bloomberg consensus (+2% vs GS estimate) and +36% yoy, on a 23% yoy rise in volumes to 1.68mn units and an 11% yoy rise in ASP to Rs77,499 from a richer mix (Glamour 125/VIDA/Destini 125) and price hikes. (GS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs17.3bn was 6% above consensus (+1% vs GS estimate) and +25% yoy off a low base. Margin of 13.3% was 21 bps above consensus but down 114 bps yoy, as gross margin fell about 300 bps qoq on 4.5% net commodity inflation. Cost control and lower other expenses helped. (GS, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guides to ~10% yoy industry growth in FY27E on GST cuts, rural spending and rate cuts. It plans to outpace the industry with 125cc and scooter launches and holds a 14-16% medium-term EBITDA margin target. Capacity is being expanded ahead of the festive season, with VIDA EV capacity going from 30k/month to 45k/month by FY27 end. It expects to offset commodity inflation in 2Q27 through cost reductions and has taken a 4.5% cumulative ICE price increase. Brokers raised FY27-29E EPS by 5-6% (Kotak) and 6-9% (GS) on higher ASPs, but both stay at SELL on market-share limits. GS raised its TP to Rs4,700 from Rs4,300 and Kotak raised its FV to Rs5,000 from Rs4,700. Kotak sees industry grow

1Q27.revNote: Revenue fell 45% yoy to Rs4.55bn (deliveries 39.2k, down 43% yoy) but rose 72% qoq as volumes recovered from a very low 4Q base. Kotak cites lower-than-expected ASPs (~Rs116k, down 4.4% qoq) and a softer revenue print than it expected. (GS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs1.65bn (-36% margin) from Rs2.37bn a year ago and Rs2.81bn in 4Q, helped by a one-time Rs550mn reversal of ACC-PLI penalties. Kotak's adjusted EBITDA margin of -48.8% was below its -34.7% estimate on weaker ASPs and gross margin (30.5% vs 38.5% qoq), and it calls the loss higher than expected. Kotak's text also says the Rs1.7bn loss was lower than its Rs2.1bn expectation, which conflicts with that call. (Kotak, GS)

4Q26.revNote: Net sales fell 57% YoY and 44% QoQ to Rs2.65 bn, 20% below estimate. Deliveries were only 20.3k units (-61% YoY) as competition and service-driven damage to the brand kept hurting volumes, and market share slid to 5% from 18.4%. ASP was also hit by a one-time change in how care packages and extended warranties are booked (a Rs200-300 mn hit) (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: The EBITDA loss of Rs2.8 bn was wider than the Rs2.1 bn estimate because other expenses linked to cost-cutting were higher than expected. This more than offset a gross margin of 38.5%, 250 bps above estimate, and the EBITDA margin was -106% against -57% in 3QFY26. The loss still narrowed from Rs6.95 bn a year ago as opex was cut to Rs3.8 bn from Rs7.79 bn (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management reiterated a quarterly opex target of Rs3.0-3.25bn and EBITDA breakeven at 20-25k units/month, versus 13k/month average in 1Q. It plans to move to dealer-based distribution and to scale cell capacity from 2.5GWh to 6GWh by Sep-26. Consolidated FCF is -Rs3.5bn per quarter, and Kotak cut FY27-29E revenue and keeps SELL with FV Rs20. GS marginally trimmed its FY27-29E EPS loss (FY27E -2.87 vs -3.59) and raised TP to Rs40 from Rs38.9 but stays Neutral. (Kotak, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone revenue of Rs139bn was +38% YoY and 3% above Bloomberg consensus (+2% vs GSe). Volumes rose 27% YoY to 1.63mn units and ASP rose 8% YoY to Rs85.5k, helped by another 50bps price hike in 1Q27 after 150bps in 4Q26 (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs17.8bn was +41% YoY and 10% above consensus (+7% vs GSe). The EBITDA margin was 12.8%, 78bps above consensus, as better mix, pricing and expense control offset a ~350bp commodity cost headwind. Gross margin fell 160bps YoY to 27.2% (GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management is upbeat on 2Q27 volumes, guiding to at least double-digit growth in ICE 2Ws and continued ~80% YoY growth in E2Ws. It guides to only ~0.5% more commodity inflation and ~0.5% price increases in 2Q. Installed capacity is on track to reach 8.3mn units by 4Q27E, from 6.8mn. GS raised FY27-29E EPS by up to 10% and its TP to Rs4,650 (from Rs4,300). JP raised FY27-29E EPS by 1.1-3.7% and its PT to Rs4,800 (from Rs4,355). Jeff raised FY27-29E EPS by 4-5%, 7-21% above Street, and its PT to Rs4,900 (from Rs4,500) (GS, JP, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs96.3bn (+10% YoY) was 1% below Bloomberg consensus, so broadly in line. ASP fell 3% QoQ to Rs1.97mn as the mix shifted towards LCVs, which JPM flagged as 4% below its estimate. (GS, Nomura, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs9.7bn was 4% above consensus and flat YoY. The margin of 10.1% was 50bps above consensus (9.6%), but down 105bps YoY and 453bps QoQ. Gross margins beat helped, as lower-cost inventory was sold and prices rose 200-225bps in MHCV and 350bps+ in LCV in FY27 so far. JPM put the gross-margin beat at 196bps versus its estimate. (GS, JP, Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Net sales rose 19% YoY (+23% QoQ) on 17% volume growth and 1.3% higher realisations, 0.3% above Kotak's estimate. CLSA also cites aftermarket +11%, power solutions +16% and defence +20% YoY. (Kotak, CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs20.7bn (+15% YoY) was in line: margin of 14.6% (-40bps YoY, +128bps QoQ) was in line with consensus, and better gross margin from a 1% January price hike and value engineering offset higher staff and other costs. JPM called it a 2% miss vs its own estimate, with a small beat vs consensus. (Kotak, CLSA, JP)

outlook.note: Management sees MHCV growth in high single digits in FY27 and stronger SCV growth. Demand into August stayed strong, with a full-year domestic truck volume outlook of HSD (GS). Price hikes of 100bps+ in MHCV and 200bps+ in LCV taken in July are yet to be passed through, and 2Q gross margin should be pressured by costlier inventory before easing from 3Q (GS). Nomura raised FY27/28/29E EPS by 8%/7% for FY27/28 and its TP to INR194 from INR169. GS raised FY28-29 EPS and its TP to Rs175 from Rs162. JPM expects marginal upward consensus revisions, and AL plans to invest up to Rs3.3bn in Optare and Rs5bn in Hinduja Housing Finance. (GS, Nomura, JP)

companies.name: Escorts Kubota
companies.note: Management has increased its FY27 tractor industry growth guidance from flattish (range of +2% to -2% YoY) to MSD (in line with 5% guidance by M&M). The company believes that it will grow more than the industry on the back of multiple launches planned in coming months across core, premium, and application-specific markets. Cost pressures are expected to continue with an additional ~1%-2% QoQ impact. The company is contemplating passing on some of the additional costs in 2Q, but nothing is finalized yet given the permanent nature of the hikes

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs31.8 bn was 3.3% above Kotak's estimate and up 28% YoY. Tractor revenue rose 27% on 21% higher volumes, and construction equipment revenue rose 39% on volume growth and cumulative price hikes (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.6 bn was only 0.9% above Kotak's estimate. Margin of 11.2% was down 190bps QoQ and 20bps below estimate, as 5-6% QoQ commodity inflation outweighed the price hikes and operating leverage. CLSA put the margin 50bps below consensus, while JP called the operating result a beat, driven by Agri margins (Kotak, CLSA, JP).

outlook.note: Management raised its FY27 domestic tractor industry outlook to mid-single-digit growth from flat, and expects construction equipment industry growth of 12-15%. It flagged a further 100-200bps QoQ commodity cost increase in 2Q and says another price hike may not fully offset it. Kotak raised FY28-29E EBITDA by 2-4% and its fair value to Rs3,450 from Rs3,400, while CLSA kept its TP at Rs3,495 and models flat FY27 industry tractor volumes on El Nino risk. JP expects marginal upgrades to consensus (Kotak, CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs163.3bn was flat YoY and 1% above consensus (2% above JPMe), helped by realisations ~1% better than expected; volumes fell 1% YoY and 14% QoQ (production disrupted by the Mobis supplier fire, exports down 20% YoY on Middle East tensions). (JP, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs15.1bn fell 31% YoY but was 1% above consensus (3% above JPMe); margin of 9.3% was down ~400bps YoY on weak export mix, commodity inflation hitting gross margin, higher employee cost (+20% YoY) and new-plant costs. Kotak calls it in line with its estimates. (JP, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guides 8-10% FY27 domestic volume growth and 8-10% export growth, with EBITDA margin of 11-14% (Kotak sees 11-13%), and has taken 100bps of cumulative price hikes in CY26. Venue capacity advance should lift capacity and exports to ~48k units/qtr in 2Q/3Q, and production should recover in 3Q, but market share is losing ground (12.7%, -200bps YoY) until new launches in 2HFY27 and JPM expects marginal downward consensus revisions. GS raises FY27-29E EPS by 6%/8%/1% (TP Rs2,530, Buy); Kotak raises FY27-29E EPS 3% on lower depreciation (FV Rs2,000, Reduce). (GS, Kotak, JP)

companies.name: Mahindra & Mahindra
companies.note: MM expects margins to improve sequentially in autos, but sees further pressures in farm in 2Q.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs 419.2bn (+23% YoY, +6% QoQ) was 1% below JPMe, with volumes in line at 462k units (+21% YoY) and tractor volumes up 18% YoY; Kotak notes ASPs up 2.9% YoY on a richer EV mix, and GS calls Core Auto+Farm revenue +2% vs GSe (JP, Kotak, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 51.1bn (+5% YoY, -8% QoQ) was 3% below JPMe and 5% below consensus; margin of 12.2% (-214bps YoY) was hit by commodity/RM inflation and a higher EV mix, with Auto EBIT margin 7.1% (-237bps QoQ, -37bps vs JPMe) while Farm margin of 18.5% was 12bps above JPMe. Kotak (standalone) was 2.1% below its estimate, GS called it in-line (JP, Kotak, GS).

outlook.note: Management maintained its mid-single-digit FY27 domestic tractor industry growth guide and aspires to mid-to-high-teens SUV volume growth, with SUV capacity rising from 64k/month to 68k/month exiting FY27 and BEV margins improving to 5.3% (+20bps QoQ). Estimate changes are mixed: GS raised FY27-29E EPS by up to 3% (TP Rs3,800 from Rs3,650), Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 1-2% on lower EBITDA margin assumptions (FV Rs4,175 from Rs4,050), and JPM expects small consensus cuts on the Auto margin miss, with monsoon/El Nino risk to tractors (GS, Kotak, JP).

companies.name: Maruti Suzuki
companies.note: MSIL expects its domestic volumes to rise 10% in FY27 (JEFe: 15%). MSIL said it had just ~13 days of channel stocks at end of Jun-Q. Maruti Suzuki’s relatively more gradual price hike strategy vs peers as it prioritizes volume growth over margin in the near term. Management guided for ~10% domestic volume growth in FY27  but could  surprise on upside and deliver mid teens growth – Low channel inventory, 130k orderback log (vs 190k in March), rise in first time buyers, 500k capacity add and upgraded Breeza with 1litre engine (thus lower pricing vs earlier model) to drive growth.

1Q27.revNote: Standalone revenue of Rs524.6bn was in line with Bloomberg consensus (0%) and up 36% YoY on 29% volume growth (0.68mn units) and ASP up 5% to Rs731.8k; ASP slipped 1% QoQ on a weaker mix. (GS) Jefferies likewise cites volumes +29% YoY and market share at a multi-year high. (GS, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs43.1bn missed consensus by 17% and fell 7% YoY, with margin at 8.2% (vs 10.0% consensus), down 352bps QoQ. The miss came from a one-time shift in raw-material settlement to a one-month lag from one quarter, costing c110bps at EBIT, plus commodity cost pass-through and price hikes that were too modest. GS says the adjusted EBIT margin would have been 5.9% vs 4.8% reported. (GS, Jeff)

outlook.note: Demand is strong: July registrations were +34% YoY, and capacity has been raised by another 250k units to 2.9mn p.a. GS expects the recent metal-price correction to flow through to 2Q margins, while Jefferies sees margins recovering from a low base but with higher depreciation weighing. Estimates are mixed: GS EPS FY27/28/29 +0.5%/-0.7%/-0.6% (TP Rs16,700 from Rs16,900); Jefferies cuts FY27 EPS 16% and FY28-29 6% (TP Rs16,500); Bernstein cuts TP to Rs16,800 from Rs18,200. (GS, Jeff, Bern)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone revenue of Rs193.3bn (+23% YoY) was about 2% below the Bloomberg consensus of Rs197bn. Volumes rose 27% YoY to 108,488 units, while ASP fell 3% QoQ to Rs1.79mn, so revenue was a little light of estimates (Nomura, CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs21.8bn (+15.5% YoY) beat on better operating leverage and tight fixed-cost control. The margin was 11.3% in the CLSA table (JP shows 11.7%) against a consensus of 10.8%. Commodity inflation cut margin by 340bp YoY, partly offset by price hikes and operating leverage (+140bp). EBITDA was 5-7% ahead of consensus (CLSA, Nomura, JP).

outlook.note: Management sees healthy double-digit MHCV growth in 2QFY27 and robust CV demand, helped by better fleet utilisation and freight rates. A 2.5% price hike taken in July should offset part of the commodity inflation. Estimates went up: JP raised FY28-29E EBITDA by 1%, CLSA raised FY27/28 EPS by 17%/7%, and Nomura raised its FY27 MHCV growth forecast to 8% from 5% and upgraded the stock to Buy. The Iveco deal is expected to close by early Nov-26 (Nomura, CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs958bn was +3% vs Bloomberg consensus and +9% YoY, helped by India PV volumes up 46% YoY. This offset JLR revenue down 10% YoY in GBP (wholesales -9%, China weakness, a supplier fire and Middle East supply issues). (GS, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs61.8bn was 1% below consensus but 24% down YoY, with margin at 6.4% (-286bps YoY). JLR EBIT margin of 2.8% was ahead of GS's estimate of 2.6%. Domestic PV EBITDA margin of 4.3% was well below GS's 6.3% because of commodity inflation, and PAT missed consensus by 47%. (GS, CLSA)

outlook.note: JLR kept its FY27 guidance of c.4% EBIT margin and breakeven FCF, and domestic PV demand is strong with inventory at about 30 days. Domestic commodity inflation is expected to add a further c.300bps QoQ in 2Q, so margin is guided only to be stable QoQ, and JLR needs a steep 2H ramp. Estimates were cut: GS FY28-29 EBITDA by up to 4% (TP Rs345 from Rs355), CLSA FY27/28 EPS by 6%/3%, and Jeff FY27-29 EPS by 10-23%, with Jeff 12-35% below Street. (GS, CLSA, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 119.9% YoY and 5.0% QoQ to INR 1,915 Cr. Products now make up about 85% of revenue, exports are about 56% of sales, and data-centre connectivity contributed INR 100 Cr (DC).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose to INR 445.3 Cr from INR 42.9 Cr a year ago, with margin up 1,832 bps YoY to 23.25%. Management says the 23%+ margin is sustainable and driven by product mix, and telecom products have held about 30% segment margins for three quarters (DC).

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 20% to 40%. It is targeting about INR 800 Cr of data-centre connectivity revenue in FY27 against INR 850 Cr+ of order visibility. The board approved INR 215 Cr of capex to expand that capacity 5x. Management expects the 23%+ margin to hold, and DC's FY27E/FY28E revenue estimates are INR 6,500 Cr and INR 9,000 Cr. Risks are OFC price normalisation, hyperscaler contract concentration and defence execution (DC).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs19.1bn (+33% QoQ, +87% YoY) came in 20% above CLSA's estimate. The optical business, 96% of the total, grew 34% QoQ and 92% YoY. The mix by region was 54% North America, 25% Europe and 22% rest of world including India. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.85bn (+97% QoQ, +192% YoY) was about 50% ahead of CLSA's estimate. Margin expanded 6.6ppt QoQ to 20%, helped by the US tariff reset (from a 50% peak to c.18%), higher utilisation, better product mix and operating leverage. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Order book rose 155% QoQ and 281% YoY to Rs186bn, led by a US$1.1bn US hyperscaler datacentre win. DC & Cloud reached 21% of revenue and is expected to scale to 50%. Management raised its margin guidance to c.23% by end-FY27. CLSA raised forecasts by 7-125% over FY27-29CL, raised its target price from Rs655 to Rs950 and kept O-PF. The Aug note adds a further US$210m of orders in the current quarter. (CLSA)

4Q26.revNote: Total income of Rs224bn was +1.3% yoy and 0.2% above Kotak's estimate. Weaker yields (Rs5.19/RPK, -1.6% vs estimate) were offset by higher ancillary revenue (+9.2% yoy) and other operating income (+53% yoy). (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs8.1bn was 18% below Kotak's estimate and down 87% yoy, hit by a ~Rs48bn forex loss (largely MTM). Adjusted EBITDAR of Rs64.0bn was 6% above estimate. The 9 paise operating-spread hit from grounded planes was partly offset by lower lease liabilities and supplementary rentals. The net loss of Rs23bn was Rs3bn smaller than Kotak expected, a modest beat. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs245.8bn (+19.9% YoY) was about 1% above JPMorgan's estimate and 2% above GS's. Yields were strong (+21% YoY to Rs6.04/RPK, PRASK +20%), which outweighed ASK growth of only 3% and RPK growth of 1% (Jeff, JP, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs30.6bn (-40.9% YoY) with a margin of 12.5% against 25.3% a year ago. JPMorgan's EBITDA estimate was Rs39.5bn, so this is a 19% miss. Fuel and non-fuel costs came in above forecasts: fuel CASK rose 81% YoY, and CASK ex-fuel ex-forex rose 11% YoY. JPMorgan says the result missed both its and consensus forecasts, and GS puts costs ex-forex 5% above its estimate. PAT was a loss of Rs3.8bn (Jeff, JP, GS).

outlook.note: Management guided flat YoY ASK growth for 2Q, with unit PRASK growth of 25%+ YoY, and has kept its FY27 single-digit capacity growth guidance. It now expects CASK ex-fuel ex-forex to rise high single to low double digits, up from mid-to-high single digits earlier, so elevated costs offset the pricing strength. Estimate changes are mixed: GS cuts FY27E EBITDA by about 4% (TP Rs5,900, Buy), Jeff trims EPS by 1-3% (TP Rs5,840, Buy), and JPM raises FY27 EPS by 47% but stays below consensus (TP Rs4,740, Neutral) (GS, Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs39.6bn (+24% YoY, +0.7% QoQ) was about 2% below Kotak's Rs40.5bn estimate, so roughly in line. Growth was led by double-digit non-aero revenue growth at Delhi, Hyderabad and Mopa (+13%/+12%/+8% YoY) despite flat pax at the top-three airports. (Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs14.5bn (+11% YoY, -2.5% QoQ) was 1.6% below Kotak's Rs14.7bn estimate and Jefferies' Rs14.7bn, so broadly in line. Margin was 36.5%, down 423bps YoY. Hyderabad's aero revenue fell on a 12% pax decline from the West Asia crisis. Duty-free spend per passenger and other assets (+22% YoY) partly offset this. (Jeff, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 38% yoy to Rs39.4 bn, 0.9% below Kotak's estimate (Rs39.7 bn) and down 1.4% qoq. No consensus figure is printed, so this is judged against Kotak's own estimate. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 47% yoy to Rs14.8 bn, 4.2% below Kotak's estimate (Rs15.5 bn) and down 13.5% qoq. Kotak attributes the miss to volatile line items. Top-three-asset EBITDA was a modest beat, and the EBITDA margin was 37.7% against 38.9% estimated. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Kotak raised FY27-28 EBITDA estimates by 3-9% for better performance at the top-three airports plus Bhogapuram (Vizag) and Nagpur, keeping FV at Rs118. It expects a 26% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-28 from non-aero growth and pax recovery, EBITDA from the new assets, DIAL F&B consolidation from Sep-26 and Delhi real estate monetisation from FY28. Jefferies expects growth to return at Delhi and Hyderabad once the West Asia crisis eases, and keeps a Buy with a Rs125 target. Net debt is flat QoQ at Rs340bn. (Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 6% YoY, about 2% below JEFe. P&A sales grew 16% on 11% volume growth and ~4% better realisation per case, while Mass Premium sales rose only 1% as realisations fell 2% (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 3% YoY but missed JEFe by 19%. Gross margin fell 219bps QoQ on a Rs240mn packaging-cost hit from supply-chain disruptions, and employee costs rose 27% YoY on luxury-portfolio investments. EBITDA margin was 11.8%, down ~30bps YoY (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management maintains its FY28 guidance of mid-teen revenue growth and 48%/18% gross/EBITDA margins, and expects India–UK FTA tailwinds in 2HFY27. Jefferies is more conservative, forecasting a 12% revenue CAGR over FY26–28e and a 16.3% FY28e EBITDA margin. It sees the EBITDA miss as driven by packaging inflation and luxury investments, and keeps its Buy rating with a Rs780 target (Jeff).

companies.name: Radico Khaitan
companies.note: P&A volume guidance raised to 25% from 20% with a 20% EBITDA margin.  Management highlighted that the vodka category in India has grown at a 20%+ CAGR during FY22–26. However, it still accounts for only ~6% of IMFL volumes, compared with 28% globally, indicating significant headroom for penetration. Magic Moments continues to dominate the category with a 60%+ market share.

1Q27.revNote: Net sales grew 11.8% YoY to Rs16.8bn, 0.7% below Bloomberg consensus and 2.8% below CLSA's estimate. Prestige & above volumes grew 35.8% and sales 36%, while regular-category sales fell 17.3% on a high base and policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 50.3% YoY, 10.6% above consensus, as margin expanded 531bps YoY to 20.7% (210bps above consensus). Gross margin expanded 610bps to 49.1% on benign raw materials and premiumisation, despite a Rs300mn packaging cost hit. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Management raised its FY27 P&A volume growth guidance to 25% from 20% and its EBITDA margin guidance to 20% (vs 16.9% in FY26, from an earlier 125bps expansion guide), driven by vodka and flavoured-vodka mix; it expects to turn net debt-free next quarter. CLSA raised FY27-29 EPS estimates 9-14% and its target price from Rs4,266 to Rs4,830; Jefferies' FY27 EBITDA margin expectation was 17.7%, below the new guide. (CLSA, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue grew 7% yoy on 9% volume growth (sell-out +13%), but realisation was dragged by an adverse contract-brewing source mix, which cost about 4% in the quarter. JPM calls this broadly in line with the Street. Kotak had it 2.8% below its own estimate. (JP, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 9% yoy and margin contracted about 165 bps to 9.2%, as gross margin dropped about 155 bps to 41% on Middle East-led input-cost inflation (~300 bps impact). JPM says EBITDA missed both its own and consensus forecasts materially. Kotak had it 1% above its own estimate. (JP, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management aims for double-digit volume growth in FY27 on a favourable base and category momentum, and has taken 2.5-3% price hikes. It trimmed the Middle East cost-inflation impact to Rs3.5-4 bn from Rs4 bn+, but expects cost pressure to persist near term. Kotak cut FY27E EPS by 7% (EBITDA +0.8%) and raised FV to Rs1,275 from Rs1,220. JPM expects downward revisions to margin forecasts. (Kotak, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Net sales grew 3.4% YoY, 2.3% below Bloomberg consensus and 4.5% below CLSA's estimate. Price/mix added 8.1%, offset by a 5.6% volume decline (P&A -3.1%, regular -16.6%). Maharashtra-made liquor disruption was a drag (CLSA, Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 17.0% YoY, 3.8% above consensus. Gross margin expanded 281bps YoY to 47.3% on better mix, headline pricing flow-through and stable raw material prices, and EBITDA margin reached 19.4%. EBITDA was 6.2% below CLSA's estimate. Kotak says the margin beat more than offset the revenue miss (CLSA, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales grew 6% YoY, in line with CLSA's estimate (+0.4%) and consensus (+0.3%). Growth was price/mix-led: P&A sales rose ~10% on ~12% realisation growth, while Popular fell ~17.6% on Maharashtra Made Liquor and Karnataka excise changes, and overall volumes fell ~3% (CLSA, Nomura, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 4.1% YoY but came in 9% below CLSA and 4.4% below consensus. Gross margin expanded 212bps YoY to 46.1%, 38bps above consensus, but A&P spend rose 31% YoY (11.5% of sales, +220bps), so EBITDA margin fell 30bps YoY to 16.0% vs 16.8% consensus (CLSA, Nomura, JP).

outlook.note: Management expects Maharashtra Made Liquor weakness to keep weighing on volumes, and higher glass costs and A&P to pressure margins through 1HFY27. Nomura expects tailwinds in 2HFY27 from the India-UK FTA, anniversarying of the MML impact and softer glass prices. Nomura left FY27-29F estimates unchanged (revenue INR136,970mn FY27F) and JP sees limited estimate changes (Nomura, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Income of Rs8,699 mn was 7.4% above Kotak's Rs8,096 mn estimate and up 19.8% yoy. Non-recurring revenue grew 34% yoy on the B&K acquisition, transactional income and carry fees, and recurring revenue grew 22.8% on AUM growth of about 19% yoy (Kotak). Bernstein also notes revenue from operations up 24% yoy, with Wealth ARR +20% and AMC ARR +21% (Bern).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PBT of Rs4,235 mn was 7.3% above Kotak's Rs3,946 mn estimate, up 12.9% yoy and 16.8% qoq. Opex rose 27% yoy, including one-off B&K-related employee costs. The cost-income ratio improved to 51.3% from 53.5% in 4Q (Kotak, Jeff). PBT growth lagged revenue because of lower treasury income than a year ago (Bern).

2Q27.revNote: Income of Rs8.5bn was 2.7% above Kotak's estimate and up 4.8% YoY, helped by non-recurring revenue (up 13% YoY, carry income of Rs1.16bn vs Rs610mn a year ago). Recurring revenue grew about 20% YoY but was 1.6% below estimate. Other income was a Rs440mn loss from MTM on treasury investments. (Kotak)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PBT of Rs3.9bn was 1.4% above Kotak's estimate but down 5.6% YoY. Operating expenses rose about 15% YoY, higher than expected, and the MTM loss in other income weighed on profit. Cost-to-income was 54.2%, down about 200bps QoQ. Jefferies says PAT was about 5% lower YoY and below its estimate because of the MTM losses. (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Net inflows were Rs125bn against Jefferies' Rs102bn estimate. Wealth saw Rs110bn (5% of opening AUM) and AMC inflows turned positive at Rs15bn after outflows of Rs26bn last quarter. ARR AUM rose 20% YoY. Management expects the cost/income ratio to fall by 100-150bps this year. It also expects to deploy about Rs18bn of capital from UBS equity inflows and to break even in the HNI and mass-affluent segments within 3-4 quarters. Jefferies trims FY27/28 EPS by less than 1%, to Rs32.57 for FY27 from Rs32.76. It sees 17%/20%/18% revenue/profit/EPS CAGR over FY26-29e and keeps its Rs1,340 PT. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Fee income of Rs4.63 bn grew 3% yoy and 1% qoq, about 3% above Kotak's Rs4.49 bn estimate. Mutual fund average AUM rose 6% yoy, with equity AUM growing slightly faster at 10% yoy. The large low-fee ESIC/EPFO mandate lifted overall AAUM 42% yoy but adds little revenue (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Core PBT (PBT less other income) was Rs2.44 bn, down 4% yoy and 3% qoq, about 1% above Kotak's estimate, so broadly in line. Operating expenses grew 13% yoy, which lifted the core cost-income ratio ~200 bps qoq to ~47%. Kotak calls it a weak but broadly in-line quarter. Kotak prints no EBITDA line, so core PBT is used as the operating-profit measure (Kotak).

outlook.note: Fund performance has improved over 1Y/3Y and funds are being added to bank and wealth recommendation lists (HDFC Bank, Kotak Bank, HSBC, LGT, ASK). Flows are not yet picking up: April was strong, May and June moderated, and monthly SIP fell to ~Rs10.9 bn (-10% qoq). Management is holding current margins and yields. Kotak made only marginal estimate changes, kept ADD and an unchanged FV of Rs1,100, and says the recent stock run-up limits upside (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net adj. revenue grew 23% YoY and fell 2.2% QoQ to Rs 13.0bn. Kotak calls revenue in line with its estimate (+0.7%), with net broking revenue up 26% YoY and interest income up 31% YoY on a Rs 61bn margin funding book. (JP, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 85% YoY and fell 24% QoQ to Rs 3.6bn, 15% above Kotak's estimate. Expenses came in 3% below Kotak's estimate (lower other expenses) despite IPL marketing spends, lifting EBITDA margin to 27.6% (+924bp YoY). PAT was 5.3% above consensus per JP. (JP, Kotak)

2Q27.revNote: Net adj. revenue rose 15.6% YoY but fell 1.6% QoQ to Rs 12.84bn. Gross broking revenue fell 9.4% QoQ to Rs 7.8bn on lower order numbers (CAS impact, lower volatility). Interest income grew 34.4% YoY on a 40.5% YoY rise in the average MTF book to Rs 74.6bn (JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 52.0% YoY and 37.1% QoQ to Rs 4.93bn. Margin expanded 920bp YoY to 38.4% because 1Q27 carried Rs 1.37bn of IPL expenses that were absent in 2Q. Staff costs fell 6.9% YoY. The report gives no consensus figure for EBITDA, but PAT came in 8.9% above consensus (JP).

outlook.note: JPM cut FY27E/28E/29E EPS by 4.5%/5.6%/9.7% to factor in the softer 2Q27. It also cut gross broking revenue estimates by 7.6%/8.9%/8.8% and lowered the target multiple to 21x from 23x, taking the PT to Rs 370 from Rs 410. It flags gross client acquisition down 18.4% YoY as a headwind to future growth. It retains OW (JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3.95bn (+12% y-y, flat q-q) was about 1.9% below consensus of ~Rs4.0bn and 0.3% below JEFe, so in line. MF revenue grew 9% y-y, with MF RTA yield down 1% q-q to 2.41bps, while non-MF revenue grew 28% y-y to 14.9% of the mix. (Jeff, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.83bn (+18% y-y, margin 46.3%, up 270bps y-y) was 3% above JEFe, because total expenses grew only 6% y-y on deferred employee appraisals. JP puts EBIT at Rs1.58bn, 2.4% above consensus. (Jeff, JP)

outlook.note: Management has guided for opex growth of under 10% y-y over the next 2-3 years, and for FY27 cost growth of under 9%. Net headcount fell about 225 q-q, with a further 4-5% reduction expected this year. Jefferies raised FY27-29e EBITDA by 3-5% (16% 3-yr CAGR) and its PT to Rs960 from Rs910. JP retained OW with a PT of Rs950, noting yield compression is easing. (Jeff, JP)

companies.name: Groww
companies.note: Groww launched its US stock offering last month. Currently, it is in the beta phase with a full rollout to all users expected later in 3QFY27. We note that the minimum brokerage for US stocks is c.5x that for domestic stocks. Should US stock orders reach 1/3rd of commodities, the newest trading product, it would translate to c.9% of FY28e PAT. Medium-term, we think this opportunity would involve offering stocks from other markets

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations of Rs15.0bn rose 66% YoY and was flat QoQ, 1% above Jefferies' estimate of Rs14.9bn. Options revenue share fell to 52% while new streams (MTF, commodities, wealth) grew to 14% of revenue. No consensus figure is printed (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA of Rs9.9bn (+94% YoY, +3% QoQ) was 6% above Jefferies' estimate. Lower indirect expenses (-9% vs estimate) lifted the margin to 66% (+237bps QoQ) despite higher IPL marketing and salary costs. No consensus figure is printed (Jeff).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 47% YoY and was flat QoQ, 3% ahead of consensus. Growth was led by MTF (+209% YoY), Float (+63%) and PL+LAS (+37%), while equity derivatives were hit by the closing auction system (CAS) and fell 14% QoQ. Other operating income was higher on IPO allotment fees (JP, Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 61% YoY and was flat QoQ, 6% ahead of consensus. Margin was 64.5% (vs 64.7% in 1Q27 and 59.3% in 2Q26), about 180bps ahead of consensus. Lower marketing spend (no IPL costs) offset higher cost to serve from tech and compute costs, more trading days and a one-time client reimbursement (JP, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guides cost-to-grow at Rs4-5bn a year (about Rs1.2bn a quarter) and MTF book growth of about Rs600-700mn a quarter. CAS-related derivatives drag is expected to normalise from Nov'26, and the US stocks launch is a new growth lever. Estimate changes are mixed: JP raises FY27E revenue and EBITDA by 1% but trims PAT by 1%, and Jeff cuts revenue by 1%. Price targets are unchanged at Rs240 (JP, Jeff) and Rs245 (Kotak) (JP, Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs11.0bn (+14% y-y, +5% q-q) was ~2% above Jefferies' estimate (Rs10.74bn), helped by blended yield rising 1bp q-q to 47bps and QAAUM up 13% y-y to Rs9.35tn. Nomura put it 4.2% above its estimate, with yield up 1.7bp q-q vs its expected 0.2bp decline. No consensus revenue figure is printed. (Jeff, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating profit of Rs8.3bn (+10% y-y) was in line with Jefferies' estimate (Rs8.26bn) because the better top line was offset by 9% higher opex (CSR, tech and general expenses). JPMorgan, the only report to give a consensus comparison, says EBIT was 3% below consensus. Nomura had it 1.9% above its own estimate. (JP, Jeff, Nomura)

2Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations of Rs11.7bn rose 14% y-y (+6% q-q) and was 3% above Kotak's estimate, as overall yields improved to 48.3bps (+1bp q-q) with the equity mix of QAAUM up 140bps q-q to 67%; QAAUM grew 10% y-y (Kotak, Jeff).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs9.26bn grew 16% y-y (+9% q-q) and was 4% above Kotak's estimate, as opex rose only 6% y-y (-4% q-q) against 14% revenue growth; core PBT was 4% ahead of estimates and Jefferies also called it a 5% operating beat (Kotak, Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies raised FY27-29E EPS by 3-5% on better revenue yields and lifted its PT to Rs3,050. It models slower AAUM growth of c.7% over FY27 given MTM headwinds. Kotak made only marginal EPS tweaks and kept FV at Rs2,800. It sees yield compression as structural, so revenue will keep growing slower than AUM. Management flagged a market-share correction in active equity flows, and alternatives remain immaterial to revenue. (Jeff, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 18% YoY and 1% QoQ to Rs15.6bn, 1% below MS's estimate of Rs15.75bn. Growth came from higher equity QAAUM (+17% YoY) and a blended yield that was stable to slightly up at 52.3bp. [MS, JP]
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PAT of Rs9.65bn rose 23% YoY and 26% QoQ, 1% above MS's estimate and above Visible Alpha (+9%) and FactSet (+4%) consensus. Higher other income (Rs1.81bn, MTM gains) offset employee costs that were up 11% YoY from ESOP expenses and wage hikes, so operating profit was 1% below MS's estimate and 2.5% below consensus per JP. [MS, JP, CLSA]
1Q27.vsBasis: PAT: consensus (Visible Alpha +9%, FactSet +4%); revenue: broker estimate (MorganStanley)

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs16.7bn rose 17.9% YoY and 7.0% QoQ, about 3% above Jefferies' estimate of Rs16.2bn. Growth came from MF QAAUM up 14% YoY and a better revenue yield of ~54bp (+1.8bp YoY), helped by the alternates mix (JP, Jeff).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PAT of Rs8.9bn rose 6.4% YoY but fell 7.8% QoQ, about 6% above Jefferies' estimate. Operating profit grew 16% YoY, but other income collapsed to Rs169mn from Rs1.8bn in 1Q27 on mark-to-market losses in a weak equity market, which held PAT growth well below operating growth (JP, Jeff, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management said gross flows were stable, with the lower net inflows driven by higher redemptions, and that SIP mix is shifting to small/mid caps where ICICI AMC is not a leader. Alternates net yields are guided at 90-95bp. FY27 ESOP cost guidance is unchanged at Rs640-680mn. Estimate changes are mixed: Jefferies raises FY27-29e EPS 1-2% on yields and its PT to Rs3,760, while CLSA raises revenue 1-2% but cuts PAT 1-2% on higher opex and lower other income (TP unchanged at Rs3,650). JPMorgan expects a modest downward revision to AUM growth and earnings after equity market share fell ~30bp QoQ to 13.7% and SIP share fell ~90bp (Jeff, CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 30% YoY and 2.6% QoQ to Rs 3.57bn, in line with consensus (JP) and 3% above JEFe. International and other investor solutions grew 182% YoY on the Ascent consolidation, while domestic MF revenue grew only 6.9% and Issuer Solutions 4.7% YoY (JP, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 1.22bn was up 7% YoY but down 5% QoQ, and 6% above JEFe on lower-than-expected opex. Margin fell to 34.2% (-733bps YoY) as lower-margin Ascent diluted it; ex-Ascent margin was 39.4%. PAT of Rs 752mn missed consensus by 5% (JP, Jeff).
1Q27.vsBasis: revenue: consensus (JP, 'in line with consensus'); EBITDA: broker estimate (Jeff, 6% above

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 PAT growth guidance to 12-15% from 10%, and EBITDA growth to 17-20%. Jefferies raised FY27-28e PAT by 1-2% and its PT to Rs 1,175 from Rs 1,125, expecting new-client wins in Ascent and platform sales to add 4-5% to consolidated revenue. Against that, blended MF yield is under pressure (Jeff forecasts a 0.6-0.7% sequential decline over the next three quarters) and corporate actions remain tepid. JP stays Neutral (Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 26% YoY and 4% QoQ to Rs 7.7bn, on equity QAAUM up 22% YoY and blended yields stable at ~40.8bp. It came in ~4% below consensus (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 31% YoY to Rs 5.08bn, with costs under control. JP puts EBIT (Rs 4.96bn) 3.9% above consensus, though Jeff calls operating profit in line with JEFe/consensus and Kotak has core earnings ~2% below its estimates. The JP figure is used for the beat call (JP, Jeff, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guides to 18-20% opex growth over FY27/28 (ex-ESOPs), above the Street's 14%/13%, and Jeff cut FY28e EPS 3% on it. Yields are stable and market share gains continue (equity share 7.4%, SIP share 11.7%). JP raised FY27E/28E/29E EPS by 2.8%/0.5%/1.7% and its PT to Rs 1,370, and kept OW. Kotak raised estimates 0-5% but downgraded to Reduce on valuation (JP, Jeff, Kotak).

companies.name: Nuvama
companies.note: Mgt's initiatives include seniorization of Wealth RMs, new fund launches & enabling commodity F&O for AS clients.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs9.1bn rose 18% YoY and 10% QoQ, led by Asset Services (+34% YoY) and Private (+27% YoY). Asset Services was helped by a base quarter that still had Jane Street, and clearing assets are up 79% from the Sep'25 lows. Wealth (HNI) revenue grew 13% and IE & IB was flat YoY. The note says PAT was ahead of JEFe on higher revenue but gives no revenue consensus figure. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating PBT of Rs4.08bn rose 17% YoY and 18% QoQ. The C/I ratio improved 41bps YoY to 55% as employee cost growth slowed. Capital Markets PBT grew 19% YoY on 17% cost growth. Wealth PBT grew 20% YoY. PAT of Rs3.1bn (+16% YoY) was 9% above JEFe and ahead of consensus. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Jefferies raises FY28-29e EPS by 3-5% and sees a 22% EPS CAGR over FY26-29e. FY27e revenue and EPS are unchanged. The PT moves to Rs2,160 from Rs1,840 on 23x Sep-28e P/E. Management still sees 25%+ growth in Asset Services for FY27, though segment revenue may normalise downward a bit. It also expects Wealth net inflows to stay healthy at 8% of op. AUM, guides to 80-90bps ARR yields in Private, and expects NII to reach 20-25% of revenue over the next few years. NII growth lagged in the quarter on lower margins, with a rebound expected in coming quarters. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Operating revenue of INR3.8bn was flat y-y (-0.1%) and +1% q-q, 1% above Nomura's estimate. MF revenue yields held flat q-q as the new TER regulation was fully passed on to intermediaries, while the equity+hybrid QAAUM fell 1% q-q (Nomura, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating PBT of INR1.6bn (+3% y-y, +23% q-q) was 17% above Nomura's estimate. Opex fell 16% q-q to INR2.2bn, with staff cost down 8% q-q and lower business-development and other costs, helped by the early VRS benefits. Strong other income (INR2.1bn, MTM gains) lifted PAT to INR2.9bn, 25% above Nomura's estimate (Nomura, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management said the new TER regulation was fully passed on, so margins are not diluted. Nomura leaves FY27-28F earnings largely unchanged and expects costs to catch up through the year. Kotak cuts core earnings by about 3% for operating readjustments. Flows are still weak: equity+hybrid net flows were negative, and overall and equity market share kept falling (-4bp/-12bp q-q). SIP flows improved. Nomura trims its TP to INR1,030 (Neutral) and Kotak keeps ADD with an FV of INR1,100 (Nomura, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs20.3bn, 1% below Bloomberg consensus (Rs20.5bn) and MS's estimate. Pantaloons (incl. OWND) grew 10% with 5% retail LTL, ethnic brands grew 4% (hit by a short wedding season) and luxury grew 30% (MS). CLSA put growth at 10.6%, 1.1% below consensus (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.17bn was 17% below consensus (Rs1.41bn) and 6% below MS's estimate. The margin was 5.8% (-33bps YoY), 112bps below consensus. Pantaloons margin fell 114bps YoY to 15.9% on OWND investments, and ethnic brands' margin was 0.2% (MS, CLSA).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 15.7% YoY to Rs19.9bn, 2.5% above consensus (3.1% above Kotak's estimate). Pantaloons grew 19% YoY, partly helped by the EOSS shift into 4Q, and ethnic and others grew 12.2%. (CLSA, Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.97bn was 11.5% above consensus, with margin 80bps ahead. It fell 3.6% YoY, and margin contracted about 200bps YoY to 9.9% because the base quarter had a tailwind from positive inter-segment EBITDA. Ethnic margin expanded 390bps on lower TCNS losses. (CLSA, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 guidance of high-single-digit Pantaloons LTL growth and 20%+ growth in both Ethnic and TMRW. It expects losses to narrow in FY27 and FY28 and the group to turn profitable by FY29. Inflation of about 4% is expected to pressure gross margin from 2Q, with only half of it passed on. CLSA made small estimate tweaks (FY27 revenue -1.0%) and kept its Rs60 TP and Hold rating. MS kept its Rs127 TP and Overweight rating (CLSA, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs20.5bn, in line with consensus (Rs20.46bn) and MSe. Lifestyle brands grew 10% (retail LTL 7%, e-commerce +20%) and emerging businesses 19% (LTL 11%), though wholesale was hit by lower primary sales (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 17% YoY to Rs3.08bn, 6% above consensus (Rs2.90bn), with margin up 76bp YoY to 15.1% vs 14.2% consensus. Gross margin fell 155bp YoY on channel mix, offset by lower rent (9.4% of sales vs 10.3%) and other opex (MS).

outlook.note: Management reiterated its Lifestyle brands plan of >300 gross store additions a year (net 150-200), adding 5-6% growth with 6-7% LTL. July demand was similar to 4Q, and it expects 3-4% cost inflation in F2H with no material margin impact after a small price increase in F1Q. MS left its Rs163 target and FY27-29 estimates unchanged, with Overweight maintained (MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 12.2% YoY on 11.7% volume growth off a weak base, but came in 5.8% below Bloomberg consensus (10.4% below CLSA). Reported growth was cut by about 2-2.5% from the franchise shift to a sale-or-return model and another 2-2.5% from the Flipkart/Myntra commission accounting change; a 50% jump in lower-ASP school shoes diluted ASP by 2%. (CLSA, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Core EBITDA grew 11% YoY but missed consensus by 16.8%. Margin was 14.2%, down 16bps YoY and 188bps below consensus. A minimum wage hike added about Rs50m to other expenses, and the new Pantnagar and Paonta Sahib plants added Rs25m of other expenses and Rs25m of depreciation. Gross margin expanded 37bps YoY to 55.0%. (CLSA, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 12.3% yoy to Rs4.6bn, in line with Kotak's estimate (+0.3%). Volumes rose 10.6% to 6.8mn pairs and online grew 19% while the MBO/distribution channel grew 5.5%. ASP rose only 1.5% to Rs668 because the marketplace billing change lowered the billed value (Kotak, CLSA).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 15.4% yoy to Rs825mn, 4.7% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded about 50bps yoy to 18.1% on operating leverage, with other expenses up only 6.6% despite 12.1% growth in A&P. CLSA put the margin 28bps above consensus but 53bps below its own estimate, which makes it broadly in line with consensus (Kotak, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 guidance of mid-double-digit revenue growth (high single-digit volume growth, 6-7% ASP growth) and a 17-19% EBITDA margin. It plans 80-120 new stores and launched the ELAN neo-casual brand. Record distributor orders support the festive season, and ASP and margins are expected to improve from 2Q as the one-offs fade. CLSA cut FY27-29CL estimates by 4-5% and its target price from Rs247 to Rs237 (Hold). Kotak trimmed revenue 1-2%, roughly held EBITDA, and raised its fair value to Rs315 (Buy). (CLSA, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 8% YoY (vs 14% in 4Q), led by 5.7% volume growth, but was 6% below Bloomberg consensus. Logistics and manpower disruptions at quarter-end meant ~3 days of billings were not delivered; this should shift into 2Q. (MS, GS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 2% YoY and was 11% below consensus. The margin of 20.3% was down 204bps YoY, the lowest since 1QFY25. The miss came from a gross margin shortfall of 188bps on raw material inflation, plus higher other expenses. (MS, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 14.1% YoY, well ahead of Kotak's 6.1% growth estimate (Rs 12.5 bn vs Rs 11.65 bn). Volume rose 10.8% and the rest came from realization/mix, with management citing encouraging demand across distribution channels. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 2.6 bn was 10.4% above Kotak's estimate, with a margin of 20.8% against the 20.3% estimate. Gross margin was 257 bps below estimate at 58.4%, likely on raw-material inflation, but lower employee costs more than offset it. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reiterated its double-digit volume growth aspiration for FY27, with above-average growth expected in the next three quarters. Price hikes of 2.2% in May and ~2.5% in January feed through from 2Q, and the 19-21% EBITDA margin guidance was maintained. Brokers cut estimates: GS lowered FY27-29 EPS by up to ~5%, and Kotak trimmed FY27-29 EPS by 5-6%, cut its fair value to Rs35,000 and kept SELL. (MS, GS, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3,014mn (+7% YoY) was 3% above Bloomberg consensus (Rs2,935mn) and 4% above MS's estimate. Customer sales grew 3.4% YoY on a high base, with SSSG of 3.8% (vs +17.6% in 1QF26), though retail area fell 1% YoY and 18 stores were net closed in the quarter. Kotak called revenue momentum sluggish, hurt by fewer wedding dates and the adhik mass. (MS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,310mn (+9% YoY) was 6% above consensus (Rs1,234mn). Margin of 43.5% was up 58bps YoY and 78bps above MS's estimate. The beat came from lower employee cost (-3% YoY) and other expenses (-1% YoY), which offset gross margin of 65.7% (-119bps YoY on the GST hike). (MS, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management sees low- to mid-teens FY27 revenue growth, led by high-single-digit SSSG, with strength from Nov-27 to Mar-28 on favourable wedding dates but a subdued Sep-Oct-27 (postponed Navratri). Higher store openings are expected in late 2Q/3Q, with net positive additions for the year. MS's FY27 consensus revenue is Rs15,489mn, and Kotak cut its FV to Rs455 from Rs535 while keeping estimates broadly unchanged. Delivery in 2H is seen as the key. (MS, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone revenue rose 21% YoY, 9.7% above Kotak's estimate (Rs36.8bn). Drivers were 35%/24% YoY growth in 2W/4W OEM, ~15% growth in aftermarket, >60% growth in home energy and >70% growth in new energy, partly offset by weak telecom and exports. JPM also called the revenue growth ahead of its own and street expectations (Kotak, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs4.1bn (+5.4% YoY) was 4.9% below Kotak's estimate. Margin was 10.1% (-140bps YoY, -80bps QoQ), 150bps below Kotak's estimate. Gross margin was 28.5%, hit by sulphuric acid prices (up 2x QoQ), alloys and polys, a lower-margin OEM mix and a higher trading mix. Other expenses ran at 12.9% of sales, with brand and IPL spend adding to costs. PAT growth was ~4.5% YoY, 7-9% below JPM's estimate and consensus (Kotak, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Standalone revenue rose 16% yoy and came in about 7% above Bloomberg consensus (Rs32.35 bn). Growth was led by >30% yoy volume growth in 2W/4W OEMs, 35% in tubular batteries, a rebound in home inverters and the scale-up of battery packs. Aftermarket grew 5-6% yoy, while telecom and exports stayed weak. New energy revenue was Rs2.8 bn, up 50% yoy (Kotak, Nomura).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.8 bn (+10% yoy) was in line with consensus (-0.4%) and 1.5% below Kotak's estimate. The margin of 10.9% (-60 bps yoy, -30 bps qoq) missed on gross margin, which fell 200 bps qoq. Causes were a 5x yoy jump in sulfur prices and a higher-mix of lower-margin OEM and battery pack sales (Kotak, Nomura).

outlook.note: Margins are pressured by raw material costs and the OEM mix. Management took a 3% price hike in June and plans a further 2-3% in 2QFY27. B2B price increases are likely to be delayed. It reiterated 9-10% medium-term lead-acid revenue growth. The Gotion LFP partnership has been terminated, adding timeline and capex risk to the new energy business. FY27 capex is guided at ~Rs17bn, Rs13bn of it for new energy. JPM expects downward consensus EPS revisions, since meeting FY27 estimates now implies 31% PAT growth in the remaining quarters versus 4.5% in 1Q. Kotak cut to FV Rs850 (Rs800 earlier) and retains SELL (Kotak, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Reported total operating income rose 52% YoY, inflated by the pass-through of a 33% YoY rise in aluminium prices. Excluding wheel assembly (now nil) and the alloy price increase, revenue grew 25% YoY. CLSA's report prints no revenue-vs-estimate comparison. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Ebitda rose 34% YoY to Rs1,606mn and was in line with CLSA's estimate. Reported margin was 11.8% (-160bps YoY) because the pass-through of raw-material costs diluted it, though per-unit profit was maintained. CLSA's adjusted margin is c.15.0%. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Management expects normalised margins of 13.5-14.0% (ex commodity inflation) and is confident of high-teens revenue growth. Supplies of HPDC alloy wheels to a Japanese OEM have started, adding c.Rs2.5bn of aluminium casting revenue by FY28. CLSA raised FY27-28CL EPS by 6-7% and its TP from Rs630 to Rs710, and maintains O-PF. (CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income grew 13% YoY to Rs25.5bn and was flat QoQ. Manufacturing revenue (Rs21.98bn) rose 20% YoY, with 16-22% growth across 2Ws, PVs and CVs, though 2W growth trailed industry production growth of 23%. A 19% YoY decline in the lower-margin trading business partly offset this. Jefferies gives no explicit revenue comparison versus its estimate. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 5% YoY to Rs2.93bn, 4% above JEFe on better-than-expected margins. Margin was 11.5%, up 20bp QoQ but down 90bp YoY. Staff costs rose 42% YoY, which kept the YoY margin lower despite gross margin gains. PAT rose 9% YoY but missed JEFe by 6% on lower financial income and a higher tax rate. (Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Total operating income rose 12% YoY (+9% QoQ) to Rs25.5bn. Manufacturing revenue grew 21% YoY, led by 18% growth in 2Ws+3Ws and 32%/70% growth in CVs/PVs on a low base. Trading revenue fell 21% YoY. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 5% YoY to Rs2.9bn, in line with Jefferies' estimate. Margin fell 90bp QoQ (80bp YoY) to 11.4%. Other expenses rose to 4.2% of sales (+100bp QoQ), including a one-time Rs95mn start-up cost in the aero/defence subsidiary and SDM (France) acquisition expenses, plus possibly higher fuel costs. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management retained its FY27 margin guidance of roughly FY26 levels and believes the worst of the cost pressure (commodity, fuel, transport, labour) is now priced in. The company won new orders in 2W/3W chassis (annual revenue of Rs650mn+), braking and suspension, and an EV localisation programme. It is also expanding into renewable sheet-metal assemblies (peak revenue of Rs1.5bn+) and aerospace. Jefferies cut FY27 EPS by 3% (Rs7.02 versus Rs7.22), broadly kept FY28-29, and expects a 21% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29E. It kept its Buy rating and raised its PT to Rs280 from Rs250 by rolling to 27x Sep-28E EPS. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs46.4bn (+19% YoY, +2% QoQ) was roughly in line with Bloomberg consensus (+1%, GS) and 2% below JPMe. India CV growth was weak at only 2% YoY, offset by a stronger-than-expected recovery in CV exports and 71% YoY growth in the defence subsidiary KSSL (JP, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs7.5bn (+10% YoY) missed consensus by 10% (GS) and JPMe by 7%, with the margin at 16.2% (-124 bps YoY). Manpower shortages, fuel changeovers from the West Asia crisis and energy and logistics inflation (~160 bps hit) hurt. Overseas subsidiaries disappointed, with US aluminium margins at -0.8%, and a US PMT plant shutdown added to the pressure (JP, GS).

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% (2H-heavy) and said Q2 should be better than Q1. The manpower situation is almost normalised, KSSL defence margins improved to 17.2% against a 22-23% medium-term target, and a capex raise of up to Rs25bn is planned. Estimates move little: JPM changes are within +/-1-2% and GS FY27-29E EPS changes range from -14% to +5%. Both houses stay Neutral, with JPM's price target at Rs1,870 and GS's at Rs2,120 (JP, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs1,397mn (+14.9% yoy, -3.7% qoq) were 3% below Bloomberg consensus (Rs1,434mn) and 6% below GS (Rs1,490mn). Map-led revenue grew 10% yoy and IoT-led 75% yoy, with the government mix down to 12% from 23% in FY26. GS calls the quarter in line overall. (GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs561mn was flat yoy and exactly in line with consensus, and 4% above GS. Margin was 40.2% (-578bps yoy), hit by about 300bps from a write-off on a government order. Map-led margin fell to 44.0% from 54.8%. (GS)

outlook.note: Management sees steady revenue burn from the Rs17.5bn order book versus an FY26 revenue run rate of Rs3.2bn, and expects an EBITDA margin above c35% in FY27E. Growth potential is seen across enterprise, automotive and public sector, including defense, oil and gas and IoT. GS raised FY27E-FY29E EPS by 5-6% on better Map-led margins and left its Rs1,500 target price unchanged. (GS)

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs 24.3bn were +36% YoY and 4.1% above Bloomberg consensus, led by Aluminium (+38% YoY, 10% above GSe at Rs 14.8bn) and Industrial (+53% YoY, 27% above GSe), with Powertrain +26% YoY (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 3.84bn was +45% YoY and 2.2% above consensus, with margin 15.8% (-29bps vs cons). Powertrain margin 18.3% (+300bps vs GSe) and Industrial margin 9.0% (+700bps vs GSe) drove the beat (GS).

outlook.note: Order wins from 5 of 6 HHP engine customers, 2 programs already in production; Powertrain utilisation ~70% with ~10% pickup visible near term, Aluminium at 80%+ with relief from DR Axion capacity in 2HFY27. Sunbeam turnaround expected from FY28E, land sale deal close. GS raised FY27E-FY29E EPS by 11-14% and TP to Rs 12,800 from Rs 11,600 (GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs43.1 bn (+30% yoy, +5.6% qoq) was 5% above Bloomberg consensus. Growth was led by alloy wheels (+67% yoy), suspension (+34%) and disc brakes (+31%). Standalone revenue rose 36% yoy, of which 12.9% was aluminium cost pass-through, which is not the full pass-through (GS). Standalone revenue was 10.8% above Kotak's estimates, helped by industry 2W volume growth above 20%, new order ramp-ups and higher realisations (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.36 bn (+20.7% yoy) was 1% above consensus, so in line. The margin of 12.4% was 50 bps below consensus and down 96 bps yoy, as raw-material inflation was only partly passed through. Standalone margin was 10.9%, 160 bps below Kotak's estimate, on higher metal prices. Kotak put consolidated EBITDA 5.4% below its own estimates on commodity headwinds and higher employee costs in India and Europe (GS, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management is confident of passing through the remaining aluminium inflation, which is 60% of BOM cost, and is in talks on steel, rubber and plastics. Aluminium prices have softened by Rs12-17/kg in 2QFY27, so standalone margins are expected to improve in 2QFY27 and 3QFY27. GS raised FY27E-29E EPS by 6%-11% and its TP to Rs3,090 from Rs2,710. Kotak cut FY27-28E EPS by 2-4% on lower gross margin assumptions and retains ADD with fair value Rs3,000 (from Rs2,750). ABS capacity expansion was cut to 0.9 mn from 1.2 mn units as machinery is shifted to disc brakes. Alloy wheel and Shendra casting ramp-ups continue (GS, Kotak).

companies.name: Exide Industries
companies.note: NMC cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines commenced sample supplies, with the Bengaluru plant’s revenue generation expected from FY27E. Phase-I capacity remains at 6GWh (expandable to 12GWh) with 25-30% initial utilisation, while FY27E revenues will be driven by 2W/3W, telecom and stationary applications before expanding into BESS and 4W as additional lines are commissioned. Exide is in the process of homologation with three 2W EV OEMs in India which comprise ~80-85% cumulative market share. While Hyundai contract is seeing some delays, Exide is in conversations with two major 4W OEMs and factory visits have started (4W line is planned for commissioning FY27 end.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 18% YoY to Rs53.1bn, 6% above JPMe and 7% above Bloomberg consensus. Growth was led by automotive OEM (+25% YoY, third straight quarter above 25%), reserve power (+20%), double-digit 2W/4W replacement and international (+20%+), helped by 4-6% price hikes (JP; Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 20% YoY to Rs6.6bn, 10% above JPMe. Margin was 12.4% (+70bps QoQ, +20bps YoY) against JPMe/Street at 11.9%/11.7%, as operating leverage and cost control offset higher input costs. Kotak put it 9.6% above its estimate (JP; Kotak).

outlook.note: Management gave no full-year revenue guidance but expects 25-30% Li-ion capacity utilisation in FY27, with homologation under way with three 2W EV OEMs. JPM expects consensus upgrades and raised FY27-29E EPS by 2-7% (FY27E EBITDA +4.8% to Rs22.8bn) and its PT to Rs514 from Rs485. Kotak also raised FY27-29E EPS by 5-12% but stays Sell (FV Rs325) on LiB capex and return-ratio concerns (JP; Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR34.1bn (+36.6% y-y) was 5% above consensus and Nomura estimates, helped by ~16-17% y-y PV industry production growth, higher EV content (8.5% of revenue), new model launches, and ~7pp from higher copper prices. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR2.6bn (+5.7% y-y) was 8% below consensus. Margin fell to 7.6% vs 8.6% consensus, as employee cost/sales jumped to 17.7% (+213bp q-q) on minimum wage revisions in Delhi-NCR, and RM/sales rose to 69.1% on copper inflation. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management is negotiating with customers to recover wage and copper cost increases (copper pass-through lags 3-6 months and should fully reflect by the Sep quarter), with 2H margin recovery expected. Nomura raised FY27/28 revenue by ~6% but cut EBITDA margins to 9.4%/9.8% (down 100bp), lowering EBITDA/EPS by ~5%; Buy and INR50 TP maintained. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Sales (ex other income) of Rs 11,054mn were +23.5% YoY and 2.9% above GS's Rs 10,744mn estimate. The report's table compares against GSe, not a consensus figure. [GS]
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 1,244mn was +25.7% YoY and 16.7% above GSe's Rs 1,066mn. Margin was 11.3% against GSe's 9.9% and 11.1% a year earlier, despite commodity, freight, labour and LPG cost pressures. Management still sees 50-100bps of commodity cost left to pass through. [GS]

outlook.note: GS raised its FY27E-FY29E EPS estimates by 11-13% and its 12-month target price to Rs 870 from Rs 780 (Buy). FY27E EBITDA rises 8.8% to Rs 5,834mn and FY27E revenue 1.5% to Rs 48,580mn. Management expects 150-200bps of fixed-cost absorption as revenue rises over the next 1-2 quarters. Pass-through of 50-100bps of commodity cost is still to come. More business from Honda is a key driver, and the Polymer division is running out of capacity to serve it. Near-term capex is high at Rs 4bn for Polymer, Rs 1.8bn for DIVCS and Rs 1.2bn for ACFMS. Management said the DIVCS demerger would help attract investment and technology partners. [GS]

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 17% YoY to Rs352bn, about 2% above Bloomberg consensus, so in line. Wiring harness grew 31% YoY and beat, and emerging businesses grew c.30% YoY. Modules & Polymers, Vision Systems and SAS were soft. Revenue was 4% below MS's own estimate. (MS, GS, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 26% YoY to Rs31.0bn, about 1% above Bloomberg consensus and in line with Factset. EBITDA margin was 8.8%, up 60bps YoY but down 230bps QoQ. Wiring harness margin fell only c.30bps YoY and QoQ despite copper and polymer inflation. EBITDA was 6% below MS's own forecast. (MS, GS, CLSA)

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs343bn (+17% yoy) was about 4% above Bloomberg consensus of Rs329.4bn (Nomura) and 6% above Kotak's estimate. Emerging businesses grew 60% yoy, and the wiring harness and vision systems divisions grew 11-19% yoy on favourable translation and content growth (Nomura, Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs37.9bn (+43% yoy, +25% qoq) was 21% ahead of consensus and 16% ahead of Kotak's estimate. Margin of 11% was 90 bps above Kotak's estimate and +200 bps yoy, helped by lower other expenses and better profitability in wiring harness and emerging businesses (Nomura, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management plans a third consumer electronics plant with c.Rs75bn capex over three years (40mn units at full capacity) and FY27 capex guidance of c.Rs60bn. GS sees 56mn units of consumer electronics capacity by FY29. GS raised FY27-29 EPS by up to 10% (TP Rs148 to Rs158) and CLSA raised FY27-28 EPS by 4% (TP Rs173 to Rs190). MS left EPS changes under 5% but lifted TP from Rs150 to Rs173 on higher consumer electronics value. MS flags a possibly softer F2Q27 in auto, with copper pressure on margins and a lag before pass-through. (MS, GS, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs10.2bn were 9.3% above BBG consensus and 4.5% above GSe, up 33% yoy. The higher-margin ADS (aerospace, defence, semiconductor) segment grew 130% yoy to Rs2.0bn, 20% ahead of GSe, and is now about 14% of revenue vs 4% a year ago, while Auto-ICE grew 21% yoy. (GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.96bn was 18.5% above consensus and 19.4% above GSe, up 48% yoy. Margin was 19.2% vs 17.7% consensus, helped by gross margin expanding 247bps vs GSe to 60.5% on the richer ADS mix. (GS)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR10.0bn (+28% y-y) was 7% above Bloomberg consensus and 4% above Nomura. Non-auto revenue rose 70% y-y, led by the Aerospace, Defence and Semiconductor division, and India exports rose 44% y-y. (Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR1.9bn (+52% y-y) was 19% above consensus, with the margin at 19.3% (+306bp y-y) against 17.4% expected. RM/sales was flat q-q at 42.3%, and other costs/sales fell 60bp q-q to 25.4%. (Nomura)

outlook.note: The ADS order book rose to Rs57bn from Rs44bn, driven by a large Semicon order from an existing customer, with more RFQs in discussion. A dedicated defence plant (Rs5bn revenue potential) and hangar expansion are planned. Sansera is in talks with customers to pass on higher steel and aluminium costs. GS raised FY27-29E revenue slightly (FY27E Rs42.9bn vs Rs42.5bn) and lifted FY28-29E EPS, while FY27E EPS was trimmed (69.1 vs 72.2) after the Rs169mn exceptional item, and raised the TP to Rs4,500 from Rs4,130. CLSA initiated at Outperform with a TP of Rs4,954, expecting ADS revenue to reach about Rs15bn p.a. by FY29 and EPS to more than double in three years. (GS, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs27.6 bn (+17% yoy) were 2.0% above Kotak's estimate. Automotive technologies grew 33% yoy on new order ramp-up, exports grew 24%, aftermarket 10% and bearings/industrial 5%. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.0 bn (+16% yoy) was 0.5% below Kotak's estimate, as higher fuel, IT and freight costs offset the stronger revenue. Margin was 18.1% (-20 bps yoy, -40 bps qoq). (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management expects exports to grow 15-20% yoy in CY2026E, backed by capacity reallocation to India and a strong order backlog, though geopolitical tension is a concern. Kotak sees PV, 2W and CV demand improving on GST rationalisation. Its CY26/27/28E EBITDA estimates moved +0.3%/-0.2%/-0.5% and the fair value rose to Rs4,225 from Rs4,150. It keeps REDUCE because the price already reflects the positives, and Koovers losses continue (EBITDA margin -17.3%). (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs2,610mn (+24.5% yoy) were 3% above BBG consensus and 2% above GS estimates. Growth was led by Decoplast (chrome plating, +38% yoy) and Walterpack (+33%), while SJS Standalone grew 16%. (GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs747mn (+34% yoy) was 9% above consensus. Margin was 28.6% against 27.0% consensus, up 194bps yoy and flat qoq. GS attributes this to better chrome plating, a higher export mix and PV segment revenues. (GS)

outlook.note: Management expects c50-60bps of raw material inflation pass-through to support profitability. It expects the export mix to rise to 15% of revenue from 10% in 1Q27, and Rs2.5bn of FY29 revenue optionality from the new chrome plating facility. Cover glass revenue should start in 2QFY28E, and FY28 revenue growth should be 1.5x-2.0x India auto production growth. GS raised its FY27-29 estimates by up to 10% and its target price to Rs3,080 from Rs2,850. (GS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs5,878 mn grew 27% yoy and was 1.1% below Kotak's estimate of Rs5,945 mn, so in line. Growth came from strong double-digit growth in PV, 2W and CV and double-digit export growth, partly offset by lower aftermarket volumes (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs880 mn (+19% yoy, +164% qoq) was 12.5% above Kotak's Rs783 mn. The margin was 15.0%, 180 bps above estimate, on a better gross margin (+6.5% qoq on favourable product mix and lower-cost inventory) and lower other operating expenses (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management now expects about 20% yoy revenue growth in FY27E, up from the earlier 12% guidance. It sees a 17% EBITDA margin as normalized for the next two years, and Rs1.7-1.8 bn of the Rs5 bn capex comes online this year. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 3-12% on higher margin assumptions (FY27E EBITDA +7.2%) but kept SELL with FV Rs1,500 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of INR13.1bn grew 54% YoY and 3% QoQ, 2.5% above Bloomberg consensus (0.7% above Nomura). BEV revenue rose 107% YoY to 44% of automotive product sales, and more than 35% of revenue came from new products (Nomura, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR3.0bn (+49.5% YoY) was 3.6% above consensus, with margin at 23.1% vs 22.8% consensus. Margin fell 70bp YoY because of higher commodity costs, a lower-margin product mix (traction motors) and delayed pass-through, partly offset by operating leverage (Nomura, JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management aspires to 10x growth over FY25-35E. Demand is healthy across markets (Europe stable and growing, US improving), the order book is INR240bn (INR8bn of it in robotics and Physical AI), and the two Denso JVs are announced. Costs have eased since April-May. Nomura raised its TP to INR848 (from INR720) on a higher target P/E, with FY28F estimates largely unchanged. CLSA raised FY27-28CL EPS by 4-15% and its TP to Rs811 (from Rs570). JP raised FY27-29E EPS by 2-3% but stays Underweight on valuation (Nomura, CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 15% yoy to Rs9.43 bn, 2% below Kotak's estimate (Rs9.63 bn) on low-single-digit growth in railways and aftermarket, partly offset by >20% yoy growth in CVs and process industries (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.78 bn (+21% yoy) was 1% above Kotak's estimate as gross margin of 40.0% beat estimates, partly offset by higher employee and other expenses. EBITDA margin was 18.8%, up 90 bps yoy and 50 bps above estimate (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 14.6% yoy and 39.8% qoq, 2.1% above Kotak's estimate. Double-digit yoy growth in export CV and process industries, plus high single-digit growth in domestic CVs, more than offset a marginal decline in railways (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 12.7% yoy and 129% qoq, 7.5% above Kotak's estimate on a better product mix. Gross margin improved 410 bps qoq, partly offset by higher other expenses. EBITDA margin was 22.2% (-40 bps yoy), 140 bps above estimate (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management gave no specific revenue or margin guidance but aims to outgrow the market and is passing through costs over the next two quarters to protect margins against rising steel, coolant and currency costs. Bharuch plant utilisation is expected to cross 70% by Aug-Sep 2026, exports are up >20% yoy, and the new rail bearing line targets first bearing by Nov 2026. Kotak raised FY27-29E EBITDA by 0-2% on higher gross margin, lifted fair value to Rs3,700 (from Rs3,650) and expects a 15% revenue CAGR over FY26-29E (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 24% yoy (26% on an adjusted base, as 1QFY26 included a Rs690 mn one-off incentive), 4% above Bloomberg consensus. Growth was led by switching (+20%), lighting (+14%), casting (+32%), seating (+28%) and green mobility (+78%), helped by industry tailwinds and new order ramp-up (GS, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.7 bn (+5% yoy, -5% qoq) was about 2% above consensus (GS) but 1.4% below Kotak's estimate. The 10.3% margin (-180 bps yoy) was hit by weaker gross margin from commodity and gas inflation (about 40 bps dilution) and minimum wage revisions. GS notes aluminium pass-through was smoother than it expected (GS, Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 18% YoY and 6% QoQ to Rs53.4bn, with broad-based growth: switches +17%, lighting +13%, castings +14%, seating +17%, and green mobility and other businesses +25%. CLSA called the operating result in line with consensus expectations. (Jeff, CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 14% YoY to Rs6.03bn, with margin at 11.3%, down 33bp YoY, as aluminium cost inflation of 4-5% weighed on castings. Jefferies said EBITDA was in line with its estimates, and CLSA said in line with consensus. (Jeff, CLSA)

outlook.note: Management kept the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance at 10.5-11.5% and expects to recover another 40 bps of raw-material inflation over the next 2 quarters. New model wins, 4W seating (production from 4QFY28) and the Inovance EV powertrain JV support growth ahead of industry. FY27-29E EPS estimates were raised by up to 7.4% (GS) and 3-7% (Kotak); GS lifted its TP to Rs1,510, and Kotak flags China tech-transfer risk for the Inovance JV (GS, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs26.3 bn (+30% yoy, +11% qoq) was 13% above Kotak's estimate. India business grew 29% yoy on broad-based double-digit industry growth across segments, and overseas grew 46% yoy on stronger order execution (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.2 bn was 4% above Kotak's estimate (+14% yoy), helped by the higher revenue print and partly offset by higher-than-expected other expenses. Margin was 8.4%, down 100 bps qoq and 70 bps below estimate, on a higher mix of lower-margin tooling sales, casual manpower cost and under-recovery of war-related inflation (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs23.7 bn grew 13% yoy but came in 4.4% below Kotak's estimate. India business grew 12% yoy, held back by slower growth in higher-content segments and Tier-2/3 supplier disruption, while overseas grew 24% on order execution (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.2 bn was 6.2% below Kotak's estimate and up only 0.7% yoy, on the revenue shortfall and higher-than-expected other expenses. Margin was 9.4% (+20 bps qoq), 20 bps below estimate, with gross margin up 90 bps qoq on better mix (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management reiterated the Romania/overseas breakeven target by end-4QFY27E and guided Rs5.0-5.5 bn capex for FY27. Net order wins carry Rs6.0 bn of annual peak revenue and the order book is Rs36.1 bn, up from Rs35.1 bn. Kotak raised FY28-29E EPS by 7-8% on higher revenue assumptions but expects margin recovery to stay below expectations given competitive intensity in EV and the B2B nature of the business, and keeps REDUCE with FV Rs650 (from Rs550) (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs33.8bn (+19% y/y, +2% q/q) was 4% above MSe. NII was 3% above on loan growth of 23% y/y, and non-interest income was 10% above on core fees (+33% y/y, 13% above MSe) from higher volumes and credit card and transaction banking fees. NIM slipped 7bp q/q to 5.89%, still better than the 5.70% MSe expected. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs14.4bn (+9% y/y, +6% q/q) was only 1% above MSe. A revenue beat was largely offset by opex 7% above MSe (+26% y/y), driven by volumes and continued investment, with cost/income at 57.6% vs 56.1% MSe. Core PPOP was 2% above MSe at Rs14.3bn (+41% y/y). (MS)

outlook.note: Management reiterated its 1.8% FY27 RoA guidance, led by better asset quality and operating leverage, and its medium-term growth aim of about 2-2.5x nominal GDP. It gave no NIM guidance. MS sees largely unchanged forecasts with possible upside risk and keeps its Rs1,205 PT. JPM revises FY27-29 estimates by 0-1% (FY27E net income +1.2%) and keeps Rs1,230. Nomura raises EPS by 3% each year for FY27-28 on lower credit cost and opex, and lifts its PT to Rs980 from Rs975 while staying Neutral. Nomura also sees margin pressure from higher CoF. (MS, JP, Nomura)

1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs116.6bn was up 1% YoY and 16% QoQ, 1.6% above CLSA's estimate. Opex rose only 5% YoY (Rs97.2bn), 4.8% below CLSA's estimate, which offset the weaker NII. Provisions were low at Rs22.2bn (credit cost 0.7%), so PBT beat by 2.7% and PAT of Rs71.1bn rose 23% YoY (CLSA, Jeff).

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs219.0bn (+7.5% y/y, +2.4% q/q) was 2.0% below JPMe. NII of Rs153.7bn (+11.8% y/y) was 3% ahead of JPMe, but non-interest income fell 1.4% y/y and came in 11% below JPMe on weak treasury income (JP). Nomura also cites a 1.6% NII beat offset by weaker fee and treasury income (Nomura).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs110.8bn (+6.4% y/y, -4.9% q/q) missed JPMe by 4.9%. The miss came from the non-interest income shortfall and opex up 9% y/y (+1% vs JPMe). Opex was inflated by Rs2.5bn of one-offs, including labour code provisions (JP, Nomura). PAT still beat on lower credit costs of 51bps vs JPMe 80bps (JP).

outlook.note: Management expects sequential NIM improvement as FCNR(B) liquidity is deployed into higher-yielding loans, but gave no 3Q NIM trajectory and reiterated its 3.8% through-cycle target. JP raised FY27-29E EPS by 1.9%/1.5%/2.5% and its PT to Rs1,620. Nomura sees a more gradual NIM recovery from 4QFY27, cut FY27-28 EPS by 2%/4% and cut its PT to Rs1,525.
