Jeff raised core estimates (FY27 EPS +4%) while factoring a 30% hit to bancassurance fees from FY28 and credit cost rising to 0.8% in FY28. Estimate changes are mixed (JP, Nomura, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Operating income was up 1% YoY and down 1% QoQ at Rs35.2bn. NII rose 6% YoY / 4% QoQ (NII ~1% above Nomura's forecast) and fee income was strong, but other income fell 17% YoY (Rs6.0bn). Jefferies notes 18% YoY net loan growth with non-MFI loans +27%. (Jeff, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs13.6bn was down 19% YoY and 6% QoQ, and Nomura called core PPOP in-line, because the NII and fee beat was offset by higher opex. Opex rose 19% YoY, with employee costs +21% (including a Rs0.6bn one-off gratuity provision for the new labour code). Lower credit costs (1.8%) drove the PAT beat (Rs5.0bn, +35% YoY; 8% above Nomura's estimate), not PPOP. (Jeff, Nomura)

outlook.note: Management cut FY27 exit RoA guidance to 1.2-1.4% from 1.6-1.8% (30bp lower NIMs from higher funding costs, 10bp higher opex), while guiding to early-to-mid-teens loan growth and falling credit costs. Nomura cut FY27-28F EPS 4-7% and the TP to INR190 (Neutral). Jefferies cut estimates by ~10% and the TP to Rs240 (Buy), seeing the guidance as conservative given possible FCNR-B inflows. Kotak kept estimates and FV of Rs235 unchanged (Buy), with a gradual path to RoA improvement driven by credit cost. (Nomura, Jeff, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs160.0bn was 1.7% above Kotak's estimate and down 0.7% YoY. NII rose 9.5% YoY to Rs125.3bn, in line with estimates (NIM 2.57%, down ~10bps QoQ). Non-interest income fell 26% YoY on fee income down 47% YoY, partly offset by treasury and recoveries. (Kotak, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs81.3bn was 15.6% above Kotak's estimate (Rs70.3bn) but down 1.3% YoY. The beat came from operating costs 9.5% below estimate (other opex down 13% vs estimate). Nomura saw core PPOP (Rs64.8bn) 4% below its estimate on lower fees, so the quality of the beat is mixed. Reported PAT fell ~70% YoY on a Rs56.8bn one-off legal settlement provision. (Kotak, Nomura, CLSA)

outlook.note: Management kept guidance: 12-14% loan growth, 10-12% deposit growth, NIM 2.8-2.9%, credit cost ~60bps, RoA above 1% and RoE ~15%. The ECL transition is a negative, with a one-time ~110bps CRAR hit and run-rate credit cost 15-20bps higher. Brokers trimmed estimates and targets, mainly for the one-off charge. Kotak cut its fair value to Rs280 (from Rs285). Nomura cut its target to Rs280 (from Rs300) and FY27F EPS by 13%. CLSA cut FY27 PAT and FY28 PAT by 2%. Kotak and Nomura (ADD/Neutral) see no re-rating trigger. CLSA stays Outperform with a Rs335 target. (Kotak, Nomura, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs94.1bn (+14% YoY, -5% QoQ) was 8% above MSe, driven by other income of Rs18.9bn vs MSe Rs11.4bn (trading income Rs4.1bn vs Rs3.0bn est.). NII was 1% below MSe and core revenue was in line (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs50.5bn (+26% YoY) was 16% above MSe on the other-income upside and opex only 1% above estimate, with cost/income at 46.3% vs 49.7% est. Core PPOP was 2% below MSe, and NIM fell 6bp QoQ to 2.52% (MS).

outlook.note: Management cut FY27 NIM guidance to 2.55-2.60% from 2.70-2.75%, citing a challenging NIM environment, while keeping loan growth at 15-16% and deposit growth at 13-14%. MS expects ROA to moderate to ~0.6% over F27-29 from 1.0% in FY26 as trading income, recoveries and credit costs normalise, and keeps its Underweight rating with a modest downward revision to consensus EPS (MS).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs4,369mn (+17% YoY, -1% QoQ) was 1% above MSe. NII beat by 2% on 18% YoY growth, offset by other income 20% below estimate. Loan growth was 11% YoY, led by non-housing loans. (MS, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs3,516mn (+16% YoY, -1% QoQ) was 1% below MSe, as opex was 8% above estimate (employee costs +5%, other opex +12%). The cost-to-income ratio was 19.5%. PAT of Rs2,678mn was in line with MSe and 2% above VA consensus on lower credit costs (12bp vs 15bp MSe). (MS, Jeff)

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs4.41bn (+7% YoY, +1% QoQ) was in line with MSe of Rs4.40bn (0% variance). NII grew 7% YoY and was in line, while other income was 10% below MSe. (MS)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs3.55bn (+6% YoY) was 1% above MSe of Rs3.52bn, with opex 2% below estimate. The PAT beat (~3% vs MSe and Visible Alpha consensus) came mainly from lower credit costs (7bp vs MSe 15bp), not operating profit. (MS, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management retains its Rs130bn FY27 disbursement guidance and expects 15% AUM growth in FY28. Tech-rollout disruption cut Sep-Q disbursements by about Rs3.6bn, and these should normalise from Dec Q. NIMs are expected to stay range-bound near term as liabilities reprice faster than assets. Jefferies lifted FY27E EPS 2.5% and trimmed FY28E by under 1%, and cut its PT to Rs1,025 from Rs1,075 (Jeff, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs169.4bn was 11.5% above Kotak's estimate (+5.4% YoY, +16% QoQ). NII grew 13% YoY, and PSLC income of ~Rs16.8bn (up ~35% YoY) and a 19% YoY rise in recoveries from TWO offset a 60% fall in treasury income. (Kotak, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs86.4bn was 24% above Kotak's estimate but only +1.0% YoY, as operating costs rose ~10% (non-staff cost +~20%). MS calls core PPOP weak, 13% below its estimate on 18% lower core fees, with the headline lifted by non-core income. (Kotak, MS)

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs167.8bn was +3.6% YoY and in line with Kotak's estimate (+0.1%). NII grew a strong 20% YoY, but non-interest income fell about 18% on a ~90% drop in treasury income and a ~25% fall in TWO recoveries and FX income (Kotak). Core revenue was in line, as the NII beat (4% above MSE) was offset by a core fee miss (~10% below MSE) (MS).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs87.6bn was +2.0% YoY and 5.1% above Kotak's estimate. Operating costs grew only ~5% YoY and staff costs were flat (Kotak). Core PPOP beat MSE by 8% on 4% lower opex (MS).

outlook.note: MS raised FY27-29e EPS by +13%/+6%/-2%. It lifted NII estimates 6-11%, raised opex 3-8% and raised credit costs 2-3bp, and it kept its Rs109 target and UW rating. Management guides NIM stable at ~2.55% near term. Kotak sees NIM turning to a modest upside as the rate-hike cycle begins and keeps its Rs165 fair value with a BUY. The one-time ECL transition provision is ~Rs120-150bn (~1% of advances, a 140-170bp hit to CET-1 per MSE) and is an overhang (Kotak, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Total income grew 22% yoy (NII +31% yoy, other income flat), about 0.7% below Kotak's estimate, so broadly in line; loan growth was ~25% yoy and NIM held at 3.8% qoq (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 28.8% yoy and was 5.6% above Kotak's estimate, helped by operating costs coming in 7.4% below estimate (+15% yoy), which Kotak called 'operating profits strong for the quarter' (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guidance is broadly unchanged: RoA is guided at ~1.5-1.6%, NIM around current levels with some downside bias from higher term-deposit rates, and slippages (~1.2%) and credit costs (~0.4%) are expected to hold. Kotak marginally raised its earnings estimates and lifted FV to Rs200 (from Rs188) but keeps SELL on valuation and gold-loan concentration (~30% of loans). It expects ECL to have a 60-65 bps impact on CAR (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs8.8bn was 1.2% above Kotak's estimate and up 7.8% YoY. NII grew 18% YoY, but non-interest income fell 17% as the base quarter had a higher treasury contribution (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs3.44bn was 5.3% above Kotak's estimate and up 5.2% YoY. Opex rose only 2.2% QoQ, and the cost-to-income ratio was 60.9% against Kotak's 62.4% estimate. Net profit rose 36% YoY, helped by a ~50% YoY fall in provisions (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management is confident of defending margins despite industry funding-cost pressure. It sees a long runway in gold loans, which grew 125% YoY. MSME and mortgage growth was softer on seasonality and deliberate origination choices. Asset quality shows no stress, and credit costs were ~40 bps. Kotak broadly kept near-term estimates, held Fair Value at Rs225 and maintained BUY (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs12.8 bn was ~2.7% above Kotak's estimate (Rs12.5 bn) and up 19% yoy. NII grew ~30% yoy on ~27% advances growth. Non-interest income fell ~15% yoy because of lower treasury income, partly offset by asset-linked fees growing ~40%. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs4.05 bn was ~8% above Kotak's estimate and up 29% yoy. Operating costs grew 15% yoy (staff cost ~+19-20%) and the cost-income ratio improved ~150 bps yoy to 68%. PAT was Rs1.8 bn (RoE 11.8%) against a loss in 1QFY26. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guides for advances growth of >20% in FY27, RoA of 1.2% in FY27 and 1.5% by 4QFY27, NIM to decline a further ~15 bps in FY27, and credit cost to fall from current levels. Microfinance has normalised, slippages are at 3.5% (near post-Covid low) and NNPL is 0.7%. Kotak keeps BUY with an unchanged FV of Rs95, expects RoE to improve, and sees FY27E EPS of Rs7.6. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Total income rose 16% YoY to Rs39.9bn as NII grew 26% YoY (+8% QoQ) on a 13bp QoQ rise in core NIM to 3.33%, while other income fell 6% YoY. Brokers split against their own estimates: JPM was 4% below, while MS had NII 2% above and fees 2% above, and CLSA had NII 5% above (JPM, MS, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 22% YoY to Rs19.0bn but fell 17% QoQ. Opex grew 11% YoY and was 1% below JPM's estimate. The PPOP read differs by broker: JPM 7% below, MS core PPoP 7% above, and CLSA a marginal beat. MS called PAT 10% above its estimate and in line with consensus (JPM, MS, CLSA).
1Q27.vsBasis: broker estimates (mixed: JPM, MS, CLSA); no consensus figure for these lines

2Q27.revNote: Total income rose 30% YoY and 16% QoQ to Rs 46.4bn, 9% above JPMe (MS: 12% above MSe). NII was up 26% YoY (3% above JPMe), and non-interest income was up 38% YoY, 23% above JPMe on strong fee and trading income. Core revenue was 6% above MSe. GS also called it a revenue beat, with NII 3% and fees 10% above GSe. (JP, MS, GS)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 35% YoY and 17% QoQ to Rs 22.3bn, 9% above JPMe (MS: 14% above MSe). Opex rose 25% YoY, 8% above JPMe, on branch, people and technology investment plus a Rs 327mn ESOP accounting impact. Core PPOP was in line with MSe (+1%), with the headline beat driven by treasury gains. Cost/income improved 42bps QoQ to 52.1%. (JP, MS)

outlook.note: Management reiterated high-teens loan growth (ex-FCNR 18% YoY) and guided to a 5-6bps per quarter NIM improvement despite the FCNR drag. GS raises FY27-29E earnings by 1-2% and sees c.20% revenue CAGR over FY26-29E on c.18% loan CAGR. JP expects street upgrades after the strong 2Q but stays Neutral on valuation (1.6x FY28E P/B). MS sees the stock pricing in NIM and ROA gains (EW). (GS, JP, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income (NII + other income) was flat QoQ and down 13% YoY only because 1Q26 included a Rs101bn profit on sale of investments. NII grew 7% YoY and 1% QoQ as 12bp of NIM compression offset 16% loan growth, slightly below Jefferies' estimate but in line with CLSA's. [Jeff, CLSA]
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs281.7bn (-21% YoY on the high base, +1% QoQ) was largely in line with CLSA's estimate. Opex grew only 4% YoY (-2% QoQ), and Nomura's core PPOP of Rs278bn was 1% above its estimate. Ex-treasury operating profit grew 8% YoY. [Jeff, CLSA, Nomura]

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs484.5bn (+6% YoY, +5% QoQ) was 1% above Visible Alpha consensus. NII grew 10% YoY to Rs346.2bn and in line with consensus, while other income was 2% above, helped by core fees (+10% YoY) and a Rs7.8bn treasury gain (vs Rs23.9bn a year ago) (GS).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating profit of Rs294.8bn (+6% YoY, +5% QoQ) was 1% above Visible Alpha consensus and 6% above GS's estimate. Opex grew 6% YoY against core revenue growth of 10%, and core PPOP rose 13% YoY, about 2% above GS's estimate. NIM fell 8bp QoQ to 3.32% (GS).

outlook.note: Estimates are largely unchanged. GS keeps EPS broadly flat with a Rs861 TP, and Nomura cuts its TP to Rs940 from Rs950 on a higher risk-free rate. Jefferies lifts FY27/FY28 EPS by 6%/1% and holds a Rs880 TP. Positives are that NIM has likely troughed at 3.32% and the rate-hike cycle should help, with GS expecting NIM to recover to 3.4% by 4QFY27. Constraints are that deposit mobilisation is the swing factor, with LCR at 113%, near the low end of the 110-120% band, and that new CEO Anup Bagchi's strategy is awaited (GS, Nomura, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Total income rose 9% YoY and 9% QoQ. NII grew 13% YoY, 3% ahead of CLSA's estimate (core NII 1% ahead), helped by loan growth accelerating to 20% YoY. Fee income grew 24% on a low base and strong business momentum. The CLSA table is in Rs bn and rounded, so these figures are coarse. No consensus or line-level estimate comparison is printed for total income (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating profit (PPOP) of Rs204bn was up 9% YoY and 12% QoQ. Opex was controlled (+10% YoY, cost/income 39.7% vs 41.4%). PAT of Rs148bn (+16% YoY) was ahead of CLSA's estimate, with credit cost at 32bps helped by a one-off corporate recovery. No PPOP vs consensus figure is printed (CLSA).

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs334bn (+15% y/y, +1% q/q) was in line with Visible Alpha consensus (0%) and 1% below GS. NII of Rs253.4bn (+18% y/y) beat consensus by 2%, while non-interest income of Rs80.5bn missed by 6% as treasury swung to a Rs2.3bn loss and a lower subsidiary dividend weighed. Core revenue grew 18% y/y. (GS, Nomura, JP)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs205.8bn (+19% y/y, +1% q/q) was 2% above consensus (in line on our +/-2% rule) and flat vs GS. Opex grew only 9% y/y against core revenue growth of 18%, with cost/income at 38.4% vs 41.2% expected by JP. Core PPOP of Rs203bn was +25% y/y and 6% above consensus, and PAT of Rs148.4bn was 6% above consensus on credit costs of 20bp. (GS, JP)

outlook.note: Brokers raised FY27-29E EPS by 4%/4%/5% (GS), 4.1%/4.6% for FY27/28 (JP) and 3%/7% for FY27/28 (Nomura), and lifted targets on the back of the beat. FCNR(B) deposits (~8% of the total) are to be deployed over the next two quarters, and loan growth estimates were raised sharply (Nomura FY27 loans +26%). JP sees NIM expansion in 4Q and FY28, with 57% of the loan book linked to repo and 50bp of rate hikes now built in. Steady-state credit costs are ~50bp. (JP, Nomura, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs82.8bn (+16% YoY, +13% QoQ) was 5% above MSe, helped by non-interest income 11% above MSe (core fees +23% YoY, 5% above MSe; other income Rs1.8bn vs Rs0.5bn est.) and adjusted NIM of 5.90%, about 12bp above MSe (MS). Nomura also flags NII +5% QoQ, 3% ahead of its estimate (Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating profit of Rs25.5bn (+14% YoY) was 12% above MSe, with opex in line (1% above) so the beat came from income. Core PPoP of Rs23.7bn (+36% YoY) was 7% ahead of MSe; Nomura puts core PPOP 10% above its estimate (MS, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 NIM guidance to 5.8% from 5.75%, cut credit cost guidance to 150-160bp from 170-180bp, and targets 1.0% ROA in FY27. MS raised FY27 EPS 34% and FY28/FY29 EPS 5% each, and PT to Rs75 from Rs65 (Equal-weight). Nomura raised FY27/28 EPS by 9-17% and PT to INR95 from INR85 (Buy) (MS, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Total income rose 32% YoY and 5% QoQ to Rs22.0bn, driven by 38% YoY AUM growth and a 55% YoY jump in NII. Stronger NII offset lower assignment income (Rs749mn vs Rs2,054mn in 4Q) and fees down 23% QoQ (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 44% YoY and 7% QoQ to Rs12.5bn as opex grew only 18% YoY. NIM rose 50bps QoQ to 7.2% on higher yields, and credit cost fell 24bps QoQ to 1.8%. PAT of Rs6.7bn was in line with Jefferies' estimate (Jeff).

2Q27.revNote: Total revenue rose 23% y/y and 6% q/q to Rs23.4bn, 3% above JPMe. NII grew 39% y/y (13% q/q) on 38% y/y AuM growth led by gold loans, while non-interest income fell 4% q/q as off-book income dropped 7% q/q (JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPoP grew 31% y/y and 8% q/q to Rs13.6bn, 2% above JPMe. NIM expanded 24bps q/q to 6.0% and gold yields rose 15bps q/q, but costs ran 5% above JPMe. PAT of Rs7.7bn was 6% above JPMe and 4% above consensus, helped by provisions 12% below JPMe, and Jefferies calls it in line with its estimate (JP, Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies raised FY27-28e EPS by 13%/7% on stronger loan growth, better NIM and lower credit costs, partly offset by lower fee income. It expects AUM growth of 24% in FY27 (guidance 25%) and some moderation in FY28, and flags risks to fee income from tighter insurance commission norms. JPMorgan expects positive Street EPS revisions, but flags gold asset quality (GNPA +29bps q/q) and a possible capital raise as watch points (Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs64.7bn was 5.4% above JPMe, helped by NII beating JPMe by 6% (Rs2.84bn of interest on tax refund included) and non-interest income 3.6% above JPMe. Core NII rose 1% q/q and was in line, with core NIM down 4bps q/q to 3.35% on loan mix change and higher RIDF; non-II fell 4% q/q on core basis while trading income rose 10% (JP). CLSA also saw adjusted NII in line with its estimates (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs27.7bn beat JPMe by 18.9% and rose 8.0% y/y, driven by opex 3% below JPMe (-2% q/q, -12.6% y/y) with cost/income improving sharply to 57.1% from 62.3% in 4Q. Core PPOP (ex tax-refund interest) was Rs25.6bn, 19.1% above JPMe (JP). CLSA likewise cited lower opex and credit costs for core PBT of Rs10.6bn vs its Rs8.5bn estimate (CLSA).

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of loan growth in line with the industry and an exit RoA of ~1%, aided by operating leverage and lower credit costs; loans grew ~3% q/q after five quarters of decline and asset quality improved (GNPA/NNPA 3.25%/0.95%). JPM raised FY27-29 EPS by 4-19% (FY27E EPS +18.7%) and its PT to Rs820 from Rs720 but stays UW on valuation; CLSA lifted FY27-29 PAT 1-3% and TP to Rs925 (downgraded to U-PF after the stock's 17% run-up); Jefferies raised FY27-29 estimates and PT to Rs1,250, seeing ~1.1% RoA by FY29 (JP, CLSA, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income grew 22% yoy to Rs18.6 bn, in line with Kotak's Rs18.8 bn estimate (0.9% below). NII rose 32% yoy on 17% loan growth and a 4.3% reported NIM, while non-interest income was 14% below estimate (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 36% yoy to Rs11.0 bn, 4% above Kotak's estimate. Opex was 7% below estimate (up 7% yoy), and NII was 4% above, lifting the cost-income ratio to 41.2% (Kotak).

2Q27.revNote: Total income rose 8.9% YoY to Rs19.3 bn, 1.9% below Kotak's estimate. NII grew 18.7% YoY on ~20% loan growth and a flat-QoQ NIM of 4.3%, partly offset by a 10.7% miss on non-interest income vs estimate (Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP grew 14.2% YoY to Rs11.6 bn, 1.3% above Kotak's estimate. Operating expenses were flat YoY, which offset the weaker non-interest income and kept the cost-income ratio at 39.9% vs 42.6% a year ago (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management reiterated its strategy and NIM guidance of ~4% for 2HFY27, and expects gross NPA <1.5% and slippages <1% of loans. It flagged yield-pressure risk in some lending segments as competitors turn more aggressive. Kotak raised its FV to Rs300 from Rs285 on NIM resilience but kept SELL on valuation, with a relative call against frontline banks given the gold-loan concentration. Its FY27E EPS is Rs31.2, with a slight dip in FY28E (-1.4%) (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income rose 9% YoY and 3% QoQ to Rs112.7bn, in line with Nomura's Rs112.8bn estimate. NII (+9% YoY, Rs79.3bn) was 2% below Nomura's estimate on a NIM of 4.22%, but fees (+11% YoY per Jeff; Rs34.0bn per Nomura) were 7% ahead. (Jeff, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 10% YoY and 5% QoQ to Rs61.3bn, about 3% above Nomura's estimate (core PPOP +4%) and c.3% above CLSA's. Fee income came in stronger and opex was lower, flat QoQ and up 8% YoY. (Jeff, Nomura, CLSA)

outlook.note: Brokers trimmed or raised estimates only modestly. Jeff raises FY27 EPS 2% on better fees and opex, and Nomura raises FY27-28F EPS 2-3% on lower opex. CLSA leaves FY27 PAT largely unchanged but trims FY28/29 by 2-3% for ECL. Management flagged a 12-15bp credit-cost impact from the transition to ECL, with a one-time net-worth hit of under 2%. Loan growth held at 15% YoY and asset quality is improving, while deposit growth (12%) lags. CEO succession after Mr. Vaswani's tenure ends in Dec-26 is the key near-term monitorable. (Jeff, Nomura, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 28% YoY and 8% QoQ to Rs24.5bn. Financial services revenue rose 45% YoY to Rs8.1bn, payments income rose 26%, and GMV grew 31% to Rs7.1tn. Marketing revenue was flat and net payment margin slipped to 8.5bps (Bern, CLSA). The reports give no total-revenue consensus or estimate, so revenue is not rated.
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.03bn was up 184% YoY and 54% QoQ, with margin of about 8% against 6% in 4Q26. Indirect expenses rose only 6% YoY, which drove the operating leverage. CLSA put it marginally ahead of its Rs1.9bn estimate (Bern, CLSA).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs22.6bn was about 2.2% above Bloomberg consensus of Rs22.2bn (JPMorgan prints +2%). It grew 19% YoY and 3% QoQ, led by Payment Services, Financial Services and Marketing Services. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA of Rs1.32bn was about 2.1% below consensus of Rs1.35bn (JPMorgan prints -2%), with the margin at 5.8% against 6.1% expected. It is up 67% YoY on adj. EBITDA of Rs790mn but down 16% QoQ from Rs1.57bn. The year-ago figure used is adjusted EBITDA because the reported year-ago EBITDA line shows -Rs900mn. Net profit of Rs1.83bn beat consensus by 16%. (JP)

outlook.note: Management reiterated its 15-20% EBITDA margin target in 2-3 years. CLSA trimmed FY27-29 EBITDA by 2-3% on higher opex and keeps Underperform with a Rs1,050 target. Bernstein's 10 Aug note adds UPI MDR to its base case (about 35bps, 3-4bps of incremental net payments margin), lifting FY30E EPS about 30% and its target to Rs2,200. Its FY27E EPS was cut to 23.19 from 24.32 (Bern, CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs 151.3bn was 0.9% above JPMe. NII (Rs 108.0bn, +2.1% y/y, +4.0% q/q) was in line and non-interest income was 2.8% above JPMe. Total income fell 4.5% y/y from a high year-ago base that included Rs 52.7bn of non-interest income, now Rs 43.3bn (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs 75.2bn (+6.2% y/y, flat q/q) came in 7.2% below JPMe because opex was 10.3% above JPMe (Rs 76.1bn, +8.1% q/q). Opex was still down 13.1% y/y. Fee income was weaker than expected, and the cost-to-income ratio was 50.3% against JPMe's 46.0% (JP).

2Q27.revNote: Total op. income grew 3% YoY and was flat QoQ. NII rose 11% YoY and 7% QoQ and came in about 3% above JPMorgan's estimate, helped by NIM up 8bp QoQ to 2.58%. That was largely offset by other income down 17% YoY, with treasury profit down 57% (Jeff, JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 4% YoY and was flat QoQ at Rs75.3bn. JPMorgan puts it about 6% above its estimate, with opex below its forecast, though CLSA notes opex was largely stable YoY at Rs77bn. PAT of Rs55.3bn (+13% YoY) beat JPMorgan's estimate by 21% and CLSA's by 20%, on lower provisions and a provision write-back (Jeff, JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management guided to a further 7-9bp NIM expansion in 3Q, helped by the 25bp repo hike (56% of the loan book is repo-linked), and sees NIM at or above its 2.6-2.7% guidance. Credit costs are guided to 25-30bp even after the ECL transition. JPMorgan raised FY27/28/29E EPS by 14.5%/7.7%/4.6% and Jefferies raised FY27E earnings by 17%. Morgan Stanley also raised F27/F28 estimates, though it stays UW on low sustainable ROA (JP, Jeff, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Total income was 8% below MS's estimate (Rs 28,373mn). NII missed by 8% as NIM fell 28bp QoQ to 4.13% (yield on advances down 43bp QoQ) and average IEA was 4% below estimate. Core fees were 4% below estimate and other income 52% below. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating profit (PPOP) beat MS's estimate by 4%, and core PPoP beat by 10%. Operating expenses were 13% below estimate and fell 8% YoY. The cost-to-income ratio was 64.7% vs 68.9% estimated. PAT beat by 9%. CLSA also called PPOP a 2% beat. (MS, CLSA)

2Q27.revNote: Total income (NII + non-interest income) rose 29% YoY to Rs32.1bn, 1% below MS's estimate. NII grew 37% YoY and beat MS by 2% (~7% above consensus) on the full benefit of the equity raise, with NIM up ~48bp QoQ to 4.61%. Core fees (+12% YoY) missed MS by 9%. (MS, GS)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 92% YoY and 51% QoQ to Rs13.96bn, in line with MS and ~17% above consensus. Opex grew only 3% YoY and beat MS by 2%. Higher provisions (credit costs ~237bp) pulled PAT down to 12% below MS's estimate, though PAT was ~11% above consensus. (MS, GS)

outlook.note: Both brokers raised earnings: MS lifted EPS by 8%/4%/4% for F27/F28/F29 and its PT to Rs370. GS raised F28/F29 earnings by 11%/12% on strong FCNR-B deposit flows and its PT to Rs310. Management guides underlying loan growth of ~22-25% and a material moderation in credit costs in H2-F27, led by credit cards. Offsets are an expected opex pickup (GS: +19% YoY in F28/F29), a 50-60% drop in insurance distribution income if the draft guidelines are implemented, and NIM normalisation in F3Q27 (GS). Both brokers see valuations as expensive. (MS, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Total income (NII + non-interest income) of Rs629bn rose 8% YoY and was 5% above MS's estimate. NII rose 15% YoY and was 5% above, helped by a 5bp QoQ NIM expansion to 2.86%. Fee income was 11% above MS's estimate (MS). JPM puts NII +3% vs JPM, with average interest-earning assets up 16% YoY (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs335bn rose 10% YoY and 21% QoQ, and was 12% above MS's estimate. The beat came from higher NII and fees, with operating expenses 2% below the estimate. Core PPoP was 18% above MS's estimate. JPM has PPOP 13% above its own estimate, with the cost/income ratio at 46.7% vs JPM's 50.1% (MS, JP).

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 loan-growth guidance to 14-15% YoY (from 12-14%). Gross advances grew 18.6% YoY, the fastest in 13 quarters, and the bank is building out a collection ecosystem. JPM expects domestic NIM of about 3% for FY27 and raised FY27E EPS 4.4% and FY28E EPS 2.1%, lifting its Sep-27 PT to Rs1,280 (OW). MS saw a modest upside vs consensus and no change to its thesis (JP, MS).

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs15.4 bn (+31% yoy, +7% qoq) was ~1.5% above Kotak's estimate of Rs15.2 bn. NII grew 35% yoy on 32% loan growth, and non-interest income rose 15%, led by fees (Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs5.9 bn (+50% yoy) was ~10% above Kotak's estimate of Rs5.4 bn. Opex came in 3% below estimate despite growing 21% yoy. Provisions fell ~56% yoy, so PAT of Rs3.65 bn beat the estimate by 22% (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 guidance: RoA >2%, NIM of 8.3% for 2HFY27, cost-assets ratio of 6.2%, credit cost of 0.8% and microfinance growth of 12-14%. Asset quality is stable and the monsoon-related stress is seen as manageable. Kotak revised estimates to include the ~Rs4 bn preferential allotment, kept BUY with Fair Value of Rs85, and noted that the valuation multiple is nearing the last cycle's peak (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income of Rs146.4 bn was 4.4% above Kotak's estimate and up 7.7% yoy. NII grew 10% yoy (5.3% above estimate) on 13% yoy advances growth, while non-interest income grew 3% yoy as treasury income fell ~45% yoy and TWO recoveries fell 13% yoy, partly offset by core fees up ~30% yoy (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs80.0 bn was 19.1% above Kotak's estimate and up 15.8% yoy. Operating expenses were flat yoy and 9.1% below estimate, which took the cost-income ratio down ~390 bps yoy to 45.3%. NIM (calc.) improved ~10 bps qoq (Kotak).

outlook.note: Kotak sees NIM bottoming out, with a ~10 bps qoq improvement on lower cost of funds and higher CD ratio, and management is optimistic about further gains. Management guides to Rs45-50 bn of TWO recoveries in FY2027 (higher yoy) and expects to mobilise ~US$2 bn of FCNR deposits. Asset quality is stable, with GNPL down 20 bps qoq and credit cost at 40 bps. Kotak retains BUY and raises Fair Value to Rs215 from Rs210. Its FY27E EPS is Rs25.2 and its FY28E EPS is Rs26.4 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income of Rs5.41 bn was 4% above Kotak's Rs5.20 bn estimate, flat yoy and up 10% qoq. NII grew 5% yoy (12% qoq) on a loan-mix shift away from microfinance, and other income came in 15% above estimate (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs636 mn was 55% above Kotak's Rs409 mn estimate and up 416% qoq, though down 31% yoy. Operating expenses were in line (+7% yoy) and NIM (calc.) rose 60 bps qoq to 6.4% (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management does not intend to raise equity in FY2027, and CAR is 17.4%. Kotak sees the provisioning phase as behind the bank: credit cost fell to 2.4%, slippages are down to 4.1% and microfinance PAR 1-90 has normalised. It expects RoE to improve on lower provisions and better PPOP, and keeps BUY with the fair value cut to Rs20 from Rs22. The cut reflects uncertainty over the timing and size of an equity raise (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs 45.8bn (+11% y/y, +5% q/q) was 5% above JPM's estimate: NII (Rs 27.9bn, +17% y/y) was in line, and the beat came from non-interest income, which was 15% above JPM on much higher P&L gains from the Security Receipts portfolio. No consensus figure is printed, so the comparison is against JPM's own estimate. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs 17.04bn (+25% y/y, +5% q/q) was 13% above JPM's estimate, helped by higher non-interest income and well-controlled opex (+4% y/y, cost/income 62.8%). Nomura separately notes core PPOP of INR14.1bn (+62% y/y) was 5% above its estimate, led by NII and fee income. No consensus figure is printed. (JP, Nomura)

2Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs47.0bn (+19% YoY, +3% QoQ) was in line with MS's estimate. NII (+1% QoQ) was 2% below, offset by non-interest income 1% above on stronger treasury and other income. NIM fell 10bp QoQ to 2.6%. (MS, Nomura)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported operating profit (PPOP) of Rs16.8bn (+29% YoY) was 2% below MS's estimate, and core PPOP of Rs15.2bn missed by 6% on ~1% higher costs and ~2% lower core fees. GS and Nomura also call a 2% and 5% core PPOP miss. PBT was in line (Rs13.6bn) on lower provisions and higher other income. (MS, GS, Nomura)

outlook.note: Focus has shifted to the 15 Oct Supreme Court ruling that the Rs84bn AT1 write-down was illegal. The bank estimates reinstating the AT1 principal at ~Rs63bn proforma. That means no CRAR impact, net worth down ~11.8% and borrowings up 10.8%. GS puts the CET-1 hit at ~250bp, and coupon liability is still unclear. NIM fell 10bp QoQ to 2.6%, and the bank targets RIDF balances below 5% by end-F27. MS stays Underweight (PT Rs17) with its thesis and the direction of 12-month consensus EPS both unchanged, and GS stays Sell (PT Rs22). (MS, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone net sales rose 44% YoY to Rs20.1bn, the highest YoY growth in 19 quarters. Electricals (C&W) grew +47% on multiple price hikes (copper pass-on, ~24-25% cumulative over 14 changes), and Communication cables grew +62% on higher OFC volumes and realisations; copper rods collapsed on LPG/PNG shortages (Jeff). The report gives no revenue variance figure vs its own estimate.
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 90% YoY to Rs2.48bn, with margin up ~290bps YoY to 12.3% and a strong beat to JEFe. The main swing was Communication, where EBIT margin rose to 29.8% from 1.2% on OFC pricing and volumes, while Electricals EBIT margin was 10.3% (+60bps YoY) (Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Standalone net sales rose 22% YoY and 22% QoQ to Rs19.5bn, led by Electrical Cables (+22% YoY, with Auto, Flexible and Power cables all growing), Communication cables (+32% YoY on optic fibre) and Copper Rods (+20%); price hikes passed on copper costs (~20% in FY26) also lifted sales (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 22% YoY to Rs2,033mn and Jefferies called it a beat, but margin was flat YoY at 10.4% (-1bp). Gross margin fell 210bps YoY to 17.5% on copper volatility (+37% YoY in Q4) and supply-chain disruption, offset by lower other expenses (Jeff).
4Q26.vsBasis: report wording (Jefferies: 'Mar26-Q EBITDA was a beat'); no consensus figure printed

outlook.note: Jefferies raised FY27-28e EPS by 3-7% and the target PE to 23x, taking the PT to Rs1,410 (from Rs1,200) with a Buy rating. It sees healthy C&W growth (electricals segment sales CAGR +17% over FY26-29e) and an OFC opportunity from AI-led fibre demand, with the backward-integration margin benefit accruing from Q3FY27e. Copper rods and FMEG remain weak, though FMEG keeps a positive EBIT (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 20% YoY, in line with CLSA's estimate and consensus, but growth was largely price-led. Lloyd grew 16% on a low base and C&W grew 27% on pricing, with volume growth in single digits (below peers). Lighting and switchgear were flat to down (4%/-3%), as switchgear exports were hit by the Middle East conflict. (CLSA; JP; MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.8bn fell 9% YoY and missed both CLSA's estimate and consensus. Margin dropped 231bps YoY to 7.3% (-351bps QoQ), mainly because A&P spend roughly doubled (ad spend 4.4% of sales vs 2.6%) and COGS inflation added to the pressure. (CLSA; JP; MS)

outlook.note: Management expects demand to improve and margins to recover as A&P normalises, and kept A&P guidance at 2.7-2.8% of sales. Brokers still cut estimates: CLSA cut FY27-29 EPS by 9-10% and its target price from Rs1,535 to Rs1,390, while JP cut FY27/28 EPS by 5.9%/4.4% and its target price from Rs1,300 to Rs1,200. MS also sees a modest downward revision to consensus EPS. (CLSA; JP; MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 23% YoY to Rs31.9bn, about 1% below consensus (JP) and 0.6% below Kotak's estimate. Cables & wires grew 25% YoY, but institutional cables grew only 4.4% and exports fell 7.3% on US tariffs and Middle East order delays. Volumes were largely flat, so growth was mostly price-led, and it lagged peers (38%/57% for Polycab/RR Kabel). (Kotak, CLSA, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 53% YoY to Rs4.0bn, about 19% above consensus (JP) and about 11% above Kotak's estimate. EBITDA margin expanded 250bps YoY to 12.4% on better mix (higher EHV and retail/dealer share) and operating leverage. JP and Kotak flag that part of the beat likely reflects commodity tailwinds and one-off inventory gains. (Kotak, CLSA, JP)

outlook.note: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 25%+ (earlier 20-25%) and EBITDA margin of 11-12% (earlier 10.5-11%), though it dropped the volume guidance (earlier 17-18%). It also targets 20%+ growth over the next 2-3 years, with Sanand contributing Rs15-20bn in FY27 and export guidance raised to 16-18% of sales. Brokers raised FY27-29E EPS by 1-5% (Kotak) and 8-10% (CLSA) on higher margins, while trimming revenue estimates slightly (CLSA -1.9%). JP sees FY27 EPS upgrades but little change to FY28. Kotak cautions the margin print is partly commodity-aided and hard to extrapolate. (Kotak, CLSA, JP)

companies.name: Polycab India
companies.note: We expect Polycab to continue to post industry-leading growth and margins. While high comps in 3Q arelikely to weigh on volume growth, recent weakness in its stock price factorsin this and competition risk.

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue rose 39% YoY and beat consensus by about 6%. Wires & cables grew 38% on copper-led pricing (about +32%) and low-to-mid single-digit volume growth. FMEG revenue jumped 68% as solar grew 2x. Exports fell 13% YoY. (JP, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 33% YoY to Rs11.4bn, about 9% above consensus. The beat came mainly from FMEG, where EBIT margin was 8% against 2.1% a year earlier on operating leverage and premiumisation. C&W EBIT margin of 13.3% was in line. EBITDA margin was 13.8% against 14.4% a year ago. (JP, MS)

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs99.0bn (+53% YoY) was 14% above consensus. Cables & wires grew 47% (domestic +50%, exports +17%), driven mainly by copper/aluminium pass-through pricing (+35-40% YoY) plus mid-to-high single-digit volume growth. FMEG revenue rose 124% YoY (JP, CLSA).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs14.2bn (+39% YoY) was 21% above consensus. The EBITDA margin was 14.4%, down 139bps YoY on a high base but up 53bps QoQ. C&W EBIT margin was 14.2% (+87bps QoQ) on a better channel and wire mix, and FMEG EBIT margin hit a record 10.1% on operating leverage (JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: JP raised FY27E EPS 5% on the 2Q beat, cut FY28E EPS 3% (aluminium MTM, more aluminium-cable mix) and set the PT at Rs9,700 (from Rs10,000). It assumes a 13.0% C&W EBIT margin in 2H (13.8% in 1H). Management reaffirmed the target of ~10% of revenue from exports by 2030 and cited a strong export order backlog. CLSA raised FY27-29 PAT 1-2% but builds in flat C&W revenue in 3Q on high comps and a 180bp margin decline over FY26-30 for competition. Jefferies made minor tweaks, keeping a ~22% FY26-29e EPS CAGR. Pricing tailwinds should last a couple more quarters, but UTCEM's C&W capex plans and channel incentives remain the key watch items (JP, CLSA, Jeff).

companies.name: RR Kabel
companies.note: Management guided for 18% W&C volume growth and a 9.5% W&C EBIT margin in FY2027E.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs31.7 bn grew 54% yoy and was ~12% above Kotak's estimate. Wires & Cables volume/value grew 17%/57% on industry tailwinds, share gains and strong exports, and FMEG grew 28% on premiumization, new products and wider channel reach (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.8 bn nearly doubled yoy and was ~17% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded 205 bps yoy to 8.9% against Kotak's 8.5%, helped by operating leverage and mix. W&C EBIT margin rose 230 bps to 9.9% and FMEG broke even at EBIT (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guided for 18% W&C volume growth and a 9.5% W&C EBIT margin in FY2027E (9.5%/10.5% in FY27E/28E). It also guided for 25%+ pricing growth in 2Q if spot LME prices sustain, and ~20% FMEG growth at EBIT breakeven. Kotak raised FY27-29E revenue by ~3% and EBITDA margin by 10-20 bps, lifting EPS 3-8%, and raised FV to Rs1,950 (from Rs1,850). It keeps SELL on valuation and expects rising competitive intensity. Management flagged some channel de-stocking in June and a likely volume hit late in the quarter from the metal price correction (Kotak).

companies.name: V-Guard Industries
companies.note: VGRD guidance of +15% (led by 10-12% volume growth

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew +24% YoY (+3% QoQ) to Rs 18.1 bn on ~+14% volume growth and ~+10% price hikes. Strong summer in South India (51% of sales) lifted Electronics (+23%) and Electricals (+28%), with Consumer Durables up 19% (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose +55% YoY to Rs 1.91 bn, with OPM up +210bps YoY to 10.5%, a beat versus Jefferies' estimate. Gross margin held at ~36.9% (flat YoY) on calibrated price hikes passing through 85-90% of inflation, and ad-spend fell to 2.2% of sales from 3.0% (Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies raised FY27-29e EPS by 2-3% after the Q1 beat and sees an ~18% PAT CAGR over FY26-28e. It estimates FY27 sales growth of +12%, below management's +15% guidance, and expects the remaining 10-15% of price hikes to pass through this quarter. Near-term demand is expected to hold on, but the effect of price hikes is yet to be seen. Margins could recover further as price transfer catches up with raw-material inflation (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 55% YoY to INR 3.96bn but was 3% below JMFe's INR 4.06bn. Aerospace revenue of INR 3.22bn (+40% YoY) was in line, while consumer revenue of INR 734mn (+190% YoY) missed JMFe by 11% (JM).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR 148mn (-46% YoY, 3.5x QoQ) was 58% below JMFe's INR 354mn, mainly on gross margin of 57% against JMFe's 61%. Aerospace EBITDA of INR 731mn (+35% YoY) missed by 25%, partly on other income of INR 67mn (-47% YoY). Consumer EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 361mn from INR 473mn in 4Q26 (JM).

outlook.note: Management maintained its FY27 guidance: revenue growth of 45-50% and 2x EBITDA growth. Aerospace is guided to 25-30% growth, with EBITDA margin of 20%+. Consumer is guided to 125-150% growth, with EBITDA breakeven by 4QFY27 at 40-50% utilisation. Capex guidance of INR 6.6bn is maintained, with aerospace capex possibly higher. JM left its FY27/28 EBITDA estimates unchanged, and Ashika kept its FY27 guidance view but expects depreciation of ~INR 400-450mn per quarter and raised its FY27 tax rate assumption to 34%. OCF was an outflow of INR 414mn on working-capital build (JM, Ashika).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 12.4% y-y to INR11.7bn, in line with Bloomberg consensus (+0.5%) and Nomura's estimate (+0.6%). Sales volume rose 8% y-y to 64,644 tons and realizations rose 5% y-y to INR178/kg. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was flat y-y at INR3.1bn, 6.5% below consensus and 7% below Nomura's estimate. The margin fell 310bp y-y to 26.4% because of a less-favourable product mix (gross margin down 106bp) and higher freight and mill-trial costs (other expenses up 231bp as a share of sales). (Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 9% y-y and 19% q-q to INR12.7bn, 12% above Bloomberg consensus. Volumes rose 2% y-y to 70,138 tons, and realisations rose 7% y-y to INR178/kg on a favourable product mix and rupee depreciation. (Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR3.6bn was 21% above consensus. Margin expanded 260bp y-y to 28.6%, 220bp above consensus, helped by gross margin up 82bp y-y to 59.7% and lower employee/other expenses as a share of sales. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management says AIAE will keep focusing on value-added offerings, but a material update is likely only after 3-4 quarters. It sees sustainable operating margins of around 20-22% on a less-favourable product mix, even as absolute profitability should grow. Geopolitical and shipping-cost headwinds make the business environment uncertain. Order book was INR9.7bn, up 31% y-y. Nomura kept Reduce with a TP of INR3,568. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 13.3% YoY to Rs33.8 bn but was ~5.7% below Kotak's estimate. Segment-2 (unitary products) grew ~12.7% and missed by ~13.3% on a delayed summer and an abrupt end after the first week of June. Segment-1 (EMP + CAC) grew 15.1% and beat by ~4.6% (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 12.5% YoY to Rs1.75 bn, ~28.4% below Kotak's estimate, with the margin at 5.2% (down 153 bps YoY). Segment-2 EBIT margin fell to 2.9% (down ~290-300 bps YoY) on input-cost inflation, a rupee fall, and ad, trade-scheme and consumer-finance spend. Only ~5% price hikes against ~13% cost inflation. Jefferies also says EBITDA missed its estimate (Kotak, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management cut FY27 margin guidance: Segment-1 (MEP + CAC) to 6.5-7% (from 7-7.5%) and Segment-2 (RAC + CR) to over 6.5% (from 8-8.5%). It expects July-August to stay soft, limited improvement in 2Q and a better 3Q on festive demand. Data-centre MEP growth guidance was raised to 12% (from 8-10%). Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by ~5-18% and moved fair value to Rs1,500 (from Rs1,585). Jefferies cut FY28-29E EPS by 5-6% and FY27E by more (Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs14.3 bn (+17% yoy, +2% qoq) was 9% above Kotak's estimate (2% beat adjusted for Awuko/Foskor), with all segments growing 16-20% yoy, led by standalone abrasives and electrominerals. Standalone and consolidated EMD sales grew 33% and 17% yoy respectively, and exports now make up 35% of the standalone mix. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.35 bn (+11% yoy) missed Kotak's estimate by 27% (12% miss adjusted for Awuko/Foskor), and the margin fell to 9.5% from the 14.2% estimated. Raw material costs for oil-linked inputs such as resin rose almost 20% and were not passed on, and Chinese competition and FX gains also weighed. Management put the total cost impact at about Rs1.6 bn in the quarter. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management raised its normalised consolidated revenue growth guidance to about 15% from 11-12% (excluding Foskor and Awuko). It raised ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% from the mid-teens, and kept its margin guidance, with abrasives expected to recover over 9M as Chinese import competition eases. Kotak raised FY28-29 revenue estimates by 2% and its fair value to Rs1,080 from Rs1,020, but keeps SELL on valuation of about 40x one-year forward EPS. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone net sales of INR34.3bn rose 18% y-y and 14% q-q, 7% above Nomura and Bloomberg consensus. Domestic sales grew 22% y-y on robust demand across end markets, while exports were flat y-y (Nomura, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of INR6.2bn fell 1% y-y and missed consensus by 7%. Gross margin fell 351bp y-y to 33.5% as pig iron and copper prices rose 17% and 42% y-y, and EBITDA margin of 18% was 276bp below consensus (Nomura, JP, Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Total operating income of Rs30.1bn grew 22% y/y and was 10% ahead of JPMorgan's estimate. Domestic sales grew 30% y/y, led by power generation (+48%) and distribution (+21%), with a ~Rs2.5bn hyperscaler data-centre delivery. Exports fell 6% y/y. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs6.4bn grew 22% y/y and was 11% above JPMorgan's estimate. The margin was 21.3%, 33bps above JPMorgan's estimate and flat y/y. Gross margin compressed ~150bps y/y but lower other expenses offset it. (JP)

outlook.note: Management expects steady business momentum across key markets. It also flags inflationary pressure and supply-chain constraints, and price hikes have been in place since July 2026 to pass on cost escalation. Demand from data centres, real estate and manufacturing stays healthy, but the margin recovery depends on pricing. Jefferies cut FY27-29E EPS by 6-7% and its target price to INR6,700 from INR7,100, JPMorgan expects downward margin and EPS revisions, and the MD has resigned (Nomura, Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 38% YoY and 12% QoQ to INR18.4bn, 6% above Bloomberg consensus and 7% above Nomura's estimate. JPM notes the press release cited multiple completions and deliveries in the quarter, which likely drove the strong print (Nomura, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR4.6bn (+19% YoY) was 3% above consensus. Gross margin fell 709bp YoY to 41.3% on lower export share (30% vs 33%) and a higher mix of lower-margin HV business, but leaner employee and other costs offset part of it. The 25.1% EBITDA margin was 76bp below consensus and in line with management's FY27 guidance of about 25% (Nomura, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR16.4bn grew 42% y-y but came in 5% below Bloomberg consensus (INR17.2bn) and 3% below Nomura's estimate, and fell 4% q-q. (Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR4.45bn (+76% y-y) beat consensus and Nomura by 7%. Gross margin expanded 468bp y-y to 47.0% and EBITDA margin rose 530bp y-y to 27.2%, 292bp above consensus. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Guidance is unchanged: management still targets INR70-80bn of base domestic order inflow and a mid-20s EBITDA margin in FY27E, while expecting commodity cost pressure to persist for a few quarters. Order inflow was weak at INR11.4bn (-30% YoY, 37% below Nomura's estimate) because of tepid TBCB tendering and a US data centre order slipping to 2Q/3Q. Nomura keeps its estimates and its INR5,675 TP, and JPM flags the order and margin disappointment (Nomura, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Sales rose 46% YoY on a low base, but were 14.7% below JEFe (Rs6,707mn vs Rs7,867mn). Wagon sales rose 38% YoY, partly offset by a 9% YoY rise in realisations, and Wheelset sales fell 73% YoY (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs649mn was 32% below JEFe (Rs954mn) and grew only 8.5% YoY. Margin fell to 9.7% from 13.0% a year earlier, as gross margins fell 700bps YoY on a high base that included specialised wagons. Slower execution on new wagon designs and subsidiary losses (Rs8mn implied EBITDA loss vs Rs91mn profit a year ago) added to the miss (Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs7.8bn fell 25% YoY and came in 14% below JEFe, as wagon sales declined 43% YoY on supply-chain issues; wheelset sales grew 19% YoY and CV load bodies 37% (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs833mn was 32% below JEFe and down 45% YoY, with margin at 10.7% vs 14.6% a year ago; gross margin at 26% surprised positively, but negative operating leverage hit EBITDA (Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies cut FY27-29E EPS by 6-20% and its PT to Rs185 from Rs210, and rates the stock Underperform. The Odisha wheel plant is expected to be operational only by end-FY28E (axles commercial production by 4QFY27, wheels by FY28 end), and component JVs are still nascent. Visibility on the new 1 lakh wagon tender is low, and wagons are 68% of FY28E EBITDA. The Rs30bn order book (~1.4x FY26 sales, 7,000 wagons) and a Rs4bn BESS order for JEM are partial offsets (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Merged standalone sales of Rs54.8 bn (+8.8% yoy) came in 3.6% above Kotak's Rs52.9 bn estimate, despite state-election labour shortages, slow water receivables and Middle East supply-chain constraints. Consolidated revenue was Rs64.1 bn (+9% yoy like-for-like). Figures are standalone, since the table gives no consolidated year-ago figure. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs4.9 bn (+13.9% yoy) was 8.5% above Kotak's estimate, with margin at 8.9% against 8.5% a year ago and 8.5% estimated. Operating leverage and favourable mix drove it; PBT rose 32% yoy on higher other income and lower interest. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs5.6 bn (+7% yoy). (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 15%+ revenue growth (about Rs270-280 bn), Rs300 bn order inflows and 75 bps+ PBT margin expansion, with 1Q delivery well ahead on margin and a possible upward revision to inflows to be revisited at end-2QFY27. Order book is a record Rs666 bn, with about Rs150 bn of YTD inflows plus L1 positions. Kotak raised FY27-29 EPS by 4-6% and Fair Value to Rs1,710 from Rs1,560. Watch points are Middle East disruption, which should make execution 2H-weighted, and the timing of large oil & gas wins. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR50.2bn was flat y-y and 2% below Bloomberg consensus (1% below Nomura). Execution was held back by Middle East disruptions, which deferred ~Rs3bn of revenue, and by labour shortages and calibrated execution of water projects. By segment, SAE was +25%, Cables +57%, Renewables -59%, Railways -45% and Civil -6% y-y (Nomura, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR2.9bn fell 17% y-y and missed consensus by 13% (Nomura by 7%). The margin of 5.8% was down 118bp y-y and 76bp below consensus, hit by elevated freight and local operating costs and by employee and other expenses growing faster than sales. Transportation and civil remained the key drags (Nomura, Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: 4Q revenue of INR63.9bn fell 7% y-y and came in 13% below consensus (9% below Nomura). T&D ex-SAE was up 1% y-y, while railways (-55%), renewables (-81%) and civil (-15%) fell; West Asia disruptions and labour/payment/ROW headwinds weighed. (Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR4.5bn fell 17% y-y and was 16% below consensus (9% below Nomura). Margin of 7.0% was down 83bp y-y and 28bp below consensus, with gross margin down 14bp y-y and employee cost up 105bp as a share of sales. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 13.4% YoY to Rs20.0bn but was 2.8% below Jefferies' estimate of Rs20.6bn. B2B sales rose 17% YoY, with after-market distribution up 23%, while B2C grew 3% and exports fell 16% (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 8.1% YoY to Rs3.0bn and missed Jefferies' estimate by 21.4%. Margin was 15.0% against 18.5% a year earlier and 18.6% expected, as higher commodity prices, logistics costs and staff costs (up 39% YoY) outweighed price hikes (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management says price hikes are being taken, which points to sequential margin improvement, and the data-centre genset delivery will be completed in FY27. Jefferies cut FY27E-30E EPS by 1-7% and its target price to Rs2,655 from Rs2,815, but still expects gradual margin recovery and keeps a Buy rating (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 15% YoY to Rs72.3bn, about 2% above Morgan Stanley's estimate. Growth was broad-based, with Home Appliances and Air Solutions up 14% and Home Entertainment up 22%. Drivers were premium demand, a strong summer for ACs and refrigerators, TV and washer strength, and rising exports (Jeff, MS, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 26% YoY to Rs9.0bn, 6% above both Morgan Stanley's and CLSA's estimates. Margin was 12.5% (+106bps YoY), helped by premium mix, operating leverage, calibrated price hikes and localisation. Home Entertainment EBIT margin reached about 19% (Jeff, MS, CLSA).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs80.5bn (+8% YoY) was about 0.8% below consensus, so in line. Broad-based demand and premiumisation after the new BEE rating transition on 1 Jan 2026 supported it. Home Appliances & Air Solutions grew 6% to Rs65.2bn and Home Entertainment grew 20% to Rs15.4bn on large-screen TV demand during the Cricket World Cup (Jeff, Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs9.5bn (-10% YoY) was about 10.7% below consensus, with margin down 240bps YoY to 11.7% against Kotak's 13% estimate. The causes were commodity price inflation, INR depreciation (about 100bps) and strategic channel investments (about 110bps). Higher e-waste expenses added about 20bps. Jefferies said the margin dip left profit below consensus but in line with its own estimate (Jeff, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 guidance of mid-teen revenue growth and an early double-digit EBITDA margin. It sees strong 2Q momentum in washing machines and exports, plus a festive-season push in premium and large-screen TVs. CLSA raised FY27-29 EPS by 2-5% and its TP to Rs1,865. Jefferies sees a 25% FY26-28e EPS CAGR and keeps its Rs1,810 TP. MS flags a modest upward revision to consensus EPS (CLSA, Jeff, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Total income rose 12% y/y to Rs7.16bn, 1.6% above Kotak's estimate (Rs7.05bn) and about 3% above JPM's. Bio-energy and Hi-Purity revenues grew 24% and 16% y/y, while Engineering fell 14% y/y. (Kotak, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs300mn fell 16% y/y, and margin was 4.2% (down 137bps y/y, up 144bps q/q). This beat Kotak's low estimate (Rs246mn) by 22%. JPM, however, saw the margin 180bps below its 6.0% estimate, citing higher material costs, a lower export share and a skew to lower-margin Africa orders. (Kotak, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Total income of Rs8.4bn was 1% below Kotak's estimate and down 1.8% yoy. Bioenergy revenue grew 5% yoy, offset by a 5.5% fall in Engineering and a 31% fall in Hi Purity (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs233mn was 51% below Kotak's estimate and down 69% yoy. The margin fell to 2.8% (down 600bps yoy) on higher site expenses (labour supply, slow execution) and cost overruns. JP also called the margin weaker than expected, citing project-site cost escalation and under-absorbed fixed costs at GenX (Kotak, JP).

outlook.note: Order inflows rebounded to Rs10bn (+26% y/y, +52% q/q), led by the ~US$50mn GenX data-centre agreement, and the backlog rose to Rs45.9bn. Policy support is firming (GOBARdhan CBG scheme, US E15), but 1G ethanol ordering stays weak and margins have yet to recover. JPM cut FY27E/FY28E EPS by 5.6%/6.0% (PT Rs364 from Rs387, Neutral). Kotak trimmed FY28/29 EPS by 2-4% (FV Rs360, Reduce). (JP, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew only 5% YoY (+10% QoQ) to Rs 6.5bn despite a sizable order backlog. GS ties the weak conversion to capex-heavy customers, especially EPCs, delaying dispatches amid geopolitical disruptions, and says the delay may be partly timing-related (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 51% YoY to Rs 341mn and the margin dropped 593bps YoY to 5.2%. Gross margin slipped 271bps YoY to 35.4%, and employee cost (+15%) and other expenses (+20%) grew far faster than revenue, so operating deleverage did the rest (GS).

outlook.note: GS calls it a weak start with operating deleverage. Order inflow was flat at +1% YoY, but the order book grew 33% YoY to Rs 21.7bn, which supports later revenue conversion. GS says some of the weakness may be timing related and flags commentary on tepid inflow and execution as the key monitorable. It keeps a Buy rating and a Rs 1,475 DCF-based target price (GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 14.8% yoy to Rs47.1bn, in line with Kotak's estimate (+0.2%) and JPM's. Digital Industries grew 25%, while Smart Infra (+11%) and Mobility (+13%) moderated despite strong order intake. (Kotak, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.9bn fell 24% yoy and missed Kotak's estimate by 18%, with margin at 8.3% (down 189bps yoy). Commodity inflation and INR depreciation squeezed margins, and other expenses rose ~250-350bps yoy/qoq, possibly including transient hedging losses. JPM puts adjusted EBITDA margin at 9.1% vs its 12.3% estimate. (Kotak, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR46.2bn (+15% y/y) was 2% above consensus and 5% above Nomura's estimate. Growth was broad-based: Smart Infra, Mobility and Digital Industries grew 15%, 14% and 15% y/y. JPM also called it in line with its estimates (Nomura, JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA of INR4.5bn (-12% y/y) missed consensus by 15% (Nomura estimate: -11%). Gross margin fell 449bp y/y to 26.2% on higher commodity costs (silver, copper) and EUR/INR forex headwinds, taking EBITDA margin to 9.7% (-287bp y/y). Material costs rose from 69% to 74% of revenue (Nomura, Kotak, JP).

outlook.note: Order inflow was strong at Rs63.3bn (+17% yoy, ~1.3x sales) and broad-based across grid, data centres, commercial real estate and automation. Margin compression from commodity and FX is the key worry, though, and consensus is likely to wait for clarity on price hikes. Kotak cut FY27/28/29 estimates by 5%/1%/0% and retains SELL. JPM stays Underweight and sees the stock sideways. (Kotak, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs8.75bn were 4.3% above JEFe, though down 12.9% YoY on a weak Freight Rail System segment (wagon sales -25% YoY in the quarter) that outweighed passenger segment sales of Rs1.73bn (+92% YoY), with 25 metro coaches dispatched vs 6 a year ago (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs972mn was 7.1% above JEFe (-4.4% YoY), as better execution and segment margins (passenger 19% vs 3.7% a year ago) were partly offset by higher overheads; margin was 11.1% vs JEFe 10.8% (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs46.7bn (+19% YoY) was about 7% below consensus (12% below Nomura's estimate). Unitary cooling grew 32% YoY but fell short of expectations, and projects revenue fell 27% YoY (Nomura, MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.7bn (+49% YoY, from a low base) was in line with consensus. The margin was 5.7% against 5.3% consensus, on a 5.3% UCP EBIT margin. It missed MS's own estimate by 13% because of the projects business (Nomura, CLSA, MS).

outlook.note: Management expects UCP margins to improve gradually to 7%+ as it passes on most of the 10-12% cost increase, with RAC channel inventory at a normal ~4 weeks. Nomura says high competition and a focus on share over profitability will delay margin recovery. It cut revenue estimates ~4% and FY27F/28F UCP margins by 50bp/70bp, leading to ~8% lower EPS, and lowered its TP to Rs1,357. CLSA raised FY27-29 EBITDA by 1-3% but cut FY27/28 PAT by 5%/1% on higher JV losses, and lifted its TP to Rs1,160 (Nomura, CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 59.1% yoy to Rs3.3 bn, 9.7% above Kotak's estimate, driven by the advanced (pharma) intermediates division (+76.5% yoy, 89% of sales) on strong CDMO growth. Specialty chemicals fell 10.7% yoy on the planned exit from commodity chemicals. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 122% yoy to Rs1.13 bn, 20.1% above Kotak's estimate, with margin up 973 bps yoy to 34.3%. Gross margin expanded 466 bps yoy to 57.9% on a higher share of pharma intermediates. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reaffirmed 25% FY2027 revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins, which Kotak considers conservative. Kotak projects 37% growth on CDMO, battery chemicals (commercial supply began, ramp-up from 2QFY27) and catalog generics. Management reaffirmed its Rs10 bn CDMO revenue target by FY2028, and four validated CDMO products start contributing from 2HFY27. Kotak made only modest estimate revisions and cut its rating to REDUCE on valuation, not on fundamentals. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs4.2bn was 11% below consensus and 2% below JPM's estimate. CRDMO fell 25% YoY to Rs3.4bn, which JPM attributes to timing-related shipment push-outs and customer inventory rebalancing, and Specialty Ingredients fell 12% on supply-chain issues. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.5bn was 14% below consensus but 7% ahead of JPM's estimate. Gross margin rose to 65% (+780bps YoY) and EBITDA margin to 36%, on in-house production replacing an imported intermediate and lower other expenses. EBITDA still fell 21% YoY on the revenue decline. (JP, Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue was 1% ahead of consensus and 3% ahead of JPMe, up 26% YoY and 44% QoQ. CRDMO revenue rose 31% YoY (+54% QoQ) while specialty ingredients rose 8% YoY (+9% QoQ). (JP, Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA margin was 43.7% (+330bps YoY, +660bps QoQ), about 370bps above JPMe, helped by gross margin of 64.7% (270bps ahead of JPMe) and lower-than-expected employee and other expenses. Nomura put the margin 209bps above its estimate, with the quarter otherwise largely in line. No consensus EBITDA figure is printed, so the beat is against the broker estimate. (JP, Nomura)
4Q26.vsBasis: revenue: consensus (JPMorgan: 1% ahead); EBITDA: broker estimate (JPMorgan)

3Q26.revNote: Total revenue fell 15% y-y and 23% q-q, 5% below Nomura's estimate. CRDMO revenue declined 19% y-y and 29% q-q on a large base, inventory destocking in established products and lumpy new-product launches, while specialty revenue grew 6% y-y (Nomura).
3Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was down 1% y-y and 27% q-q, 7% below Nomura's estimate. Gross margin rose 693bp q-q to 66.6% as the company brought a China-sourced intermediate in-house, helped by mix and currency, so EBITDA margin expanded 519bp y-y to 37.7%. That largely offset the revenue decline (Nomura).

outlook.note: Management called 1QFY27 the softest quarter and expects growth to pick up from 2Q, with double-digit FY27 revenue growth and margins sustained. About 60% of full-year guidance is covered by the order book, and the pipeline has 100+ early-stage projects and 10 late-phase molecules. JPM kept its estimates unchanged (19%/18% revenue/EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29E) and raised its PT to Rs900 on a roll-forward to Sep'27. Nomura expects FY27 revenue growth of 17%+ against the 19.2% it currently models. (JP, Nomura)

companies.name: Blue Jet Healthcare
companies.note: Competition from Divi's

4Q26.revNote: Revenue fell 31% YoY but rose 22% QoQ and beat consensus by 7% (JPMorgan). Contrast media sales of Rs1.9bn (+91% YoY, +55% QoQ) on higher ABA HCL volumes offset near-zero PI & API sales (-99% YoY on bempedoic acid destocking) (JP, Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 49% YoY but rose 52% QoQ, and beat consensus by 14% (JPMorgan). Margin was 30.4% (-1,070bps YoY, +600bps QoQ), helped by contrast media operating leverage, a gross margin of 56.4% and INR depreciation lifting export realisations. It missed JPMorgan's own estimate by 8% but was 42% above Kotak's (JP, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs2.9bn fell 17% YoY but rose 25% QoQ, in line with consensus/JPMe. Contrast media revenue was up 19% YoY but down 40% QoQ, while pharma intermediates/API fell 43% YoY but rebounded to Rs1.2bn from Rs24mn in 4Q on resumed supply of the bempedoic acid intermediate (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs981mn (-19% YoY, +38% QoQ) was about 2% above consensus (4% above JPMe), i.e. in line. The 33.5% margin was ~70bps/~150bps above consensus/JPMe, as weaker gross margin (53.2%, from 56.4% in 4Q) was offset by lower other expenses (JP).

outlook.note: JPMorgan makes no material estimate changes and keeps UW with a Mar-27 PT of Rs370. Management guided strong order book visibility for at least 3-4 quarters and raised capex estimates. JPMorgan still flags product concentration (two products ~80% of revenue), a flat contrast media run rate and competition for bempedoic acid from Merck's oral PCSK9 (JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue fell 23% YoY and 32% QoQ to Rs4.22bn, 17% below consensus (though 3% above GS's own estimate). Pharma CDMO (~30% of sales) fell 38.7% YoY on customer shipment phasing and deliveries moving from Q1 into Q2, with softer Agrochemicals and Formulations partly offset by Sapala and resilient API (GS). Jefferies also cites sales declines in all 3 divisions (GS, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA collapsed to Rs12mn (0.3% margin vs 20.4% a year ago), 96% below consensus, as low sales deleveraged fixed costs. PAT swung to a loss of Rs241mn (GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management says Q1 was the bottom and expects sequential improvement from Q2FY27 and YoY growth from 2HFY27, driven by scheduled CDMO deliveries, restocking orders and a low base. EBITDA margin is guided flat in FY27 and to improve in FY28. Brokers trimmed numbers: GS cut FY28-29 EPS 5-7% (Buy, TP Rs500), Jefferies cut FY27-29 EBITDA 3-10% (Underperform, TP Rs350) (GS, Jeff).

companies.name: Concord Biotech
companies.note: Mgt. maintained guidance of higher revenue growth vs historical avg (we imply it as 20%+) with EBITDA margin improvement led by lower power cost and operating leverage on injectable facility.

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs3.3 bn fell 24% YoY (+17% QoQ), 14% below Kotak's estimate and 19% below consensus, on deferred orders and logistics disruptions. API revenue fell 27% YoY on geopolitical disruptions, including airspace constraints, and shipments deferred to April 2026. Formulations fell 8% YoY on weak tenders and exports. (Kotak, Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.2 bn fell 38% YoY (+20% QoQ), 8% below Kotak's estimate and 27% below consensus. Margin contracted about 795 bps YoY to 36.4% on the weak sales base, though it improved sequentially. Excluding the Valthera injectables unit and Stellon Biotech, margin was 40.4%. (Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs2.6bn (+26% YoY, -21% QoQ) were ~5% above Kotak's estimate on a very low base. API revenue rose 42% YoY to Rs2.2bn, helped by product launches, deferred revenue from Mar-Q and a forex tailwind, while formulations fell 23% YoY. Jefferies also called it a 4% beat. (Kotak, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs824mn (+34% YoY, -31% QoQ) was ~1% below Kotak's estimate, but Jefferies saw an 8% beat against its own number. Gross margin expanded to 78.9% (+100bps YoY) on a favourable product mix. EBITDA margin was 32% (+190bps YoY, -436bps QoQ) and below Kotak's 34% estimate. (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 sales growth guidance at 18%+ (better than the historical rate) and expects EBITDA margins to improve, moving toward ~40% in FY28E. It has good visibility into 2QFY27 and a steady launch pipeline (2-3 launches a year). Jefferies raised FY27-29E EPS by 1-2% and its PT to INR1,268 (Hold). Kotak tweaked FY27-29E EPS by 0-4% and raised its fair value to Rs1,550 (ADD). (Kotak, Jeff)

companies.name: Divi's Laboratories
companies.note: Management reiterated its double-digit FY27 growth guidance. Strong  Q1 and F2H27 project ramp-ups could drive ~20% revenue growth, in our view.

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs28.3bn (+9.5% YoY) were 1.3% below Kotak's estimate. Custom synthesis grew 15.7% YoY and nutraceuticals 17.1%, while generics were flat at +0.8% YoY on pricing pressure (Kotak). Jefferies and JPMorgan put the revenue shortfall at about 2% vs their estimates (Jeff, JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs9.34bn (+5.4% YoY) was 3.6% below Kotak's estimate. Margin was 33.0%, down 128bps YoY, as gross margin fell 158bps on RM costs and higher freight from the Middle East conflict (Kotak). Jefferies had it 3% below its estimate and JPMorgan 4% below (Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 28% YoY (+9% QoQ) to Rs30.8bn, about 12% above consensus (16% above JPMe). Custom synthesis (~60% of revenue) rose 45% YoY on validation batches shipped in the quarter, nutraceuticals rose 19% and generic APIs 6% (JP, GS, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 72% YoY to Rs12.55bn, about 41% above consensus (47% above JPMe). Margin was 40.7%, up about 1,050bps YoY and 775bps QoQ, helped by a richer custom-synthesis mix (gross margin 68%) and operating leverage. Management cautioned against extrapolating the quarter's margins (JP, GS, Kotak).

outlook.note: Brokers upgraded estimates after the beat: GS raised FY27-29E EPS by 3-10% and its TP to Rs9,070. JP raised FY27E/FY28E adj. EBITDA by 11.7%/10.8% and its PT to Rs9,100, and Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 10-17%. Management reiterated double-digit growth as custom-synthesis programmes move from validation toward commercial supply, which is subject to customer and regulatory approvals and may be lumpy quarter to quarter. GS expects CS to compound at about 28% over FY26-29E. Kotak flags lower Entresto sales in the EU as a risk (GS, JP, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 22.0% YoY to INR 14.77 bn (+0.4% QoQ), the strongest Q1 on record. Growth was driven by complex generics, which are now 50% of finished dosages against 39% a year ago. The note gives no consensus or broker estimate for the quarter, so there is no beat/miss call (DC).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 37.4% YoY to INR 3.39 bn, and margin expanded 256 bps YoY to 22.9% (down 99 bps QoQ). Gross margin was 65.6%, up 74 bps YoY, on the complex-generics mix. Raw material and freight inflation was offset by US opening inventory levels. Peptide CDMO EBITDA was negative at INR 8 Cr. No consensus or estimate is given in the note, so there is no beat/miss call (DC).

outlook.note: Management says Gagillapur (GGP) remediation is essentially complete and it is fully ready for FDA re-inspection, though timing is unknown. Nine US launches are contingent on clearance. The Genome Valley plant adds about 40% to formulation capacity, with utilisation expected to cross 50% by FY27 year-end. FY27 capex guidance is maintained at INR 600 Cr, and the peptide CDMO is targeting PAT-positive performance for FY27, with H2 stronger than H1. DC forecasts a FY26-28 revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR of 13.7%/21.5%/22.4%, with a target price of INR 959 (ACCUMULATE). The note flags risks from US dependence (~74% of revenue), tariffs and the GGP approval timeline (DC).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs20.3bn (+29% YoY, +12% QoQ) was 11% above Street and 8% above Kotak's estimate, led by CDMO (+67% YoY), mainly small molecules (Synthesis +69% YoY); ARV was soft at Rs6.7bn (+3% YoY). (Kotak, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs6.4bn (+67% YoY, +25% QoQ) was 29% above Street and 22% above Kotak's estimate. Gross margin rose 330bps YoY to 62.7% on higher CDMO mix, and operating leverage lifted EBITDA margin to 31.5% (+720bps YoY). (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management guides gross margin to stay near current ~63% levels on better product mix, expects the CDMO quarterly sales run-rate (~Rs8.3bn) to be broadly sustained, and targets CDMO at ~50% of sales by FY2030E. FY27E capex guidance was raised to ~Rs20bn from ~Rs15bn. Kotak raised FY27-29E EBITDA 20-23% and Jefferies 21-24%, but both see valuation as stretched (Kotak SELL, Jefferies Hold). (Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue was 33% above consensus and 27% above GS's estimate, up 119% YoY. Commercial CMS drove the beat: CMS revenue rose to Rs4.4bn (~67% of sales), of which commercial CMS was Rs4.2bn. GDS grew 17% YoY, helped by Prime and Specialty (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was 65% above consensus and up 546% YoY. Margin rose to 34.7%, which GS puts 924bps above its estimate. Gross margin improved to 61.2% from 55.3%, and operating leverage helped. Management says the elevated margin reflects favourable mix, operating leverage and FX (GS).

outlook.note: GS raised FY27-29E EPS by 9-11% and lifted its 12m TP to Rs23,300 from Rs20,550, after the beat and stronger commentary on CMS and peptide projects. Management expects FY27 to be a growth year, sees no abrupt destocking risk, and keeps its c.20% medium-term growth aspiration. It cautions that quarterly numbers will stay lumpy. Long-term EBITDA margin guidance stays at 25%+. Peptide module 1 should be commissioned shortly, and module 2 could be activated this year (GS).

companies.name: Piramal Pharma
companies.note: Mgmt alluded to broadbased growth recovery in CDMO, with both India and overseas units doing well. For FY27, mgt. has guided for low- to mid-teens revenue growth (in INR terms) and EBITDA & PAT growth faster than revenue.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 17% YoY to Rs22.7bn, about 6% above broker estimates and described by GS as meaningfully above consensus, on broad-based growth: CRDMO +19%, CHG +17% and ICH +15% (Kotak, GS, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 83% YoY to Rs1.95bn, 22% above Kotak's estimate (41% above Jefferies'), and GS says it was well above consensus. Margin was 8.6%, up 308bps YoY, on operating leverage and higher overseas-site utilisation (Kotak, GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 guidance of low-to-mid-teens revenue growth, with EBITDA and PAT growing faster, and still targets 25% EBITDA margin by FY30. GS says PPL is on track to beat guidance. After the beat, GS raised its target price to Rs250 from Rs225 and Jefferies raised its FY27 EBITDA estimate by 10%. Kotak lifted its fair value to Rs265 and sees a ~35% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29E (GS, Jeff, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs5.5bn (+12% YoY, -8% QoQ) was in line with MSe and consensus; CRO/discovery grew 24% YoY while CDMO grew only 5% on a high base (+113% in 1Q26) (MS, Kotak, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.48bn (+22% YoY) was about 2% above consensus and 4% above MSe; margin rose 234bps YoY to 26.7% on controlled opex and a higher commercial mix, though it was down 262bps QoQ (MS, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management expects 2HFY27 to be stronger than 1H, helped by commercial project ramp-ups, late-stage pipeline conversion and better asset utilisation. It has 90%+ sales visibility for FY27 and capex guidance of Rs11-13bn, with the new capacity already sold out. Kotak raised FY27-29E EBITDA by 3-5% and its fair value to Rs1,450, and Jefferies raised FY27/28 EPS by 4%/5% and its PT to Rs1,610 (MS, Kotak, Jeff).

companies.name: Syngene International
companies.note: FY27 guidance was lowered from flat sales to single-digit sales decline. Syngene is undertaking project rationalization in CRO to weed out low-value projects, which will create additional near-term pressure, while long-term growth visibility remains unclear on weak pipeline. Syngene aims to be register double-digit growth in FY28 after a tough FY27. Syngene believes growth can come back on operationalization of Bayview facility, winning new projects in Mangalore and Librela sales.

1Q27.revNote: Sales fell 16% YoY and 15% below consensus (11% below GSe), driven by inventory destocking in biologics manufacturing (Librela) and the planned shedding of low-margin CRO contracts. Syngene cut FY27 guidance to a single-digit decline from flat. (GS, Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: GS's adjusted EBITDA of Rs908mn (12.3% margin, down 1,127bps YoY) was 49% below consensus and GSe, on lower gross margins and operating deleverage. Other brokers show a higher reported EBITDA of about Rs1.4bn (Jeff: -33% YoY, 28% below its estimate). Mid-20s FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was kept. (GS, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management cut FY27 sales guidance to a single-digit decline from flat, with H1 expected to be weaker, and kept mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance. Growth is expected to return only from FY28 (double-digit aimed), led by Bayview, Mangalore and a Librela recovery. GS cut FY27-29E EPS by up to 28% and its TP to Rs450 from Rs525. Jeff cut FY27-29E EBITDA by 7-12% and EPS by 14-27%. Kotak cut FY27E EBITDA by 6-10%. (GS, Jeff, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales fell 4.6% YoY to Rs58.1bn as cement volumes fell 6% YoY to 10.0mt (Jefferies est: -2%) and blended realisation was down 10% QoQ. Nomura puts blended realisation 12% below its estimate. No report prints a revenue consensus. (Jeff, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 41% YoY to Rs4.6bn against Jefferies' estimate of Rs6.5bn, and Nomura says adjusted EBITDA of Rs4.34bn missed Bloomberg consensus by 30%. EBITDA/t of Rs457 was Rs70 lower QoQ, hurt by planned maintenance at larger integrated units and a higher volume mix sold to parent Ambuja (MSA). JPMorgan says EBITDA missed its numbers by 40%. (Jeff, Nomura, JP)

outlook.note: Management says cement demand should stay soft at about +5% YoY in FY27. It expects peak fuel-cost inflation from West Asia to hit Q2 profitability, partly offset by cost-saving initiatives. Nomura cut FY27F EBITDA by 20% on lower volumes and higher costs, left FY28F/29F broadly unchanged, and cut its TP to INR1,150 from INR1,250 (Reduce). It still expects EBITDA/t to rise about INR40 QoQ in 2Q. JPMorgan expects the Street to cut numbers and expects the stock to trade with the Ambuja share-swap ratio. (Nomura, JP, Jeff)

companies.name: Ambuja Cements
companies.note: Guiding to 8% volume growth for FY27

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs95.0bn fell 8% YoY and came in 11% below Visible Alpha consensus (4% below MSe). Consol volumes of 17.1mt were down 7% YoY, a sharp miss, as management cut low-margin non-trade volumes (-21% YoY) and trade volumes fell 2%. Blended realization was flat QoQ at Rs5,569/t (MS, JP, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs15.9bn fell 19% YoY. The brokers disagree on the print: MS has it 5% below Visible Alpha consensus and MSe, while JP has it 3% ahead and CLSA says it was above Bloomberg consensus and its own estimate. We call it in line. EBITDA/t of Rs931 was ahead of forecasts (MSe Rs950, JP c.Rs930, CLSA Rs918) on cost savings of Rs206/t QoQ, though JP notes part of this is inventory gains. Reported PAT of Rs6.6bn beat consensus on lower depreciation and minority interest (MS, JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management guided to 8% YoY volume growth in FY27 and a total cost target of Rs4,250/t by end-FY27, falling to Rs4,000/t in FY28. Capacity should reach 119mt by end-FY27 from 109mt now, with 8-10mt added each year after. Management prioritises profitability over volumes, which are expected to stay soft in the non-trade and south India segments. CLSA cut FY27-29 EBITDA by 1-11% and its TP from Rs490 to Rs480, while JP sees little room for earnings revisions and stays Neutral (CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue of ~Rs38.9bn was up 7% YoY and about 4% above Visible Alpha consensus (3% above MSE). Volumes grew 9% YoY to 7.6mt and realisations rose 5.9% QoQ on pricing in the East and South and a premium-product share of 25% (MS). Volume growth of 9% beat the industry's 6-7% (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs8.05bn was down 9% YoY and 11% QoQ but about 9% above consensus and 4% above MSE. EBITDA/t was Rs1,055 vs MSe Rs1,030, with opex/t about 1% above MSe on Rs125-150/t cost inflation. JPM puts it 6% ahead of its own estimate and CLSA 8% ahead of its estimate and Bloomberg consensus (MS, JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management guided to a further Rs70-80/t cost increase in 2Q, mainly logistics, and expects volumes to grow in line with the industry in FY27 excluding the acquired Jaypee assets. Those assets should reach EBITDA breakeven in about two quarters, with full ramp-up over 7-8 quarters, and capacity is targeted at 66.7mtpa by 3QFY28. Estimate changes are mixed: MS cuts FY27/FY28 EBITDA by 4% and raises it by 4% with PT Rs1,800 (UW), JPM cuts EPS 2.6%/7.8% with PT Rs1,800 (Neutral), while CLSA raises FY27-29 EBITDA 2-6% and PT to Rs2,250 (MS, JP, CLSA).
