1Q27.revNote: Standalone net sales of Rs38.7bn were 8.5% above Kotak's estimate and up 21% YoY. Grey volumes grew 18% YoY and white cement 29%, and blended realisation was Rs5,948/t (+2.2% YoY, +7% QoQ). Jefferies also called a beat on better volumes and pricing (Kotak, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs6.39bn was 4.9% above Kotak's estimate (Jefferies estimate Rs5.95bn) but fell 5.1% YoY. Volumes drove the beat. Blended EBITDA/t was Rs983 (Rs1,228 a year ago), as cost/t rose 8.1% YoY on higher other expenses and maintenance, and margin was 16.5% against 21.1% (Kotak, Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Standalone net sales of Rs36.8bn were in line with Kotak's estimate (Rs36.8bn), up 9% YoY on 12.3% higher grey cement volumes and 16% higher white cement volumes. Blended realisations were flat QoQ and down 3.1% YoY at Rs5,556/ton (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs6.7bn was 0.9% below Kotak's estimate of Rs6.76bn, down 9% YoY. Higher volumes and lower blended costs (Rs4,546/ton vs Rs4,607/ton est., on lower RM-energy costs) were largely offset by lower realisations. EBITDA/ton was Rs1,010 vs Rs1,037 est. and Rs927 in 3QFY26 (Kotak; Jeff also called it in line).

outlook.note: Management expects double-digit volume growth in FY27 (~23 mn t) and costs to rise ~Rs150/t in 2Q on fuel, freight and maintenance. Price hikes are expected to hold and gradually offset this. Kotak trimmed FY27/28/29E EBITDA by 0-2% (volume up, margin pressure) and raised Fair Value to Rs4,200 with a SELL rating. The Jaisalmer/North expansion is on track for 1HFY28 (Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs18,964 mn (+21.6% YoY, flat QoQ) was in line with Kotak's estimate of Rs18,902 mn (+0.3%). Blended volumes rose 15.1% YoY to 3.8 mn t and realizations rose 5.6% YoY to Rs4,977/t. Cement volumes grew 26% YoY on the North ramp-up, while GGBS grew only 2.3%. (Kotak, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2,986 mn (-7.5% YoY, -18% QoQ) was 6% below Kotak's estimate of Rs3,177 mn. Blended costs rose 12.2% YoY to Rs4,194/t on higher raw-material and power and fuel costs (+31% vs estimate). Startup losses at the new Nagaur plant were about Rs370 mn, and EBITDA/t fell 20% YoY to Rs784. Jefferies also noted the miss against its Rs3.2 bn estimate, citing the Nagaur ramp-up and a weaker GGBS mix. (Kotak, Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs18.95bn rose 10.9% YoY and 16.9% QoQ, 0.7% above Kotak's estimate. Blended volumes grew 7% YoY (cement +12%) and blended realisations rose 4.3% QoQ to Rs4,749/ton, though GGBS volumes were hit by slag shortages at Dolvi and RMC plant closures in Maharashtra (Kotak, Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.65bn (+46% YoY, +28% QoQ) was 4.5% above Kotak's estimate and about 7% above Jefferies' Rs3.4bn, driven by better realisations. EBITDA/ton was Rs915 (est Rs850), partly offset by higher freight and other costs from slag rerouting and Nagaur expansion (Kotak, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management guides for high-teens FY27 volume growth, with high-single-digit GGBS growth. The Nagaur plant is at about 68% exit utilization, with breakeven targeted by Sep-26. Margin improvement is expected to come in 2HFY27, and a further 1/2.5 mtpa grinding unit is due by 2QFY27/FY28. Kotak changed FY27/28/29E EBITDA by +1.2%/-3.3%/-4.8% and kept its FV at Rs150. Jefferies cut FY27-28 EBITDA by 7-9% and kept its PT at Rs150. Both kept BUY. (Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR31.3bn rose 9% YoY and was 3% above Nomura's INR30.3bn estimate. Grey cement volumes grew 4% YoY to 5.3MT, in line with estimate, and blended realisation improved 7% QoQ, 4% ahead of estimate, on better pricing across key markets (Nomura). Jefferies also cites volumes +5% YoY, below industry growth of 7-7.5% (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR5.7bn (+10% YoY) beat Nomura's estimate by 22% and Bloomberg consensus by 16%. Unit EBITDA of INR1,072/t was up over INR90/t QoQ, 23% above estimate, on better realisation. RM+P&F cost/t was flat QoQ and 8% below estimate, offsetting freight cost/t that was 8% above estimate (Nomura). Jefferies calls it a 15% beat, helped by a sharp cut in petcoke mix (Jeff).
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA vs Bloomberg consensus; revenue vs broker estimate (Nomura), as no consensus revenu

outlook.note: Management says July pricing has held at June levels, an unusual trend as prices typically fall sequentially in the monsoon. 2Q variable costs are guided to rise by under Rs50/t QoQ. The 2MT Limla grinding unit (Vadraj) was commissioned in Jul-26, keeping the company on track for 35MT capacity by FY28. Jefferies raised FY27 EBITDA estimates by about 2% and its PT to Rs430 from Rs410, and flagged seasonal softness and lagged cost inflation for 2Q. Nomura maintained Buy and a TP of Rs400 (Jeff, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 10% YoY on 12% volume growth to 4.5mt, partly offset by a 2% YoY fall in blended ASP, and was about 0.6% above Kotak's estimate (Rs22,731mn actual vs Rs22,592mn). State elections in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and West Bengal disrupted demand. (CLSA, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.07bn (-23% YoY, -18% QoQ) was in line with Bloomberg consensus (CLSA). Jefferies called it ahead of its own Rs2.81bn estimate, while Kotak saw a miss on lower margins. EBITDA/t was Rs686 (-31% YoY), as power and fuel cost/t rose 11% YoY on imported fuel costs tied to the Middle East conflict. (CLSA, Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA: consensus (CLSA, Bloomberg); revenue: broker estimate (Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs26.1bn rose 9% YoY and 24% QoQ and was 3% above Nomura's estimate. Volumes rose 5% YoY to 5.5MT and blended realisation rose 2% QoQ to Rs4,693/t. No consensus revenue figure is printed, so the call is against Nomura's estimate. Kotak had revenue 4.8% below its own estimate. (Nomura, Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.7bn (+16% YoY) missed Nomura's estimate by 2.5% and Bloomberg consensus by 11%. Higher raw material costs (+18% vs estimate) and freight (lead distance 276km vs 256km QoQ) drove the miss. Unit EBITDA of Rs671/t was 4% below Nomura's estimate. Jefferies also called it a miss against its Rs4.1bn estimate. (Nomura, Jeff)
4Q26.vsBasis: EBITDA: consensus (Bloomberg, per Nomura); revenue: broker estimate (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 capex at Rs8bn and the ~31mtpa capacity target. Brokers expect margin pressure to peak in 2QFY27 on lagged fuel costs and higher diesel prices, with recovery from 2HFY27 only if input costs ease. Jefferies cut FY27-28 EBITDA by ~9% each and trimmed its target price to Rs900. Kotak tweaked EBITDA by 0-1% and stays SELL. CLSA stays Underperform. (Jeff, Kotak, CLSA)

companies.name: Shree Cement
companies.note: Mgmt expects these issues to normalize from 2Q, with fuel costs likely having peaked in 1Q

1Q27.revNote: Standalone net sales of Rs56.2bn (+13.6% YoY) were 0.6% above Kotak's estimate, as 17% YoY blended volume growth (10.5mn t) offset ~3% lower realisations (Rs5,360/t) on a weaker trade mix. No consensus figure was printed for revenue. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs10.7bn (-12.6% YoY) missed Kotak's estimate by 6.3% and consensus of Rs11.3bn by about 5%. Costs rose to Rs4,336/t (+4.3% YoY) after petcoke and gypsum shipments from the Gulf were disrupted, which forced a shift to higher-cost domestic coal and a lower-quality product mix. EBITDA/t fell to Rs1,024. (Kotak, JP)

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 volume guidance at a minimum of 40mn t and capex at Rs15bn, and expects fuel costs to have peaked in 1Q with trade mix and margins normalising from 2Q. Kotak sees margins bottoming in 2QFY27 and cut FY27/28E EBITDA by 5.1%/1.7%. Jefferies cut standalone EBITDA by about 3%. Meghalaya clinker/grinding capacity is due by March 2028 per Kotak, while Jefferies expects the North East expansion online by 4QFY28. (Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales were c.3% above consensus and c.4% above MSe, helped by consolidated volumes up c.12% YoY (MSe c.9%) and blended realisation up 3.4% QoQ (MSe +2.5%). Domestic grey cement realisation rose 3.7% QoQ. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs50.2bn was c.3% above Visible Alpha consensus but c.2% below MSe, as opex/t was higher than expected, with power and fuel at Rs1,312/t vs MSe Rs1,261/t. EBITDA/t of Rs1,214 was 4% below MSe, while CLSA and JPM called the quarter a beat on volumes and costs. (MS, CLSA, JP)

2Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs233bn (+19% yoy, -5.5% qoq) came 2.1% above Kotak's estimate. Consolidated volumes grew 12.9% yoy to 38.2mt, ahead of the ~10% industry growth, and blended realisations rose 2.2% qoq (+5.2% yoy). No consensus revenue figure is printed. (Kotak)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs37.2bn (+20% yoy, -26% qoq) was broadly in line with consensus (Nomura, Jeff) and 7-9% above the brokers' own estimates. Better realisations and volumes were offset by a 7.8% qoq rise in cost/ton on higher fuel and RM costs. EBITDA/t was Rs974, down qoq but up yoy. (Kotak, Nomura, Jeff)
2Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA: consensus (Nomura, Jeff); revenue: broker estimate (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management expects demand to stay strong through March 2029, backed by data centers, private capex, metro and urban housing, with South capacity already sold out. Late-September price hikes of Rs7-10/bag should offset the ~Rs6/bag fuel cost increase, and Nomura sees 3Q EBITDA/t recovering ~Rs80 to Rs1,050 on 12% YoY volume growth. Against that, Nomura cut FY27/28/29 EBITDA by 5%/1%/1% and its TP to Rs13,700 from Rs13,900, citing a higher cost base. Management admits costs may not have peaked, and a weak monsoon is a FY28 risk. (Nomura, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 27.5% yoy and 7% qoq to Rs3,266 mn, 3.9% above Kotak's Rs3,143 mn estimate. The qoq increase came from the LSM vertical (+12.5% qoq), as deliveries deferred from 4QFY26 shipped in 1QFY27. CEM revenues rose 1.5% qoq, and Baker Hughes contributed about Rs700 mn (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 27.5% yoy to Rs1,028 mn, 8.0% above Kotak's estimate. The main driver was gross margin, which jumped 617 bps qoq to 49.8% (4QFY26 was hit by higher input costs and a Rs70 mn inventory loss from a fire). EBITDA margin was 31.5%, up 437 bps qoq (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management called FY27 demand the strongest it has seen, with firm order visibility and rising customer urgency in Europe. It targets 70%+ of revenue from CRAMS and CEM within two years, up from about 50% now. FY27 capex is guided at Rs3-3.5 bn, mainly for Site-5 (Magnum), where new LSM products start contributing from 2QFY27. Kotak left estimates and its Rs1,070 Fair Value unchanged and kept SELL on valuation (74X/54X FY27E/FY28E P/E) and negative free cash flow from heavy capex (Kotak).

companies.name: Asian Paints
companies.note: Maintained its 8%-10% volume growth guidance for FY27.

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 10.6% YoY, about 5% above Bloomberg consensus (6% above CLSA). Standalone volume growth was 12.4%, with 3-4% of it from up-stocking ahead of price hikes, and double-digit growth in all three months. (CLSA, Kotak, Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 24.4% YoY, about 13% above consensus. EBITDA margin expanded 214bps YoY to 19.3%, 138bps above consensus. Gross margin rose to 44.8% on lower-priced raw material inventory and better mix. (CLSA, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 17.9% YoY, 4% above Bloomberg consensus and 3% above CLSA. India decorative sales rose 16.6%, driven by 9% volume, about 3% mix and about 5% price, after a total 12% price increase staggered through the quarter. International revenue grew 27% YoY. (CLSA, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 33.5% YoY and was 18% above consensus. Margin expanded 239bps YoY to 20.6%, 251bps ahead of consensus. Gross margin was 43.6%, helped by 30-45 days of pre-war low-cost inventory and higher pricing/mix, despite about 25% material inflation. (CLSA, MS, GS)

outlook.note: Management kept its 8-10% FY27 volume growth guidance. It expects 2Q margins to contract as the low-cost inventory is exhausted but to stay in the 18-20% range, with a worse mix in 2Q. Estimate changes are mixed: GS raised FY27-29 EPS by about 8% and lifted its target price to Rs2,725 (Sell), while CLSA changed FY27-29 EPS by -1% to +1% and cut its target price to Rs1,860 (Underperform). (CLSA, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs18.5 bn (+25.0% yoy, +10.7% qoq) was 1.6% above Kotak's estimate of Rs18.2 bn. Management said growth was driven entirely by pricing, with consolidated volumes flat yoy and slightly down qoq. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.9 bn (+67.1% yoy) was 46.6% above Kotak's estimate, with margin at 21.3% against 14.8% estimated. Lower-cost inventories held amid rising finished-goods prices added about 300 bps, so normalised margin is nearer 18%. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management gave no FY2027 volume guidance, and cited limited visibility, higher freight and insurance costs, and the 1Q windfall pricing benefit expected to fade from 2QFY27 as key product prices correct. Kotak cut FY27E revenue by 11.2% but left EPS largely unchanged at Rs269 (normalised quarterly EPS of about Rs60-65). It trimmed Fair Value to Rs5,870 from Rs5,900 and kept SELL. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue fell 4.2% yoy to Rs18.4 bn, 0.9% above Kotak's estimate. Weak agrochemicals (domestic ex-Roundup -9%, Roundup -21%, exports -36%, traded seeds -28%) on adverse weather and delayed, deficient rain, largely offset by DeKalb corn hybrids +23% yoy (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 5.5% yoy to Rs3.68 bn, 8% above Kotak's estimate. Gross margin expanded 464 bps yoy to 43.5% on favourable pricing and a richer mix toward DeKalb, and EBITDA margin rose 184 bps to 20.0%. Other expenses +9.1% and employee costs +8.1% partly offset this (Kotak).

outlook.note: Kotak cuts FY2027E-29E EBITDA by 4-7% and revenue by ~3% each year, building in lower agrochemical volumes (including Roundup) amid El Nino. It partly offsets this by raising DeKalb growth to 12% for FY27E (from 2%) and gross margin by 50-100 bps. FY28-29E EPS is cut 7-8%, while FY27E EPS is unchanged at Rs167 on the one-off flubendiamide gain. Rating ADD; FV Rs4,450 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs18.7 bn (up 25% yoy, 21% qoq) were 7.2% above Kotak's estimate. Volumes of ~70.6 mn liters rose 7.0% yoy, and realization of Rs265/liter (up 17% yoy) was 6.2% above estimate, helped by two rounds of low double-digit price hikes during Jan-Jun 2026 (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.9 bn (up 41% yoy, 50% qoq) was 55% above Kotak's estimate. Margin of 26.4% compared with the 18.2% estimate, as price hikes, better sourcing and inventory gains more than offset raw-material cost inflation. Gross profit rose 31% yoy and was 32% above estimate (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management kept its 21-24% medium-term EBITDA margin guidance, but cautioned that raw-material inflation will become more visible in 3QCY26 as low-cost inventory runs out. Volumes are growing at ~2x industry levels. Kotak raised CY2026E EBITDA by ~11% and CY2028-29E by 2-7%, but kept a cautious long-term view on volume growth. The stock is likely to stay rangebound given Stonepeak's Rs194/share open offer for 26%, following BP's sale of its 65% stake (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs2,684 mn were 5.6% above Kotak's estimate, up 10.5% yoy and 7.7% qoq. The qoq rise came from higher realizations at the parent company and HALS revenue rising to Rs600 mn, from Rs450-500 mn in 4QFY26, on a richer product mix. A two-week production loss in April held back volumes (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs964 mn was 8.0% above Kotak's estimate, but down 3.4% yoy. Gross margin fell 255 bps qoq as input-cost inflation was not fully passed through. A 13.9% qoq drop in other expenses offset this. EBITDA margin was 35.9%, against 41.1% a year ago (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management targets FY27 HALS revenue of Rs2.5-3 bn, with volumes above 3,000 tons against about 1,000 tons in 1QFY27. It expects EBITDA margins to keep improving as higher-grade HALS sales rise. The Geneus Chem and Kemin tie-ups add visibility. Raw material and shipping cost volatility remains a risk, and no further price-increase benefit is expected next quarter. Kotak raised FY27E EBITDA by 8.8% to Rs4.5 bn and cut its fair value slightly to Rs1,040 from Rs1,060 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 36% YoY and 22% QoQ, driven by Phenolics (+36% YoY, +24% QoQ) on elevated phenol spreads, and Advanced Intermediates (+33% YoY, +13.6% QoQ). Sales were 10.2% below Kotak's estimate of Rs28.7bn (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.4bn was up 185% YoY and 44% QoQ, 12.9% above Kotak's estimate. EBITDA margin expanded to 21.0% (+429 bps vs Kotak's estimate, +1,093 bps YoY) on strong phenol spreads, possibly some low-cost raw material inventory, and better Advanced Intermediates margins. Morgan Stanley calls it a strong beat vs MSe and Street, with core EBITDA of ~Rs5.2bn, ~3x YoY (Kotak, MS).

4Q26.revNote: Net sales of Rs21.2 bn were 0.5% above Kotak's estimate, up 7.4% qoq but down 2.7% yoy. Phenolics revenue fell 6.8% yoy, while advanced intermediates rose 8.2% yoy on better pricing (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.76 bn beat Kotak's estimate by 5.8%, up 78% qoq and 19% yoy. The margin was 17.7% (+705 bps qoq). Phenol spreads spiked late in the quarter after the Iran war, and phenolics segment EBIT nearly doubled qoq to a 20% margin (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management says volume demand has improved across all verticals, feedstock availability is no longer a constraint, and 1QFY27 is a strong start to a strong year for Advanced Intermediates. New MIBK/MIBC/acetophenone units are due in Aug-26. Kotak expects phenol spreads to moderate, advanced the polycarbonate commissioning to 2HFY29 (FY29E EBITDA up, FY27E unchanged) and kept fair value at Rs1,950. MS flags modest upside to consensus EPS and announced a Rs25bn BPA capex plan (Kotak, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs13.0 bn grew 25.3% yoy and 10.3% qoq, 2.1% above Kotak's estimate. Growth was led by Chemical Intermediates (+37.5% yoy) and Nutrition & Health Solutions (+35.8% yoy), with Specialty Chemicals up 11.5% yoy. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.99 bn rose 40.1% yoy and was 3.3% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded 162 bps yoy to 15.3%, helped by gross margin up 171 bps yoy. Chemical Intermediates contributed nearly Rs400 mn of the ~Rs560 mn yoy EBITDA increase, while Specialty Chemicals EBITDA was flat qoq. (Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs11.8 bn grew 12.1% yoy and qoq, 2.8% above Kotak's estimate, with a broad-based pickup across all three segments led by volume growth; Specialty Chemicals revenue rose 12.7% qoq and Chemical Intermediates 10.2% qoq (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.63 bn rose 10.9% yoy and 28.5% qoq, 3.9% above Kotak's estimate. Specialty Chemicals margin expanded 161 bps qoq to 26.9% on a higher share of value-added CDMO products and better Fine Chemicals contribution, and the other two segments also reported higher EBITDA (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management retained its FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs7.5-8 bn, which implies sequential growth in revenue and EBITDA, and said it could beat guidance if booked orders (Rs15 bn order book) materialise. Kotak raised FY27E revenue and EBITDA by 4.4% and 6.8%, raised FY28-29E revenue and EBITDA by 1-2%, and raised fair value to Rs960 from Rs940. The CDMO pipeline has more than 25 confirmed molecules, up from 22 last quarter. Acetyls pricing remains a risk in 3Q and 4Q. (Kotak)

companies.name: Kansai Nerolac Paints
companies.note: The company reiterated its F27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13–14%, with 2Q margin expected to remain flat YoY.  management reiterated its focus on improving profitability by not participating in low margin, high-volume products.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs23.7bn, in line with FactSet consensus (0% variance) and 1% below MS's estimate. Decorative value growth was high single digit, industrial grew double digits led by auto, and blended pricing rose 5% (MS). Kotak calls it a ~3.6% beat on its own estimate, with decorative growth of 7-8% lagging the industry (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 8% YoY to Rs3.28bn, 5% above consensus of Rs3.12bn, though 8% below MS's estimate. Margin was 13.8%, down 19bps YoY and 65bps above consensus. Gross margin fell 112bps YoY to 35.0% as lower-cost inventory was only partly offset by a lag in B2B price increases (MS, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management retained its FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13-14% and expects 2Q margin to be flat YoY. It plans a further 3% price flow-through in Decorative and 3-5% in Industrial, and expects demand to improve with a November Diwali. Competition stays high and KNP is losing market share in decorative paints. Estimate changes were mixed: Kotak raised FY27E EPS by 8% on easier raw-material prices, Nomura trimmed FY27E EPS from 8.66 to 8.56 with its target price unchanged, and MS stays Underweight (MS, Kotak, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs10.5bn (+44% y/y, +11% q/q) was 12% ahead of JEFe, led by HPP (Rs5.4bn, +33% y/y, 26% above JEFe) on higher volumes and realisations. CDMO (Rs1.8bn, +82% y/y) and Specialty Chemicals (Rs3.25bn, +48% y/y) were in line to slightly ahead. (Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.6bn (+73% y/y) was 16% ahead of JEFe/consensus, driven by HPP momentum and continued strength in CDMO and specialty chemicals. Margin held steady q/q at 34.2% (+566bp y/y) on operating leverage despite a 165bp q/q gross margin correction. (Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.vsBasis: broker estimate (Jefferies); EBITDA also stated vs consensus

outlook.note: Jefferies raises FY27/28E PAT by 8%/4% and projects a 23% EPS CAGR over FY26-29E, with the 15ktpa R32 expansion on track for 3QFY27 and new capex in CDMO (Rs1.25bn cGMP4 phase 2) and advanced materials (Rs0.9bn) adding growth. Management sees EBITDA margins sustainable at 32-33% regardless of R32 pricing. Kotak raises EPS 6-11% for higher R32 prices, and MS sees normalised margins of 32-33% but flags rising R-32 competition from F2H27 (Underweight). (Jeff, Kotak, MS)

companies.name: Neogen Chemicals
companies.note: Traction in the organolithium business seems strong, while battery chemicals are nearing an inflection point.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs2.5 bn (+34% yoy, +1.5% qoq) was in line with Kotak's Rs2,507 mn estimate, driven by volume-led growth in organolithium, inorganic chemicals and battery chemicals (battery revenue Rs190 mn vs Rs50 mn a year ago); about Rs150 mn of the growth came from higher lithium and raw material prices. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs482 mn (+53% yoy) was 23.7% above Kotak's Rs390 mn estimate. Gross margin was 46.6% (204 bps above estimate) and opex was lower than expected, lifting EBITDA margin to 19.3% (+240 bps yoy). Some of this came from low-cost inventory sold amid rising prices. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 base-business revenue guidance to Rs9.5-10.5 bn (from Rs8.75-9.5 bn). It guides base EBITDA margin at 18% ±1-1.5% for FY27 and 18-20% for FY28, and kept FY27 battery chemicals revenue guidance at Rs3 bn, with most of it in 2HFY27. Kotak raised EBITDA estimates by 11-16% and pulled forward full battery-chemicals utilisation by a year to FY2031. It retained ADD with fair value Rs2,190 (from Rs1,770). (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue fell 10% y/y to Rs 17.0bn, 1% below JEFe. CSM exports fell 13% y/y on 8% lower volume and pricing pressure, and pharma revenue fell 25% y/y, 40% below JEFe. Domestic revenue rose 3% on 12% volume growth, with prices down about 9% (Jeff, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 29% y/y to Rs 3.7bn, 8% below JEFe. Margin was 21.6%, down about 570bps y/y, on negative operating leverage, with staff costs up 12% y/y and other operating costs 11% above JEFe. Gross margin was 56.7%, down about 70bps y/y (Jeff, Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue fell 12% y/y to Rs15.7bn, 1% below Jefferies' estimate. CSM exports declined 15% y/y and domestic revenue fell 9%, partly offset by Pharma, up 23% y/y. (Jeff, Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 26% y/y and was 5% below Jefferies' estimate. Margin dropped to 21.5% from 25.5% a year ago on negative operating leverage, despite gross margin of 57.8%. (Jeff, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to low-single-digit from high-single-digit. Pricing pressure persists in CSM and generics, and pharma order deliveries slipped to 2H. Jefferies cut FY27/28E EPS by 12%/11% and its PT to Rs 2,910 (Buy). Kotak cut EPS by 10-15% and its fair value to Rs 2,010 (Sell), and sees earnings falling for a third straight year in FY27. Positives are a stable US$1.2bn CSM order book, a 2H export recovery hope, 50% biologicals growth and net cash of about Rs 38bn (Jeff, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 21.3% YoY to Rs45.5 bn, 3% ahead of Kotak's estimate (GS: ~2% ahead of its estimate). Standalone underlying volume growth was 11.3% with roughly 10% pricing; Consumer & Bazaar grew 22% and B2B 14% (Kotak, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 27% YoY to ~Rs11.9 bn, 8% above Kotak's estimate (GS: ~20% above its estimate). Margin rose 115 bps YoY to 26.2%, helped by operating leverage, low-cost inventory and proactive price hikes, despite gross margin falling 65 bps YoY to 53.5% on raw-material inflation (Kotak, GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management is confident of sustaining double-digit underlying volume growth and expects EBITDA margin near the upper end of the 20-24% guidance band if raw-material prices stay easy. It cautioned that 2Q margins will moderate as the low-cost inventory is exhausted and that pricing benefits may fade as rebates are calibrated. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 4-10% and fair value to Rs1,785 (from Rs1,650), keeping ADD. Jeff holds at Rs1,610 PT, citing a ~59x 1-year forward P/E (Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs6,624 mn (+14.1% yoy, +2.0% qoq) was 1.9% above Kotak's estimate. The flavors segment jumped 63% yoy, helped by customer order preponement (~15% of flavors revenue). Fragrances rose only 9% yoy and were down 4.4% qoq, and global ingredients was softer (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs887 mn (+21.3% yoy) was 20.9% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded 80 bps yoy and 404 bps qoq to 13.4%, on gross margin up 29 bps yoy to 42.9% and lower operating expenses. Net income was also boosted by a Rs300 mn one-off insurance claim (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs6,499 mn (+14.6% yoy, +11.3% qoq) was in line with Kotak's Rs6,466 mn estimate. It included a one-off Rs350 mn sale of low-margin products; adjusted for this, growth would be 8.4% yoy. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs600 mn was 18% below Kotak's Rs732 mn estimate, and margin fell to 9.2% (vs 12.9% a year ago). Low-margin inventory liquidation cut gross margin 300 bps qoq to 39.5%, and employee costs rose 36% yoy, including one-offs. Management says adjusted EBITDA margin was 13.5%. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guided to double-digit revenue growth and margin improvement for FY2027, with a normalized flavors run-rate of ~Rs950-960 mn per quarter. It expects debt to decline from 3QFY27 by ~Rs250 mn each quarter. Kotak raised FY27E EBITDA by 11.3% (to just over Rs3 bn) and adjusted EPS by 25%, and kept its fair value at Rs270 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 32% y/y to Rs50.3bn and came in 13% above JEFe, led by Chemicals (+26% y/y, 9% above JEFe on strong refrigerant gas performance), Packaging Films (+42% y/y, 15% above) and Technical Textiles (+28% y/y, 21% above) (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 49% y/y to Rs12.4bn, 27% above JEFe and 31% above consensus, led by Packaging Films (EBIT 66% above JEFe, margin up 771bps q/q to 17.3%) and Technical Textiles (EBIT 83% above JEFe), both helped by inventory gains; MS also called it a solid beat vs MS and Street estimates (Jeff, MS).
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA vs consensus (Jeff); revenue vs broker estimate (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management maintained guidance of 15-20% top-line growth for chemicals in F28, with firm refrigerant gas pricing, capacity expansion and steady greenshoots, but sequential softness in F2Q and F3Q (India and Middle East). Specialty chemicals are seen at a trough with only gradual recovery as pricing pressure offsets volume gains. MS flags a >2x increase in domestic R32 capacity as a competitive risk from F2H27, and rising raw material costs. MS sees modest upward revisions to 12-month consensus EPS but stays Underweight (PT Rs2,209). A Rs2.5bn BOPET thick film line was announced (MS, Jeff).

companies.name: Tata Chemicals
companies.note: The near-term outlook for soda ash is challenging due to oversupply from China and elevated raw material and freight costs caused by Middle East tensions.

1Q27.ebitdaNote: India business was the sole source of positive surprise in 1QFY27, registering a 1,120 bps qoq jump in EBITDA margins to 28.4%, despite 12%/19% qoq declines in sales volumes of soda ash (attributed to a transient shift in product mix toward salt) and icarbonate. Management explained that the jump in profitability was due to a ~Rs2/kg rise in soda ash prices, even as the company benefited from low-cost coal inventories

companies.name: UPL
companies.note: Company guided for revenue growth of 7-11% and EBITDA growth of 10-14% in FY27.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs 102bn (+10% y/y) was 2% below JEFe, broadly in line. Growth was driven entirely by a 10% favourable FX impact, with volume -3% and price +3%. Weather-hit crop protection in Europe, India and LatAm offset strong seeds growth (Advanta +26%). (Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 14.5bn (+4% y/y) was 7% below JEFe despite an inventory gain in crop protection. Margin contracted about 90bps y/y to 14.2%, with staff costs +16% and other costs +24%. A Rs 500mn forex loss compared with a Rs 930mn gain a year earlier. (Jeff, Kotak)

outlook.note: FY27 guidance is revenue growth of 7-11% and EBITDA growth of 10-14%, with a strong volume-led 2Q expected, US$150mn from new products and continued deleveraging. Jefferies cut its FY27E EPS by 41% and its PT to Rs 715 from Rs 810, but kept Buy. Kotak made minor estimate changes, trimmed FV to Rs 640 from Rs 650 and kept Reduce. Risks include the Middle East conflict, El Niño, higher-cost inventory hitting the P&L from 2Q, and the reorganisation plan. (Jeff, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs6,959 mn (+28% yoy, +15% qoq) was 10.7% above Kotak's estimate. Growth came mainly from INR depreciation (exports ~55% of revenue) and price pass-through of higher raw material costs after the Middle East supply disruptions. Volume growth in antioxidants and new products also helped. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,705 mn (+6.8% yoy) was 1.3% below Kotak's estimate. Gross margin fell 637 bps yoy to 46.0% on elevated raw material costs, and EBITDA margin fell 497 bps yoy to 24.5% (27.5% expected). Employee costs rose 17% qoq. (Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs6.0 bn was 17.3% above Kotak's estimate and up 13.8% QoQ, but fell 6.9% YoY. The YoY decline reflects weak IBB and ATBS volumes (ATBS demand softened after Oct 2025, IBB hit by Iran-war raw material shortages), while the subsidiary VOPL contributed negative implied revenue of Rs66 mn (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.70 bn was 20.6% above Kotak's estimate, with margin at 28.2% (76 bps above estimate, 130 bps lower QoQ). Gross margin of 52.5% was 311 bps below estimate, but EBITDA margin beat as the higher revenue base and lower employee costs offset it. EBITDA was down 5.6% YoY (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guided to at least 15% volume and revenue growth in FY27 (2H stronger than 1H). It is confident of EBITDA margins of 26-27%. ATBS capacity is now 50 KTPA, and the Veeral Organics plant re-engineering is slated for completion by Dec 2026, a slip from September. Kotak raised FY27E-29E revenue by ~3% but trimmed margins, cutting EPS ~2%. Kotak cut its fair value to Rs1,170 from Rs1,200 and retains SELL, citing growth challenges and the Kemin agreement risk. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs16.2bn, up 10% YoY, was 1% ahead of CLSA's estimate. Admissions rose 8% to 37m and ATP rose 7% to Rs273, so movie ticket sales grew 15% to Rs8.4bn. F&B grew 13% on SPH of Rs161, up 9%. Ad revenue fell 2%. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs5.3bn, up 33% YoY, was 5% ahead of CLSA's estimate, with the margin up 5.5ppts to 32.6% on operating leverage. Kotak's pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA of Rs2.1bn (+104% YoY) was a ~27.5% beat versus Kotak's estimate, with margin up ~590bps to 12.9%. Falling film hire costs and F&B gross margin of 78.8% (+225bps) helped. (CLSA, Kotak)

outlook.note: Brokers see a strong content pipeline and net-cash balance sheet. Management guided ~80-100 net screen additions in FY27, mostly asset-light, and cut FY27 capex guidance to Rs3.5bn from Rs4bn. CLSA retained its 11-13% revenue/EBITDA CAGR through FY29 and its Rs2,135 TP. Kotak trimmed FY27-29E EBITDA marginally, raised EPS 1-2% and lifted FV to Rs1,525 from Rs1,500. Kotak flags a high 2HFY27 base from Dhurandhar. The company announced a Rs3bn buyback at Rs1,450. (CLSA, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 8% YoY (flat to down 1% QoQ) to Rs462.5bn, helped by 4% YoY higher dispatch volumes (198mt) and 4% higher net realisation (Rs2,338/t); FSA volumes were up 1% and e-auction volumes up 25% YoY (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 4% YoY to Rs120.7bn (margin 26.1%, down 3.2pp YoY); cash EBITDA fell 9% YoY and was 11% below Jefferies' estimate as cash cost per ton rose 10% YoY to Rs1,820, mainly on higher material consumed (explosives, oil and lubricants). Recurring PAT was up 1% YoY, in line, on a favourable stripping adjustment and lower depreciation (Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies expects a recovery in power demand (Jun-Q up 8% YoY, and a weak monsoon or El-Nino could boost it further) to lift dispatch volumes, with 5-6% volume growth to 790mt in FY27E. It fine-tunes estimates (FY27 revenue +2%, EPS +1% vs prior), forecasts EBITDA of Rs457bn in FY27E, keeps a Buy with a Rs500 PT, and flags an interim dividend of Rs5.5/sh (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 50% YoY and beat MS's estimate by 3.7%, led by commercial mining (+62% YoY) and copper, with airports up 35% YoY and non-aero revenue up 53% (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 54% YoY and beat MS's estimate by 9.7%. Airport EBITDA was +41% YoY, IRM +86% and copper EBIT Rs4.9bn (36% beat), offset by mining services (-16% YoY) and new energy (-19%). Adjusted PAT missed by 21% on higher depreciation and interest from the Navi Mumbai airport and Ganga Expressway (MS). Jeff puts reported EBITDA at Rs56.4bn against its Rs50.3bn estimate; the table here shows adjusted EBITDA of Rs51.1bn.

outlook.note: Jeff raises FY27-28 EBITDA by 8-13% and lifts its SOTP-based target price to Rs3,830 from Rs2,800. It expects a 23% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-31, with airports at about 40% of SOTP. Navi Mumbai international ops began in mid-July, data-centre capacity is 65.4MW with a 400MW hyperscale order added, and a 1.7GW module line was commissioned. MS sees 51% of EBITDA from incubating businesses but flags a modest cut to next-12-month consensus EPS after the PAT miss and higher interest and depreciation (Jeff, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales of Rs487.2bn were up 21% YoY and 4% above JPMe. UltraTech (+16% YoY, 5% above JPMe), Financial Services (+28% YoY), chemicals (+10%) and Paints (+64% YoY, Rs16.6bn, ~9% price hikes) drove the growth. Pivot (B2B e-commerce) grew 75% YoY but fell 10% QoQ on customer inventory optimisation. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs77.7bn was up 28% YoY, flat QoQ and 15% above JPMe. More than half of the beat came from the UTCEM and ABCAP results. The rest came from chemicals EBITDA of Rs4.9bn (+16% YoY, +62% QoQ), which beat on realisations and was supported by all three sub-segments. Combined Paints and Pivot losses narrowed by c.Rs1.5bn QoQ. Jefferies calls standalone EBITDA of Rs9.5bn (+147% YoY) 'much ahead of estimates'. (JP, Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Standalone net sales of Rs117.7bn rose 31.9% YoY and 12.9% QoQ, 8.8% above Kotak's Rs108.3bn estimate. Growth was led by Paints & B2B e-commerce (+27% QoQ, revenue ~Rs42bn), with CSF revenue up 13.9% YoY on 11.5% higher volumes. The notes show standalone figures only, not consolidated, so the figures differ in scale from the consolidated figures already held for other quarters. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs5.4bn was up 145% YoY and 3.9% above Kotak's estimate (Jefferies' own estimate was Rs4.8bn, about 12% below actual). The beat came from CSF EBITDA doubling YoY on volumes, product mix and benign pulp prices, plus narrower paints losses (Rs3.0bn vs Rs3.1bn QoQ). Chemicals EBITDA was Rs3.04bn, slightly ahead. (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management guides 50%+ YoY Paints revenue growth in FY27 and FY28, with Opus profitability of Rs100bn revenue in FY28 intact. Pivot is on track to break even by exit-FY27. Management warned that 2Q chemicals margins could face pressure from higher-cost inventory. A new 0.25% brand royalty to Aditya Birla Holdings (capped at Rs2.25bn) is a standalone drag, but consolidated numbers are largely unaffected. JPMorgan raised FY27E/FY28E EBITDA by 3.3%/2.2%, EPS by 6.9%/3.6% and its PT to Rs3,780. Jefferies raised FY27E/FY28E EBITDA by 30%/7% and its PT to Rs3,910. (JP, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue fell 21% YoY and was ~7% below Bloomberg consensus (about 1% above Nomura's estimate). Management cited slower execution from delayed payments, adverse weather, the West Asia crisis and labour shortages. (Nomura, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 42% YoY and was ~11% below consensus. Margin dropped to 9.4% from 12.9% a year ago, about 270bp below Jefferies' estimate, on lower revenue and weaker operating leverage and higher fuel and logistics costs. Jefferies put EBITDA 27% below its estimate. (Jeff, Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue fell 19% YoY and 12% QoQ, 23% below Bloomberg consensus, as execution of overseas projects was severely hampered by the West Asia Crisis: vendors demanded advance payments, key materials such as diesel and gas were scarce, and client liquidity constraints added to the delays (Nomura).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 43% YoY to INR1.67bn, 55% below consensus. Margin was 6.4%, down 272bp YoY and 740bp QoQ, as higher fuel and logistics costs from the West Asia Crisis hit fixed-price overseas contracts. Adjusted EBITDA margin excluding one-offs was also 6.4% (Nomura).

outlook.note: Order inflow was strong: Rs157bn YTD (52% of the Rs300bn FY27E guidance, which was maintained), the order book is Rs433bn (3.6-3.9x book-to-bill), and the pipeline is Rs1.5trn for the balance of FY27. Management expects execution to pick up from 2HFY27 to FY28, with Croatia and Vadhvan as drivers. Against that, receivable days and net debt are rising, with delayed payments continuing. Jefferies cut FY27E EPS by 3% and the target price to Rs290 (Hold); Nomura cut FY27-29E EPS by 12-14% and the target price to Rs361 (Buy). (Jeff, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs2,042mn (+42.2% YoY) was 5.6% above Visible Alpha consensus and 1.9% above MSe. The beat was led by growth businesses, mainly Superloads and vehicle financing, which grew 152.6% YoY; core payments and telematics revenue grew 20.1% YoY. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA of Rs546mn (+15.7% YoY, +8.8% QoQ) was 4.5% below consensus of Rs572mn but 2.5% above MSe. Margin was 33.1% of net revenue (+170bps QoQ, +31bps vs MSe), though contribution margin of 92.6% was 109bps below MSe as the company stepped up Superloads investment. (MS)

outlook.note: Superloads is in 14 cities with ~50% QoQ growth, and Bangalore is above 50% of the ~5,000 loads/month threshold. Tolling was hit by macro weakness in April but recovered in May-Jun, and telematics device renewal rates are stable at ~80%. MS says results were in line with consensus, its thesis is unchanged and next-12-month consensus EPS is largely unchanged; Equal-weight, PT Rs650. (MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs24.2 bn (+33% yoy) was 15% ahead of Kotak's estimate, driven by a significant contribution from the O&G segment (Rs2.7 bn) and T&D (Rs1.1 bn). Figures are standalone, as printed in the exhibit. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.67 bn (+15.6% yoy) was about 16% ahead of Kotak's estimate, helped by a pick-up in oil & gas and transmission. Margin was 11.0%, in line with Kotak's estimate, versus 12.7% a year ago. Reported PAT missed by 7% on lower other income (lower InvIT distribution). Kotak gives no consensus figure, so the call is against its own estimate. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guidance is unchanged: FY27 order inflow of Rs200-220 bn, 15-20% revenue growth and stable margins. 1QFY27 order inflow was weak at Rs12.7 bn (-40% yoy). Road awarding delays and margin dilution from diversification remain the key risks, and Kotak keeps EBITDA margin at 11-12%. Kotak left its FY27-29 estimates and Rs900 FV unchanged and upgraded the stock to REDUCE from SELL after a 28% fall over the past year. (Kotak)

companies.name: IRB Infrastructure
companies.note: Toll roads have started dolingout lofty dividends, Rs1.33bn,up 72% YoY, driving its PAT up 51%YoY. IRB did well with its strategic equity, as it won a concession of assets worth US$1.9bn over FY23-24 and won another US$1.4bn concession under Modi 3.0. There is more to come as it aims to win from NHAI’sUS$30bn in asset monetisation plan during Modi 3.0. IRB, India’s No.1 toll platform with 10% national share, has steam left from equity released from churning assets, in our view.

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs19.3 bn was 6% below Kotak's estimate and down 10.3% yoy, as strong BOT and InvIT segment performance was offset by lower construction revenue (Rs8.1 bn vs Rs12.0 bn a year ago) on a declining order book (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs10.8 bn was 3.7% below Kotak's estimate but up 8.5% yoy. The margin of 56.2% beat the 54.6% estimate on a favourable mix, with a higher share from BOT and InvIT segments. Recurring PAT was 26% ahead of expectations on a lower tax rate (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs21.4bn was 13.7% above Kotak's estimate (Rs18.8bn) and up 1.8% YoY. Strong BOT (+13.5% YoY) and InvIT & Others (+87% YoY) revenue offset a 21% YoY fall in construction as the order book declined. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs11.5bn was 15.7% above Kotak's estimate and up 21.1% YoY. The margin was 53.9% against Kotak's 53.0% estimate, helped by a favourable mix of more BOT and InvIT contribution. Recurring PAT was 25% ahead of expectations, driven by higher InvIT distribution. (Kotak)

companies.name: Larsen & Toubro
companies.note: Our channel checks point to decadal growth opportunity for L&T in EU’s energy transition following its successful entry of an offshore wind HVDC project, which again yielded a Euro2bn order from TenneT this quarter.Its US$78bn backlog is up 28% YoY and appears solid in the current environment. L&T is emerging as a global Capex cycle play.

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated sales rose 6.7% YoY to Rs679bn, 1.4% below Jefferies' estimate, as E&C execution was weak. Bernstein also flags a revenue miss versus 10-12% guidance, citing the Middle East conflict and early-stage execution on large projects (Jeff, Bern).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA fell 3.2% YoY to Rs61.2bn, 8.3% below Jefferies' estimate, with margin at 9.0% against 9.9% a year ago and 9.7% estimated. E&C margin was stable at 7.6% (Jefferies). CLSA adds that, excluding a roughly 50bps non-cash ECL provision, the core margin was up 30bps (Jeff, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 guidance of 10-12% growth in both orders and revenue with flat core margins (7.8%), and expects 2H execution to be stronger, but this depends on the Middle East conflict easing. Order inflow rose 14% YoY, the order book is a record Rs7.8trn (+27%), and working capital fell to 4.9% of sales. Jefferies kept its FY27-30E estimates and raised its PT to Rs5,000 from Rs4,885 on a higher subsidiary valuation and a rollover, while CLSA kept Rs4,842 (Jeff, CLSA, Bern).

4Q26.revNote: Net income (NCC parent) was Rs53.2bn, down 1.1% YoY and flat on a higher base. The prolonged monsoon and tighter central-government oversight of state water capex hurt execution, which fell 1% YoY. The year-ago figure is back-calculated from the printed YoY, because the table gives no 4QFY25 column. No consensus or estimate for the quarter is printed. (CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 9.3% YoY to Rs4.5bn, with margin at 8.4% (down 76bps). Sites were loaded for ~15% top-line growth, but revenue did not arrive, so fixed costs went unabsorbed. Recurring PAT fell 11.1% YoY to Rs2.2bn. The year-ago figure is back-calculated from the printed YoY. No consensus or estimate for the quarter is printed. (CLSA)

outlook.note: NCC withdrew its FY26 guidance in 2Q and gave none for FY27, citing the Middle East crisis and its effect on government capex. CLSA cut FY27-28CL EPS by 21%/17% and its target price from Rs234 to Rs216, citing weak FY26CL, material cost pressures and slower project starts. It cut FY27/28CL revenue forecasts by 18.9%/18.0%. Offsetting this, the backlog was at a record US$8.7bn (+16% YoY), FY26 orders were Rs319bn, a further Rs17bn was won in April, and the pipeline is Rs2.5tn. (CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR 1.77bn (down 12% YoY) missed Visible Alpha consensus by 21% and GS by 20%, mainly due to spill-over of execution. Defense was 80.4% and Space 7.7% of revenue (GS, 2026/08/10).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR 331mn (down 19% YoY) missed consensus by 33% as margin fell 179bps YoY to 18.7% (GS 24.2%, consensus 22.1%), tracking the revenue decline (GS, 2026/08/10).

outlook.note: Management execution slipped in Q1, so GS cut FY27E/FY28E EPS by 0.6%/1.1% but raised FY29E/FY30E/FY31E EPS by 5%/7%/20% as key defense orders move from development to production. It expects revenue to rise 15-20% over the next two years, EBITDA margin of 27-30% over five years, and order accretion of INR 57-60bn over three years. Order book was INR 21.5bn at June-26 end, plus a INR 22bn HAL order in July. TP raised to INR 2,230 from INR 1,860, Buy maintained (GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 1.73bn, 5% below GS's INR 1,810mn estimate. Energy (incl. Oil & Gas) rose 27% YoY to INR 1.38bn and Aerospace rose 25% to INR 287mn; the other brokers' own-estimate comparisons are roughly in line (+0.7% vs Choice's estimate) (GS, Choice).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 31% YoY to INR 644mn, 1% ahead of GS's estimate. Margin expanded 138bps YoY to 37.3% on a higher gross margin, which offset a 42% YoY rise in employee cost from headcount additions (GS).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 27.3% YoY and 1.8% QoQ to INR 1,615 mn, 5.7% below Choice's estimate of INR 1,714 mn; growth was driven by strong execution, with the Energy segment growing 34.2% YoY (ICICI) (Choice, ICICI).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 34.5% YoY to INR 613 mn but fell 1.4% QoQ, 6.3% below Choice's estimate of INR 654 mn. Margin of 38.0% was up 204 bps YoY and down 124 bps QoQ, against an estimated 38.2%, helped by favourable mix and operating leverage (Choice, ICICI).

outlook.note: Management reiterated 25%+ long-term revenue growth and a 32-35% EBITDA margin guidance. The FY26 expansion is ~80% stabilised, with full closure by Q3FY27 and the ramp-up expected from H2FY27. GS expects earnings growth to accelerate from Q3FY27. It left EBITDA estimates broadly unchanged (+0.6% FY27E) and cut PAT 3.6% for FY27E on higher depreciation and interest. GS raised its TP to INR 3,315 and ICICI upgraded to BUY. Choice raised its TP to INR 2,150 but downgraded to SELL on valuation (GS, ICICI, Choice).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR 5.7bn (+131% YoY, +19% QoQ) was 41% above Visible Alpha consensus and 15% above GS. Channel checks show growth came from Akash Weapon System (AWS) revenue spilling over from 4Q26 after supply-chain delays, with AWS and ATGM contributing about equally and exports negligible (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR 831mn (+50% QoQ, against a year-ago loss of INR 454mn) was 62% above consensus and 52% above GS. EBITDA margin was 14.5% versus consensus 12.6% and GS 11.1%, helped by a favourable product mix (GS).

outlook.note: Management's supply-chain issues look largely resolved, so GS sees no risk to its FY27E revenue of INR 56.1bn. GS flags downside risk to its FY27E EBITDA margin of 16% as lower-margin platforms such as Astra come into execution, and does not expect much support from higher-margin exports. The FY27E order book is about INR 266bn (9.6x book/bill, ttm), likely to taper as execution picks up. GS keeps Sell with an unchanged TP of INR 1,150 (GS).

companies.name: Bharat Electronics
companies.note: Order inflow was Rs37.5bn & Order book: Rs723bn (-3% YoY, -2% QoQ). The governmenthas accelerated Make in India (MII) defence orders, driving BELto guide for inflow up 83%in FY27

4Q26.revNote: Revenue from operations of Rs102.2bn was up 12% YoY and 43% QoQ, exactly in line with JPM's estimate (0% variance), on order execution such as LRSAM; FY26 revenue rose 16% (JP, CLSA).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs29.8bn was up 6% YoY and about 1% below JPM's estimate, with margin at 29.2% (-16bps YoY) against 29.5% expected. Full-year margin of 29.2% beat the 27% guidance on a roughly 220bp better gross margin from indigenisation and mix (JP, CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 25% YoY to Rs55.3bn, about 9% above Bloomberg consensus (11% above Nomura's estimate) and 8% above Jefferies' estimate. BEL mined a flat Rs723bn order book, led by LRSAM and Akash missile execution. (Nomura, Jeff, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs13.9bn (+12% YoY) was about 2% below consensus, which is in line, and 3% above Nomura's estimate. The margin fell 297bp YoY to 25.1% against 28% guidance because gross margin dropped 775bp to 45.5% on product mix, not cost escalation. Lower other expenses partly offset this. (Nomura, Jeff, CLSA)

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 guidance of Rs550bn+ order inflow (QRSAM about Rs300bn, awaiting CCS approval), 15%+ revenue growth and 28%+ EBITDA margin. Brokers left estimates broadly unchanged: Nomura kept estimates and its Rs454 TP, CLSA kept its Rs522 TP, and Jefferies cut FY28-29E EPS by 2-3% and its TP to Rs550 from Rs585. 1Q order inflow fell 17% YoY, and QRSAM has slipped to about 2QFY27. (Nomura, Jeff, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs9.1 bn fell 7% YoY but came in 7% ahead of Kotak's estimate. Shipbuilding grew 48% YoY, partly offset by a 38% YoY decline in ship repair after the one-off INS Vikrant and Vikramaditya repair orders. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.58 bn was 9% above Kotak's estimate but down 32.5% YoY. Margin of 17.3% was in line with the 17.1% estimate versus 23.9% a year ago, as shipbuilding margins were weak and ship-repair margins were still above the normalized 18-22% range. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 12-15%, in line with Kotak's expectation, but a blended EBITDA margin of about 14%, 250-300 bps below Kotak's estimate. Shipbuilding margins are guided at 10-12%, ship repair at 22-24%, and operating cash flow should improve. A Rs65 bn capex plan through FY2030 and a 50:50 ship-repair JV with Drydocks World were announced. Kotak retained its estimates and FV of Rs860 (Kotak)

companies.name: Data Patterns
companies.note: Management remains confident of achieving 20-25% revenue growth and 35-40% margins in FY27E. Drone/Counter-drone business is gaining traction, and management expects this business to be an important growth driver ahead. Rs9 bn order book (1x FY26 revenues) is up 14% YoY, order flow visibility remains high:

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 1.16bn but came in 31% below Visible Alpha consensus (INR 1,688mn) and 7% below GS's estimate. Customer approvals were delayed temporarily, and Q1 is seasonally weak (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 2% YoY to INR 314mn, 46% below consensus (INR 585mn) and 18% below GS's estimate. Margin was 27% against 32% a year ago, hurt by adverse product mix, employee costs up 17% YoY, higher repair and maintenance costs and a INR 20mn provision for long-pending receivables (GS). Jefferies put EBITDA 9% below its own estimate (GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 35-40% EBITDA margins. It expects about INR 20bn of additional order inflow in FY27, on top of the INR 17bn of negotiated orders. The order book is INR 9.3bn, with a pipeline of INR 20-40bn. The Q1 execution and margin miss is the near-term risk. GS kept its Buy and INR 4,165 TP. Jefferies kept FY27-28E earnings unchanged, raised its PT to INR 5,545 from INR 4,875 on a roll-forward, and sits 3% (FY27 revenue) and 3% (FY27 EPS) below consensus (GS, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs55.1bn was up 14% YoY and about 4% above Bloomberg consensus. Product revenue rose 76% YoY on higher deliveries of ALH (3 vs nil), AL-31FP engines (3 vs 1) and RD-33 engines (6 vs 5), partly offset by a delay in Mk1A aircraft (CLSA, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs15.3bn was up 17% YoY and about 10% above Nomura and consensus estimates. The margin expanded 68bp YoY to 27.7%, helped by operating leverage on lower other expenses, and was well above Kotak's 24.3% estimate despite gross margin contracting 280bp per Nomura (CLSA, Nomura, Kotak).

outlook.note: Backlog is up 32% YoY to Rs2.55tn (about 25x book-to-bill in manufacturing) and gives long execution visibility. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% and an EBITDA margin of about 30-31%. Tejas Mk1A deliveries should start in 2H, with engine supply ramping to two a month, and the GE engine deal and Mk1A resolution at the IAF review in September are the key catalysts. Estimates were largely unchanged at Nomura and raised 2-3% for FY28-29 at Kotak. Target prices went up: CLSA to Rs5,481 (from Rs5,265), Nomura to Rs6,314 (from Rs6,040) and Kotak to Rs5,305 (from Rs4,810) (CLSA, Nomura, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs29.4bn rose 12% YoY and was 2% above Kotak's estimate (3% above JPMorgan's), driven by execution of the P17A frigates, P15B destroyers and the ONGC order; it fell 24% QoQ from a seasonally high 4Q (Kotak, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.47bn (+48% YoY) was 8% above Kotak's estimate and 11% above JPMorgan's. Margin of 15.2% compared with 11.5% a year ago and Kotak's 14.3% estimate, helped by lower other expenses (lower provisions). Higher interest costs held PAT (Rs5.5bn) only 5% above Kotak's estimate (Kotak, JP).

outlook.note: Order book fell to Rs180-182bn (-11% QoQ, -39% YoY, ~1.5x book-to-bill), the lowest in six years. Both brokers see the P75I submarine award (Rs70-900bn) as the key catalyst, with most execution only starting in 2HFY28/FY29. The pipeline is Rs2.5tn, about 10x the current order book. Kotak retained estimates and Fair Value of Rs1,950 (SELL); JPMorgan stays Underweight with a Rs2,394 target and says margins may not be sustainable and a further award delay is a risk to FY28/29 revenue (Kotak, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 97% YoY to INR 1.92bn, 2% below GS's estimate of INR 1.95bn. Growth came from the ramp-up of operations at Aerolloys and faster execution of Titanium/Superalloys castings contracts (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 457% YoY to INR 489mn, about 4% ahead of GS's estimate, with margin at 25.5% (about 150bps above GS). Trac operations continued to improve and higher-margin Aerolloys contracts picked up; subsidiary EBITDA margin rose 200bps QoQ to about 51% (GS).

outlook.note: GS expects higher-margin Titanium and Superalloys castings contracts to expand margins further. New Airbus, BrahMos and MoD contracts move PTCIL up the value chain, and Trac operations have stabilised. Annual estimates are unchanged (only the quarterly EPS phasing changed) and TP is unchanged at INR 25,770; catalysts are EBCHR mill commissioning and Safran approval of Titanium ingots (GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 70% yoy and came in 9.3% above Kotak's estimate, led by defense (+123% yoy, Pinaka and exports of defense explosives and ammunition), international explosives (+65%) and domestic explosives (+52%), the latter two helped by elevated ammonium nitrate prices (Kotak; MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 90% yoy and was 15.5% above Kotak's estimate. Margin of 27.7% was about 150 bps ahead, driven by operating leverage and a higher defense mix. MS says the EBITDA beat to its own estimate was 30%, and that earnings beat the Street by 33% (Kotak; MS).

Kotak raised FY27-29 EPS by 2-6% and its FV to Rs11,200 (from Rs10,300), while keeping SELL on valuation. On the proposed Omnia acquisition, management guides to combined EBITDA of Rs68-70 bn and PAT of Rs34-35 bn by FY28E, with net debt/EBITDA below 2x. GS expects it to be EPS accretive (Kotak, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs21.1bn (+13% YoY) was 1% above consensus, led by India multi-channel revenue growth of 17.7% (vs 8-11% in the prior quarters) and 12% growth in International. GlobalBees fell 1% on a planned brand transition and a Flipkart settlement. (MS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs597mn was 26% below consensus (Rs809mn) and 20% below MS. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4% YoY, with a 4.2% margin. India margin was 5.7% (-289bps YoY) on diaper competition, higher manufacturing costs and a 260bps gross margin decline. (MS, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 12.0% yoy, in line with Kotak's estimate (+0.1%). India multi-channel grew 11.4% (GMV +11.8%, orders +10.1%, AOV +1.5%), international 9.5% and GlobalBees 15%. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs701 mn was 6.3% below Kotak's estimate, and adjusted EBITDA (ex-ESOP) of Rs1,187 mn was 11% below. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management expects India growth to stay elevated in F27, helped by offline expansion (+100 stores), RocketBees and Qwik. It expects manufacturing margin losses to fully recover by 2Q via price pass-through. Even so, Kotak trimmed India revenue and margin estimates again and cut its fair value to Rs250 from Rs350, on slower India margin scale-up and slower GlobalBees growth. MS says margin improvement is still awaited. (Kotak, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of INR2,012mn (+16% y-y) came in 3.6% below consensus (INR2,086mn) and 1.5% below Nomura, as the standalone Consumer business grew a slower ~18% y-y to INR781mn versus Nomura's INR818mn, partly offset by OLX revenue up ~29% y-y (Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA of INR689mn (+46% y-y) was 6.7% above consensus (INR646mn), with margin 34.3% vs 31.0% consensus, aided by higher revenue, marketing spend down 9% y-y and other expenses up only 2.6%. OLX margin of 33.6% (Nomura: 29.6%) was the key surprise (Nomura).

outlook.note: Management expects MAUs to keep growing (~80mn in 1Q, 95% organic) and is rolling out the Spinny partnership, Elite programs, financing and escrow/logistics in OLX; costs are expected not to rise much further after tech/AI spend in 1Q. Nomura's estimates are largely unchanged (FY27F revenue INR9,263mn vs 9,454mn old), but TP rises slightly to INR3,340 from INR3,286 (Nomura).

Adjusted for the inventory-led shift, consolidated revenue grew 66% YoY (CLSA).

Quick Commerce adjusted EBITDA margin was 0.6% of NOV (+34bp QoQ), and Food delivery adjusted EBITDA grew 34% YoY. Higher losses in the Others segment (Bistro, Nugget) left consolidated adjusted EBITDA 4% below MS's estimate (MS) and 9% below GS's (GS); GS and MS both call the quarter in line (CLSA, MS, GS).

CLSA made 0-1% estimate tweaks and lifted its target price to Rs506 from Rs505. GS cut its FY27 Zomato adjusted EBITDA estimate by 6% but raised FY28/29 estimates on higher NOV, and moved its target price to Rs345 from Rs350 (CLSA, GS).

1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 68% YoY to Rs2.36bn, 3% above consensus and 4% above MS estimates. Margin was 8.5%, up 196bp YoY, helped by gross margin up 123bp and lower marketing spend as a share of sales. Fashion EBITDA turned positive for a second quarter. (MS, GS)

4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.2bn was 7.5% above consensus (CLSA says 8%). Margin was a record 8.4%, up 195bps YoY and 47bps above consensus, driven by rising own-brand salience in Beauty. Fashion EBITDA broke even for the first time on marketing efficiency (CLSA, JP, Kotak).

MS sees strong delivery and margin broadly in line, with growth accelerating across businesses on a better consumption environment. (GS, MS)

Jefferies also calls revenue in line, and slightly below its own estimate. (Kotak, Jeff)

EBITDA up 2% (JP, MS).

EBITDA breakeven has been pushed out, and JP sees it around FY30. CLSA downgraded to Hold and cut its FY29 EBITDA estimate by 12% (TP Rs357 to Rs318). MS flagged a modest consensus shortfall and lower forward EPS revisions, though July quick commerce NOV growth showed early green shoots. (CLSA, JP, MS)

1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs54.7m (-34.9% YoY) missed CLSA's Rs76.2m by 28%. The margin fell to 10.6% against an estimated 14.6%. Employee costs rose 41.6% YoY to 40.1% of revenue as the company invested in AI-led product development, talent and sales and marketing (CLSA).

outlook.note: Management expects standalone and Shipway growth of 15%+ and 20%+ YoY respectively from 4Q27 onwards. It also expects Shipway to break even from 3QFY27, with operating leverage benefits in 2HFY27. Investments will keep margins subdued through 1HFY27. CLSA cut FY27/28 EPS by up to 2% (FY27 net profit forecast -11.9%) and kept its Rs128 TP and O-PF rating (CLSA).

2Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue rose 41.4% YoY to Rs5.37bn, 3.5% above consensus and 2% above MS's estimate. India consumer services ex-InstaHelp grew 26.6% YoY, native products grew 40% and international operations grew 82%. (MS)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs1.44bn was about 25% worse than consensus (Rs1.15bn loss) and 2.8% better than MS's estimate. The shortfall is driven by InstaHelp, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs1.74bn against MS's Rs1.7bn estimate, while the core India business earned Rs340mn. GS also flags the higher consolidated loss as driven by InstaHelp. (MS, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs5.3bn (+43.9% YoY, +24.1% QoQ) was about 3% above consensus (Rs5.1bn) and 6.8% above MS's estimate. Growth was broad-based: India consumer services ex-Instahelp NTV grew 29% YoY (6% above MS), Native revenue rose 60% and International was in line (MS, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs650mn was narrower than consensus (loss of Rs765mn) and MS's Rs734mn loss, with the beat led by a ~20% beat in adjusted EBITDA of India consumer services ex-Instahelp (margin 6.9% of NTV). Instahelp losses stayed elevated at ~Rs1.3bn, and GS notes the loss was larger than its own Rs400mn estimate (MS, GS).

outlook.note: Management maintained its consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven guidance of F3Q28, with Rs10bn by F2031. Native is expected to grow NTV 50-55% YoY in 2Q+3Q, and the company is proposing to raise up to Rs25bn of capital. Instahelp losses remain high amid competition, and MS flags a modest downward revision to next-12-month consensus EPS, keeping Overweight with a Rs165 PT. (MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs10.5bn grew 24% YoY, 4% ahead of JPMe and 1% below consensus. Online grew 38% and offline 19%; the delayed NEET exam shifted some collections into 2Q. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA (post-IndAS) was Rs265mn against Rs71mn JPMe and a Rs286mn loss a year ago. Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin was -4.2%, 320bps above JPMe, with online margin at 12% (vs 6%) and offline loss narrowing to -22% (vs -27%). (JP)
1Q27.vsBasis: revenue vs consensus (Bloomberg); EBITDA vs broker estimate (JPM), as no consensus is prin

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs9.19bn was 6% ahead of consensus (Rs8.63bn) and 1% ahead of JPMe. Growth was 51% YoY, driven by offline at +54% YoY, with online at +44% YoY. Revenue fell 15% QoQ from Rs10.82bn. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA of Rs718mn was well above JPMe's loss of Rs553mn. No consensus figure is printed for this line. Pre-IndAS Adj. EBITDA margin was 1.1% against JPMe's 0.6% and -23% a year ago. (JP)
4Q26.vsBasis: consensus (revenue); broker estimate (JPMorgan) for EBITDA, no consensus printed

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 revenue growth guide of 30%+ and offline EBITDA breakeven, and says NEET revenue was shifted rather than lost (July collections +50% YoY). JP upgraded to OW and kept its Rs148 PT. GS (Neutral, Rs133 PT) cut FY27-29E revenue by up to 2% and raised adjusted EBITDA by up to 4% on higher online mix. PW is exiting lending (FinZ) and is expected to transfer the loan book to an RBI-registered partner. (JP, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs38.9bn (+13% YoY) came in about 9% below consensus (Rs42.8bn) and 11% below JPMorgan's estimate, as Consumer Durables grew only 8% YoY on a high year-ago base. Electronics grew 29% YoY to Rs9.85bn. (CLSA, JP, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.27bn (+28% YoY) is stated before Rs154mn of high-cost inventory booked for acquisitions. On JPMorgan's like-for-like Rs3.12bn it was about 2% below consensus, but margin was 8.0%, roughly 60bps above consensus and 100bps above Kotak's estimate. Consumer Durables margin rose to 7.8% (+30bps YoY per CLSA) and Electronics margin to 9.5% (+312bps YoY per CLSA) from 6.4%; Railways margin fell about 670bps. (CLSA, JP, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs41.5 bn (+10.5% yoy) was 0.8% above Kotak's estimate. Consumer durables grew 7% yoy to Rs29.8 bn, and electronics grew 21% yoy to Rs10.2 bn on PCBA scale-up and the Unitronics, Power One and Shogini acquisitions. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.58 bn (+22% yoy) was 4.3% above Kotak's estimate, with margin at 8.6% in the table, about 20 bps above estimate. Electronics margin expanded to 10.8% from 5.9% a year ago, while consumer durable margin fell to 7.5% from 8.4%. Kotak's text calls operating performance in line. Higher D&A and interest left PBT 17% below estimate. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guides FY27 Consumer Durables growth in line with the RAC industry at 13-15%, Electronics growth of 40%+ and Railways growth of 30-35%. Consumer Durables margins are now guided to stay at current levels, replacing the earlier 50-100bps decline guidance. Kotak notes the Q1 margin strength came from temporary tailwinds (pre-stocking of compressors and copper, premium mix). PCB margins are expected to recover from about 12% to 15-16% from 3QFY27. Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 4.5-5% and trimmed fair value to Rs8,600 from Rs8,710. JPMorgan stays Neutral. (Kotak, JP, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs4.84bn (+50% yoy) was well ahead of consensus (13% above per JP, 9% above per Nomura) and 12.7% above Kotak's own estimate. Growth was led by Clean Energy (+141% yoy), Industrial (+50%) and Mobility (+44%), with India up 54% and US up 47% (Kotak, JP, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs580mn (+94% yoy) came in with a 12% margin, up 270bps yoy and 160bps ahead of consensus (JP). Nomura puts the consensus margin at 10.9%. Employee costs were much lower than Kotak expected (17.2% of sales vs 19.8%), which more than offset a weaker gross margin (34.7% vs 38%). Operating leverage also helped, and US operations reached EBITDA breakeven ahead of the guided 2HFY27 timeline (Kotak, JP, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 26-30% from 24-27%. JP expects a further upgrade to 30-35%. The order book is Rs22.08bn (+23% yoy), although order inflow fell 25% qoq. Semiconductor equipment and HVDC/data-centre programmes are ramping. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS 5-7%, JP raised revenue 4-11% and EPS 14-26% over FY27-29E, and Nomura raised revenue and EBITDA margin estimates, lifting EPS 4%/5%/11% over FY27-29E (Kotak, JP, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3.7bn grew 34% YoY and came in 3.5% above consensus (Rs3,612mn). Growth was driven by Aerospace (+41% YoY), Defence (+34%) and Industrial (+87% YoY), while MedTech declined 2% YoY. (JP, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs392mn was 6.5% above consensus (Rs368mn) and up 56% YoY. Margin expanded to 10.5% (vs 9.0% a year ago) on better product mix and cost control, 30bps above consensus. (JP, Kotak)

2Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 27% YoY to Rs3.93bn, driven by Aerospace and Industrial while Defence and Medtech were soft. It was 1% below consensus (3% below JPMorgan's estimate) and in line with Kotak's estimate (Kotak, JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA margin fell to 8.7% (130bps YoY, 180bps QoQ), against Kotak's 9.8%. JPMorgan puts it 160bps below consensus. Higher sales, marketing and product development spend and a weaker mix (more product development orders) drove the miss. Management cut the FY27 margin guide to 9-10% (Kotak, JP).

outlook.note: Management maintains FY27 growth guidance of about 30% and expects to grow 30% in FY28, backed by a record order book of Rs28.1bn (+23% YoY). It cut FY27 margin guidance to 9-10% from earlier double digits, and expects double-digit margins only from 1QFY28 as the investments continue until 4Q. JPMorgan cut FY27-29E EBITDA margins by 50-130bps, which lowers EPS by 4-5%. FY27E EPS goes to Rs11.99 from Rs12.50. (JP)

companies.name: Dixon Technologies
companies.note: Dixon has a strong order book and expects 20-25% q-q growth in 2Q; the annual volume target remains unchanged

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 21% YoY and 48% QoQ, about 8% above consensus (Rs143.4bn), driven by higher smartphone ASPs. Mobile & EMS rose 22%, Home Appliances 22% and Consumer Electronics 47% (refrigerator upstocking after the BEE price increase). (JP, Jeff, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 4% YoY to Rs4.63bn, about 4% below consensus (Rs4.81bn). Margin dropped 78bps YoY to 3.0% as PLI benefits ended and higher memory/input costs were passed through on a fixed Rs-per-unit EBITDA, which diluted the percentage margin. Mobile & EMS margin fell to 2.6% from 3.4%. Reported PAT was lifted by Rs5.3bn of other income (an MTM gain on the Aditya Infotech stake). (JP, Jeff, GS)

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 mobile volume guidance at 32mn ex-Vivo, guided 2Q QoQ growth of 20-25%, and expects Vivo JV production to start in 3Q. It does not expect margins to improve in FY27 (memory prices not falling), with recovery in FY28 as components (display/camera modules) ramp. Estimates are mixed: JP raised FY27E revenue 13% but cut EBITDA 5% and adj. EPS 6-7%. GS cut FY27E EBITDA 5% but raised FY28/29E EBITDA 7%/9%. Jeff raised FY27E EPS 5% on other income. (JP, GS, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs9.46bn (+40% YoY) was 9.6% above consensus and 12.4% above JPMe. Growth was led by Railways (+81%), IoT/IT (+69%), Automotive (+35%) and Industrial (+31%). Core EMS grew 66% YoY, helped by the ramp-up of a delayed government order. Smart meter revenue fell 9% as Kaynes deliberately held back growth there (JP, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.48bn (+31% YoY) was 13.0% above consensus. The margin of 15.6% was 120bps lower YoY but about 50bps ahead of consensus and flat QoQ. PAT missed consensus by 15% on higher depreciation, interest and tax rate, and lower other income (JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management guides to positive operating cash flow by end-FY27 and a smart-meter receivables turnaround by end-FY27. OSAT and PCB operations are now expected to start from 3QFY27, with FY27 revenue of Rs4.5-5bn. Net working capital days rose to 163 from 125 in 4Q. Estimate changes are mixed: JP raises revenue 4% but cuts EPS 8-9% on a higher tax rate, Jeff raises FY28-29e EPS 2-3%, and CLSA moves PAT between -9% and +10%. JP Neutral with PT cut to Rs3,600 from Rs3,700; CLSA Hold with PT raised to Rs3,580 from Rs3,240 (JP, CLSA, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 68% YoY to Rs15.9bn, 17% above consensus and 12% above JPM, with growth across all verticals except Industrial: IT & Railways +199%, Healthcare +100%, Auto +78%, Consumer +68%. CLSA also called it a topline-driven beat on faster ramp-up and front-loaded consumer schedules (JP, CLSA, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.62bn was 21% above consensus. The margin of 10.2% was up 100bps YoY and 30bps above consensus, although down 172bps QoQ from 11.9%. Kotak noted a slight miss against its own 10.4% estimate, on lower gross margin (24.5% vs 25%) from an unfavourable mix (JP, Kotak, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and says it will exceed that guidance, with EBITDA of Rs7bn+ (10.5-11% margin, vs 11.3% in FY26). The order book is Rs67.7bn, and the Rs8bn multi-layer PCB facility is on track for trial production in 4QFY27. Working capital rose to 71 days from 63, and the Board approved a Rs10bn QIP. CLSA raised FY27-29 PAT by 16-19% and its TP to Rs1,290 (Hold); Kotak raised EPS by 6-16% and its FV to Rs1,300 (Reduce); JPM expects consensus to be raised (CLSA, Kotak, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 88% YoY but fell 21% QoQ to Rs7.02bn. Options transaction charges were 2.1x YoY, and the bullion segment was up 3.6x YoY but down 27% QoQ on lower volatility. Revenue was 2% below Jefferies' estimate. No consensus revenue figure is printed. (Jeff, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 104% YoY to Rs5.26bn, with margin at 75.0% (+572bp YoY, -453bp QoQ). JP puts it 5% below consensus. Opex grew 53% YoY, led by statutory fund contributions (+119% YoY) and employee costs (+28%). Core EBITDA was 2% below MSE's estimate. Other income of Rs496mn and a 21% tax rate lifted PAT to Rs4.13bn, in line with Jefferies and 8% above consensus per JP. (Jeff, JP, MS)
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA: consensus (JP, 5% below); revenue: broker estimate (Jefferies, -2% vs JEFe)

outlook.note: Volumes stayed soft in July: futures ADTV was down 9.9% MoM and options ADPTV down 6.5% MoM. QTD ADTR is 13% below MSE's F27 estimate (Rs109.2mn) and 9% below VA consensus. JP expects downward revisions to consensus core operating earnings. MS remains OW and Jefferies Buy (PT Rs3,600), citing volatility upside. JP stays UW (PT Rs2,560). (MS, JP, Jeff)

companies.name: Devyani International
companies.note: FY27 store guidance remain unchanged (200-225 NNUs, KFC 100-120).

India business EBITDA fell 3.2% on adverse operating leverage. (Kotak)

1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 24% y/y to Rs2.55 bn with margin up 100 bps y/y to 16.1%, helped by gross margin up 90 bps to 69.1%. On a pre-Ind AS 116 basis, Kotak has EBITDA +38% y/y, 4.2% above its estimate, and GS calls it 'well ahead' of its estimates. On the reported (Ind AS) EBITDA, JP says the number was in line with JPMe and Kotak puts it only 0.9% above its estimate. The beat is therefore driven by margins and is clearest pre-Ind AS 116 (JP, Kotak, GS).
1Q27.vsBasis: revenue: Street (JP); EBITDA: broker estimate (Kotak, GS)

outlook.note: JP expects upward earnings revisions on the margin beat. Kotak raises FY27-29E pre-Ind AS EBITDA by 2-3% and sees potential for 25%+ pre-Ind AS EBITDA growth in FY27E on a soft base. The Sapphire merger is expected to complete by end-FY27 (Kotak, GS, JP).

The consolidated consensus looks thin and not comparable with the standalone one (MS, Jeff).

Consolidated margin beat MS's estimate by 79bp on better international margins, while the standalone margin was 53bp below MSe (MS, Jeff).
