Standalone revenue grew 6.4% YoY, a 2.4% miss vs Kotak's estimate, as Domino's India LFL growth slowed to flat on a high base, lower AOV after the delivery threshold was cut to Rs99, and weak dine-in. (Jeff, Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA grew 25% YoY. Standalone EBITDA of Rs3,444 mn was ~2% above Kotak's estimate, and Jefferies called it ahead of its own estimate. Gross margin expanded ~100 bps YoY to 75.5%, but energy and wage inflation held the standalone EBITDA margin flat YoY at 20.5%. Kotak's pre-Ind AS margin of 12.1% was 20 bps below its estimate. (Jeff, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: BK India revenue grew 23.6% yoy to Rs6.8 bn, 6.6% above Kotak's estimate of Rs6.4 bn. SSSG of 12.6% (Kotak est. 7%) was the highest in 15 quarters and was entirely traffic-led. ADS rose 9% yoy to Rs131k, with 71 net store additions yoy to 590 stores. The figures are the BK India standalone table; Indonesia revenue (Rs1.4 bn, -4% yoy) is not included (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA grew 134% yoy to Rs527 mn, 26.6% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 7.7% (+365 bps yoy, versus Kotak est. 6.5%). Gross margin expanded 315 bps yoy to 70.8% on supply-chain cluster benefits, menu mix and utility savings, with no pricing contribution. Reported (Ind AS) EBITDA was Rs975 mn, +43% yoy (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: BK India revenue grew 17.1% YoY to Rs5.7bn, in line with consensus per CLSA (Kotak: ~2.8% above its estimate). SSSG was 6.3% against 4.5% in 3Q, and ADS was up about 3% YoY at Rs111k (CLSA, Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA of Rs409mn was up 54% YoY, with margin up 170bps YoY to 7.1%. CLSA puts it ~9% above consensus (5% above its own estimate) and Kotak puts it 34% above its estimate, on gross margin up 240bps YoY to 70.2% (menu mix, supply-chain efficiencies) and operating leverage (Kotak, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management says growth momentum carried into 2Q ("very good start"). It targets a 72% GM over 2-3 years, about 80 new stores a year toward ~800 by FY29E, and a 7.5-8% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin in FY2027E. Kotak raised FY27-29E pre-Ind AS EBITDA by 5-14% after the results and by a further 6-8% after the management meeting. It lifted fair value from Rs70 to Rs81 and then Rs100 (23X Sep-2028E EV/EBITDA), and upgraded the rating to ADD. Indonesia remains weak (ADS bottomed, Popeyes under review), but Inspira's Rs10.5 bn infusion funds India growth (Kotak).

companies.name: Sapphire Foods India
companies.note: KFC, PH

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 14.7% yoy to Rs8.9 bn, 1.1% above Kotak's estimate, led by a 10.3% yoy rise in store count to 1,074. KFC revenue grew 17.2% on 5% SSSG, Sri Lanka grew 16% and Pizza Hut 3% (Kotak, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA rose 23.9% yoy, 4.6% above Kotak's estimate. Pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA grew 37% to Rs749 mn, about 7% ahead, with margin up 135 bps yoy to 8.4%. Gross margin rose 140 bps yoy to 68.8% on price hikes and lower discounts, partly offset by higher energy costs and weak Pizza Hut and Sri Lanka margins (Kotak, GS).

outlook.note: Management maintained KFC guidance of 60-80 new stores a year and sees 15-20% system growth at 5-6% SSSG. Price hikes of about 2% have had no visible impact on demand. Pizza Hut profitability and Sri Lanka margins (wage and energy inflation) remain drags, and Sri Lanka margins need at least two quarters to normalise. Kotak raised FY27-29E pre-Ind AS EBITDA by 1-2% and expects about 20% FY27E growth (Buy, FV Rs275). GS raised FY27E/28E sales by about 1% and cut FY27E pre-Ind AS EBITDA by 2% (Kotak, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Net operating revenues of Rs4.5 bn (+20.6% yoy) came in 5.8% above Kotak's estimate (KIE: +14%). Consolidated net contract gains were 20.2% and LFL growth 4.2%. Growth was driven by new units at Delhi T1/T2, Cochin T1 and Noida, even though traffic was muted by the Middle East conflict. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.62 bn (+11.0% yoy) was 10.4% above Kotak's estimate. The margin of 35.8% was 150 bps better than the estimate but fell 310 bps yoy, on higher staff and other costs from new-store mobilisation at Noida and Cochin. Gross margin rose 240 bps yoy to 85.7%, partly due to a reclassification of lounge aggregation costs. (Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Net operating revenue grew 25.7% yoy to Rs4.6 bn, 9.2% above Kotak's estimate. System sales rose 27.7% on 6.1% LFL growth and 17.3% net contract gains, helped by pricing and new outlets across Cochin, Delhi T-1/T-2 and Navi Mumbai (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 38.3% yoy to Rs1.9 bn, 20.5% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded 370 bps yoy to 40.4%, driven by operating leverage, lower manpower costs and a one-off reclassification of Rs78 mn of cost of services into other expenses (Kotak).

outlook.note: Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 2-5% and revised fair value to Rs1,365 on 33x Sep-28E PE. It expects growth to hold in FY27E, with 50+ outlets under development and passenger traffic recovering in 2H as international routes restart from Sep-Oct. Pre-opening costs should normalise over 12-18 months. The Delhi T-3 contract expires end-2Q and Chennai/Kolkata renewals are an overhang on FY28E PAT, so Kotak downgraded the rating to REDUCE from ADD on valuation after the run-up. (Kotak)

companies.name: Westlife Foodworld
companies.note: WLDL expects mid-single digits SSSG for the rest of FY27.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 11.9% yoy to Rs7.35bn, 2.3% above Kotak's estimate, as SSSG accelerated to 4.3% (Kotak est. 3%) on double-digit guest count growth from the Rs99 everyday value platform; on-premise and off-premise both grew about 12% (Kotak, JP). GS also flagged sales growth of 11.9% vs its 9.3% estimate (GS).

Margin fell about 50bps yoy to 12.6% because of input and energy inflation (food, paper, gas, labour, A&P, diesel). Gross margin held at about 67.5%, cost governance cushioned the hit, and G&A fell 7% yoy (Kotak). GS noted restaurant operating profit grew only about 2% yoy, while EBITDA growth was lifted by lower corporate overheads (GS).

outlook.note: Management expects mid-single-digit SSSG to continue (May and June were MSD and the momentum carried into July) and targets 100-150bps yoy EBITDA margin expansion for FY27. It sees 1Q as the peak pressure on gross margin, held at 67% or better. It also reiterated 60+ store additions in FY27 (580-630 stores by CY27) and has taken no price hike yet, with about 3% annual pricing guided. Brokers nudged estimates up only slightly: Kotak raised FY27-29E EBITDA 0-1% (Reduce, FV Rs490), GS raised FY27/28 EBITDA 1-2% (Neutral, PT Rs500), and JP stays Overweight (PT Rs570). GS sees the margin target as ambitious for FY27 (Kotak, GS, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 63% y-y to Rs15.7bn, about 1% above JEFe, led by transaction charges (+80% y-y) on index options market share gains, while listing services revenue fell 4% y-y on weak book building (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 71% y-y to Rs10.7bn, 2% above JEFe, with margin up c.315bps y-y to 68.5% as opex (ex. SGF) grew 49% y-y, slower than revenue; Jefferies calls the quarter in line (Jeff).

outlook.note: Volumes have weakened since the results. Jefferies (17 Aug) downgraded to Underperform and cut FY27-29e EPS 5-12% and its PT 16% to Rs2,940. It cites headwinds to prop-trader activity from the STT hike, RBI bank-guarantee norms and the Closing Auction Session (CAS), and August options ADTO down 12% vs July. JPMorgan (14 Sep) upgraded to Overweight on the view that the CAS overhang will ease after SEBI's proposal to change the expiry-day settlement price. It still trimmed FY27-29E ADPTV 9.8%/11.8%/14.1% and EPS 4.7%/5.5% (FY27E/FY28E), and cut its PT to Rs3,950. Estimates are being cut by both houses, so the call is negative with a recovery possible (Jeff, JP).

companies.name: Central Depository Services (India)
companies.note: Risks from competition, lack of pricing power and cyclicality.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs2,930mn (+13% y-y) was 4% above JEFe's Rs2,813mn, led by the KRA segment and IPO/CA charges; annual issuer charge growth slowed to 12% y-y vs a 36% 3-year CAGR (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs1,379mn (+6% y-y) was 1% below JEFe's Rs1,396mn, in line. Opex grew 10% above JEFe, so margin fell 330bps y-y to 47.1% vs JEFe's 49.7% (Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies cut FY27-29e EPS by 3-4% on higher opex and slower transaction growth (6% y-y). It sees EBITDA margin expansion limited to 100-150bps over the next two years, and flags competition risk as NSDL gains with fintechs and large discount brokers. The PT rises to Rs1,275 only on roll-forward, and the rating stays Hold (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew just 1% YoY (flat QoQ) as cash-supply disruption during the five state elections hit Services revenue (+9% YoY), which missed estimates; mgt put the hit at Rs250mn (~4% of revenues). The Product segment pulled back, and Tech & Payments rose to 18% of mix from 16% in FY26. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 7% YoY to Rs1,688mn, with margin up 144bps YoY to 26.6% on efficiency initiatives, which surprised positively. Jefferies still called it an operating profit miss because of the revenue shortfall; core profit was a tad below its estimate. PAT fell 11% YoY to Rs837mn on higher depreciation, cushioned by lower tax. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Mgt says cash supply has recovered to 70-80% of normal volumes, with normalisation expected by Sep-26. It cut FY27 services revenue guidance by ~2% but raised its FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 27% from 25-26%, and guides 35-40% growth for Tech & Payments. Margins depend on passing on cost inflation through price hikes to banks, which is still under discussion. Jefferies cut FY27-29E earnings by 6-8% and its PT to Rs315 from Rs380, and kept Buy. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs18.9bn was 7% above Kotak's estimate and up 40% YoY. Premium grew 41%, with digital and POSP growth at similar rates, and the take rate was stable at about 21%. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.4bn was 25% above Kotak's estimate, with margin up 325bps YoY to 9.9%. Contribution margin improved and non-core expenses grew only 9%. Jefferies, on adjusted EBITDA of Rs1.9bn (+2.1x YoY), saw it below its own estimate because of higher indirect expenses, mainly advertising and promotion (+50%). (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management expects renewals to grow 50%+ for at least the next 12 months, and Kotak sees momentum continuing in FY27E with 39% YoY premium growth. Kotak raised FY28E earnings by 10.9% and FV to Rs1,875 from Rs1,800. Jefferies raised FY28-29e PAT by 3-5%. The overhang is possible commission-structure guidelines and the regulatory risk of commission cuts. (Kotak, Jeff)

companies.name: Pine Labs
companies.note: FY27 revenue growth guidance was retained at 21-23.5%. and the Adj Ebitda margin is expected to be maintained at or above FY26 levels and working capital intensity to stay in check.

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 17% YoY but came in 4% below both consensus (Rs7,328mn) and JPMorgan's estimate. Issuing & Acquiring grew 24% YoY while Digital Infra lagged at 14%, with a slower POS rollout and chip shortages weighing on the latter. Revenue fell 6% QoQ. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA of Rs1,450mn was 5% below JPMorgan's estimate (no consensus given). The margin expanded sharply YoY to 21% from 14% on indirect cost control, but was 40bps below JPMe, and contribution margin fell 70bps QoQ on lower digital infra CM. (JP)

1Q27.revNote: Core revenue grew 19.6% YoY to Rs7,369mn, in line with consensus (+0.2%) and +0.9% vs MSe. Issuing and acquiring grew 31% YoY, while digital infra lagged at 15%. Revenue came at the low end of the company's 20-21% guide. (MS, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA of Rs1,264mn (+4.5% YoY) was 16.5% below consensus and 12.7% below MSe. Margin fell to 17.2% (-367bps QoQ) from 20.8%, because of upfront investment in sales (500 more salespeople) and AI/tech (tech costs +33% YoY), plus a lower contribution margin from the mix shift to distribution in issuing. (MS, JP)

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 21-23.5% and expects margins to recover in 2H on festive-season mix, with Adj. EBITDA margin not going below the FY26 level of 20.6%. Both houses cut estimates on the 1Q margin miss: JP cut FY27E Adj. EBITDA by 12.1% (Rs7,657mn to Rs6,733mn) and FY28E by 6.0%, and lowered its PT to Rs145 from Rs155. MS flagged a modest downward revision to consensus EPS. (JP, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Record revenue of Rs70.4bn (+21% YoY, +7% QoQ), 2.2% above Bloomberg consensus. Growth was broad-based: hospitals +22% YoY, offline pharmacy +22%, 24/7 +13%, diagnostics and retail +15%. Hospital volume grew 13% (CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs10.9bn (+28% YoY) was 3.9% above consensus, with margin up 92bps YoY to 15.5%. Hospital EBITDA grew 20% (margin 24.2%), offline pharmacy margin was 7.3%, and digital-health losses narrowed to Rs196mn from Rs732mn a year ago (CLSA, JP, Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 18% YoY, in line with expectations, on steady growth across all segments: hospitals +16% on 7-9% growth in IP volumes/ARPP, offline pharmacy +21%, 24/7 +13% and diagnostics & retail +24%. Kotak's estimate was 0.2% below the print and Jeff's was 3% below. (CLSA, Kotak, Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs10.1bn grew 31% YoY and beat Kotak's estimate by ~10% and Jeff's by 8%. The margin rose 154bps YoY to 15.3%, in line per CLSA, helped by Healthco margin of 5.5% (about 400bps ahead of Jeff's estimate) on lower 24/7 cash burn. New-hospital losses of Rs414mn dragged hospital margins down 92bps QoQ to 23.9%. (Kotak, Jeff, CLSA)
4Q26.vsBasis: broker estimate (Kotak, Jeff); revenue in-line per CLSA

outlook.note: Management guides for 20% hospital revenue growth in FY27 (13-14% for established hospitals) and a Rs1.5bn loss from new beds, with breakeven in 2HFY28. It expects online pharmacy breakeven by 2QFY27 and 20%+ diagnostics growth. Jefferies raised FY27 EBITDA by 4% and JPMorgan expects positive consensus revisions. CLSA kept its estimates and raised its target price to Rs9,560 from Rs9,280 (CLSA, Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue rose 21.6% yoy to Rs13.1 bn, 5.9% above Kotak's estimate. Kerala grew 24.6% yoy as it recovered from the nurses' strike. AP and Telangana grew 32.9%, Karnataka and Maharashtra grew 16.3%. The QCIL merger is consolidated from 1 July 2026. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 27.5% yoy to Rs2.64 bn, 7.0% above Kotak's estimate. The margin was 20.2% (+93 bps yoy), or 21.2% on operating EBITDA (+118 bps yoy), helped by a better payor and case mix. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reiterated 10-15% EBITDA synergies (Rs1.5-2 bn) from FY2027E and guides to ~24-25% combined EBITDA margins by FY2028/29E. About 4,200 beds are planned to FY2030E, ~53% brownfield. Kotak raised FY2028-29E EBITDA by 5-6%, rolled its valuation forward to June 2028E and lifted fair value to Rs900 from Rs770 (ADD). Kotak models ~22%/25% pro forma sales/EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29E. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs6.1bn (+26% YoY, +9% QoQ) was 4% above both MS estimates and consensus. Growth was driven by roughly 8% volume and 8% value growth, with same-store sales up 16% and mature facilities up 37% YoY; recently added centres contributed the rest. (MS, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.7bn (+33% YoY) was 6% above MS estimates and consensus. Margin was 27.8%, up 152bps YoY, helped by operating leverage on the stronger revenue and 55bps above Jefferies' estimate, though down 87bps QoQ. (MS, Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR5.6bn (+23% YoY) was 2% above Jefferies' estimate, i.e. largely in line. Growth came from 24% volume growth, with cataract surgeries up 29% YoY and same-store sales up ~14%, and 16 net new facilities in the quarter. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR1.6bn (+23% YoY) was 10% above Jefferies' estimate. Margin was 28.6% (+16bps YoY), ~200bps above estimate, on a gross margin of 79.1% (+154bps YoY) and lower-than-expected employee costs. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management is on track to add 60 centres in FY27 (about 40 surgical) after 16-18 net additions in 1Q27. Same-store sales growth is expected to normalise over time, though it improved to ~16% in 1Q27. Jefferies raised FY27-29E EBITDA by 3-4%, upgraded to Buy and lifted its PT to INR600. MS trimmed FY28 EPS by 3.5% but raised its PT to Rs576 on higher EBITDA expectations and stayed Overweight. The merger is expected to close by Nov'26. (Jeff, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs 8.0bn rose 19.1% YoY (13.5% QoQ), the fastest growth in four years, and was 5% above Factset consensus (7% above MSe). Patient volume grew 8.2% and realisation per patient rose ~10% on the CGHS price hike (~2-3% company-level impact) and better mix. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 2.5bn rose 29% YoY and was 16% above consensus (21% above MSe). Margin expanded ~232bps YoY to 31.0% as faster growth flowed through with operating leverage, and gross margin held at 81%. (MS)

outlook.note: Management now leans toward mid-teens FY27 revenue growth, against low-to-mid teens earlier, and told Nomura's Tokyo NDR it expects mid-teens growth to be sustained in the medium term. The CGHS price benefit should last another 2-3 quarters, and capex guidance was raised to Rs 1.4-1.5bn. Nomura raised FY27F estimates 2-4% and its TP to INR 2,150 (from 2,085). MS raised FY27/FY28 EPS 5.4%/7.8% and its PT to Rs 1,960 (from 1,819). Management cautions that the underlying patient-volume trend will only be clear after Q2/Q3, because of the fever season. (Nomura, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 17.5% YoY to Rs25.5bn, 1.4% above GS's estimate. Hospitals revenue grew 19.0% YoY on higher occupied beds and bed additions, while Diagnostics grew 10.3% (gross) with ARPOB growth slowing to low single digits (GS, Jeff, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 9.6% YoY to Rs5.38bn, 4.1% below GS's estimate. Margin was 21.1% (-120bps vs GS, -152bps YoY) as ESOP costs in hospitals (Rs307mn per Nomura) offset strong gross margins. Jefferies called EBITDA in-line with its estimate, while Nomura had it 3% below (GS, Nomura, Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR 23.6bn (+17.8% YoY, +4.4% QoQ) was about 2% above Nomura's estimate of INR 23.3bn. Hospital revenue rose ~19% on facility expansion and ~17% higher occupied beds, with ARPOB up ~2% (its slowest growth in 21 quarters). Diagnostics revenue grew 11.7% (Nomura). Jefferies also calls revenue 2% above its estimate (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR 5.3bn (+22.2% YoY) missed Nomura's estimate by 3%. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (+82bp YoY), 109bp below the 23.6% Nomura expected (Nomura). Jefferies had EBITDA 4% above its own estimate, led by a 5% hospital EBITDA beat on bed expansion (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management maintained its guidance of mid-teen revenue growth and ~25% hospital margins after ESOP costs by FY28. Diagnostics is expected to deliver double-digit growth with 24-25% margins. Fortis plans about 400 beds for the rest of FY27. GS lifted FY27-29 revenue and changed EBITDA by about +/-2%, while Jeff cut FY27-29 EBITDA by 1-4% on ESOP charges (the ESOP expense is around Rs1.3bn a year). Targets: GS Rs975 (Neutral), Jeff Rs1,125 (Buy), Nomura Rs990 (Neutral) (GS, Jeff, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs13.0bn (+27% YoY, +13% QoQ) was about 7% ahead of consensus (JP) and 10% ahead of Kotak's estimate. Growth came from strong inpatient volumes (+28% YoY) and outpatient volumes (+35% YoY), with ARPOB up 5% to Rs70,244 on case mix and shorter ALOS. (JP, Kotak, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.87bn (+26% YoY) was about 12% ahead of consensus (JP) and 16% ahead of Kotak's estimate, despite clinical-talent investments. The margin was 22.0% (flat YoY, +96bps QoQ), broadly in line. Noida EBITDA losses narrowed to Rs49mn from Rs236mn in 4Q, and the ex-Noida margin was about 24%. (JP, Kotak, CLSA)

outlook.note: Management now expects Noida to reach EBITDA breakeven earlier than guided, around end-2QFY27 (Kotak) against the prior 2HFY27. The bed-expansion plan is intact: about 90% more capacity to ~7,105 beds, Guwahati raised to 650 beds, capex of Rs48.5bn. Kotak raised FY27-29E EBITDA by 4-6% and CLSA raised its estimates and target price. JP expects upward consensus revisions. Kotak, CLSA and JP.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 35% yoy (+10% qoq) to Rs11.8 bn, in line with consensus (GS) and 4% above Kotak's estimate, on ramp-up at new hospitals plus mature-region growth of 16.5% yoy driven by ~8-10% ARPOB growth (GS, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 16% yoy to Rs2.2 bn but was ~6% below consensus (GS); margin of 18.9% was 144 bps above GS's estimate but down ~320 bps yoy on pre-operating costs at new units such as Kondapur, though Kotak calls it in line with its estimate (GS, Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Sales grew 34.8% yoy and 7.7% qoq to Rs10.7 bn, 1.2% below Kotak's estimate and largely in line, as new hospitals ramped up and ARPOB grew ~14% yoy (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.1 bn (+4.3% yoy) was ~5% below Kotak's estimate (-4.8%). Margin fell to 19.2% (-563 bps yoy) on losses of ~Rs320 mn at new hospitals, caused by delays in insurance empanelment. Mature hospitals held ~29% margins (Kotak).

outlook.note: Mgmt expects a strong 2Q; new-unit EBITDA losses narrowed to Rs260 mn from Rs475 mn in 4Q, Mahadevapura reached breakeven and Thane is expected to turn positive in 2Q, with insurer empanelments largely done by end-FY27. GS trims/raises FY27-29E EBITDA by -3% to +6% and keeps Buy with a Rs1,000 TP, while Kotak cuts FY27-29E EBITDA by 2-4% and stays at Reduce with a Rs775 FV (GS, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 15% YoY to Rs28.3bn, about 1% above consensus and 2% above GS's estimate. Growth was led by a 10% YoY rise in occupied bed days and 5% higher ARPOB. The discontinued CGHS oncology drugs still weighed on growth, and ex-oncology gross revenue grew 20% YoY (GS, JP, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 16% YoY to Rs6.74bn, 6% below consensus in GS's table but 2% above GS's estimate. Margin was 23.8%, which GS put 197bps below consensus. Better gross margin was offset by higher hospital opex and the ramp-up of new brownfield capacity and the Kalinga Hospitals acquisition. JP and Jeff both called EBITDA in line with consensus, so brokers disagree on the consensus comparison (GS, JP, Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 10% YoY and 3% QoQ to Rs25.4bn, driven by higher occupied bed days. This was partly offset by the discontinuation of chemo drugs for institutional patients (oncology share fell to 21.2% from 25.7%) and by flat ARPOB QoQ on higher ALOS. CLSA calls network revenue in line with consensus; JPM sees it ~2% below JPMe. (CLSA, JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs6.8bn (+12% YoY, +7% QoQ) was in line. Margin of 26.7% was up 30bps YoY despite higher clinician costs from aggressive hiring ahead of expansions. CLSA calls EBITDA in line with consensus; JPM calls it largely in line. (CLSA, JP)

outlook.note: Expansion is largely on track: 202 beds at Max Smart are operational and the remaining 198 come in 2Q. Pune (450 beds) has preliminary approval for FY30. Brownfield expansions are expected to be monetised from H2FY27, and the CGHS oncology drag should fade from Dec-26Q as the base normalises. Some bed additions are delayed (Vaishali, Nanavati and Dwarka pushed to FY30). Jeff therefore cut FY27-29E EBITDA by 2-3%, and GS changed its EBITDA estimates by -3% to +1% and trimmed its target price to Rs1,200 from Rs1,250. Ratings remain Buy/OW (GS, Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs4.5bn grew 16.6% yoy and 6% qoq, about 3% above Bloomberg consensus (Rs4,389mn) and in line with broker estimates. Patient volume grew 10% and realisation per patient rose 6% on richer mix. TruHealth grew 22% and specialty 17%. (GS, Kotak, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,112mn rose 23.9% yoy, about 2% above consensus (Rs1,089mn) and in line with broker estimates. Margin was 24.7%, up 145bps yoy, on operating leverage and efficiency gains. Gross margin was 79.2%, up 119bps yoy. (GS, Kotak, MS)

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 revenue growth guidance at 14-15% (9-10% patient volume growth) and guided to 100-150bps of EBITDA margin expansion. The medium-term margin target is 27-28%, and it plans 500+ net new centres in FY27. GS raised its TP to Rs550 (from Rs525) and cut FY27-29E EPS by 5% for the quarter and outlook, while keeping Sell on valuation. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 1-3% and its FV to Rs655 (from Rs625). (GS, Kotak)

companies.name: Narayana Hrudayalaya
companies.note: NARH plans to add ~1,935 beds in the next four years, of which 1,235 beds would be coming up in its flagship Bengaluru and Kolkata clusters by FY2030E.

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs25.9 bn (+76% yoy) beat Kotak's estimate by 4%, helped by the PPG (UK) consolidation from 6 Nov 2025 and Cayman sales up 70% yoy (+9% vs Kotak's estimate) on a ~6X jump in insurance sales. India hospital revenue grew 12% yoy to Rs12.3 bn (+3% vs Kotak's estimate), with ARPOB at Rs51.0k/day (+10% yoy). (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.1 bn (+43% yoy) was 3% below Kotak's estimate, a marginal miss, and margin was 19.7% (-458 bps yoy). The UK business contributed Rs846 mn, but corporate expenses were higher at Rs682 mn. India EBITDA was 11.5% above Kotak's estimate, while Cayman EBITDA was in line. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs26.8 bn (+78% yoy) was 1.6% above Kotak's estimate. The yoy jump reflects the UK asset (PPG) consolidated from 6 Nov 2025, so it is not comparable on a yoy basis. India hospital revenue grew 16% yoy to Rs12.9 bn, led by realisation and volume, and Cayman sales grew 39% yoy. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.7 bn (+39% yoy) was 2.7% below Kotak's estimate, largely on lower overseas margins. Margin fell to 17.5% from 22.4% a year ago, as Cayman margin dropped to 24.0% from 36.5% expected and NHIC losses widened. India hospitals EBITDA grew 39% yoy. (Kotak)

outlook.note: After the results Kotak upgraded to BUY from ADD (21 Aug) and raised EBITDA by 1-3% on higher Indian hospital margins. It models India hospital sales/EBITDA CAGRs of 15%/14% over FY2026-29E, expects the Indian insurance claims ratio to recede and Cayman to break even by end-FY2028E, and sees EBITDA margin rising from 8.8% to 11.5%/12.5% by FY28/29E (Kotak's 3 Aug note had cut FY27-29E EBITDA by 5-7% on insurance losses). (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 23.7% y-y to INR 2,818mn, 4.8% ahead of Nomura's estimate. Treatments grew 13.3% y-y and revenue per treatment rose 9.2%, helped by international expansion (international now 44% of revenue). (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 34.3% y-y to INR 639mn, 11.8% above Nomura's estimate. Margin was 22.7% (+179bp y-y, 141bp ahead of estimate), driven by a 175bp gross-margin gain. Adjusted for Saudi Arabia and ESOP costs, margin was 23.1%. (Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 21.2% y-y and came in 5.3% ahead of Nomura's INR2,523mn estimate, driven by 15.2% y-y growth in treatments and 5.2% y-y growth in revenue per treatment (Nomura).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew only 4.8% y-y and missed Nomura's estimate by 8.9%. Other expenses rose 32.6% y-y, including a INR100mn provision for expected credit loss, and higher business development spend. EBITDA margin was 20.2% (24.0% adjusted for the provision) vs 23.4% a year ago (Nomura).

outlook.note: Management guides to 15–20% revenue growth over the coming years, with plans to add 40–50 clinics a year in India and 12–15 in the Philippines, and to enter Saudi Arabia (tender awaited) and Kazakhstan. Nomura assumes a 16% FY26–29F revenue CAGR and 23–24% EBITDA margin. It raised FY27F revenue 2% and EBITDA 1% (FY27F EBITDA INR 2,786mn), but cut FY27F net profit 3%. TP rose to INR 780 from INR 680 on a higher sector multiple. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs4.7bn (+33% YoY, +2% QoQ) was 8% ahead of consensus and 3% ahead of JPM's estimate, driven by 22% YoY growth in operational beds and occupancy up 100bps YoY to 41%. ARPOB grew 6.2% YoY, about 80bps below JPM's forecast (JP; Kotak also saw a 7% beat vs its estimate).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.3bn (+30% YoY, -7% QoQ) was 5% above consensus and 2% above JPM's estimate. Margin of 28.6% (-70bps YoY, -280bps QoQ) was 70bps below consensus on higher employee costs and doctors' professional fees (JP, Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs4.6 bn (+24% yoy, +3% qoq) was 7% ahead of Kotak's estimate of Rs4.3 bn. Organic growth was 9-10% yoy, and 15-16% yoy excluding the two acquired hospitals (Warangal, Guwahati). IP footfalls grew 18% yoy and ARPOB rose about 11% yoy in FY26 (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.4 bn (+26% yoy) was 8% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 31.5% (+50 bps yoy, -153 bps qoq) against Kotak's 31.0%, helped by volume leverage (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management targets a ~20% revenue CAGR over the next four years and expects 2QFY27 growth of around 20% YoY. It expects pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margins to revert to 24-25% by end-FY27 as newer hospitals ramp up. Capacity is planned to rise by ~1,160 beds to 3,595 by FY29E, with new Guntur and Malad units and the Super Prime acquisition. JPM expects upward consensus revisions after the beat, and Kotak raised its FY28-29E EBITDA by 5% while trimming FY27E slightly and lifting fair value to Rs1,685 from Rs1,500 (JP, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Bajaj Finserv is a holding company and reports no consolidated GWP, so this line is Bajaj General's (BAGIC) GWP, the insurance top line in Jefferies' Exhibit 5. It rose 11% YoY to Rs57.9bn, or about +10% excluding tender-driven crop and government health business. Slower motor OD, crop and travel growth was offset by health and commercial lines. No consensus figure is printed. The beat call rests on Jefferies' headline that all three businesses beat estimates and on GS's note that topline was +3% vs GSe. GS's +3% is for the consolidated topline, not GWP (Jeff, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Core profit is Bajaj Finserv's share of profit from Bajaj Finance, BAGIC and BALIC, plus its share of BALIC's VNB (Jefferies Exhibit 4). It rose 21% YoY to Rs36.5bn and was flat QoQ, the fifth straight quarter of roughly 20% growth. Bajaj Finance's share of profit was up 27% and BALIC's VNB share was up 95%, partly offset by BAGIC's share of profit down 24% on a 104.7% combined ratio. Jefferies says all three businesses beat estimates, and GS has consolidated PAT 9% above GSe. No consensus figure is printed (Jeff, GS).

outlook.note: Jefferies raises core profit estimates by 2-4% and sees 24% EPS CAGR over FY26-29. Bajaj Finance reiterated its FY27 AUM growth corridor of 22-24%, with NIMs to trend down 10-15bps. BALIC is expected to see VNB margin of ~20% and APE growth of ~20% in FY27, and BAGIC is prioritising underwriting discipline over premium growth. GS raises FY27-29E EPS by c.5% and its TP to Rs1,780, but keeps Sell. Kotak raises FV to Rs2,600 (from Rs2,430) and says the holdco discount has widened to 35%. (Jeff, GS, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: GWP grew 6% YoY to Rs 110.3bn, with growth across both domestic and international books. The business mix was largely stable, with fire at 30% of NWP, motor 19% and health 23%. The note gives no estimate or consensus for GWP, so it is not rated (JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: PBT rose 1% YoY to Rs 29.6bn. JPMorgan puts net profit 31% above its estimate, mainly from forex gains as the rupee depreciated and a smaller underwriting loss (Rs 3.6bn, -15% YoY). The combined ratio of 103.4% was in line with its 103.2% estimate. Investment income fell 22% YoY, and the Rs 2.4bn higher catastrophe reserve provisioning held back profit. The beat call is based on net profit because the note gives no PBT estimate (JP).

outlook.note: JPMorgan raised its Mar-27 PT to Rs 500 from Rs 480 (1.4x FY28E P/BV) and kept its OW rating. It cut its FY27E/FY28E combined ratio estimates by 20bp/30bp to 105.3%/103.9%, which lifts APAT by 10%/4%. It expects the underwriting improvement to continue on a better business mix, especially overseas, where the FY26 combined ratio stayed high at 120%. Solvency of 421% is a comfortable buffer (JP).

1Q27.revNote: GWP fell 8% YoY to Rs27.3bn and was 2.9% below MS's estimate of Rs28.1bn. Fire GWP fell 37% on intense competition, and motor OD GWP fell 3% as the CV book shrank and the new-car portfolio did poorly. Management put market share ahead of growth, and this was its first-ever quarter of share contraction. (MorganStanley, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: IGAAP PBT fell 28% YoY to Rs1.16bn, 39.6% below MS's estimate and short of consensus. The combined ratio was 112.4% (108.6% a year earlier). Motor OD loss ratio rose to 75.9% (69.3%) and fire loss ratio to 83% (73.1%) on one large loss, and the expense ratio rose on mix. (MorganStanley, Jeff)
1Q27.vsBasis: PBT: consensus (MS text: missed our estimate and consensus); GWP: broker estimate (MorganS

outlook.note: Management expects growth challenges from motor and fire competition to persist, though it expects motor OD loss ratios to stabilise in 2Q after pricing actions in Feb, Apr and May. Jefferies cut FY27-29e EPS by 5-7% and revenue by 12-13%, and cut its PT to Rs380 from Rs395. MS flagged a meaningful downward revision to next-12-month consensus EPS. The Supreme Court motor TP judgment impact is not quantified and is provided for within reserves. (Jeff, MS)

1Q27.revNote: APE grew 9% YoY to Rs35.2bn, 3% below Jefferies' Rs36.1bn estimate. Growth stayed subdued because the HDFC Bank banca channel was flat YoY and parent-bank volumes were softer. Retail protection (+42%), annuity and non-par savings grew strongly, while Par fell about 50%. No consensus APE figure is printed, so the call is against the broker estimate (Jeff, MS, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB rose 9% YoY to Rs8.8bn, 1% above Jefferies' estimate and 5% ahead of Morgan Stanley's. Morgan Stanley also calls it ahead of consensus, but prints no consensus number. VNB margin was 25.0%, flat YoY and 95bps above Jefferies' estimate, helped by better product mix. That offset a 60bps GST hit and a 40bps persistency-related assumption change (Jeff, MS, GS).
1Q27.vsBasis: APE: broker estimate (Jefferies); VNB: consensus (Morgan Stanley)

2Q27.revNote: Total APE rose 12.9% YoY to Rs 47.3bn, 1.7% above JPMe. Retail APE growth improved to 11.3% as the banca channel recovered (HDFC Bank APE +13%, ~48% of individual APE). Protection and annuity were strong, but agency slowed to 6% (JPM, Kotak, Jeff).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB rose 14.8% YoY to Rs 11.6bn, 1.7% above consensus and 1.7% below JPMe. Margin was 24.5%, +39bp YoY but about 40-53bp lower QoQ, held back by expenses, assumption changes and a 40bp residual GST impact. Kotak calls it in line; Jeff calls it a 4% beat vs JEFe (JP, Kotak, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management plans to grow VNB in line with or faster than APE and to neutralise the remaining ~40bp GST drag (down from 60bp) in coming quarters. JP expects limited VNB estimate revisions and a range-bound stock until IRDAI's distribution-commission paper is clarified, though the 2H base is more favourable. Jefferies left FY27-29 VNB unchanged (it did raise other FY27-29e estimates) and expects agency APE growth to pick up in 2H27 (JP, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: NEP rose 16% YoY to Rs59.5bn, about 5% above Jefferies' Rs56.6bn estimate, on 10% GWP growth led by motor (+21%) and health (+26%) (JP, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PBT fell 46% YoY to Rs5.4bn as the combined ratio worsened to 107.2% (+430bp YoY). Drivers were a Rs1.65bn motor third-party provision after the Supreme Court homemaker-compensation ruling, two large fire losses (Rs0.63bn), and a 76.4% loss ratio. Investment yield also slipped to 1.9%. PAT of Rs4.03bn was 47.4% below consensus (JP, Jeff).
1Q27.vsBasis: NEP: broker estimate (Jefferies JEFe Rs56.6bn); PBT: JPM states PAT 47.4% below consensus

2Q27.revNote: NEP rose 17.7% YoY and 11.8% QoQ to Rs66.5bn, 22% above MS's estimate of Rs54.5bn, helped by higher inward reinsurance and retention; GDPI growth was only ~3% YoY, below industry growth of ~7%, with Fire down 13% on pricing pressure (MS, GS).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PBT of Rs12.5bn (+15.8% YoY) was 22.9% above MS's estimate, driven by investment income up 28.8% YoY to Rs15.7bn (Rs4.53bn capital gains on the NSE listing) and reversal of Motor TP provisions made in 1Q. The combined ratio of 107.0% was 30bp worse than MS's estimate, as Rs1.18bn of CAT losses added 1.7ppt (MS, JP).

outlook.note: Management guides Motor loss ratios of 65-67%, expects Motor growth to moderate from 3Q as the base kicks in, and says the Fire premium decline narrowed to -13.6% in Sep vs -21% in 2Q, with growth set to improve. It expects retention to rise 3-5ppt and sees itself better placed than peers if IRDAI's proposed commission caps and EOM limits are implemented. MS raised FY27 PAT 5% and FY28/29 ~2% each, and JP expects consensus upgrades. GS cut EPS by up to 2%. (MS, JP, GS)

1Q27.revNote: APE of Rs21.4bn grew 15% YoY, 1% above JEFe, so in line. Growth came from retail protection APE (+60% YoY, helped by GST tailwinds), annuity (+33%) and group funds (+42%), while savings slowed (+6%) and agency (+2%) and banca (+6%) stayed weak. No consensus APE is printed. (Jeff, JP, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB of Rs5.7bn grew 25% YoY, 11% above JEFe and 7.1% above consensus (JP). VNB margin was 26.7%, up 222bp YoY and about 240bp above JEFe, on a richer mix: protection was 27.9% of APE, up 590bp YoY, with better rider attachment and bond yields. (Jeff, JP, GS)
1Q27.vsBasis: VNB: consensus (JP: +7.1% vs consensus); APE: broker estimate (Jefferies)

2Q27.revNote: APE grew 16% YoY to Rs 28.0bn, in line with JEFe (Rs 27.9bn), led by group business (+39.6% YoY), annuity (+66%) and retail protection (+36%, GST tailwind). Retail APE grew 10.7%, with agency and banca each up only ~4% (Jeff).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB rose 20% YoY to Rs 7.1bn, 2% below JEFe (Rs 7.2bn). The margin of 25.4% was +100bp YoY but 129bp lower QoQ and 50bp below JEFe because of a higher group-funds mix. JPM calls it a mild miss (2.7% below JPMe), while Kotak has VNB 2% above its estimate (Jeff, JP, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management gave no guidance on APE or VNB growth, and the draft distribution reforms (commission/EoM caps; credit-protect commission cuts) leave the outlook uncertain. Kotak cut FV to Rs700 from Rs775 with a 12-13% VNB cut and a nearly flat FY28E APE. Nomura expects 13% APE growth and 14% VNB growth in FY27F and kept its Rs710 TP. JPMorgan sees limited changes to consensus and expects sideways stock action (Kotak, Nomura, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Total APE grew 8.2% YoY to Rs137bn, but came in 7% below GS's estimate (Rs146.8bn). Individual APE rose 7% and group APE rose 10%, while the Par/Non-Par/Group mix shifted toward non-par. No consensus APE figure is printed, so this call is against GS's own estimate. (GS, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB rose 61% YoY to Rs31.4bn, about 13% above consensus of Rs27.8bn and 28% above GS's estimate. VNB margin expanded 750bp YoY to 22.9% (consensus 18.2%), driven mainly by mix (+650bp) and economic assumptions (+290bp), partly offset by GST input-credit loss (-190bp). (JP, GS)

4Q26.revNote: APE rose 22% YoY (+53% QoQ) to Rs 229.5bn off a low base. Individual APE grew 16% and group APE 37%, led by agency (+12.9%) and non-par (JP's NPAR share up 7.4pp in FY26) (Bern, JP). No report gives a consensus APE figure, so no beat/miss call.
4Q26.ebitdaNote: VNB of Rs 58.9bn (+67% YoY) was well above JP's consensus of Rs 42.7bn (about 38% higher) and above JPM's own forecast of Rs 38.7bn; Jefferies puts the beat at 22%/33% vs JEFe/FactSet consensus. VNB margin rose to 25.7% from 18.7%, helped by non-par mix (about 300bp) and a favourable yield curve (about 340bp), partly offset by GST and persistency (about 280bp) (Bern, JP, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management expects margins to improve further from the 1Q base, subject to RFR movements, with the non-par and protection mix shift continuing. JPMorgan raised FY27/28E VNB by 4.1%/4.7% (PT trimmed to Rs500 from Rs505, OW) and GS raised FY27-29E EPS by up to 4% (TP Rs475 unchanged, Neutral). Watch-points: agent count down 3% YoY, a weak ULIP/banca mix, and an undefined dividend policy. (JP, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Total APE rose 15.2% YoY to Rs 19.2bn, 2.4% below Kotak's Rs 20bn estimate, so broadly in line. Protection APE grew 23.5% (individual protection +42%) and Axis Bank channel APE +14%, offset by a 9% YoY rise in the proprietary offline channel after policy cancellations. (JP, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB of Rs 4.46bn (+33.1% YoY) was about 10% above consensus (Jeff) and 9.4% above JPMorgan's estimate. VNB margin was 23.2%, up 315bps YoY and about 360bps above Jefferies' estimate. About 70% of the expansion came from yield-curve movement and the rest from favourable mix. (JP, Jeff, Kotak)
1Q27.vsBasis: VNB vs consensus (Jeff: 10% above); APE vs broker estimate (Kotak)

outlook.note: Brokers expect continued APE growth ahead of peers (Jeff: 16% APE CAGR to FY29e, VNB margin 26.5% in FY27e, up 130bps, with 21% VNB growth). Management guides to a moderation in the non-PAR savings decline into FY27. Estimate changes were small: Jeff PT unchanged at Rs 2,250, JPM PT trimmed to Rs 2,150 from Rs 2,160, and Kotak raised its fair value to Rs 1,950 from Rs 1,920 and upgraded to BUY. Risks are pending commission guidelines and Axis Bank's possible move towards a 30% stake. (Kotak, JP, Jeff)

companies.name: Niva Bupa Health Insurance
companies.note: Niva plans to grow at least 8-10pp above the industry. We see next leg of growth (22% 3yr CAGR) being driven by: (1) the agency channel, where Niva is targeting health professionals (e.g., yoga instructors, gym trainers) to grow its network, (2) growth beyond the top 100 cities (c.80% of premiums currently), (3) mid-single digit price hikes, and (4) new policy launches.

1Q27.revNote: GWP (post-1/n basis) of Rs21.5bn grew 32% YoY and came in about 1% above MS's Rs21.2bn estimate. Retail health GWP grew 46.5%, with fresh business up 41% YoY, while group business was largely flat as the company exited large, unfavourable group contracts. (MS, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PBT of Rs1.84bn (+88% YoY) was about 50% above MS's Rs1.23bn estimate. The loss ratio improved ~382bp YoY to 63% on mix shift away from group and lower provisions, and CISR improved ~3ppt to 100.2%. Expense ratio was up ~86bp YoY, and PAT of Rs1.38bn (+93%) beat MS estimates and FactSet consensus. (MS, Jeff, Nomura)

outlook.note: Management targets growth 8-10pp above the industry, and momentum held in July 2026. Hospitalization trends in July are in line with expectations. Management retained its FY29 CISR guidance of 99%, which MS says should drive mid-to-high-teens ROE. Jefferies raised FY27-29e Ind AS earnings by 2-9% and lifted its PT to Rs105. Nomura expects a 161bp expense-ratio reduction over FY26-29 as the GST drag fades in 2H. (MS, Jeff, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: APE of Rs53.8bn (+36% yoy) was 18.7% above Kotak's estimate, driven by group term (group protection APE up ~4x yoy, 21-26% of APE). Individual APE grew a more modest 14% yoy, with par up 33% and non-par up 26% while ULIP rose only 7%, and the bancassurance channel grew 10% against 24% in agency (Kotak, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: VNB of Rs14.1bn (+30% yoy) was 17.8% above Kotak's estimate (+15% vs GS, +16% vs JPM), driven by strong individual-business margins. Reported VNB margin was 26.2%, down 120bps yoy and 20bps below Kotak's estimate, on 110bps of GST drag and a 60bps mix drag from group business (Kotak, GS, JP).

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 14-15% individual APE growth and VNB margin of 26-28%, with the GST impact guided to be lower from Q2. Kotak raised VNB estimates by 2-5% on better product mix and 2-4% higher growth, and GS raised FY27-29E VNB by up to 4%. Kotak flagged a pick-up in the SBI bancassurance channel as the key monitorable (Kotak, GS).

companies.name: Star Health
companies.note: We see another 100bps loss ratio improvement by FY28e, led by price hikes, rise in fresh policies, and home care services.

1Q27.revNote: IFRS insurance revenue of Rs49.2bn grew 13% YoY, 1% below Jefferies' estimate of Rs49.8bn. GS separately put GDPI growth at about 19% YoY, in line with its estimate, with retail GWP up 23% on volume growth and new-to-insurance customers (Jeff, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Insurance service result of Rs4.25bn rose 48% YoY and was 18% above Jefferies' estimate. The loss ratio improved to 67.5% (-104bps YoY, 72bps better than expected) for the fourth consecutive quarter of improvement, and the combined ratio came in at 97.1%, 89bps ahead of the estimate (Jeff, GS).

outlook.note: Jefferies sees another c.100bps of loss-ratio improvement by FY28e from price hikes, fresh-policy growth and telemedicine/home care. It expects GWP growth to slow to about 14% in 2HFY27 on a high base but sees tailwinds from 4Q price hikes. It raised FY27-29e EPS by 1-2% and its PT to Rs725 (Buy). GS raised FY27-29E EPS by up to 6% and its PT to Rs645 (Buy), expecting profitability momentum to continue in FY27 (Jeff, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$46.1 mn (+19.5% yoy, +7.3% qoq) came in 2.1% above Kotak's US$45.2 mn estimate. Growth was led by streaming unification (+26% yoy) and monetization & marketplace (+17%), while cloud modernization grew only 5.5% on a high base. Excluding the unfavorable base effect, c/c growth was ~24% (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs298 mn (6.8% margin) was 14.3% below Kotak's Rs348 mn estimate and up 25% qoq. The miss reflects one-off buyback and IPO expenses (Rs250 mn) and wage increases in a seasonally weak quarter. Adj. EBITDA margin was 11.5%, up 640 bps yoy, as R&D and S&M leverage offset a 220 bps yoy gross margin decline (Kotak). The year-ago EBITDA was Rs-12 mn, so yoy growth is not meaningful.

outlook.note: Kotak expects healthy underlying growth, with 1HFY27 at ~46% of FY revenue. It sees streaming unification leading growth, with the cloud modernization base effect fading. Adj. EBITDA margin is guided to ~12.5% in 1HFY27 and 15.1% in FY27E. Kotak raised FY27-29E revenue by 1.7-2.3% and EPS by 2.8-3.4%, and lifted fair value to Rs700 (ADD). Risks are industry consolidation stretching sales cycles and rangebound gross margin (Kotak).

companies.name: Birlasoft
companies.note: new deal TCV declined 25% y-y.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$145.2mn was -3.6% y-y and -0.1% q-q in USD terms (+0.3% q-q in cc), in line with Nomura's US$145.15mn estimate. BFSI grew 4.9% q-q, while Manufacturing (-3.7%) and Energy & Utilities (-1.2%) declined. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR2,227mn (16.1% margin, -230bp q-q) was in line with Nomura's 16% expectation, as the 4Q one-off benefits normalised. EBITDA rose 40% y-y off a low 1Q26 base (12.4% margin). (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management is focused on improving deal wins and the pipeline so that FY27E is a growth year; new deal TCV fell 25% y-y, though the book-to-bill is 1.2x. Wage hikes from 1 July should dilute 2Q margin by 170-200bp, about half of which management plans to recoup, and steady-state EBITDA margin is guided at about 15%. Nomura left revenue estimates unchanged (FY27F -1.8%, FY28F +3.5% y-y) and changed FY27-28F EPS by about 1% (Nomura).

companies.name: Coforge
companies.note: 12-month executable order book is at US$2.2bn, up strongly by 44% YoY without including the recently announced US$230m deal.

1Q27.revNote: US$592mn (+34% YoY, +21% QoQ) was 5.9% above Bloomberg consensus of US$559mn (CLSA's consensus of US$576mn gives a 2.8% beat). Growth was 22.3% QoQ in constant currency, driven by two months of Encora contribution. Organic business grew 1% QoQ in cc against flat expected, or 5.2% excluding exited businesses, with broad-based growth across verticals (JP, CLSA, MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs11,233mn (+74% YoY) beat consensus by 5.9%, with margin of 20.3% vs 20.1% consensus (+25bps). Ebit margin of 16.0% was 40bps above consensus, with Encora G&A synergies coming in as planned. Net profit missed consensus by 5.9% on higher hedging losses and finance costs (JP, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management reiterated strong revenue growth over coming quarters with a 15.5% FY27 Ebit margin. The 12-month executable order book is US$2.2bn (+44% YoY), excluding the newly announced US$230mn deal. CLSA raised FY27-29 EPS 2-5% and its target price to Rs2,170 from Rs2,045, and MS sees a modest upward revision to consensus EPS. JP expects near-term earnings to moderate on FX losses and finance costs, with long-term earnings inching up (CLSA, JP, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$5,481mn was up 4.5% y-y (4.1% in constant currency, inside the 3.2-4.7% guided band) and 1.3% q-q, all of it organic. Nomura calls it a marginal miss; no consensus or estimate figure is printed, so the call is judged in-line. North America grew 5.5% cc and Financial Services 11.7% cc. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of US$1,017mn was up 6.4% y-y, with margin at 18.6% (+30bp y-y, +40bp q-q). Gross margin rose 60bp q-q on operational efficiencies, with headcount flat q-q. Adjusted EBIT margin of 16% matched Nomura's estimate, though the headline calls margins a marginal miss. The report tables US$ only, so EBITDA is in US$ mn, not INR. (Nomura)

outlook.note: CTSH cut the top end of its FY26 revenue growth guidance to 4.0-5.0% cc (was 4.0-6.5%) on macro uncertainty, including ~150bp of inorganic contribution. It kept its FY26 adjusted EBIT margin guidance at 16-16.2%. Management flagged cautious discretionary spending in retail, consumer goods and travel, and expects short-cycle revenue to improve in 4Q. Nomura raised FY26-27F EPS by ~1-3% on a lower share count from a larger buyback, and lifted its TP to US$75 (from US$74). Buy retained. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: DET revenue of US$162.5 mn was flat YoY (-0.1%) and down 0.6% QoQ, 0.6% above Kotak's estimate and in line with expectations. Strategic units fell 8.2% cc QoQ (-26.2% YoY) on the energy ramp-down, partly offset by Transportation (+2.6% QoQ) (Kotak, JP, MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2,566 mn (+15.8% YoY, +7.0% QoQ) was 3.6% above Kotak's estimate, and 3.3% above JPMe. The margin rose to 16.7%, with EBIT margin up 80 bps QoQ to 13.2% against Kotak's 12.5%. The beat came from G&A optimisation (down 160 bps QoQ) and a weaker rupee, partly offset by higher S&M spend (Kotak, JP).

outlook.note: Management expects YoY growth only in 2HFY27, so FY27 is likely flat. The 15% EBIT margin target slips by a couple of quarters to 2QFY28. Kotak cuts FY27-29E revenue by 2-4% and trims EPS by up to 1%, while JPM cuts FY28-29E EPS by 4-5%. Positives are the large-deal pipeline at US$300 mn (nine deals) and order intake of US$168 mn (+5% YoY) (Kotak, JP, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 2.9% q-q in constant currency to US$126mn (+15.3% y-y), slightly ahead of Nomura's +2% q-q estimate, led by North America and rest of the world; top-10 clients grew 3.9% q-q. No consensus figure is printed, so the call is vs Nomura's estimate. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR2,652mn (+20% y-y by the table, -6.5% q-q) was at a 23.0% margin (-260bp q-q, -60bp y-y), in line with Nomura's expectation. The q-q dip came from salary hikes (~210bp) and investment in physical assets (~50bp), partly offset by currency and SG&A optimisation. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management expects sequential growth in 2QFY27E and still targets top-quartile industry growth. ACV wins were US$40.8mn (+26% y-y), but FY27 ACV guidance is only matching or modestly exceeding last year's ~US$170mn. The 24-28% EBITDA margin band is intact, with gains to be reinvested. Nomura nudged FY27-28F EPS by ~1% and lifted its TP to INR1,830. It downgraded to Neutral on valuation, with ~12% revenue CAGR expected over FY27-28F (Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$288mn, up 11.2% y-y and 1.8% q-q (cc growth 2.2% q-q, +11% y-y), in line with Nomura's expectation. Growth came from BFS and Telecom & Media among verticals and from Europe among geographies. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR4,513mn (margin 16.6%, +90bp y-y, -10bp q-q); EBIT margin of 12.4% (+20bp q-q) was in line with Nomura's expectation. Operational performance was in line, but reported earnings were hit by one-offs: a contract-termination provision (INR357mn), a regulatory penalty (INR284mn) and a fair-value adjustment (INR76mn). Reported net income fell 2% y-y. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management kept its 10-13% cc y-y revenue growth guidance for FY27E, despite a Healthcare contract termination (about 1.0-1.5% drag), and kept its FY27E EBIT margin guidance at 12.25-12.75%. It won four large deals (ACV above US$5mn) and 12 new logos in 1QFY27, with a healthy pipeline. Nomura changed FY27-28F EPS by 2-5%, raised its target price to INR310 from INR300 and kept Buy. It expects 11.5-12.6% USD revenue growth and EBIT margins of 12.6-13.1% in FY27-28F. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs9.12bn (+3.0% QoQ, +20.0% YoY) was 2.6% below consensus (Rs9.37bn) and 2.5% below MS estimates. The miss came from a ~14% QoQ decline in the TMT vertical, caused by client-specific issues. In constant currency, revenue grew 9.0% YoY and fell 0.3% QoQ. Ex-TMT, growth was +2.7% QoQ, the slowest in 8 quarters (MS, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs1,429mn (15.7% margin) was 17.9% below consensus (Rs1,741mn), though up 39.1% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.8% (+189bps YoY, -526bps QoQ) against MS's 17.8%. Margins were hurt by headcount build-up ahead of revenue (headcount +12-14% YoY) and the wage hike, which was absorbed for only one month. The wage-hike impact will carry into 2Q (MS, GS).

outlook.note: Both brokers cut estimates. MS lowered its USD revenue assumptions by 4.7-9.4% and adj. EBITDA by 12-16% for FY27-29, and now expects FY27 revenue growth to slow to ~10% (14% in FY26) with adj. EBITDA margin broadly flat at 17.7%. GS cut FY27-29E revenue by 4-5% and EBIT by up to 14%, and expects ~3.5% QoQ growth in 2Q. Management expects TMT challenges to ease, with growth returning in 2Q and large-deal ramp-ups supporting 2H. Price targets: MS Rs871 (from Rs1,036), GS Rs810 (from Rs930) (MS, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$3.65bn (-0.5% QoQ cc, +2.6% YoY cc) was 60bps ahead of consensus on a QoQ cc basis, a small beat well inside 2% on the level. IT&BS was flat QoQ and Software was up 2.2%, which offset a 3.7% decline in ER&D. Retail (+5.8%) and BFS (+2.4%) grew, while Telecom fell 7.8% on a large-client reduction (Jeff, JP, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT of Rs58.3bn (+18% YoY) came in line with consensus, with margin up 40bps QoQ to 16.9%. IT&BS margin expanded 70bps while Software margin fell 170bps. Restructuring costs weighed 62bps on margin, and the brokers' FY27 guide of 17.5-18.5% was unchanged (Jeff, JP, GS).
1Q27.vsBasis: consensus (JP text); Jefferies table shows +1% vs its own estimate on both lines

2Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of $3,724mn was 0.6% below consensus and 0.7% below JPMorgan's estimate, so in line. Constant-currency growth was 2.3% QoQ, with Services up 3% (ER&D +4.1%) but Products & Platforms down 5.8% QoQ on a sharp fall in multi-year subscription contracts (JP, Jeff).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT of Rs64.8bn was 3.4% above consensus. Margin rose 130bps QoQ to 18.2%, about 70bps ahead of consensus, led by IT&BS margins up 120bps QoQ and P&P up 250bps, despite 84bps of restructuring costs (JP, Jeff).

outlook.note: FY27 overall revenue guidance was raised to 2.5-4.0% from 1.0-4.0%, and the Services guide to 3-4% from 1.5-4.5%. Stripping out the 65bps inorganic contribution, the Services midpoint is cut by 15bps. The guide implies only 0.1-1.4% QoQ cc growth in 2H, which is soft. The FY27 EBIT margin guide is maintained at 17.5-18.5%. Deal wins of $3.2-3.3bn were up 27% YoY. Jefferies cut FY27-29E US$ revenue by 1-2% and raised EPS by up to 2% on higher margins (Jeff, JP).

companies.name: Hexaware Technologies
companies.note: Weaker-than-expected 6-7% growth guidance for CY26

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$405 mn (+4.4% CC QoQ, +6.1% YoY) was 0.6% below Bloomberg consensus of US$408 mn and 2.3% above JPM's estimate, so in line on the 2% band. JPM headlines it as a revenue miss. Growth was led by Professional services (13%), Healthcare & Insurance (7%), Banking (4%) and Mfg & Consumer (4%), with drags in Tech (-3%) and Travel & Transport (-1%) (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: JPM tables EBIT only, not EBITDA, so EBIT is shown. EBIT of Rs5,236 mn was 4.2% above consensus (Rs5,023 mn) and 3.4% above JPM's estimate. Margin expanded 30 bps QoQ to 13.6%, 50 bps ahead of consensus, with up 59.1% YoY. Net profit missed by 13.5% on FX losses (JP).

outlook.note: CY26 revenue growth guidance was cut by 110 bps at the midpoint to 6-7%, from 7.6% earlier, on delayed deal ramp-ups and a worsening macro. JPM says this implies a 2.7% CQGR over 3Q-4QCY26 and expects consensus earnings cuts. EBIT margin guidance is maintained at 13-14%. Kotak (Sep) adds that CEO Srikrishna Ramakarthikeyan steps down on 28 Oct 2026, a risk that could delay the recovery. Management still targets about 10% YoY growth by the 4QCY26 exit (JP, Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of US$112.5 mn grew 26.5% y/y and 2.6% q/q, about 0.4% above Kotak's estimate and just short of Nomura's US$113 mn. North America and Enterprise Medical Solutions led, while Europe declined q/q; top-client revenue fell 0.8% q/q (Kotak, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,742 mn (+12.2% y/y) was 3.5% below Kotak's estimate. The margin of 16.4% was up 10 bp q/q but down about 400 bp y/y, about 60 bp short of Kotak's estimate, on workforce transformation costs and upfront costs in select GenAI engagements (Kotak, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management expects FY27 organic growth above FY26 and EBITDA margin to normalise to 19-20% by 4QFY27. A US$10 mn+ ACV deal begins contributing revenue from 3QFY27. Kotak sees 2HFY27 EPS growth above 41%, keeps revenue estimates and raises EPS about 1%, and lifts fair value to Rs735 (Buy). Nomura trims its FY27 EBITDA margin by 10 bp to 17.2% and its FY27 revenue estimate about 0.3%, and keeps Neutral with a Rs500 target (Kotak, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of US$5,082mn grew 2.9% YoY and 0.8% QoQ, with constant-currency growth of 1.0% QoQ against consensus and JPM at 2%. Organic revenue was about flat QoQ, as client-specific issues hit Communication (-2.4% QoQ) and Others (-14% QoQ), while Optimum added to Life Sciences (+10.5%) (Jeff, JP, MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs114.1bn rose 15% YoY and 2% QoQ. It was 1% below Jefferies' estimate, since the revenue miss was offset by an EBIT margin of 21.1% (+10bps QoQ) that was in line with consensus. FY27 EBIT margin guidance of 20-22% was retained (Jeff, JP).

outlook.note: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance was cut to 1-3% from 1.5-3.5% (JP/Jeff). That is a cut in organic growth guidance to -0.5-1.5% from 1.25-3.25%, and organic growth would be about -0.1% QoQ in 1Q (MS, JP). Margin guidance was kept at 20-22%. JPM expects consensus earnings cuts after the lowered growth guidance. Large-deal TCV was US$3.6bn, down 5% YoY but up 13% QoQ, and Ashish Kumar Dash was named CEO designate (JP, Jeff, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$97mn (+2.5% QoQ, +12.3% YoY; CC growth slowed to 12% from 12.6% in 4Q26) was 1.1% below the US$98mn consensus. Growth came from the top accounts, with Top-10 accounts up 4.6% QoQ, while revenue from clients outside the Top-10 was flat. Nomura calls it a marginal miss against its US$100mn estimate. (JP, Nomura, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: The report tables EBIT, not EBITDA, so this line is EBIT. EBIT was Rs2,591mn (+23.5% YoY, -2.7% QoQ), 0.7% below consensus. EBITDA margin fell 200bp QoQ to 33%, but was flat at 35% after adjusting for one-off acquisition-related costs. Net profit of Rs1,922mn was 3.0% below consensus. (JP, Jeff)

outlook.note: The TruBridge acquisition closed on 10 July 2026. Management now expects TruBridge steady-state revenue of about US$300mn a year, against about US$340mn originally. Jefferies cut TruBridge's FY27 revenue 14% to US$300mn. EBITDA margins are guided to fall to 26-27% pro forma, then recover to the mid-30s over 18-24 months. JPMorgan cut FY27-28E revenue 4-5% and now expects 12%/14% growth, from 16%/14%. Jefferies cut FY27-29 pro forma revenue 4-6%, expects growth to slow to 7% in FY29, and downgraded to Hold with a Rs1,900 target. Nomura lowered FY27-28F EBITDA margins to about 28% (34% earlier), kept Neutral and raised its target to Rs1,680. (JP, Jeff, Nomura)

companies.name: Just Dial
companies.note: Cash>Market Cap

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 9.9% yoy (6.6% qoq) and came in 3.5% above Kotak's estimate. Realizations rose 6.2% yoy to ~Rs20.5k per campaign and paid campaigns rose 3.5% yoy to ~639k. Implied collections growth accelerated to 13.7% yoy (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs874 mn was 5.4% below Kotak's estimate of Rs924 mn, and margin of 26.7% was down 221 bps qoq against an estimated 29.2%. Employee cost rose 11.0% yoy and other expenses rose 27.9% yoy (13.4% above estimate). Other income of Rs1.3 bn lifted PBT 30% above estimate (Kotak).

outlook.note: After the 27 Aug note on new CEO Dinkar Ayilavarapu, Kotak raises FY2027-29 revenue estimates by 1-4% and the fair value to Rs1,175 from Rs1,100. It expects the new management to push merchant acquisition and B2B growth and to revive collections, which grew 14% yoy in 1QFY27 after 1.6% in FY26. It bakes in no margin expansion because tech, advertising and merchant-acquisition spend must rise. There is no clarity yet on returning the Rs60 bn cash balance (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of 176.8mn was flat to slightly down YoY (-1%) and 2% above GS's estimate. INR sales of Rs16,750mn were in line with Bloomberg consensus (Rs16,671mn). Constant-currency revenue fell 3.6% QoQ, led by Asia (-29% QoQ on project ramp-downs and no seasonal product sales), partly offset by the US (+10.4%) and Europe (+1.2%). (GS, Kotak, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2,878mn was 5.9% below consensus (Rs3,057mn) and down 11% YoY. Margin fell to 17.2% (-393bps QoQ, vs 18.3% consensus) on unanticipated program closures and higher subcontracting costs. The Asia margin dropped 920bps to 9.7%. (GS, Kotak, JP)

outlook.note: Management expects a similar 2Q, a good exit to the year in 4Q and a better 2H than 1H, citing order wins of US$257mn (book-to-bill 1.45x). Margins are expected to inch up each quarter but not return to the normal ~20% even by 4Q. Kotak sees FY27E EBITDA margin of 19.3%, well below the earlier 20.2-21.5% guidance, and cuts FY27 estimates. JPM cuts FY27 EPS by 6.3% on FX losses and JV losses. GS raises FY27-29 EPS by up to 1% with TP unchanged. (GS, JP, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of $310mn was 0.5% above consensus ($308mn) and 0.8% above JPM's estimate. It grew 1.3% QoQ (1.5% CC) as Sustainability (+4.4% QoQ) and Mobility (+2.3%) offset a 3.1% decline in Hitech. The -7.6% YoY is on a base that includes the SWC business ($335mn year-ago); JPM adds SWC back to the 4Q26 figures (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: The report gives only EBIT, not EBITDA. EBIT of Rs4,613mn was 2.6% above consensus (Rs4,498mn). The margin expanded 47bps QoQ to 15.7%, 26bps ahead of consensus, on operating leverage and efficiencies. The year-ago (Rs3,812mn) and prior-quarter (Rs4,352mn) EBIT are not printed. They are backed out of the printed +21.0% YoY and +6.0% QoQ growth rates (JP).

2Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of US$317mn (+2.7% CC QoQ) was 0.7% ahead of consensus (US$315mn) and 1.2% ahead of JPM's US$313mn, so in line. Sustainability grew 4.8% QoQ and Mobility 2.3%, while Hi-Tech slipped 0.7%. The -5.9% YoY decline reflects the divested SWC business. Year-ago EBIT is derived from the printed 24.7% YoY (JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT of Rs4,965mn beat consensus (Rs4,772mn) by 4.0% and JPM's Rs4,800mn by 3.4%. The margin was 16.3%, up 64bps QoQ and 46bps above consensus. Margin drivers were a richer mix toward Sustainability, a larger share of AI-led work, and a higher fixed-price mix. The ~16.5% guide was reached two quarters early (JP, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management is cautiously optimistic as clients start spending on R&D again. It guided to 2H growth better than 1H, about 2% QoQ CQGR over 3Q-4Q, and to double-digit Sustainability growth in FY27. Margins are guided to hold around 16.5% despite a 50-80bps wage-hike headwind in 3Q. JPM raised FY27-29E revenue and EPS by 1-3% and its Sep-27 PT to Rs3,700 from Rs3,300. Nomura cut no estimates, raised FY27-28E EPS by ~3-4% and its TP to Rs3,500 from Rs3,290. Both stay Neutral (JP, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of US$1,224mn was 0.4% above consensus (US$1,219mn) and in line with CLSA's estimate. CC growth was just +0.3% QoQ and +6.4% YoY, with BFSI (+3.1% QoQ) and tech (+3.2% QoQ) offsetting a sharp fall in manufacturing (-6.2% QoQ). (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT of Rs17,993mn was 2.9% above consensus (Rs17,481mn) and 2.5% above CLSA. The margin of 15.5% was up 36bp QoQ and 121bp YoY despite ~100bp of wage-hike impact, helped by operational efficiencies and forex gains. The report gives EBIT only, not EBITDA. (CLSA, Nomura)

2Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of US$1,235mn was +1.0% QoQ and +4.7% YoY (1.1% CC QoQ, 5.1% CC YoY), in line with Bloomberg consensus (+0.2%) and CLSA. BFSI (+3.0% QoQ) and production (+3.6%) offset a 4.1% fall in technology & services; Middle East and a top-client productivity pass-through weighed on hi-tech by about 0.6-0.7%. (CLSA)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: The report tables only EBIT, so the EBITDA line is EBIT: Rs18,381mn, +11.5% YoY and 1.4% below consensus (2.3% below CLSA), which is in line on the 2% band. The EBIT margin of 15.6% was 7bp up QoQ and 29bp down YoY, and 26bp below consensus. PAT missed by 6.2% on FX losses and lower other income. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Management expects 2HFY27 growth to beat 1H and aims for FY27 growth close to FY26's (5.3%), with similar or better EBIT margins in 2H and the Randstad IT deal due to close by end-3Q. Order inflow was weak at US$1.26bn (-21% YoY, book-to-bill 1.0x), and CLSA cut FY27-29 EPS by 3-4% and downgraded to Hold (TP Rs4,403). GS kept its FY27-29E estimates broadly unchanged and stayed Sell, and Nomura moved EPS <1% and downgraded to Neutral. (CLSA, GS, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$471mn (+2.1% QoQ cc, +7.7% YoY) was 0.6% above the Bloomberg consensus of US$468mn and in line with JPMe, led by TMT (+15.5% QoQ on ramp-up of recent deals) while Insurance and Logistics declined QoQ. New deal TCV was US$461mn (+13% QoQ), the third straight quarter above US$400mn. (JP, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported on an EBIT basis because no report tables EBITDA by quarter. EBIT of Rs6,481mn was 5.2% below consensus; the margin of 14.8% fell 60bps QoQ and was 70bps below JPMe/consensus, on ramp-up costs for new deals, the TAP acquisition (35bp impact) and higher forex losses. (JP, Nomura, MS)

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 guidance of high-single-digit to low-double-digit revenue growth and an EBIT margin of 14.75-15.75%. It expects 2QFY27 to be the best QoQ cc growth quarter in three years (about 3%), with the Red Oak consolidation baked in, and total pipeline is up 28% YoY. Nomura trimmed FY27-28F EPS by 1-4% and its TP to INR2,620 (from 2,640), while MS sees consensus EPS largely unchanged. (JP, Nomura, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3.57bn, up 11% YoY, was in line with Jefferies' Rs3.57bn estimate. License revenue grew 48% YoY on a low base, helped by a few large contract closures, and SaaS grew 45%. Services fell 24% on delayed project starts, and India was flat. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs559mn (+24% YoY) was about 2% above Jefferies' estimate, and the margin of 15.7% was up 164bps YoY. Employee costs came in lower than expected, adding about 330bps, but higher non-employee costs offset part of that. Profit (PAT +26% YoY) beat on higher other income. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management says order bookings are healthy and growing in double digits with larger deal sizes, and expects FY27 growth to be better than FY26. Jefferies expects double-digit growth only in FY28 because slower support revenue and weaker implementation revenue are still in the base. It cut FY27/28 revenue estimates by up to 1% (FY27 -1%, FY28 <-1%), raised margin estimates slightly, and moved FY27 EPS +1% and FY28 EPS -1%. PT rolled over to Rs630 from Rs610 on 20x PE. (Jeff)

companies.name: Persistent Systems
companies.note: Management is confident about revenue growth going forward on the back of deal wins and the pipeline. It expects the large tech deal to ramp up from 2Q (75-80% ramp-up) and remain in 3Q, which it believes should aid revenue growth. Deal bookings moderated after an exceptionally strong June quarter performance but remain sufficient to support near-term growth.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$452mn (+3.8% QoQ, +16.1% YoY; 4.1% CC QoQ) was 0.7% above the US$449mn consensus and 0.9% above JPM's estimate. Growth came from Hi-Tech (+7.7% QoQ) and BFSI (+2.3%), while Healthcare was flat (-0.2%). Hi-tech got in-quarter revenue from the mega deal (JP, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs8,022mn (+4.5% QoQ, +31.2% YoY) was 1.1% below the Rs8,111mn consensus. The margin of 18.6% was 47bps below consensus. Lower utilisation (-60bps) and higher AI-tool spend (-20bps) were only partly offset by FX (+30bps) and lower doubtful debts (+20bps). Year-ago EBITDA is not printed in the JPM note, so it is backed out from the printed +31.2% YoY (about Rs6,114mn) (JP, Kotak).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$488mn (+7.8% QoQ, +20.0% YoY) was 1.7% above consensus of US$479mn, so in line on our 2% band, and 1.2% below CLSA's estimate. Growth came from ramp-up of the US$650mn mega deal in hi-tech (tech cos & emerging verticals +13.3% QoQ) and BFSI (+6.8% QoQ). North America grew 10.9% QoQ while Europe fell 10.0% (CLSA, Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT of Rs6,977mn (+19.5% YoY) was in line with CLSA's estimate but 2.4% below consensus of Rs7,145mn. Margin fell 100bp QoQ to 15.0% against consensus of 15.6%, on wage hikes (180bp), lower utilisation (20bp) and about 90bp of mega-deal amortisation, partly offset by currency and SG&A gains. Reported EBIT is used because the CLSA table gives no EBITDA line; net profit missed consensus by 11.7% on higher interest expense and FX losses (CLSA, Kotak, MS).

outlook.note: Management's aspirational EBIT margin is 16-17%, and it expects large-deal amortisation to ease as costs are optimised and revenue scales. Deal wins were soft (ACV +7% YoY, net new ACV +3%) after a strong 1Q, and macro and Middle East conditions slowed decision-making. The Nagarro acquisition is expected to close within 1-2 quarters. Estimates moved in both directions: CLSA cut FY27-29 EPS by 6-9% (target price Rs6,488) and kept its High-Conviction Outperform rating. Nomura cut FY27F EPS by 22% (one-time acquisition cost) but raised FY28F EPS by 3%, and kept Neutral (CLSA, Nomura).

4Q26.revNote: US$ revenue of US$77.4 mn was 0.7% above Kotak's US$76.9 mn estimate and up 157% yoy, including ~US$44 mn from Sojern; organic revenue grew ~13% yoy, with DaaS up 14.1%, MarTech (organic) up 29% and distribution down 21.4% (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,470 mn was 18.1% above Kotak's Rs1,245 mn estimate; margin rose 440 bps qoq to 20.5% (vs 17.5% est.) on Sojern cost synergies realized ahead of timeline and rupee tailwinds, and includes Rs209 mn of deferred Sojern consideration (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guides FY2027 revenue of Rs30-31 bn (65-70% yoy; US$310-320 mn, with 12-15% organic growth) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.5-22.5% ex earn-out, and says it will keep a conservative approach to the guide. Kotak raised FY2027-28E EBITDA margin by 190-210 bps and EPS by ~21-25%, though it expects growth to slow to mid-single digits from 4QFY27 on full Sojern consolidation and keeps SELL with FV Rs600 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$208mn (+15.2% YoY, -6.4% CC QoQ) was 1.1% above consensus and in line with JPMorgan's estimate. The QoQ decline was seasonal (open enrolment); underlying growth ex-seasonality was 5.1% organic CC QoQ. (JP, Kotak, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4,665mn (+34.8% YoY) was 1.7% above consensus. Margin was 23.8% (+127bps YoY). Adjusted margin fell 90bps QoQ to 24% on wage hikes (50bps), the Karnataka/Telangana minimum wage revision (40bps) and weaker operating leverage (100bps), partly offset by FX tailwinds (100bps). (JP, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 low double-digit organic revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25%. The margin guide now includes a 120bps hit from statutory minimum wage revisions, and JP says margins are no longer expected at the upper end. Deal wins had ACV of US$35mn (+10% YoY) and 27 net new clients were added. Estimates: JP FY27 revenue +1% with margins -30bps and EPS -1%. Jeff raised EPS 1-4% and Kotak raised EPS 2-3%. Jeff and Kotak raised their targets to Rs54 and JP kept Rs58. (JP, Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs722.8bn was 0.3% above consensus and 0.6% above JPM's estimate. Constant-currency growth was a soft 0.4% QoQ, but India grew 7.6% QoQ and drove the small beat, while international revenue fell 0.1% CC QoQ as geopolitical uncertainty led clients to defer projects (JP, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT of Rs173.2bn was 0.3% below consensus and 1.3% above JPM's estimate. Margin fell 130bps QoQ to 24.0%, because wage hikes cost 170bps and FX and efficiencies recovered only 40bps. That is broadly in line with consensus and about 20bps ahead of JPM; GS put it 40bps below its own estimate (JP, GS).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of US$7.6bn grew 0.5% QoQ in constant currency against consensus and JPMorgan estimates of 0.6% and 0.4%. Growth in international markets (+1.1-1.2% QoQ) and the UK (+3.5%) was offset by a 10% QoQ decline in India (Jeff, JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT margin was flat QoQ at 24.0%, down about 120bps YoY. It was roughly 20bps below consensus, with JPMorgan putting the miss at 20bps and Goldman at 50bps vs Visible Alpha, so the EBIT line is in line. Subcontracting costs rose 80bps QoQ, and employee-cost gains of 100bps were offset by higher overheads. Jefferies expects margins to fall further once the BSNL deal starts in 3Q (Jeff, JP, GS).

outlook.note: Deal TCV of US$9.6bn was down 4% YoY, and headcount rose by about 4K. GS expects 3Q revenue growth of +0.5% QoQ, with EBIT margin up 20bps to 24.2%. It sees FY27E organic growth of 2.3% and a margin 80bps lower YoY, as investments and competition continue to weigh. Jefferies expects margins to fall further once the BSNL deal starts in 3Q. JP says estimate changes will depend on the call commentary. (GS, Jeff, JP)

companies.name: Tata Elxsi
companies.note: Management remains optimistic about improved performance during the rest of the year with gradual margin expansion. ided by the ramp-up of large deals, lower revenue leakages in large programs and a promising deal pipeline. However, we note that the company’s growth in the past several quarters has remained volatile due to the weakness inJLR contributes 24% of revenues, and the limited visibility due to business challenges remains a key risk. The stock trades at an expensive 25X FY2028E EPS auto and steep a decline in the healthcare vertical. European auto OEMs remain under pressure, while the top account is likely to stabilize near the current levels.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue Rs10.2bn (US$ via the report's Rs94.80/US$), in line with MSe and FactSet consensus (-0.2%); cc growth +1.3% QoQ with Media +2.9% while Transportation (-0.4%) and Healthcare (-0.3%) stayed soft (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA 13% below consensus: margin fell 346bp QoQ to 21.2% on ~150bp of temporary costs and higher other expenses; EBIT missed consensus by 12.2% (MS).

2Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of US$110.3 mn was up 5.9% yoy and 2.5% qoq, 1.2% above Kotak's estimate, with broad-based growth: media & communications +3.4% qoq, healthcare +3.5% and transportation +2%. The US grew 7.4% qoq while Europe fell 1.1% (Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2,314 mn was 5.4% above Kotak's estimate, with the margin at 21.9% (EBIT margin up 70 bps qoq to 19.7%). Drivers were the absence of one-time costs, cross-currency tailwinds of 60-70 bps and utilization rising to 78% from 74.7%, which more than offset wage hikes (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management expects improved revenue growth in 2H on large-deal ramp-up, lower revenue leakage and a promising pipeline, with gradual margin expansion. Near-term growth is exposed to furloughs, and Europe auto remains weak. Kotak raised FY27-29E revenue estimates ~3% and EPS 2-3%, lifted fair value to Rs3,200 from Rs3,000, and kept SELL (Kotak).

companies.name: Tata Technologies
companies.note: EBIT. Management also guided for continued expansion in margins going forward as it enjoys operating leverage benefits. FY27 org guide of strong DD maintained. Management reiterated its guidance of strong double-digit organic CC revenue growth in FY27 on the back of deal ramp-ups and strong pipeline.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs16.6bn was 3% above Visible Alpha consensus and GS's estimate, up 5.9% QoQ. Services grew 4.3% CC QoQ on ramp-up of recently won large deals, and Technology Solutions grew 4.3% QoQ on the education business (GS, Kotak, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.67bn was 1% above consensus, so in line. The margin of 16.1% was 36bps below consensus and 44bps below GS, as upfront large-deal investments and a lower gross margin in tech solutions offset rupee depreciation. Management dropped its earlier 18% exit-margin guidance in favour of a more gradual expansion (GS, JP, Kotak).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs16,988mn was in line with Visible Alpha consensus (0%) and 1% below GS's estimate. It grew +28.4% YoY and +2.1% QoQ (+1.9% QoQ in constant currency). Services revenue rose 23.6% YoY to Rs12,514mn, while Technology Solutions rose 10.5% YoY. [GS]
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2,733mn was 1% below consensus, which counts as in line, and 3% below GS's estimate. Margin was 16.1%, 10bps below consensus and 34bps lower YoY. GS calls it a slight margin miss. Services EBIT margin was 32.6%, and VW softness at the recently acquired ES-Tec (about 10% of revenue) weighs on profitability. [GS]

outlook.note: Management expects sequential growth to continue through FY27, helped by a US$138mn full-vehicle deal with a leading luxury European OEM that starts ramping in H2 FY27. It also reiterated double-digit organic revenue growth guidance for FY27 and expects sequential margin improvement from the 16.1% level in 2Q27, even though 3Q27E is seasonally weak. VW weakness is a near-term drag on ES-Tec growth and margins. GS cut FY27/FY28 EPS by 7%/5%, raised FY29 by 4% and lifted its TP to Rs560 from Rs540, with a Sell rating. [GS]

companies.name: Tech Mahindra
companies.note: EBIT. With strong performance in 1HF27, we see room for company to report F27 revenue growth ahead of MSe and consensus expectations. Its orderbook continued to grow strongly, up 25% YoY,despite no mega deal winsthis quarter. Management reiterated its stance of achieving a 15% EBIT margin in FY27 with revenue growth of more than double the industry revenue growth rate. Itwould like to focus on market share gains without sacrificing margins. TechM excelled with strong execution on multiple fronts driving beat on growth, margins and deal wins. Growth was broad-based across geos, verticals, clients and service-lines.

2Q27.revNote: US$ revenue of $1,693mn was 1.0% above Bloomberg consensus ($1,677mn) and 0.2% above CLSA. Growth was +2.4% QoQ / +7.2% YoY in constant currency, ahead of the 1.9% CLSA expected, and was led by telecom (+5.8% QoQ) and retail/travel/logistics (+9.9% QoQ). Manufacturing fell on a ramp-down with EU auto customers. (CLSA, MS)
