2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBIT is shown here, not EBITDA, to match the row's earlier quarters. At Rs23,871mn it was 2.8% above consensus (Rs23,231mn). The 14.8% margin was +34bp QoQ and +261bp YoY, and 27bp above consensus. The beat came mainly from lower SG&A, with Project Fortius savings and volume growth partly offset by wage hikes. (CLSA, Nomura)

outlook.note: Management reiterated its FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% and 90-100% FCF-to-PAT conversion. It guides to normal 2H seasonality, with about 0.5% revenue headwind from a European auto client in 3Q. It expects BFSI growth to re-accelerate to 8%+ next quarter. Deal wins were $1,023mn (+25% YoY, -5% QoQ), the fourth straight quarter above $1bn. Estimate changes were minor (Nomura FY27-28 EPS about +1%; CLSA TP Rs1,463 to Rs1,494), with ratings unchanged. (Nomura, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: IT services revenue of US$2,615mn fell 1.4% QoQ (-1.2% CC) and rose 1.0% YoY. Total revenue of US$2,626mn was 0.7% below consensus (US$2,645mn) and 0.4% below CLSA's estimate. Energy, manufacturing & resources and healthcare declined most, and the 2Q guide of -1.5% to +0.5% CC QoQ is weak. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBIT of Rs38,427mn was 6.3% below consensus and 9.1% below CLSA's estimate. Margin was 15.7% against 16.6% consensus, down 148bp QoQ and 36bp YoY. Management cited two months of salary hikes, AI investments and large-deal ramp-ups. Morgan Stanley also put EBIT 6% below consensus. The EBIT figure is consolidated, as CLSA does not table an IT-services-only EBIT. (CLSA, MS)

2Q27.revNote: IT services revenue of US$2,612 mn was down 0.1% QoQ and up 0.3% YoY (flat CC QoQ, +0.6% CC YoY), 0.6% above consensus and 0.5% above JPM's estimate. BFSI (+1.0% CC QoQ), Consumer (+2.6%) and Energy/Manufacturing (+1.1%) grew, while Healthcare (-3.8%) and Tech (-2.6%) declined. (JP, Kotak)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: IT services EBIT of Rs40,726 mn was 1.3% above consensus and 7.7% higher YoY. Margin expanded 50 bps QoQ to 16.5%, against consensus of 16.0%, helped by operational efficiencies and rupee depreciation. Management gave no timeline for returning to the 17-17.5% band. (JP, Kotak)

outlook.note: 3Q27 CC QoQ revenue guide of -1.5% to +0.5% reflects seasonal furloughs and no change in demand versus 1Q. JP calls it weak (JPMe -2% to 0%), while Nomura sees it in line with its estimate. Deal TCV was weak at US$2.6bn (-23% QoQ, -45% YoY) as two signings slipped into 3Q. Management targets margins gradually rising toward the 17-17.5% band. JP raised FY27-29E earnings by 1% and margins by 20-30bps; Nomura raised FY27-28F EPS by 5.2-5.5% (buyback) and its TP to INR200. (JP, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 49% yoy to Rs7.3 bn, about 2% above Kotak's estimate of Rs7.2 bn. SSSG accelerated to 39% from 34% in 4Q, and the note puts the revenue beat at 2%. The 2% gap is borderline, so the line is classed in-line against the broker estimate. Growth came from broad-based SSSG, 21% consumer base growth and a 41% AOV rise on gold price inflation. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA of Rs548 mn (+134% yoy) was about 4% above Kotak's Rs527 mn estimate. Margin was 7.5% against 7.3% estimated, up 270 bps yoy, on contribution margin expansion (+85 bps yoy to 32.7%) and operating leverage. The note uses Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA because reported EBITDA is Rs854 mn after inventory gains. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 store-addition guidance of 20% (~70 net new stores) and targets 50% medium-term revenue CAGR and ~15% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin (7.5% now). It sees growth momentum strengthening as gold prices stabilise. Demand dipped in May after the customs duty hike to 15% from 6%, then recovered, and July trends are in line with June. Kotak raised FY27-29E revenue by 4-7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA by 7-11%, and lifted fair value to Rs800 from Rs625. It also cut the rating to ADD from BUY after a 50% share price rise. It forecasts SSSG of 19%/16% in FY27E/28E, well below management's aspiration. (Kotak)

companies.name: International Gemmological Institute
companies.note: The certification market (by volume) is projected to expand at a 17-19% CAGR over CY25-30, per management. Guidance of 15% top-line growth and 20% EBITDA growth for F27 reiterated. Management emphasized that the growth would be volume-led.

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 21% yoy and was ~4.2% above Kotak's estimate. Certification revenue rose 21%, with LGD up 35% on new customer additions and capacity adds at growers. ASP rose 3.7% on a richer mix, and volumes rose 16%. The AGL acquisition added ~2pp to growth (two months of consolidation). (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA grew ~21% yoy and was ~6.1% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 64.0%, down 20 bps yoy but 415 bps above the prior quarter. Standalone margin fell to 74.2% on higher commissions to Dubai and the US plus ~Rs25 mn of AGL deal costs. Subsidiary margins expanded 275 bps. AGL added ~3pp to EBITDA growth. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 23% YoY to Rs3.7bn, 8% above FactSet consensus (2% above MS). Growth was led by 21% YoY volume growth in standalone, with LGD loose stones +38% and LGD jewellery +30% in standalone, and the AGL consolidation added about 3% (organic growth 20%). (MS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA rose 29% YoY, 7% above consensus (4% above MS). Margin expanded 269bps YoY to 60.4%. Strong subsidiary profitability, up 27ppts on the US business traction, offset a 416bps YoY standalone margin decline from higher commission payouts, marketing (IPL) and headcount costs. Organic EBITDA growth was 27%. (MS, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue and 20% EBITDA growth, with AGL adding a further 2-3% to top-line growth. Pricing has been stable since May 2024, grower capacity is expanding (growers expect to double in three years), and EBITDA margin is expected to stabilise in the 60-64% range. Kotak raised EPS by 2-4% and fair value to Rs400 (from Rs380). (MS, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs213.6bn, about 0.4% below Bloomberg consensus of Rs214.5bn, and 7% above MS's own estimate. Jewellery sales grew 38% YoY on domestic growth of 38%, with studded growth strong. The top line was already known from the business update. (MS, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs28.9bn (+58% YoY) was 29% above consensus, but this flattered by one-offs. These were Rs4.07bn of inventory gains after the gold import duty hike and about 80bps from domestic/global gold price mismatches. Adjusted for these, GS and MS call the quarter in line, with Tanishq domestic EBIT margin at 10.9%. (MS, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs23.6bn rose 37% YoY but fell 9% QoQ and came in 2% below JPM's estimate, so it is in line. The Gas terminal division grew 38% YoY to Rs21.8bn (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs7.1bn (+197% YoY, +14% QoQ) was 27% above JPM's estimate. Gas division operating income rose 335% YoY to Rs5.8bn, with margin at 26.4% vs 8.4% a year ago. Liquid division margin also improved to 61.5% from 55.8% a year ago. Adj. PAT of Rs4.8bn beat JPM (Rs3.6bn) and the Street (Rs3.7bn) (JP).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs25.9bn (+52% YoY, +50% QoQ) was 37% above JPMorgan's estimate of Rs19.0bn. The gas terminal division drove it, with revenue up 65% YoY to Rs24.1bn and distribution volumes up 72% YoY. The liquid terminal division fell 24% YoY. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs6.2bn (+53% YoY, +110% QoQ) was 51% above JPMorgan's Rs4.1bn. Gas division EBITDA rose 170% YoY. Overall EBITDA/t of Rs3,455 (+155% YoY) was well ahead of JPMorgan's Rs1,501, likely on pricing and efficiency gains. Liquids EBITDA fell 38% YoY and came in 35% below JPMorgan's estimate. (JP)

outlook.note: JPM expects upward consensus EPS revisions for FY27/28E after the beat. It sees multiple earnings tailwinds: capacity commissioning in 1HFY27, procurement efficiencies and lower freight costs, market-share gains after the KGPL LPG pipeline starts, 9 more LPG pipeline projects under consideration, and a reported 30-day LPG storage buffer in India. The earnings call details were not yet available (JP).

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs22.6bn were down 1.1% YoY and 1.5% above Jefferies' estimate. EXIM volumes fell 2% YoY while domestic volumes rose 6%, trailing a 7% rise in port container volumes (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.2bn was 6.3% below Jefferies' estimate and down 1.5% YoY. Margin was 18.6% against 18.7% a year ago and 20.2% estimated, the lowest since Mar-21. Higher domestic empty-running costs hurt even though the land license fee (LLF) was lower. JPMorgan also called the quarter an earnings miss (Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue was flat YoY and 1%/2% below JPMe/BBGe: handling volumes grew 9% (EXIM +10%), but handling realizations fell 8% YoY and EXIM realizations fell 3%, so volume did not turn into revenue growth (JP, GS, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 2% YoY and was 1% below JPMe, with the margin up 41bps YoY to 20.2%. EXIM EBIT margin gained 108bps YoY to 21.8% on lower empty running costs, while domestic EBIT margin recovered QoQ to 3.5% but was below 5.0% a year ago. GS saw it as weak against its Rs4.9bn estimate; Jeff saw it 19% above JEFe (JP, GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 volume growth guidance to 15% for EXIM (from 8%) and 25% for domestic (from 15%), 18% overall (from 9.5%), on DFC commissioning from Q2 and a claimed 160bps market share gain. Jeff raises FY27-28E EBITDA by 1-4% and its PT to Rs650; GS lifts its PT to Rs480 but calls the guidance optimistic given monsoon and competition, and JP expects no major consensus revisions (Jeff, GS, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 28% YoY to Rs29.3bn, in line with JPMe and Street. Express parcel volumes rose 55% YoY and PTL tonnage 18% YoY, with express revenue +33% and PTL revenue +25%; the quarter's yields were also firm (JP). MS calls the top line good, with PTL revenue beating MSe by ~5% on better yields (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY to Rs1.42bn, ~25% below Street (Rs1.9bn) and 23% below JPMe, and the margin was 4.9% against 6.5% a year ago. Diesel price hikes since mid-May, tight labour and higher statutory minimum wages cost an estimated Rs1.2bn (~4% of sales). Adj. EBITDA margin was 2.6% against 5.3% in 4Q and 3.3% a year ago (JP). MS also flags missed service EBITDA and adj. EBITDA margins (MS).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 30% YoY to Rs28.5bn, 1% above JPMe, driven by Express Parcel shipments up 73% YoY to 306mn and Part Truck Load tonnage up 20%. JPM says it was ahead of JPMe/BBG consensus, but no revenue consensus figure is printed. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs2.14bn rose 80% YoY and was about 9% above Street (Rs1.97bn) and 6% above JPMe (Rs2.02bn). Express Parcel service EBITDA margin rose to 18.8% and PTL service EBITDA margin to 13.5%. (JP)
4Q26.vsBasis: EBITDA: consensus (Street Rs1.97bn); revenue: broker estimate (JPMorgan, JPMe Rs28,092mn),

outlook.note: Management guided FY27 express parcel volume growth of 20-30% and PTL tonnage growth of 18-22%, and expects the cost impact to be offset in 2Q through price revisions and yield increases. Management also kept its medium-term margin guidance unchanged. JP's FY27-29E EBITDA is largely unchanged (FY27E trimmed 1%), but it cuts its target multiple from 29x to 26x and PT to Rs590 from Rs650. MS cuts FY27E and FY28E adj. EBITDA by 18% and 7% on slower margin recovery, and trims PT to Rs500 from Rs510 (JP, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs5,493 mn were flat YoY (-0.2%) and 2.0% below Kotak's estimate. Ex-Snowman Logistics, revenue fell 4% YoY, with rail throughput down 5.4% and CFS throughput down 7.8%, as imports were hit in April and May by the West Asia crisis (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs1,171 mn was 3.8% above Kotak's estimate but down 1.9% YoY. Ex-Snowman EBITDA fell 7% YoY to Rs885 mn, in line with the estimate (-0.3%). Margin was hurt by higher empty running, fuel costs, minimum wages and a trade imbalance that cut double stacking to 38% from 42%+ (Kotak).

outlook.note: Kotak cut estimates by 6% on lower volumes and EBITDA per TEU, and cut fair value to Rs75 from Rs82. Management expects margins to improve in both segments as the West Asia effect recedes and CFS pricing rises. Catalysts are the full WDFC commissioning to JNPT, the Ankleshwar and Indore ICD starts and the Jaipur ICD ruling due in September 2026. Kotak keeps BUY (Kotak).

companies.name: Shadowfax
companies.note: Management raised its F27 growth expectation from 27-30% YoY to 38-40% YoY, and we see potential for a positive surprise given a good start to the year (1Q 64% YoY).

1Q27.ebitdaNote: absorbed cost inflation as well as high investments but still better than expected margins

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 30% yoy, in line with Kotak's estimate (+0.2%). India security grew 37% (1.4% ahead of estimates) on education, healthcare, e-commerce and BFSI wins. International grew 31% on defense and aviation wins, and FM grew 8%. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.1 bn was up 36% yoy and flat qoq, 2.9% behind Kotak's estimate. International margin of 3.5% (versus the 3.9% estimate) disappointed, partly offset by India and FM. Group margin was 4.5%, up 21 bps yoy. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Kotak raises revenue estimates by 1-3%: India business by 2-4% over FY2027-28, plus about 3% in international on currency appreciation over FY2027-29. The Rs1 bn buyback (max price about Rs478.5) and the Labor Code migration of about 15,000 contracts should support margins and working capital. Fair value rises to Rs450 (from Rs430) with ADD maintained. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs3,120 mn rose 8.8% YoY and were 3.6% above JEFe, helped by a 3% volume beat; volumes rose 7% YoY and blended realisations rose 1.4%. Surface Express (83% of revenue) grew 8.7% YoY, while multimodal segments grew 10-63% off a low base. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs336 mn rose 12.4% YoY and was 21% above JEFe, driven by the volume beat and operating leverage. Margin was 10.8% vs 9.2% estimated, which offset pressure from fuel price hikes. This is the third consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth. (Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs3,268 mn rose 6.3% YoY on 5% volume growth, but came in 2.6% below JEFe's Rs3,355 mn. Multimodal businesses (air, rail, C2C, e-commerce) drove the growth. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs331 mn (+17.6% YoY, margin 10.1%) was 5.6% above JEFe, helped by about Rs30 mn of lease expenses shifted below EBITDA under accounting standards. Adjusted for that, EBITDA would have been 4% below JEFe. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management guides for 11-12% YoY FY27E volume growth vs 10% earlier, led by business development and strong demand momentum. Sep-26Q should see the full impact of price hikes passed on for diesel costs (+9%). Capex plan is Rs1.3-1.4 bn in FY27E, with 40+ sorting centres planned vs 28 in FY26. Jefferies raised FY27E EPS 6% to Rs25.6 and lifted PT to Rs770 from Rs635, with a Buy rating. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs6.04bn rose 8% YoY (+5% QoQ). Print ad revenue (65% of the total) grew 11% YoY, led by non-metro Hindi print and better advertiser sentiment. Radio ad revenue fell 2% and circulation was flat. CLSA says all lines were above its estimate (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.36bn rose 23% YoY and 31% QoQ, and margin widened 3ppt YoY to 22.6%. SG&A and other costs fell 2% YoY, which offset raw material costs up 12% YoY on higher newsprint prices (+13% YoY, +8% QoQ). CLSA says it was above its estimate (CLSA).

outlook.note: Management said ad demand was strong and broad based, led by real estate, jewellery, FMCG and government. Newsprint prices rose 8-13% on supply disruptions. CLSA left FY27-29 forecasts unchanged, kept its O-PF rating and Rs290 target, and calls the stock cheap at 9x FY28 PE with Rs12.4bn cash (CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs4.3bn (+8% QoQ, -14% YoY) was in line with CLSA's estimate. The YoY decline reflects deconsolidation of Nodwin from Aug 25; adjusted for that, revenue grew 9% YoY, with Adtech up 41% QoQ (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Ebitda of Rs465m (-40% QoQ, -2% YoY) was 10% below CLSA's estimate. Margin fell 9ppt QoQ to 10.8% as advertising and promotion spend jumped 38% QoQ (CLSA).

outlook.note: CLSA cuts FY27CL net profit by 42.3% (revenue and Ebitda forecasts unchanged) to factor in an exceptional item. It flags equity dilution ahead, with a board meeting on 6 Aug to consider fund raising for the accelerated Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition (US$303m). The stock looks expensive at 48x FY28CL PE, so CLSA retains U-PF with a TP of Rs215. Bluetile and BestPlay's combined revenue and Ebitda (Rs5,180m/Rs550m) are tracking ~120% of Nazara's current scale, with the deal valued at est. 13x EV/Ebitda against Nazara's 32x (CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs14.2bn (+13% YoY, +68% QoQ) was ~10% above Kotak's Rs12.9bn estimate. The sports/IPL franchise business grew 33% YoY to Rs6.3bn (~21% beat) on a later IPL start, SRH's 4th-place finish and higher central revenue and sponsorship. Ad revenue fell 2.6% YoY to Rs2.8bn (~8% above estimate) and domestic subscription rose 3.3% to Rs4.9bn (in line). CLSA also put revenue 15% above its estimate. (Kotak, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA is EBIT plus depreciation plus movie amortisation (Rs6,422mn + 290 + 618), derived from Kotak's table because the note prints no total EBITDA line. CLSA's Rs7.3bn (+19% YoY) matches. It was ~24% above Kotak's Rs5.9bn estimate. EBIT rose 25% YoY to Rs6.4bn (~31% beat), with direct costs down 4.7% and SG&A down 3%. Core TV EBITDA excluding cricket was +11.8% at Rs3.6bn, and cricket operating profit +25-26% at Rs3.1bn. (Kotak, CLSA)

4Q26.revNote: Total revenue of Rs8.5 bn was down 6.7% yoy but in line with Kotak's estimate (+0.2%). Ad revenue fell 10% yoy (~2.4% miss) on subdued FMCG spending and likely share loss to the leader, and cricket revenue fell 45% on a later IPL start. Domestic subscription grew 10.5% yoy (~1.6% beat). (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA is derived as EBIT plus depreciation plus movie amortization, since Kotak's table does not print a total EBITDA. It is about 2.5% below Kotak's estimate, so treated as in line given the broker's 'in-line quarter' verdict. EBIT of Rs2.9 bn (-8.9% yoy) was ~2.2% above estimate on better cost control. Core-business adjusted EBITDA of Rs3.1 bn (ex-cricket, after movie amortization) was ~7.4% above estimate. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 6-7%, driven by sports forecasts and lower core costs, and lifted fair value to Rs750 from Rs740. It sees no recovery in core ad revenue near term because of the TV-to-digital shift, ad budgets moving to sports, and Middle East war and RMG-ban pressure. Tight cost control should hold core profitability. CLSA kept its forecasts and Rs615 target (12% EPS CAGR FY26-29CL), noting about 80% of market cap is the IPL franchise. (Kotak, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs19.1bn (+4.5% YoY) was 2.8% below Kotak's Rs19.6bn estimate. Ad revenue fell 11.5% YoY to Rs6.7bn on the Middle East conflict and weak April-May, and subscription revenue grew 15.8% on higher linear pricing, digital subscribers and ARPU. CLSA also called revenue about 3% below its estimate. (Kotak, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 65% YoY to Rs789mn and margin fell 840bps to 4.1%, but it was in line with Kotak's Rs776mn estimate. Programming costs rose on the FIFA WC and content investments, and A&P spend rose 62% on FIFA and the sports channel launch. Core EBITDA fell 75% to Rs745mn. (Kotak, CLSA)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs20.2bn fell 7% YoY and 11% QoQ, 3% below CLSA's estimate. Domestic advertising was down 3% YoY (Rs7.6bn, also 3% below estimate), subscriptions rose 4% YoY to Rs9.2bn (in line), and other/movie revenue fell 47% YoY. (CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA was a loss of Rs2.7bn against a Rs2.9bn profit a year ago, because accelerated movie-rights amortisation (50% in the first two years) caused a one-time Rs3bn hit. Total costs rose 21% YoY. CLSA's headline calls it an 'Ebitda loss'. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Management is cautiously optimistic, citing a June ad recovery, FIFA-led subscription growth and the festive season. It gave no margin guidance, and FIFA will lift both revenue and cost in 2Q. Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 5-6% on higher content costs and trimmed fair value to Rs110. The SEBI order on the promoter warrants (appeal filed with SAT) clouds the funding timeline, while the JioStar arbitration outcome is likely in 3Q. (Kotak, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs15.0 bn (+43.1% yoy, +28.2% qoq) were 4.6% above Kotak's estimate. Consolidated volumes rose 3.8% yoy to 55.5 kt, led by plastic and copper (copper 4.1 kt vs nil a year ago). Lead volumes fell 5% yoy to 43.9 kt on Middle East supply disruption (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA of Rs1.4 bn (+24.5% yoy) was 1.4% below Kotak's estimate, which the broker called a miss. Product mix shifted toward lower-margin copper and lead volumes were lower. EBITDA margin was 9.2% vs 9.8% estimated, and PAT of Rs1,009 mn was 1.2% below estimate (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management expects the scrap shortage to continue into 2QFY27, with only gradual relief as it diversifies sourcing; lead utilisation is ~50% vs the ~70% norm, and the rubber expansion is postponed. Copper margins are targeted to rise from Rs55/kg to Rs65-75/kg over 2-3 years. Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 8-9% and fair value to Rs1,765 from Rs1,910, and maintains ADD (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales of Rs848bn were up 32% YoY and 9% QoQ. They were 1% below Visible Alpha consensus (5% below MSe), so in line with consensus. Higher LME aluminium prices drove most of the growth, partly offset by lower copper volumes (-15% YoY) from maintenance shutdowns (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs139bn (+76% YoY, margin 16.4%) was 26% above VA consensus (~Rs110bn) and 17% above MSe (Rs119bn). Domestic aluminium EBITDA of Rs77bn was 15% above MSe, helped by a record EBITDA/t of US$2,331. Copper EBITDA of Rs9.2bn was 15% above MSe on strong sulphuric acid realizations. Novelis adjusted EBITDA of Rs48.8bn was 12% above MSe (MS).

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated net sales of Rs781bn (+20.4% YoY, +17.5% QoQ) were 7.2% above Kotak's estimate. Higher aluminium volumes and prices, plus higher sulphuric acid realisations in copper, drove the beat; Novelis' reported EBITDA stayed hit by the Oswego fires. India net sales rose 34.3% YoY (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs101.8bn (+5.9% YoY, +27.6% QoQ) beat Kotak's estimate by 20.4%, with beats in both aluminium and copper. India aluminium EBITDA was Rs51.8bn (+9.3% YoY) on better volumes and margins. India copper EBITDA of Rs9.1bn (+48% YoY) was an all-time high on sulphuric acid realisations. Jefferies also put EBITDA 11% above its estimate (Kotak, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management expects aluminium downstream volumes and external alumina sales to improve from 2QF27, and copper volumes to rebound from 2Q as maintenance ends. Downstream EBITDA of >US$300/t is not sustainable and US$250/t is the more sustainable level. Aluminium cash costs are likely to rise another 5-6% QoQ in 2Q on higher coal prices. Hindalco has hedged 29% of F27 aluminium volumes at US$3,004/t and 21% of F28 at US$3,160/t. The new Birla group brand royalty is small (about 1% of F27 EBITDA). All projects are on track, and net debt/EBITDA is expected to stay around 2x. MS flags 'modest revision higher' to consensus EPS and maintains OW, with a Rs1,140 target. Kotak (Novelis) says the worst

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs137.5 bn were 10.1% above Kotak's estimate (+77% yoy, +1% qoq), helped by higher lead/silver volumes, including ex-10kt of lead concentrate sales (about 9 tons of silver equivalent), and higher realisations (LME zinc +30% yoy, silver US$70/oz vs US$34). Zinc volumes rose 5% yoy. No consensus figure is printed. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs80.5 bn (+109% yoy, +4% qoq) was 4.3% above Kotak's estimate, on higher lead/silver volumes from external lead concentrate sales and lower costs. Zinc CoP was US$851/t, the lowest in nine years, on higher by-product (sulphuric acid) realisations, and margin rose 160 bps qoq to 59%. Jefferies also calls it a 6% beat vs JEFe. (Kotak, Jeff)

2Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs150.9 bn (+77% yoy, +10% qoq) were 5.8% above Kotak's Rs142.7 bn estimate, helped by zinc volumes +5.9% yoy, lead volumes +13.2% yoy, silver volumes +18% yoy, and LME zinc prices +33% yoy to US$3,776/t (Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs92.5 bn (+108% yoy, +15% qoq) beat Kotak's Rs87.6 bn estimate by 5.6%, as higher sulfuric acid by-product prices, lead concentrate sales and silver lowered the zinc cost of production to a nine-year low of US$703/t (-29% yoy). EBITDA margin was 61% vs 52% a year ago (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management cut FY27 zinc CoP guidance to US$825-850/t from US$975-1,000/t on sulfuric acid realizations, and reiterated silver production guidance of ~680 tons. A further ~0.6 mtpa expansion is likely to be announced toward end-FY2027, though 3/5 of operating mines (65%+ of ore output) expire in 2030. Kotak raised EBITDA estimates +17.6%/+0.5%/-1.6% for FY27/28/29 but kept SELL with Fair Value Rs500 on rich valuations (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs53.0 bn were 4.1% above Kotak's estimate and up 39.3% yoy, helped by aluminum realizations of US$3,930/ton (+41% yoy) and LME aluminum at US$3,561/ton, with volumes flat at 113k tons; alumina volumes rose 14% yoy but realizations fell 21% (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs27.1 bn beat Kotak's estimate by 5.7% (+81% yoy, +15.2% qoq), led by the aluminum division, where EBITDA of Rs23.7 bn (+157% yoy) came from lower costs (US$1,707/ton vs US$1,885 estimated) and better realizations. Alumina EBITDA of Rs3.4 bn (-41% yoy) was a partial offset on weak realizations (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27/28 alumina volume guidance of ~0.2/0.8 mn tons. The 1 mtpa refinery is to be commissioned by Nov-Dec 2026. Alumina realizations are expected to improve ~US$40-50/ton qoq in 2QFY27, and captive coal is ramping to 4.8 mtpa, which should keep aluminum costs near peak levels. Kotak raised FY28/29 EBITDA estimates by 2.7%/3.7%, upgraded to BUY from REDUCE and lifted fair value to Rs420 from Rs410. Capex for the 0.5 mtpa smelter only picks up from FY2029E (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs67.9bn (+1% YoY) was 3% below Bloomberg consensus and 1% below GS, as blended realization of Rs5,794/t was down 1% YoY and lower than expected on sales volume of 11.7mt (+1.8% YoY). JPM also noted revenue fell short of consensus on lower other mineral sales (GS, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs24.7bn was flat YoY and 4% below consensus, though 6% above GS on lower than expected cost of materials (margin 254bps above GSe). EBITDA/t of Rs2,105 rose 22% QoQ but fell 2.2% YoY. JPM saw a 7% beat vs Street, with higher royalty per tonne a negative (GS, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 61% YoY, 22% above JPMorgan's estimate and 27% growth vs the BBG consensus, on 21% higher volumes (15.3 mt) and a 33% rise in ASP to Rs7,303/t, with HRC sales likely recognised from NMDC Steel (JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 29% YoY to Rs26.4 bn, ahead of BBG consensus growth of 14% but 27% below JPMorgan's estimate; costs per ton rose 44% YoY, faster than the 33% ASP gain, so EBITDA/t rose only 7% to Rs1,728 (JP).

outlook.note: Management has taken two price cuts so far in 2Q, and a seasonally weak Q2 is likely to weigh on near-term performance. Receivables from NMDC Steel and RINL rose slightly QoQ. GS cuts FY27E/28E/29E EBITDA by 2.9%/1.7%/1.6% and keeps Sell with a TP of Rs84. JPM stays Underweight (TP Rs75), flagging the price cuts and sales volumes well below production (GS, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs242.5bn was in line with both JPMorgan's estimate and the Street, up 54% YoY and down 2% QoQ, helped by higher zinc-silver prices and the demerger-adjusted base (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs85bn (+99% YoY, +12% QoQ) came in 5% above JPMorgan's estimate and 7% above Bloomberg consensus. Zinc India EBITDA of Rs81bn was 2% ahead of JPMorgan's estimate, and Zinc International and FACOR also did slightly better than expected (JP).

companies.name: Vedanta Aluminium

VAML expects US$175-200/tcost savings overthe next four quarters, of which 70% would be from higher alumina production/Sijimali bauxite mine and the rest from coal mining.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 12% QoQ and 46% YoY to Rs214bn, helped by higher production (aluminium 632kt, +4% YoY) and higher aluminium price realisation (US$3,553/t, +26% YoY, with LME +46% YoY). CLSA calls the results largely in line with its estimates and consensus. (CLSA)

Ebitda/t rose to US$1,767 (+105% YoY) on tailwinds from aluminium prices and a lower aluminium cost of production (COP down US$20/t QoQ to US$1,831/t), despite the Middle East conflict impact of US$50-100/t. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 COP guidance of US$1,650-1,700/t and expects COP to rise only marginally QoQ in 2Q on maintenance shutdowns. FY27 aluminium/alumina production is guided at 2.6-2.7mt/4.0-4.1mt (76% integration vs 65% in 1Q). Key projects (Ghogharpalli coal block, Sijimali bauxite mine) are on track and could deliver US$175-200/t cost savings over the next four quarters. FY27 capex guidance is Rs70bn, with Rs12bn spent in 1Q. Net debt fell to Rs295bn from Rs330bn, and an Rs8/share interim dividend was announced. CLSA leaves its estimates unchanged and keeps Outperform with a Rs540 target price. (CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Net operational income grew 19% yoy but was 1.7% below Kotak's estimate. NII was a 2% miss, which would be nearly in line without the change in disbursement recognition from cheque handover to cheque realisation. NIM fell 33bp qoq to 8.0% (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 19% yoy but was 2.8% below Kotak's estimate, on lower NII and credit-cost pressure. Opex rose 20% yoy, in line with AUM growth, and cost-to-average AUM was stable at 2.9%. Reported PAT was 5% below Kotak's estimate (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guides for about 20% AUM and PAT growth in FY27E, more than 20% disbursal growth over the remaining three quarters, spreads above 5.5% and credit cost of about 25bp. Kotak trims estimates by less than 1% and raises FV to Rs640 from Rs630. Nomura makes no estimate changes and flags monsoon as a bigger risk than the West Asia conflict (Kotak, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Total income rose 17% YoY to Rs4.2bn on 15% AUM growth and a 41% YoY disbursement pick-up. It was 1% below MS's estimate: NII missed by 2% on higher calculated borrowing costs (NIM 6.9% vs 7.1% est), partly offset by higher other income. MS flags a modest shortfall vs consensus. (MS, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP grew 22% YoY to Rs2.3bn and was in line with MS's estimate, as opex came in 3% below estimate on operating leverage (cost-to-income 44.1% vs 46.6% a year ago). Credit cost of 22bp was above MS's 20bp estimate, so PAT (+23% YoY) was 1% below. (MS, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guides to 22-23% disbursement growth and 17-18% loan/AUM growth in FY27, expects loan spreads (5.06% reported) to be below 5% by exit-FY27 after the 10bp PLR cut, and aims to keep ROA/ROE stable via operating leverage. Estimate changes are small (Jefferies trims FY27-29e EPS ~1%; Kotak revises -1% to +1%). Brokers see recent management exits and NIM pressure as risks. (MS, Jeff, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone (NBFC) total income of Rs23.6bn was +26% YoY and +8% QoQ, about 1% above Kotak's estimate of Rs23.2bn. NII was 2% below the estimate, offset by fees and fair-value gains; loan growth was 28% YoY and AUM grew 28% (Kotak). Caveat: only the standalone NBFC table is printed, so this is not the consolidated line, and its scale (Rs23.6bn = 235,530 lakh) does not match the sheet's existing 1Q26/4Q26 figures. The other reports cover only the housing subsidiary (MS 260716) or give no table (MS 260731).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone PPOP of Rs15.7bn was +23% YoY and +12% QoQ, about 1% above Kotak's estimate of Rs15.4bn. Operating costs were only slightly above forecast and credit costs fell. PBT of Rs11.8bn beat MS's estimate of Rs11.4bn, and Kotak headlined the quarter 'Earnings beat' (Kotak, MS).

companies.name: Aptus Value Housing Finance
companies.note: Aptus is also evaluating new loan products beyond housing and SME loans in NBFCs to diversify and scale up book in the medium term

1Q27.revNote: Total income Rs4.41bn (+19% YoY, +2% QoQ) was 4% below Kotak's Rs4.59bn estimate: NII (+16% YoY) fell 9% short on spread compression, with calculated NIM down to 11.5% vs 12.5% est, only partly offset by assignment income 40% above est. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP Rs3.51bn (+18% YoY) was 5% below Kotak's estimate on the lower NII, with opex (+23% YoY) a touch above est. Morgan Stanley saw PPOP 1% above its own estimate as other income ran 18% above, while credit cost of 0.7% (+30bp YoY) drove the 5% PAT miss. (Kotak, MS)

outlook.note: Management guides FY27 AUM growth of 22-24% (Rs10.5bn disbursements, +36% YoY; July disbursements +25% YoY) and credit cost of ~60bp, but 30+dpd rose to 6.9% on NBFC-book collection issues. Estimates were trimmed slightly (Kotak EPS (-)1/+1%, Jefferies FY27-28e EPS -2%) with spreads expected to moderate; ratings remain Buy/Overweight (Kotak FV Rs400, Jeff PT Rs350, MS PT Rs405). (Kotak, Jeff, MS)

companies.name: Bajaj Finance
companies.note: Management’s tone on the analyst concall was strong.

1Q27.revNote: Total income (NII per company definition) of Rs152.2bn grew 22% YoY and 7% QoQ, 1.2% above MS's Rs150.5bn estimate. NII was +23% YoY (0.5% above est.), and fees and commission income of Rs23.8bn was 4.6% above est.; JP also had NII +1% vs its estimate. Strong B2B loan growth, a B2C return to strong growth and consolidated AUM +24% YoY drove it. (MS, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs101.4bn was +19% YoY and +8% QoQ, 1.3% above MS's estimate (JP: +2% vs JPM). Reported PAT of Rs59.9bn (+27% YoY) was 3% ahead of est. and consensus, helped by provisions 19.7% below est. and net of an additional Rs2.96bn prudent provision. (MS, JP)

2Q27.revNote: Total revenue rose 21% YoY and 5% QoQ to Rs159.7bn, in line with JPMorgan's Rs159.7bn estimate. NII grew 24% on 26% AUM growth, and fee income grew 33% (JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 21% YoY to Rs107.0bn, in line with JPMorgan's estimate. Cost/income was 33.0% (+39bps YoY), and opex grew 23% YoY. Both were in line (JP).

Two more repo hikes could add NIM pressure beyond the 10-15bps contraction already guided. Brokers trimmed FY28/29 EPS by about 2-3% for lower insurance commissions (JP: FY28E EPS -2.4%; MS: -3.2%), and cut PTs to Rs1,260 (JP, MS).

2Q27.revNote: Total operating income of Rs12.5bn rose 14% YoY and was 5% above Kotak's estimate. NII grew 10% YoY and was 7% above estimate on better-than-expected margins (calculated NIM 3.1%, 18bps above estimate, as cost of borrowings fell 7bps QoQ to 7.0%). Fee and commission income was up 84% YoY and 25% above estimate, partly offset by assignment income 47% below estimate (Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs10.1bn rose 15% YoY and was 6% above Kotak's estimate. Opex grew 12% YoY, slower than 25% AUM growth, so the cost-to-income ratio improved to 19.1%. Core PBT was 2% above estimate and PAT of Rs7.6bn was up 18% YoY, 5% above estimate. Credit cost stayed benign at 0.1%. JPM also put PAT 3%/4% above JPM/Street (Kotak, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Total revenue of Rs11.7bn grew 16% y/y and was 1% above JPMe. NII rose 9% y/y but was 1% below JPMe on a 14bp q/q reported NIM decline, offset by non-interest income up 68% y/y on fees (+80%) and assignment income (JP, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPoP of Rs9.4bn rose 18% y/y and was 1% above JPMe, i.e. in line. The CIR was 19.6% and opex rose 7% y/y. The PAT beat of 4-5% came from credit costs of just 5bps (JP's 'beat is all provisions'), while Kotak called core PBT 1% below its estimate (JP, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management kept AUM growth guidance of 21-23% and NIM compression of 20-25bps for FY27. Competition in home loans (especially PSU banks) and a possible fee hit from IRDA insurance-commission proposals keep margins under pressure. Kotak cut FY28-29 estimates by 3-4% and fee income by 20%. Jefferies raised FY27e EPS 4% but cut FY28e by 4%. JPM said guidance was not raised and expects new-loan spreads to fall 3-4bps QoQ. Houses stay at Add (Kotak), Hold (Jefferies) and Neutral (JPM) (Kotak, Jeff, JP).

companies.name: Cholamandalam
companies.note: AUM growth has already accelerated to 23%, which is at the upper end of the FY27 growth guidance.

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income rose 28% YoY and 3% QoQ, about 2% above MS's estimate. NII (+27% YoY) was in line, while other income beat by 11% on stronger fees (+40% YoY per CLSA) as AUM grew 22% YoY. (Jeff, MS, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP grew 30% YoY, 4% above MS's estimate and 5% above CLSA's. Operating costs came in about 3% below MS's estimate and fees were stronger than expected, so the line grew faster than AUM. (MS, CLSA, Jeff)

outlook.note: Jefferies raises FY27-28E EPS by 5%/3% on slightly better AUM growth and lower credit cost. CLSA raises its FY27-29 PAT estimates by about 3% and its TP to Rs1,970, and expects 18-20% AUM growth. MS flags the QoQ asset-quality slippage as seasonal. (Jeff, CLSA, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Total income rose 26% YoY and 10% QoQ to Rs12.3bn. NII grew 28% YoY as NIM improved 20bps to 14.4% and loan yields rose 60bps QoQ to 21.8%, with AUM up 16% YoY. Other income fell 7% YoY. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 34% YoY and 12% QoQ to Rs8.7bn. Opex grew only 10% YoY, so the PPOP margin rose 110bps YoY to 10.6%. The bottom line beat consensus by 15% (CLSA) and 33% (Nomura), driven mainly by credit costs falling to 2.8% from 8.8% a year earlier. (CLSA, Nomura)

It says FY27 ROA will be above its 4-5% guidance and will pass lower credit-cost benefits on to customers, possibly cutting lending rates by 50bps from 2H27 if credit costs stay low. It is cautious on the monsoon. CLSA raised FY27 PAT by about 20% and its target price to Rs1,900 from Rs1,750. Nomura raised FY27 net profit by 8% and its target price to Rs1,830 from Rs1,740. (CLSA, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs6.67 bn was in line with Kotak's Rs6.67 bn estimate (+10.5% YoY). NII grew 10.2% YoY to Rs6.36 bn on AUM growth, partly offset by falling yields (24.0% vs 25.1% a year ago). (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs4.24 bn missed Kotak's estimate by 4.1% (+5.2% YoY). Operating expenses rose 21% YoY (employee costs +21%) and the cost-to-income ratio rose 276 bps YoY to 36.5%. Core PBT missed by 4%. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Asset quality is improving: 1+ dpd fell 60 bps QoQ to 16.7%, the third straight quarterly improvement. Management is accelerating growth (disbursements +16% YoY), and Kotak models 17% loan growth for FY27. Credit costs stay elevated at about 1.8% on write-offs, and opex is rising on higher employee payouts (+22% in FY27E). Kotak cut estimates 3-5% (core 1-2.5%), retained BUY and moved fair value to Rs710 from Rs705. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs3,085m was 3% above CLSA's Rs3,003m estimate and up 4% YoY. NII was in line (Rs2,424m, -1% vs estimate), and the beat came from other income of Rs661m, 20% above estimate (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs1,021m beat CLSA's Rs854m by 19% and rose 18% YoY. Opex was 4% below estimate at Rs2,064m, and total opex has stayed at Rs2.0-2.1bn for seven quarters (CLSA).

4Q26.revNote: Total income of Rs2,980m was flat YoY and 1% down QoQ, about 3% below CLSA's Rs3,057m. Other income came in 12% below estimate at Rs677m, and NII was 4% lower QoQ at Rs2,304m (CLSA).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: PPOP (operating profit) of Rs931m was 1% above CLSA's Rs925m and in line with its estimate. It was up 3% YoY, with opex 4% below estimate at Rs2,050m. PPOP has been rangebound at about Rs900m for five quarters (CLSA).

outlook.note: Management reiterated the Rs100bn AUM target for FY27 and the 2.5% credit cost guidance, saying credit cost could be closer to 2%. It expects a further 15-20bp NIM improvement by year-end and opex growth of about 5% in FY27. CLSA raised FY27CL PAT by c.40% on lower provisions and FY28-29CL PAT by c.10% on higher NII, raised its target price to Rs260 from Rs205 and upgraded to O-PF (CLSA).

companies.name: HDB Financial Services
companies.note: PPOP. AUM growth should improve & credit cost should ease, partly offset by dip in NIM due to rate hikes. Tighter insurance norms pose fee risks, which we partly factor in our est.

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs31.8bn (+17% YoY, +4% QoQ) was in line with MS's Rs31.7bn estimate (0%). (MS, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management guides to NIM above 8.2% near term and about 8% over the medium term, ROA of about 2.5% and credit cost of about 230bp. Disbursement momentum is improving (+19% YoY), and Nomura raised its FY27-29 AUM growth by 1pp. Estimates still came down: Jeff cut FY28 EPS 7%, MS cut FY28-29 EPS by 5.6%/5.0% (mostly on the insurance commission draft norms), and Nomura trimmed FY27-29 net profit by 2-6%. Nomura upgraded to Buy; MS kept OW and Jeff kept Buy, with target prices of Rs800/Rs800/Rs790. (Jeff, MS, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue rose 30% YoY and 7% QoQ to Rs3.3bn. NII grew 31% on 26% AUM growth (31% disbursement growth) and calculated NIM up 4bps QoQ to 6.2%. DA/FV gains rose 31% YoY. (Jeff, Bern)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 33% YoY and 6% QoQ to Rs2.2bn. Higher DA income offset opex growth of 24% YoY, and cost-to-income held at about 32.5%. (Jeff, Bern)

outlook.note: Disbursement growth rebounded to 31% YoY, the highest in 10 quarters, and the BT-out rate fell to 4.5% from 6% in 1QFY26, which eases the competitive-intensity worry. Spreads were steady at 5.3%, asset quality was stable and credit cost was 47bps against Jefferies' 40bps estimate. Jefferies kept Buy with a Rs1,460 PT, and Bernstein kept Outperform with a Rs1,450 PT. Bernstein expects margins to stay stable going forward. (Jeff, Bern)

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income (net operational income, i.e. NII plus other income) rose 22% YoY to Rs3.1 bn, 1% above Kotak's estimate. NII grew 31% YoY on 29% AUM growth and core NIM expansion of 73 bps YoY to 10.0%, while fee income was soft (+3% YoY). No consensus figure is printed, so the call is vs Kotak's estimate. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 20% YoY to Rs1,985 mn, in line with Kotak's estimate of Rs1,989 mn. Operating expenses grew 26% YoY, faster than income, and the cost-to-income ratio was 36%. Margin strength offset this, and PAT grew 20%. No consensus figure is printed, so the call is vs Kotak's estimate. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Kotak retains BUY with an unchanged FV of Rs975 and revises estimates by 4-6%, mainly on a better-than-expected margin trajectory despite rising rates. Credit cost estimates go up to 60-65 bps from 50 bps. 30+ dpd rose to 5.2% from 4.0% in 4QFY26, but management expects recoveries to be stronger in 2H and the disbursement dip (-28% on a norm change; 18% growth otherwise) to catch up. Semi-fixed rate loans are due for repricing in 2H. (Kotak)

companies.name: L&T Finance
companies.note: PPOP. However, at 1.9x NTM P/B for an F28e ROE of 14% (vs. 13.6% in 2QF27), we believe valuation already prices in a lot of future improvement while underestimating emerging risks – insurance commissions, El Nino.  Maintain UW

NII was 6% above Kotak's estimate on a 28% AUM rise and a 40bp q/q NIM gain to 8.9%, but fee income was 19% below estimate and down 11% q/q, so the combined line was broadly in line (Kotak). JPM also saw NII 4% above its estimate and lower fees offsetting it (JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs 21.4bn (+32% y/y, +6% q/q) was about 1% above Kotak's estimate. Opex grew 28% y/y, in line with AUM growth, and the cost-to-income ratio improved 119bp y/y to 39.0% (Kotak). JPM also called PPOP in line with its estimate (JP).

Risks flagged: El Nino (Sept 2W collection efficiency down 50bp MoM) and the draft consultation paper on insurance commissions (~25% of F26 PBT). MSe sits 8% below consensus in F28 and 5% below in F29, but MS does not expect immediate cuts. Maintains UW at Rs210 target (MS).

companies.name: LIC Housing Finance
companies.note: Intense competition and c.65bps lower spreads on new loans vs. back book should pressure spreads/ NIMs.

1Q27.revNote: Total operating income was flat YoY and down 8% QoQ, about 7% below MS's estimate. NII fell 7% QoQ as NIM compressed 22bps QoQ to 2.58% (below Jefferies' 2.7% estimate), and non-interest income fell 26% YoY to Rs420mn. (Jeff, MS)

PAT of Rs14.9bn (+9% YoY) held in line only because of a Rs1.1bn provision write-back from ARC sales and a large NPA recovery. (MS, JP, Jeff)

outlook.note: Loan growth is slow at 4% YoY and flat QoQ, and NIM is compressing (22bps QoQ). MS says its F27-29 EPS forecasts are significantly below consensus on lower loan growth, NIM and NII, and that consensus will need to cut meaningfully. JPMorgan expects negative consensus revisions after the broad PPoP miss, and Jefferies flags weak NII growth. Disbursements were a positive (+14% YoY). (MS, JP, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Total income (NII + non-interest income) rose 21% YoY and 1% QoQ to Rs27.7bn, 0.5% above JPMe. NII of Rs24.1bn (+20% YoY) was in line, and non-interest income (+38% YoY, +4% QoQ) beat on higher trading income, partly offset by a miss on fees. AUM grew 12.7% YoY. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP rose 30% YoY to Rs17.6bn, 2.8% above JPMe, helped by cost/income improving to 36.5% (opex -3% vs JPMe). PAT of Rs9.0bn (+70% YoY) beat mainly on lower credit costs of 168bps; Jefferies puts it about 10% above consensus. (JP, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management kept FY26-31 AUM CAGR guidance at 16-18% and credit cost guidance at 1.3-1.7%, but JPMorgan sees NIM under pressure from elevated cost of funds and a weak monsoon (23% rainfall deficit) as a risk to growth and asset quality. Nomura (6 Aug) stays Buy with a Rs415 PT and sees the merger of the housing subsidiary adding only 5-6% to book value and loan book. (JP, Jeff, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Total income of Rs17.7bn rose 25% YoY and 17% QoQ, and was 3% above MS's estimate. NII beat by 4% on higher gold loan yields (+60bp QoQ to 17.7%) and 12% QoQ gold loan growth. Other income missed by 26% on a net loss on derecognition of financial assets. (Jeff, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: PPOP of Rs10.1bn rose 52% YoY and 29% QoQ, and was 5% above MS's estimate. NII beat and opex was in line, with opex up only 1% YoY at Rs7.6bn. Consolidated NIM improved 65bp QoQ to 10.3%. (Jeff, MS)

outlook.note: Management guides 25-30% gold loan growth and gold yields of about 18% (±25bp) for FY27, with about 500 new gold branches planned. Jefferies raised FY27-28e EPS by 8-13% (PT Rs430) and MS raised F27-29 EPS by 14-15% (PT Rs360, EW). CLSA lifted PAT estimates by 5-6% (PT Rs350, Hold) and noted limited upside after a 17% rally in three months. (Jeff, MS, CLSA)

companies.name: Muthoot Finance
companies.note: Competition is rising as several NBFCs expand branches, though manageable for now. However, this can pressure customer accretion and yields in the near term.

Jefferies cuts FY27-28e EPS by 7%/8% and downgrades to Hold (PT Rs3,300); MS largely maintains forecasts but builds a 5% QoQ fall in gold loans in 2QF27 and expects sharp consensus cuts, staying OW; Bernstein stays Outperform (PT Rs4,500) but flags that selective rate cuts and a mix shift to lower-yielding loans keep margins under pressure (Jeff, MS, Bern).

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue (NII + other income) rose 35% YoY and 7% QoQ to Rs17.9bn, led by NII up 50% YoY to Rs13.5bn on 25% AUM growth and a 21bps QoQ rise in calculated NIM to 5.34%. Other income grew only 5% YoY. No line-level consensus or broker estimate is printed (Jeff).

The 40GWh battery cell plant is to be commissioned this year. Jefferies trimmed FY27-29E EBITDA by 1-6% on the Retail and O2C misses, and kept its Buy with a Rs1,705 target. JPMorgan stays OW with a Rs1,660 target. (JP, Jeff, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Adjusted revenue of US$309.7mn (+9.4% YoY in USD) was 4.3% above Visible Alpha consensus of US$296.9mn, with beats across segments, especially Hotels & Packages (+4.9%) and Bus (+4.4%). Gross bookings grew 19.9% YoY in constant currency, and GS notes revenue growth accelerated to 20% cc from 13% in 4Q. (MS, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: The metric is adjusted EBIT, as the MS table shows no EBITDA. At US$51.4mn (+8.6% YoY) it was 8.4% above consensus of US$47.4mn. Margin was 16.6% of revenue and about 1.8% of gross bookings, flat QoQ, even with ad spend up to 5.5% of gross bookings from 5.2% in 4Q. GS says EBITDA growth was largely in line with its estimates. (MS, GS)

4Q26.revNote: Adj. revenue of US$282mn (+7.9% YoY, -9.4% QoQ) was 1.7% above consensus (US$277mn) but 5.5% below JPMorgan's US$298mn. Bus ticketing grew fastest (+12.7% YoY) while Air (+5.4%) and Hotels & Packages (+5.8%) were softer, and take rate rose 64bps YoY to 10.1% (JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBIT of US$47mn (+4.1% YoY) was 5.7% above consensus (US$44mn) and 5.6% below JPMorgan's estimate. Margin on adj. revenue was 16.5%, 63bps ahead of consensus but 61bps down YoY; the Middle East conflict and higher fuel-driven air fares hurt late-quarter volumes (JP).

outlook.note: GS sees a high probability of FY27 revenue growth of at least 20% YoY, helped by non-air businesses and a favourable base, and forecasts 22% cc GBV growth for FY27. Visibility into Sep-26 is limited because air demand is weak and westbound travel is soft. Management aims to keep adjusted EBIT at about 1.8% of gross bookings, stable or improving gradually, while marketing spend stays elevated. GS's estimate changes are small: FY27E revenue US$1,288mn vs US$1,286mn earlier, FY28E US$1,540mn vs US$1,547mn. Management gave more detail on fungibility structures for a possible India subsidiary listing. (GS, MS)

4Q26.revNote: Net sales rose 82.5% YoY to Rs8.1bn, helped by the Classic Vacations acquisition (Rs2.7bn of revenue); organic revenue grew 21.4%. GTV grew 29% on 39% growth in Hotels, but March was disrupted by the Middle East conflict, with about 40% of relevant travel corridors affected. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 47% YoY to Rs1,053mn, but margin fell to 12.9% from 16.0% a year ago and 13.7% last quarter. Organic EBITDA grew only 9% (Adj. EBITDA +5% LFL, versus +62% ex-March) because the March disruption compressed operating leverage, and the company also had higher SG&A and integration costs. Adj PAT of Rs601mn was 8% above Jefferies' estimate of Rs557mn. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales rose 81% YoY (14% QoQ) to Rs9,258mn, helped by Classic Vacations and favourable currency; organic revenue grew 16% YoY, trailing organic GTV growth of 22% as volume was prioritised over take rate in the Middle East (Jeff, GS). GS calls organic GTV growth 9% ahead of its estimate, but neither note gives a revenue estimate or consensus figure.
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 84% YoY to Rs1,435mn with margin up to 15.5% (17.8% adjusted, per Jeff), as SG&A grew only ~4% organically against ~12% gross profit growth. GS puts organic adjusted EBITDA growth at 25% YoY, c.30% ahead of its estimate. Jefferies calls it a clear margin inflection (Jeff, GS).

outlook.note: Management expects 2Q GTV to grow QoQ and operating leverage to continue, with SG&A growth below gross profit growth and GP-to-EBITDA conversion (now 26%) still improving. GS sees 20%+ EBITDA growth for the foreseeable future and raised FY27-29E revenue by up to 2% and EBITDA by up to 1%, with its PT going to Rs1,800 from Rs1,730. Jefferies raised FY27-28 EPS by 3-8% and its PT to Rs1,905 from Rs1,615 (Jeff, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Sales grew 25% y-y versus Bloomberg consensus of +17%, led by East Asia Pacific (+34%), Americas (+29%) and Europe (+20%), with price hikes passing through RM inflation. Underlying growth ex-commodity pass-through was 20% (Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 15% y-y versus consensus of +11% and Nomura's +14%. Margin fell 165bp y-y to 18.8% as gross margin slipped 75bp to 59.4% and other expenses rose 102bp as a share of sales; underlying OPM was 19.6% (Nomura).

outlook.note: Management raised FY27E guidance to high-teens sales growth, with OPM sustained at ~20% despite high RM prices, and expects to recover the full cost increase through pricing. It targets ROCE of 25% by FY29E (from 18%) and a 20-22% tax rate. Nomura raised FY27-29F EPS by 3% and its TP to INR325 from INR300 (Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated total income rose 12% YoY, 1% below Bloomberg consensus. Standalone value growth was 12.7% (volume 8.4%, pricing ~5%), and decorative value growth was 13.5%. Protective, GI and powder coatings grew more slowly because price hikes lagged in B2B segments (MS, Kotak, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 15% YoY to Rs6.07bn, about 2% above consensus, with margin up 44bp YoY to 16.9% (consensus 16.5%). Operating efficiencies and low-cost inventory offset a 54bp YoY gross-margin decline to 40.9%. Kotak puts the beat at 5.5% against its own estimate and Nomura calls EBITDA above estimates (MS, Kotak, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management guides to better 2Q growth as the full impact of price hikes flows through: volume growth of 7.5-8% with pricing of 7.5-8.5%, and a favourable base. FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17% is maintained, with YoY margin expansion in 2Q although margins dip sequentially on seasonality. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 4-10% and FV to Rs540, and Nomura raised TP to Rs675 (from Rs650). Competitive intensity from Birla Opus has eased but stays elevated, and the MS rating is Underweight (Kotak, Nomura, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 19.7% yoy to Rs3.7 bn, 3.2% above Kotak's estimate, driven by price hikes taken from late-March and double-digit volume growth across categories. Decorative paints grew 18.7%, in line with the industry, and Apple Chemie grew 40% (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 40% yoy to Rs620 mn, 28.5% above Kotak's estimate. The margin expanded 245 bps yoy to 16.8% (estimate 13.5%) even though gross margin fell 135 bps. A&P spend was cut 25% yoy to 4.3% of revenue, and operating leverage helped (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 9.7% yoy to Rs4.25 bn, 0.6% ahead of Kotak's estimate (KIE: +9%). Decorative paints grew 8.5% yoy, a tad better than peers but below the 1.5-2X industry growth aspiration. Growth was helped by demand recovery since November, some channel stocking in March ahead of the price hike, and Apple Chemie at +34.7% yoy. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 9.3% yoy to Rs956 mn, 3.3% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 22.5%, down 10 bps yoy, as a 180 bps gross-margin expansion was offset by sales team expansion and higher A&P spends (employee costs +28% yoy, A&P +~30%). (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management says demand is back to near-normal and July was as good as or marginally better than 1Q. It plans to step up trade schemes and influencer spending in 2Q to widen the growth gap with peers, which may weigh on near-term gross margin by about 200-250 bps. It declined to guide on 2Q margins, and no further price hikes are planned at current raw-material levels. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 4-6% on easing raw-material prices and lifted fair value to Rs975 from Rs900, but kept REDUCE with a cautious sector view (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs18bn (+4% YoY, +6% QoQ) was 3% below consensus and 2% below JPMe, well short of the 13.6% IPM growth, as the anti-diabetes franchise fell 7% YoY and Novo's insulin brands (Mixtard -34%, Novomix -8%) were phased out. Abbott's portfolio excluding Novo Nordisk insulin and GLP-1 brands grew 15% YoY per IQVIA. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.2bn (+17% YoY, +13% QoQ) was in line with consensus and 2% above JPMe. Margin rose to 28.8% (+320bps YoY), 80bps above consensus, because gross margin improved to 48.6% (+280bps YoY) as lower-margin Novo insulin brands were phased out. Adjusted PAT of Rs4.1bn was 5% below consensus on higher interest and tax costs and lower other income. (JP)

outlook.note: JPMorgan expects downward revisions to consensus estimates and a downward stock reaction after the revenue and PAT miss, and keeps a Neutral rating (Mar-27 target Rs27,500). Offsetting positives: underlying portfolio growth of 15% YoY is about 150bps ahead of IPM, and the gross margin mix is improving. (JP)

companies.name: Ajanta Pharma
companies.note: FY27 guidance was reiterated at high double-digit growth. India to grow in mid-teens, continuing the strong performance from FY26. USA growth would moderate to mid-single digit due to a high base effect and price erosio anticipated in the coming quarters.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs16.3bn, 8% above Jefferies' estimate. India (+24% YoY, 9% beat) and the US (+57% YoY, 37% beat) drove the beat, Africa grew 29%, and Asia fell 16% (27% below estimate) on the Middle East conflict (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 21% YoY to Rs4.23bn, 4% above Jefferies' estimate. Gross margin reached ~79.8% (+101bps YoY), the highest since 2020, but EBITDA margin was 26.1%, down 92bps YoY, on higher employee and other expenses (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management retained FY27 guidance of high double-digit growth for Africa and Asia and mid-teens growth for India. US growth should slow to mid-single digit on price erosion from competition, and Asia is expected to rebound as delayed deliveries pick up. FY27 gross margin is guided at 78% (+/-1%) and EBITDA margin at 27% (adjusted for forex loss). Jefferies raised FY27-28 EPS estimates by 1-2% and moved its PT to INR4,050 from INR3,550 (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue rose 6.4% yoy to Rs6.4 bn but was 4.1% below Kotak's estimate. Ex-GNP sales grew 27% yoy, while the GNP business fell 52.6% on inventory rationalisation and CDMO sales declined sequentially (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 22.9% yoy and beat Kotak's estimate by 4.6%. The margin was 33.1%, up 450 bps yoy, as gross margin gained 510 bps on a lower-GNP mix and new launches (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guides FY27E sales growth of 10-12% yoy, skewed to 2HFY27 as CDMO picks up, with two CDMO contracts to be commercialised in 2HFY27. It keeps its 30-32% EBITDA margin guidance (including other income) and says it could guide to 34%, but holds a cushion for Middle East war impact. Kotak raises FY27-29E EPS by 5-7% and its fair value to Rs1,400 from Rs1,315 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Total revenue of INR37.4bn (+11% y-y, +4% q-q) came in ~1% below consensus. Domestic formulations grew ~10% y-y, an improvement on the prior two single-digit quarters but lagging peers. There were no price increases across the large NLEM portfolio and trade generics were flat. International sales grew 16% y-y (Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR7.66bn (+4% y-y) was ~6% below consensus. EBITDA margin fell 144bp y-y to 20.5% even though gross margin expanded 262bp to 67.9% on product mix and currency. Overheads rose sharply, with other expenses +26% y-y and employee costs +17%. CDMO expenses of ~INR600mn a quarter drag margin by ~160bp (Nomura).

4Q26.revNote: Total revenue of Rs36.0bn (+15% YoY, -4% QoQ) was broadly in line with consensus; Nomura had it 1% above its own estimate. India sales grew 9% YoY (acute +10%, chronic +16.1%) and international sales rose 25% (Nomura, JP 2026/05/29).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.2bn (+32% YoY, -38% QoQ) was 11% ahead of Nomura's estimate on a gross margin of 65.4% (+606bp YoY, 420bp above Nomura). JP puts it ~9% below consensus because R&D (6.4% of revenue, +45% YoY) and one-time expenses offset the gross margin beat, so the EBITDA margin of 14.4% was ~170bp below consensus (Nomura, JP 2026/05/29).

outlook.note: Nomura raises FY27 sales estimates 7-8% to include Occlutech from 2QFY27, with no material change to EBITDA or PAT estimates. It expects gross margin to hold and EBITDA margin to expand over the years as operating leverage builds. It cuts its target price to INR6,850 from INR6,890 and keeps Buy. Near-term costs for the CDMO and MedTech ramp-up remain elevated (Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Sales grew 16.3% YoY to Rs91.5bn, 0.9% above Kotak's estimate. Growth was broad-based: EU +25.6%, growth markets +19.6% QoQ and +37.8% YoY, and US flat to slightly ahead at US$399mn (+3% QoQ) (Kotak). CLSA called it an in-line quarter with revenue +16% YoY across all geographies, and GS saw a beat on Europe and growth markets (Kotak, CLSA, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 17.3% YoY to Rs18.8bn, 1.6% below Kotak's estimate (in line). The margin was 20.6%, +18bps YoY and -52bps vs estimate. Gross margin gained 153bps YoY to 60.4% and R&D fell to 4.4% of sales (Kotak). CLSA described margins as flattish YoY at 20.6% (Kotak, CLSA).

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs88.5bn were 1.3% above Kotak's estimate and +5.6% YoY. EU (+30% YoY) and emerging markets (+25% YoY) offset a 13% YoY drop in US sales (no Revlimid contribution) and seasonal US softness. Excluding gRevlimid, sales grew 15% YoY (Kotak, CLSA).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs18.0bn was 1.2% above Kotak's estimate but only +0.5% YoY. Margin was 20.3%, down 104bps YoY, as higher opex (Pen-G plant) offset the gross-margin gain (+216bps YoY to 61.3%). Management guides to 21%+ EBITDA margin in FY27 (Kotak, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, a 21%+ EBITDA margin (Rs80bn+ EBITDA) and R&D of Rs14-15bn. Lannett consolidates from 2QFY27E and is expected to drive a ~9% US sales CAGR over FY26-29E, but Eugia-III regulatory issues persist. Estimate changes were marginal: Kotak FY27-29E EPS ~+1%, CLSA NP +3%, and GS EPS from -3% to +2%. Kotak raised FV to Rs1,535 and CLSA raised TP to Rs1,600 (Kotak, CLSA, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 10% YoY but fell 4% QoQ, 5% below Bloomberg consensus though only 1% below GS. Biosimilars grew +17% YoY and Generics +21%, while Services fell 16% YoY. Jefferies also called it a miss against its own estimate, with revenue 9% below. (GS, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 13% YoY to Rs8.5bn but fell 17% QoQ. It was 12% below Bloomberg consensus (3% above GS), and margin of 19.5% was 168bps below consensus. Generics EBITDA turned positive at about 7% margin on operating leverage and lower R&D. Jefferies put EBITDA 12% below its estimate. (GS, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management called Jun-Q a trough and expects improved performance in 2HFY27, led by biosimilar launches (bAflibercept, bDenosumab) and generic liraglutide ramp-up, but gave no specific FY27 guidance. Both brokers cut estimates: GS lowered FY27-29 EBITDA by up to ~5% and Jefferies by 1-5% (FY27 EPS cut to Rs6.04 from Rs6.95) on weak Syngene and slow biopharma ramp-up. GS kept Neutral (TP Rs425) and Jefferies kept Hold (TP Rs410). (GS, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs71.2bn grew ~4% YoY and were 1% above GS and 1% below consensus. India grew ~12% (branded Rx +15.4%) and EM/EU grew strongly, offset by the gRevlimid cliff, Lanreotide supply constraints and a 5% YoY decline in South Africa (GS, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs11.9bn fell 33% YoY and was 2% below consensus, with the margin at 16.7% (-924bps YoY, 30bps below consensus). Lower gross margin (-574bps YoY, inferior product mix) and operating deleverage drove the decline. Higher R&D (~7% of sales) and war-related costs added to it (GS, MS).

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 EBITDA margin guidance at 18.5-20% (2H stronger than 1H) and the US$1bn North America exit run-rate target (~US$250mn in 4QFY27), with Ventolin ramp-up and gAdvair and peptide launches still to come. GS cut FY27-29E EPS by 5% to +1% and trimmed its TP to Rs1,375 from Rs1,400. Jefferies raised FY27 EPS 2% on forex but sees downside risk to US guidance and to margins if launches are delayed. MS says the US$1bn target leaves limited room for setbacks (GS, Jeff, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Sales of Rs4.2 bn (+22% yoy, +20% qoq) were ~4% ahead of Kotak's estimate (Rs4,066 mn). India sales grew 23% yoy (~21% ex-Wokadine), led by a continued uptick in the chronic mix. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs931 mn (+33% yoy, +50% qoq) beat Kotak's estimate by ~10%. Margin was 22.0%, +110 bps vs Kotak's estimate and +190 bps yoy, helped by gross margin of 81.6% and lower SG&A as a share of sales (30.7% vs 32.8% a year ago). (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~17% sales growth (~15% organic) and 20%+ PAT growth, with EBITDA margin expected to improve on mix, efficiency and operating leverage. It is cautious about extrapolating 1QFY27 margins to the full year, but hopes to sustain current levels. Kotak raised FY27-29E EBITDA by 3-9% on higher sales and margins, and expects Corona to surpass its guidance. It rolled the fair value forward to Rs2,175 from Rs1,850 and kept ADD. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs80.7bn was down 5.6% YoY and 1.8% below Bloomberg consensus (0.8% above CLSA), so in line. US sales fell 35% YoY to Rs22.0bn on no Revlimid sales. The base US business, India (+17%), Europe (+13%) and RoW (+42%) all grew. (CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs8.3bn was 40% below consensus. The margin was 10.3% against 17.0% consensus and 25.2% a year ago. An inventory provision of Rs2.4bn for the gSema API and about 1% from higher solvent and freight costs (Middle East conflict) drove the miss. (CLSA)

outlook.note: Management guides to double-digit growth in the US base business (ex-gRevlimid, ex-gSema) and a ~20% EBITDA margin (ex-gSema) in FY27. It expects gSema supply to resume in Nov 2026 and Abatacept approval in Dec 2026, and the solvent/freight cost drag to ease. FY27 gSema volume was cut to 6-7m pens (from 10-11m), so CLSA cut FY27 revenue 2.4% and net profit 6.1%, and JPM cut FY27/28 EPS 12-17%. Nomura kept Buy, seeing margins as unsustainably low. (CLSA, JP, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs25.8bn (+22.8% YoY, +4.5% QoQ) was 8.5% above Kotak's estimate, led by international sales (+34% YoY; Europe +33%, Canada +25%, RoW +45%) with a 6-7% FX tailwind. India grew only ~10% YoY (~6-7% excluding Amaryl and Roche's nephro portfolio). JPM likewise had revenue 7% ahead of its estimate. (Kotak, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs5.08bn (+25.8% YoY) was 8.2% above Kotak's estimate, on the revenue beat. EBITDA margin was 19.7% (+46bps YoY, flat QoQ), in line with Kotak. Gross margin of 58.4% (-209bps vs Kotak's estimate, -341bps YoY) was hurt by a higher Europe and ARV mix. JPM noted the margin was 30bps below its estimate, though EBITDA was 6% above. (Kotak, JP)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of low-to-mid-teens revenue growth, now toward the upper end of the range, and 70-100bps EBITDA margin expansion. Gross margin guidance was trimmed to 59-60% (from 60-61%) on mix. Management expects India to grow in line with the industry from 2Q and faster in 2HFY27. Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 3-5% (FV Rs2,225). JPM raised FY27/28 earnings estimates by 2-4%, but India growth is still lagging the industry (JPM kept Neutral). (Kotak, JP)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR19.4bn (+38% YoY, +2% QoQ) was 8% above Jefferies' estimate of INR17.9bn, driven by ~20% organic growth (like-for-like) plus recent acquisitions, despite ~2.5ppt drag from discontinued low-margin business. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR970mn (+94% YoY, +13% QoQ) was 18% above Jefferies' estimate; margin rose to 5.0% (+143bps YoY) on gross margin expansion to 11.4% from rising MedTech contribution and operating leverage. (Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR19.1bn (+43% YoY, +12% QoQ) was 6% above Jefferies' estimate of INR18.0bn, aided by recent acquisitions. Organic growth was ~17% YoY. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR860mn (+76% YoY) was 15% above Jefferies' estimate of INR747mn. Gross margin expanded 109bps YoY to 10.9% and EBITDA margin rose 85bps YoY to 4.5%. PAT missed because of higher depreciation, finance costs and one-off minority interest. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 guidance of 23% revenue growth and ~5% EBITDA margin (already achieved in 1Q), excluding any acquisitions, and sees 20%+ revenue growth and 6%+ margin over three years. Jefferies sees upside risk to FY27 guidance, raised FY27E EBITDA 4% and FY29E EPS 10% (FY27/28 EPS unchanged), and kept Buy with PT INR1,800. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs18.0bn (+20% YoY, +3% QoQ) was in line with consensus (0% variance) and 4% above GS estimates; growth was broad-based, with CDMO +20% and B2B +19% YoY, and the US the key driver (+32% YoY). Management put constant-currency growth at ~15% (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.9bn (+33% YoY) was 4% above consensus and 11% above GS estimates; margin rose ~275bps YoY to 27.2% (103bps above consensus) on higher CDMO contribution, better utilisation and cost optimisation (GS). Gross margin was 65.3% (Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 22% YoY and 3% QoQ, about 6% above consensus (and 6% above GS's estimate). The US business grew 26% YoY on 5 new launches, including Dalbavancin, and higher volumes from recent GPO contracts. Nomura also cites steady Cenexi revenue, CDMO contract growth and INR depreciation (Nomura: sales 5% above consensus). (GS, Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 48% YoY to INR 5,130 mn, about 23% above consensus. Margin was 29.4%, up 505bp YoY and 417bp ahead of consensus, on better gross margin from mix and operating leverage. Nomura puts the beat at 22% vs consensus. (GS, Nomura)

3Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs16,955mn grew 22% yoy and came in 3% above consensus (7% above GS estimates). Growth was driven by the US business (+16% yoy, with 9 new products in the quarter and better share in key products from new GPO contracts) and Cenexi (Rs5.2bn, +22% yoy in cc terms). RoW grew ~12% yoy. (GS)
3Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4,350mn rose 21% yoy and was 5% above consensus (10% above GS estimates). The margin was 25.7%, down 35bps yoy but 66bps above Bloomberg consensus, on a better gross margin from improved mix. Cenexi turned EBITDA-positive at ~3% margin after losses in 1H. (GS)

outlook.note: Management guides at least ~15% constant-currency growth for FY27 (up from ~12-13%), with upside if the RTU bag line is approved in 3QFY27, and sees ~20% revenue growth over the next four years on CDMO wins (a 55-SKU contract with peak revenue of US$90-100mn from CY29). Near-term EBITDA margin aspiration is ~30%, with longer-term potential of ~35%, and Cenexi guidance of EUR200mn is retained. Brokers raised FY27-29E EPS by 8-10% (GS, Jeff) and 9%/5%/5% (Nomura). GS, Jeff, Nomura.

1Q27.revNote: Total revenue grew 21% y-y to INR27.9bn, with every segment up double digits: exports +34%, subsidiary (Unichem) +19%, domestic formulations +13%. Price hikes passed on to API customers and in branded generics helped, and INR400mn of lumpy institutional generic sales shipped late from 4QFY26. Excluding that, revenue growth was ~19% (Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Core EBITDA rose 50% y-y to INR6.4bn, with the margin up 449bp y-y to 22.9% as gross margin widened 135bp to 71.4% and operating leverage kicked in. Excluding the lumpy institutional sales, EBITDA growth was 45%+ (Nomura).

4Q26.revNote: Total revenue of INR23.9bn was up 6% y-y and 3% ahead of Nomura's estimate. India sales grew 12% y-y (1% ahead) and exports grew 9% y-y (5% ahead), led by export formulations up 16% y-y. [Nomura]
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Core EBITDA of INR4.9bn grew 20% y-y and was 16% ahead of Nomura's estimate. Gross margin rose 257bp y-y to 71% on a higher formulations mix (76% of sales vs 73%), and EBITDA margin expanded 229bp y-y to 20.5%. [Nomura]

outlook.note: Management raised its FY27E guidance: revenue growth of 14-16% y-y (from 12-13%) and an EBITDA margin of ~23% (from ~22%); it sees the margin reaching ~25-26% over the next two years. Nomura raised FY27F/FY28F sales/EBITDA/PAT estimates by ~2.5%/~9.0%/~13%, lifted its target price to INR2,060 from INR1,725 and kept Buy (Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Sales were 7% above Bloomberg consensus (6% above GS estimate) and grew 32% YoY and 11% QoQ. Growth was broad-based: US sales were Rs34.3bn (US$366mn, +43% YoY), helped by base-portfolio volumes and Tolvaptan, and India grew 13.9% YoY. (GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was 12% above Bloomberg consensus (14% above GS estimate) and grew 50% YoY. Margin was 29.8% (+358bps YoY), driven by gross margin expansion, better product mix, India profitability and cost efficiencies. (GS)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of high-single-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin of about 25%, which implies moderation after a strong 1Q. US sales are guided to US$1.1-1.2bn, a step-down to US$250-280mn per quarter from 2Q as competition builds in Tolvaptan and Mirabegron. GS raised FY28-29 EPS (Rs117.7/126.2 vs Rs111.2/107.2 earlier) but cut FY27 EPS to Rs95.9 from Rs112.6, and stays Neutral with a Rs2,500 target price. Kotak (1 Sep) sees margins troughing in FY27 as Tolvaptan and Mirabegron sales fall, trimmed FY27-29E EPS by 1-8% and cut fair value to Rs2,525 from Rs2,730, but stays at ADD and calls the margin fears overdone. (GS, Kotak)

companies.name: Mankind Pharma
companies.note: Guidance of DD growth in India with potential ~100bps margin improvement was retained.

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs34.4 bn (+11.8% YoY) were 2.3% above Kotak's estimate of Rs33.7 bn, so broadly in line; organic domestic growth was about 10.5% YoY, with OTC up 20% and BSV up 25%+ in 2HFY26 on a low base (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs9.3 bn (+36% YoY) beat Kotak's Rs7.6 bn estimate by 23%, largely on lower staff costs (including a waiver of management incentives) and cost control; adjusted for the one-off staff-cost benefit, the beat was 19% and margin 26.1%, up about 360 bps vs Kotak's estimate (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 13% YoY to INR40.3bn, 2% above Jefferies' INR39.5bn estimate (in line). Export formulations rose 29% YoY (15% above estimate) and India formulations rose 11% YoY (in line), while consumer healthcare grew only 4% (6% miss) after cash-and-carry discontinuation. Bernstein also called sales in line with its ~13% growth forecast (Jeff, Bern).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 25% YoY to INR10.6bn, 7% above Jefferies' INR9.9bn estimate. Gross margin was 72.8% (+226bps YoY, 175bps above estimate) and EBITDA margin was 26.2% (+249bps YoY, 120bps above estimate). Jefferies called it a better-quality beat than Mar-Q. Bernstein saw EBITDA broadly in line with its estimates (Jeff, Bern).

outlook.note: Management retained double-digit domestic growth guidance for FY27 with potential ~100bps margin improvement. Exports are guided to high-teens growth, and BSV to high-teens growth in FY27. Consumer healthcare is expected to rebound from Sep-Q, with high-single to low double-digit growth for the rest of 9MFY27. Jefferies left EBITDA estimates largely unchanged, cut FY27 EPS 2%, and raised its PT to INR3,220 from INR3,000 (Buy). Bernstein stays Underperform (TP INR2,057), citing Acute-segment weakness and rising R&D spend (Jeff, Bern).

1Q27.revNote: Sales rose 22% y-y and 1% q-q, 1% ahead of Nomura's INR18,629mn estimate. Own pharmacies grew 18% and franchise sales 164%, but private-label pharma grew only 2%. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating EBITDA fell 11% y-y and 40% q-q, 29% below Nomura's estimate. Gross margin fell 163bp y-y to 24.5% on weaker private-label mix and more franchise sales. Overheads rose 34% y-y, with pharmacy salaries up 30%. EBITDA margin was 3.5% against 4.9% estimated. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Management kept its plan to add 800 stores in FY27 and said it can meet or exceed INR4.4bn FY27 operating EBITDA, in line with Nomura's estimate. It aims to lift private-label share by 0.25–0.3% q-q, raised the membership fee to INR149 from INR99, and cut the non-UPI discount to 19% from 20%. Labour Code wage increases (Karnataka +60%, Telangana +25%) will show their full impact in 2QFY27. The INR1,150mn wellness/food-park capex was put on hold after the stock fell 13%. Nomura kept Buy and its INR1,190 TP. (Nomura)

companies.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries
companies.note: Maintained its FY2027E guidance of high single-digit topline growth.

4Q26.revNote: Total sales of Rs146bn (+13% YoY) were about 1% above Bloomberg consensus. Growth was volume-led, with India up 15% on 6% volume growth versus 2% for IPM, plus new launches. Emerging markets and innovative medicines were also strong, while US generics were soft (CLSA, JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs35.3bn was 11% below consensus, and margin fell to 24.2% from 26.7% a year ago and 31.0% last quarter. The causes were lower milestone income, seasonality, lower Revlimid sales and higher spending in some geographies including the US. Some of the elevated spend is expected to normalise (CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Sales grew 10.5% YoY to Rs153bn, broadly in line with consensus (GS: -1% vs consensus; JPM: in line). India grew 16% YoY on volumes, new launches and pricing, and Innovative Medicines rose 13% to US$351mn. These offset US generics weakness, with US sales down 9.5% YoY to US$427mn. (MS, JP, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose only 5.5% YoY to Rs43.0bn, a 28.1% margin (-133bps YoY, +394bps QoQ). JPM puts it about 2% below consensus because staff costs rose 15.2% YoY, while MS calls the quarter in line with consensus. Gross margin expanded to 80.6% on a richer mix. (MS, JP)

outlook.note: Management retained its FY27 guidance of high-single-digit consolidated revenue growth, with R&D expected to rise from the Q1 level and the tax rate staying near Q1 levels until Organon closes. Drivers are Leqselvi, Unloxcyt, semaglutide and Ilumya. Estimate changes are mixed: JPM cuts FY27E adj. EPS 5.3% to Rs50.37, while GS moves its FY27-29E EPS by -1% to +3%. (MS, JP, GS)

companies.name: Torrent Pharmaceuticals
companies.note: Torrent expects FY27 to be a strong year. For FY27, Torrentexpects theIndia base business to continue to outperform IPM, double-digit growth in JB Chem and base business margin improvement of 50bps. JB integration is ahead of schedule and cost synergies from JB should play out faster than previously expected.

4Q26.revNote: Sales of Rs41.97 bn were 2.2% above Kotak's estimate and up 41.8% yoy, helped by JB Pharma consolidation from 21 Jan 2026. The base business grew 16% yoy (Rs34.2 bn), led by India (~15% yoy, outgrowing the IPM) and Brazil, partly offset by weak Germany. Nomura and Jefferies called the base-business sales in line with their estimates. (Kotak, Nomura, Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs13.56 bn was 7.1% above Kotak's estimate and up 40.7% yoy, with the margin at 32.3%. Base-business EBITDA grew 16% yoy to Rs11.2 bn at a 32.7% margin, and the JB print was muted. Jefferies and Nomura called EBITDA in line with their own estimates. (Kotak, Jeff, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 55% YoY (+17% QoQ) to Rs49.2bn, 7% above consensus and 2% above GSe, helped by the JB Chem consolidation. The India base business grew 19% YoY (price +7.7%, volume +5.1%, new launches +6%) against IPM growth of 12%, and Brazil beat GSe by 9% (GS). CLSA also called the revenue a beat, with Brazil/US base revenue up 27%/36% YoY on new launches (CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 59% YoY (+23% QoQ) to Rs16.6bn, 11% above consensus and 2% above GSe. Margin was 33.8% (+87bps YoY, +151bps QoQ), driven by better gross margin, operating leverage and JB Chem synergies (GS). JPM puts JB's EBITDA margin at 35.3% (+650bps YoY), supported by synergies of over Rs750mn, which more than offset the base business margin of 33.3% (~70bps below JPMe) (JP).
