outlook.note: Management expects the India base business to keep outperforming the IPM, with c.50bps margin expansion in FY27, and double-digit growth in JB India Rx. JB cost synergies are running ahead of the FY27 target of Rs900mn. gSema supply should normalise by Aug 2026, though sales may fall short of the Rs2.5bn guidance. GS raised FY27-29E EPS by 5-46%, CLSA raised FY27-29 estimates (FY27 revenue +17.9%, net profit +11.1%) and its target price to Rs4,810 (Hold), and JP raised its target price to Rs5,950 (OW) (GS, CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR80.2bn (+22% YoY, +6% QoQ) was 4% above Jefferies' estimate, helped by India formulations (+19.5% YoY, 6% beat) and International (+34% YoY, 14% beat); US grew 5% QoQ and was in line (Jeff). Bernstein also flags broad-based growth, with Consumer Wellness +67% YoY partly on the Comfort Click acquisition (Jeff, Bern).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR18.7bn (-8% YoY, -2% QoQ) was 3% above Jefferies' estimate, but margin fell to 23.4% from 30.9% a year ago, on higher employee cost (+36% YoY) and R&D and other expenses. Bernstein attributes the margin dip to acquisition-related costs and continued investment, and sees a deliberate reinvestment phase rather than a margin reset (Jeff, Bern).

4Q26.revNote: Total revenue of INR75.9bn (+16.2% YoY) was 5% above Nomura's estimate. Growth was strong across all key segments: exports formulations were 8.8% ahead, and Europe + Emerging Markets grew 45% YoY. India formulations grew 14% and US revenue rose USD9mn QoQ (Nomura; Jeff also calls it 9% above its estimate).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Core EBITDA of INR19.1bn (-11.8% YoY, +15.6% QoQ) was 15% ahead of Nomura's estimate. Margin was 25.2%, 227bp above the estimate, on better product mix, a favourable currency and operating leverage. The YoY fall reflects a high base from gRevlimid in 4QFY25 (Nomura; Jeff: 19% above its estimate).

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance: high-teens revenue growth, ~24% EBITDA margin, and single-digit US growth on 30-40 launches. India formulations are expected to grow mid-teens, 300-500bps ahead of the IPM. Jefferies cut FY27 EPS 3% but raised FY28/29 EPS 5-11% and lifted PT to INR1,370 from INR1,200. Bernstein sees ex-US growth broadening, with Saroglitazar's PDUFA date in October 2026 and a US launch expected in April 2027 (Jeff, Bern).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR107bn was up 26% y-y and 11% above Bloomberg consensus. Cargo traffic grew 13% y-y, helped by the NQXT acquisition and higher container transshipment volumes. Ports, logistics and marine revenue grew 15%, 10% and 101% y-y respectively (Nomura).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR60bn rose 20% y-y and was 8% above consensus and 6% above Nomura's estimate. EBITDA margin was 56.1%, down 291bps y-y and 132bps below the consensus margin of 57.4%, so the beat came from higher revenue and not from margins (Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR108bn (+19% y-y) was 2% above Bloomberg consensus and 2% below Nomura's estimate, so in line. Total ports and marine revenue grew 21% and 67% y-y, while logistics was flat y-y. Port traffic rose 15% y-y, led by a 196% jump in international port traffic on NQXT consolidation and maturing assets, along with higher realisations from a favourable mix (Nomura). MS puts domestic ports +12%, international +80% and marine +67%, and calls the revenue a 9% beat on its own number (MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR65.4bn (+19% y-y) was 6% above Bloomberg consensus and 3% above Nomura. The EBITDA margin was 60.4%, 244bp above Nomura's estimate and 219bp above consensus. The beat came from a better mix and a 67.5% ports margin (+2bp y-y). Logistics EBITDA grew only 3% as rail volumes fell 19% y-y on the Middle East crisis (Nomura). MS calls adjusted EBITDA a 17% beat, with domestic ports +11% and international ports +256% (MS).

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 guidance of revenue Rs430-450bn, EBITDA Rs250-260bn and net debt/EBITDA above 2.5x, and said it would revisit it after H1. Nomura leaves estimates largely unchanged and forecasts a 19% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29, with net debt/EBITDA at 1.9x (Nomura). MS sees modest upside to consensus EPS and cites the Colombo Phase 2 and Mundra container catalysts, though domestic volume growth was a muted 2% (MS). CLSA notes the FY31 plan of 1bt traffic, a c.15% CAGR (CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs2,338mn, 15% above Jefferies' estimate of Rs2,041mn. Liquid revenue grew 31% YoY as the JNPA terminal ramped up and realisations stabilised. Gas revenue fell only 3% despite a 45% drop in India's LPG imports, helped by parentage-backed sourcing. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 16% YoY to Rs1,794mn, 14% above Jefferies' estimate, with the margin at 76.8% (+211bps YoY). Liquid segment EBIT margin improved to 54.7% from 43.2%. The beat came from revenue, since the margin was in line with the estimate (76.9%). (Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs2,435 mn grew 22% YoY and came in 5% above Jefferies' estimate of Rs2,328 mn, led by Liquid revenue up 31% YoY and Gas revenue up 15% YoY on 19% higher LPG throughput (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,792 mn (+24% YoY) was 7% below Jefferies' estimate of Rs1,918 mn, with margin at 73.6% against a 82.4% estimate. Adjusting for the Hindustan Aegis consolidation in FY25, Jefferies puts the miss at 24%, as LPG throughput was lower with Middle East tensions (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management reiterated its USD 5bn capex plan through FY31E. Expansions at JNPA and Kandla remain on track and lift Liquid and LPG capacities by 25% and 34%. Jefferies cut-in 1-3% EBITDA revisions to reflect new capacity and raised its FY27 revenue and EPS estimates by 3% and 6%. It models a 36% FY26-30E EBITDA CAGR and raised its target price to Rs280 from Rs240, but downgraded the stock to Hold because the growth is priced in. (Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3,001 mn was 10.7% above Kotak's estimate and up 19.8% YoY, as realisations rose 25% YoY (17% above Kotak's estimate) on a full price hike from April, a favourable mix and one-off provisions plus storage-linked income. Volumes were weak at -5.5% YoY because of the Middle East disruption, with liquids down 45% and container volumes up 2% (Kotak, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,824 mn was 11.4% above Kotak's estimate and up 23.1% YoY, with margin at 60.8%. Kotak calls it a 5% beat on an adjusted basis; Jefferies puts EBITDA 12% above its estimate after adjusting for Rs316 mn of prior-period income. The beat came from higher realisations, partly offset by a 23% YoY rise in other expenses that included seasonal items (Kotak, Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 6.3% YoY to Rs2,677 mn, 3.6% above Kotak's estimate, even though volumes fell 3% YoY. Blended realisation rose about 10% YoY, helped by the January 2026 price hikes of about 3%, and the bulk segment was weak. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 10.8% YoY to Rs1,736 mn, 10.3% above Kotak's estimate, with the margin up 260bps YoY to 64.9%. The margin gain came from better realisations and lower opex: cost de-escalations, the timing of staff costs, lower repair and maintenance, and lower bulk volumes. EBITDA is adjusted for SEIS income. Jefferies, adjusting for Rs496 mn of prior-period income, also calls it 13% above its estimate. (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management guides FY27 container volumes up 4-5% YoY (helped by Maersk's new Far East service) and bulk and liquid volumes down 12-19% YoY. The liquid jetty ramp-up is expected to take 3-5 years. Kotak keeps FY27 EBITDA largely intact but cuts FY28/29 EBITDA by 4-5% on lower container and liquid volumes, and trims fair value to Rs184 from Rs186 (BUY). Jefferies broadly maintains estimates, with a 4-9% volume cut offset by better realisations and margins, and raises its target to Rs131 (Underperform). It sees concession renewal talks progressing but any update is 12-18 months away (Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR14.4bn (+18% y-y) was about 1% above Bloomberg consensus (Nomura) and 2% below Kotak's estimate. Port revenue rose 11% y-y on 6% volume growth, and logistics revenue grew 72% y-y on the rakes business and Navkar volumes. Fujairah was weak. (Nomura, Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR6.7bn (+16% y-y, -12% q-q) was about 2% above consensus (Nomura) but 2.5% below Kotak's estimate. Logistics drove half of the EBITDA growth. Margin was 46.6%, down 85bp y-y, on a higher share of lower-margin logistics and an INR80-90mn one-time crane shifting expense. Fujairah disruption cost INR0.6-0.7bn. (Nomura, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management maintained its FY27E/28E EBITDA guidance of INR30bn/50bn (15%/67% y-y growth). Port volume growth guidance is a muted 5% for FY27, including a ~1.5% Kolkata terminal impact. Keni port commissioning slipped by up to a year to FY30E, and Tuticorin and Kolkata were also deferred. Nomura raised FY27F/28F EBITDA by 1% and its TP to INR392 (Buy). Kotak raised FV marginally to Rs325 for the QIP (Reduce). (Nomura, Kotak)

companies.name: ABB India
companies.note: Management believes commodity inflation and INR depreciation will continue for the next few quarters. While demand from data centres and power is strong, we believe broader industrial capex growth will remain subdued. Camera modules ramping up and displays to start from 4QFY27E. order inflows (OI) grew 50%/2% y-y/q-q to INR43.6bn in 2QCY26.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs35.6bn grew 21% y/y and 12% q/q, about 8% above consensus (1% above Nomura's estimate and 6% above JPM's). Electrification was the standout, with revenue up 31% y/y on data centres, metals & mining, cement and buildings. (JP, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.47bn was in line with consensus (Nomura, on adjusted EBITDA) but 10% below JPM's estimate. The margin of 12.6% fell 108bps y/y and 27bps q/q as copper (+32%) and silver (+97%) cost inflation lifted material costs to 62.9% of revenue; forex was a partial offset. (JP, Nomura)

outlook.note: Management expects order-inflow growth to stay firm, led by data centres, power and water, but flags that margin headwinds from commodity inflation, competition and supply-chain bottlenecks will persist near term, with price hikes showing up only after a lag. Nomura raises FY26/27/28 revenue estimates by 1%/9%/12% but cuts EBITDA margin by 180/115/55bp, leaving PAT -11%/-1%/+7%. JPM's EPS changes are -1%/+1%/+8%, and it sees mid-teens EBITDA margins as hard to reach soon. (Nomura, JP)

companies.name: Bharat Heavy Electricals
companies.note: BHEL’s power segment order flow YTD in FY27 based on announcements is down 13% YoY while FY26 was down 27% YoY. Underperformrating on Bharat Heavy Elec. (BHEL) as the entry of Chinese suppliers, JSWToshiba, L&T and Thermax into its core thermal equipment segment question its market dominance and its backlog looks to have peaked, while the stock is pricing in a lot more.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 40% YoY to Rs77.0bn, 36% above consensus and 14% above MS's estimate. Power segment revenue grew 52% YoY, helped by execution picking up on a low base and a 27% YoY larger backlog (MS, CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.0bn (6.5% margin vs -9.8% a year ago) was above consensus of Rs4.3bn and above MS's estimate of Rs3.0bn. CLSA says the quality was average, as 723bps of the 1,633bps margin gain came from lower other expenses, which include non-cash provisions and FX gains (MS, CLSA, JP).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 24% yoy to Rs93.0bn but came in 12.7% below Kotak's Rs106.6bn estimate. Industry segment revenue rose 45% yoy, while Power grew a modest 17% as execution slowed from 1Q (Kotak). CLSA calls the 24% growth a good print, but inflows fell 81% yoy (Kotak, CLSA).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 77% yoy to Rs10.3bn at an 11.0% margin, 1.6% below Kotak's estimate in dollar terms. Gross margin of 36.5% beat the 35% guidance (~600bps yoy gain, ~400bps above Kotak's estimate), which offset the revenue shortfall. Jefferies calls it a 12% EBITDA beat against its own estimate and CLSA a positive surprise (Kotak, Jeff, CLSA).

outlook.note: Estimates rise: Kotak raises estimates 3-5% with a lower working-capital assumption and a roll-forward (FV Rs160 from Rs150), CLSA raises FY27-29 PAT by 10-11% (TP Rs351 from Rs306), and Jefferies raises FY27-30E EBITDA by 17%+ (PT Rs335 from Rs270). Order flow is the weak spot: 2Q inflows were only Rs35-40bn, down 14% for 1H. The backlog was up 17-18% yoy but flat to down 1% qoq, the first qoq decline in three years. All three see thermal ordering peaking and rising competition (Kotak, CLSA, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs56.6bn grew 4.3% YoY and 25% QoQ. Standalone revenue rose 1.7% YoY to Rs30bn on 4.9% higher unit sales at the Kolkata distribution business. No consensus or broker estimate for the quarter is printed (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs10.75bn fell 1.6% YoY and 8.7% QoQ, with the margin at 19.0% against 20.1% a year ago. Chandrapur's generation and lower Malegaon and Rajasthan losses helped, but Haldia's decline offset them. PAT was Rs4.0bn, up 3.9% YoY, which Kotak calls unexciting with mediocre standalone and subsidiary performance (Kotak). CLSA also calls the 3% PAT growth modest, though PAT excluding treasury income grew 6% (CLSA).

outlook.note: CESC plans to double PAT to Rs28bn by FY30 (Rs15.4bn in FY26). It is acquiring a 1.4GWp operating solar portfolio from ReNew at an EV of Rs48.6bn (about 9x EV/EBITDA) and targets 4.8GWp of renewables by FY29E. Execution on organic renewables has been tardy, and Kotak sees valuations as full (13x P/E, 1.6x P/B on FY28E), so it keeps Reduce with an unchanged FV of Rs172 (Kotak). CLSA is more positive: it sees improving earnings quality and keeps its Rs204 target with an Outperform rating (CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs32.8bn (+14% y/y, -5% q/q) was about 6% below consensus (Nomura) and 4.3% below Jefferies' estimate. Power Systems grew 31% y/y to Rs14.0bn on a 59% higher order book, while Industrial Systems rose only 6% and Semiconductors/Others fell 11% (Nomura, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.17bn (+9% y/y, -11% q/q) missed consensus by about 10% (Nomura) and was 16% below Jefferies' estimate. The EBITDA margin was 12.7% against 13.2% a year ago. Semiconductor losses ran 55% above expectations, and Industrial Systems margins fell 144bp y/y to 8.7% after a one-off Rs200mn railway provision, which offset Power Systems margin expansion of 212bp to 23.2% (Nomura, Jeff, JP).

outlook.note: Power Systems outlook remains strong: the order book is Rs144bn (+59% y/y, 2.8x FY26 sales), transformer capacity is being expanded from 23 GVA to 75 GVA with a further 45 GVA planned, and export order inflow rose 84% y/y. Management expects high-teens growth in motors, but railway execution should stay flattish and Industrial margins should stay near 9%. Semiconductor losses are expected to continue near term. Estimates were cut after the miss: Nomura cut FY27F EPS by 5% (Buy, TP Rs1,100), Jefferies cut it by 4% (Hold, TP Rs855), and JPMorgan kept Overweight with a Rs930 target (Nomura, Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations more than doubled to Rs8.3bn (+107% y/y, +49% q/q), driven by RE Services revenue rising to Rs3.0bn (from Rs0.4bn) and RE Power Sales revenue up 47% y/y to Rs5.3bn, as 530MW was commissioned in the quarter. No consensus or quarterly estimate is printed; JPMorgan calls the quarter broadly in line with full-year estimates (JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 58% y/y and 57% q/q to Rs4.2bn. RE Power Sales EBITDA margin expanded from 78.25% to 87.16% on operating leverage, and RE Services margin improved from 8.69% to 11.19%. Reported PAT turned positive at Rs552mn against a Rs166mn loss a year ago. Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 50.6% from 66.1% because of the larger share of lower-margin RE Services revenue (JP).

outlook.note: Management reiterated guidance of at least 1.5GW of RE capacity commissioning in FY27, with 403MW (40%) of the ~1GW STU-connected and onsite solar target already done in Q1, and at least Rs30bn reported EBITDA in FY28. Contracted-under-execution capacity of 2,510MW gives 18-24 months of commissioning visibility. Data and AI customers are 42% of the 6.0GW contracted capacity. JPMorgan maintains Overweight with a PT of Rs1,478 (13x FY28E EBITDA) (JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 69% YoY, 17% above consensus (25% above Jefferies' estimate), driven by strong execution and the HVDC revenue ramp-up, with the order book of Rs322bn (4.0x FY26 sales) supporting the run-rate. (Jeff, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 135% YoY to Rs3.6bn, 41% above Jefferies' estimate. The margin was 14.6% (+410bps YoY) against the 13.0% expected, as operating leverage more than offset a 380bps YoY fall in gross margin from product mix. (Jeff)
1Q27.vsBasis: revenue: consensus (JP: 17% above consensus); EBITDA: broker estimate (Jefferies)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue from operations of Rs27.5bn (+46% YoY, +32% QoQ) came in 13% above both JPM and consensus, helped by exports at 37% of order inflow and strong HVDC/project execution (JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs4,163mn (after Rs315mn derivative/FX loss) was 5% above consensus. Adjusted operating EBITDA of Rs4,478mn was 13% above consensus, but its 16.3% margin was flat QoQ because gross margin fell 261bps and other expenses rose 27% QoQ (JP).

outlook.note: Order inflow was Rs51bn, of which Rs17bn was HVDC exports; excluding HVDC, orders rose 26% YoY. The first BESS order and several data-centre orders were won, and one large HVDC order is expected to be tendered in the next 6-12 months. The Vadodara large-power-transformer capacity is due by CY28. JP raised FY27/28 adj. EPS by 9.7%/6.3% and its PT to Rs40,500; Jeff raised its PT to Rs45,790 and expects 30%+ revenue growth to continue. GS has a Neutral rating on valuation, while citing strong execution and broadening growth beyond HVDC. (Jeff, JP, GS)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales rose 18% YoY to Rs38.1bn on the 250MW Subansiri Lower unit commissioned in the quarter, but Parbati II and Subansiri revenue is booked at only 80% of the proposed tariff (CLSA). Kotak's standalone revenue of Rs35.4bn was 3% below its estimate (Kotak). [CLSA, Kotak]
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 31% YoY to Rs23.5bn with margin up 571bp to 62%, on higher incentives and rate-regulated income. Kotak's standalone EBITDA was 5% above its estimate. [CLSA, Kotak]

4Q26.revNote: Standalone net sales of Rs27.4 bn (+33% YoY) were 22% above Kotak's estimate, helped by one-off revenue from Parbati II (Rs2 bn revenue shortfall recognised) and 3x250 MW of Subansiri Lower commissioned in 2HFY26 (Kotak). CLSA's consolidated revenue was Rs28.2 bn (+25% YoY). No consensus figure is printed in either note.
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA of Rs12.4 bn (+35% YoY) was 45% above Kotak's estimate, and margin was 45% in line with the year-ago level, again helped by the Parbati II and Subansiri one-offs; Kotak says earnings growth was driven by one-offs, including a Rs15.2 bn deferred tax credit at PAT level. CLSA's consolidated EBITDA was Rs12.0 bn (+21% YoY), with recurring PAT down 10% YoY (Kotak, CLSA).

outlook.note: CLSA sees the best still to come in 2HFY27: Teesta V restarted in Jul-26, 250MW more at Subansiri Lower, and the final tariff order for Parbati II, which could add about Rs11bn to PAT. It forecasts 90% growth in ex-minority REE over FY26-30CL and keeps its Rs117 target price. Kotak is cautious: Parbati II and Subansiri tariff orders are still pending, which keeps earnings depressed until CERC approves them. It targets 2.7GW of commissioning by Mar-27 and largely maintains its estimates (CLSA, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales after regulatory adjustment of Rs113.9 bn were flat YoY and 10% below Kotak's Rs126.7 bn estimate. Transmission revenue fell 1% YoY. It was hit by a regulatory step-down on projects older than 12 years (Rs3.3 bn revenue drag) and a Rs(-)1.1 bn regulatory deferral balance, partly offset by consultancy (+28% YoY) (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs94.3 bn was up 1% YoY and 9% below Kotak's Rs103.9 bn estimate. The base quarter had Rs2.3 bn of interest income accrued for delayed tariff approvals. Reported PAT of Rs36.0 bn was down 0.9% YoY against the Rs38.8 bn estimate, and Bernstein also called it an earnings miss (Kotak, Bern).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue from operations of Rs117bn fell 5% YoY and missed consensus by about 10%. Management attributed the decline to projects completing their 12-year high-depreciation tariff period, which lowers regulated revenue (Bern).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs90.7bn fell 11% YoY and missed consensus by about 17%, as operating costs jumped to Rs26.0bn from Rs20.5bn a year ago, taking margin to 78% from 83%. PAT of Rs45.5bn beat on a deferred-tax benefit, but Bernstein calls the quality of earnings poor and sees a miss again in FY27 (Bern).

outlook.note: Management maintained its FY27/28E capex guidance of Rs370-450 bn and its capitalization guidance of Rs300-350 bn. It is backed by Rs1.75 tn of orders in hand, about 80% of them TBCB. Kotak sees earnings growth lagging because TBCB projects are back-ended, and cut fair value to Rs285 from Rs295 with REDUCE. Bernstein says its estimates are below consensus but not as low as the reported quarter. CLSA stays Outperform on a 15% capitalisation growth guide (Kotak, Bern, CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 39% YoY to Rs24.9bn, 8% above Jefferies' Rs23.0bn estimate (JP: 12% above its Rs22.2bn). Power Transmission grew 42% YoY and Power Generation 36% YoY, helped by exports (up 75% YoY in 9MFY26). (Jeff, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 72% YoY to Rs5.9bn, 31% above Jefferies' estimate (JP: 33% above). Margin expanded about 450bps YoY to 23.6% (Jefferies' estimate 19.4%) on lower raw-material and other costs plus operating leverage. (Jeff, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 27% YoY and 25% QoQ to Rs23.9bn, 4% above consensus and 2% above JPM. Generation (+29% YoY, 11% above consensus) drove the beat, while Transmission (+26% YoY) was 1% below consensus. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.98bn (+39% YoY) was 6% above consensus and 4% above JPM, with margin at 20.8% against 19.1% a year ago. Generation margin expansion from operating leverage helped; generation EBIT was up 94% YoY, while transmission EBIT margin fell to 16.8% from 20.3%. (JP)

outlook.note: Jefferies sees Power T&D ordering staying robust on India's transmission and data-centre spend. It raised its FY26-28E EPS by 1-8% and its PT to Rs4,800 from Rs4,500 (Buy). Order book is up 16% YoY, but Generation order backlog is down 3% YoY and Generation growth is expected to be a stable 10-12%. JPMorgan raised FY26E EPS 8.1% and its PT to Rs3,600 from Rs3,500, but stays Neutral because Generation orders lag and TX ordering momentum is the key watch. (Jeff, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Net sales rose 98% YoY to Rs9,994mn in 4QFY26, and FY26 revenue was up 26% on generation growth of 25% to 13,302MU. The report does not print the year-ago figure, so 5,047 is backed out of the printed +98% and is approximate. No consensus or broker estimate for the quarter is given (CLSA, 2026/05/19).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 71% YoY to Rs4,126mn, but margin fell 647bps to 41%, with other costs up 47%. The year-ago figure of 2,413 is backed out of the printed +71% and is approximate. Recurring PAT was a loss of Rs3.3bn, down 158% YoY, hit by losses of Rs2.6bn at SJVN Green and Rs930mn at the new Buxar thermal plant (CLSA, 2026/05/19).

outlook.note: CLSA cut FY27-28CL EPS by 35% and 23% on project start delays (including Arun 3, now pushed to FY30) and a lack of rail-based coal supply at Buxar. It cut its DCF-based TP from Rs90 to Rs72 and kept Hold. Leverage has tripled over FY23-26, capex of Rs250bn is still due over FY27-29, and the dividend was cut in FY25 and FY26 (CLSA, 2026/05/19).

companies.name: Thermax
companies.note: Thermax’s June Qtr order flow was tepid at just 2% YoY rise. Data centres was 17% of the orders, which management highlighted is a key growth area ahead including chiller/boiler exports to US

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs23.0bn grew just 7% y/y and was 6% below JPMorgan's estimate. Industrial Infra revenue fell 9% y/y, and Rs3bn of finished goods could not be shipped because of elevated Gulf shipping rates. Industrial Products grew 11% and Green Solutions 41%. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs686mn was down 70% y/y and 75% below JPMorgan's estimate. Margin fell to 3.0% from 10.5%. A Rs910mn cost over-run on one legacy government project in Industrial Infra, a Rs100mn commodity cost headwind in Industrial Products and a Rs200mn loss at FEPL in Green Solutions drove the miss. (JP)

outlook.note: Management guided to significant margin improvement in Q2-Q4, with revenue above Rs30bn per quarter versus Rs23bn in Q1. Legacy PSU projects are now under 5% of the order book, and Industrial Infra margin is seen near 10% once they wash out. Management also expects to beat last year's total order inflow. JPMorgan still cut FY27E EPS 18.6% and FY28E EPS 4.5%, and lowered its PT to Rs4,139 from Rs4,335. It stays Neutral on valuation. Jefferies cut FY27-29E estimates 10-11% and its PT to Rs5,200 from Rs5,930, but kept Buy. (JP, Jeff)

companies.name: Waaree Energies
companies.note: expects margin improvement 2HFY27 onward from cell capacity addition and US manufacturing expansion. management maintained its FY27E EBITDA guidance of INR70-77bn as it expects operating performance to improve in the upcoming quarters, led by: 1) increased sale of high-margin DCR modules, 2) ramp up of US revenue, and 3) higher offtake in non-DCR segment. Waaree is setting up 3.5GWh cell capacity on LFP technology sourced from China. It has imported 10GWh of equipment from China. It is also investing in a Na-ion optionality. Ramp up in BESS volume in FY28 (after product qualification) is likely to aid Ebitda growth.

1Q27.revNote: Adjusted revenue of INR75.8bn (+71% y-y, -11% q-q) excludes a one-off INR3.5bn refund of reciprocal duties (reported INR79.3bn). It was 6% below Bloomberg consensus but 14% above Nomura's forecast. Module sales rose 89% y-y to 3.6GW and retail revenue rose 130% y-y, while US exports from India fell 72% y-y. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA of INR10.9bn (+9% y-y, -31% q-q) was 30% below consensus and 13% below Nomura's estimate. Adjusted gross margin fell 977bp y-y to 22.4% on higher raw material costs, and EBITDA margin fell to 14.4% (-489bp vs consensus). Kotak also cites weak non-DCR demand and delayed US clearances. (Nomura, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reaffirmed its FY27E EBITDA guidance of INR70-77bn. It expects module utilisation to recover to 70-75% in 2HFY27, cell output to rise to 1.1-1.2GW in 2QFY27 and about 1.5GW in 3QFY27, and India-to-US shipments to restart from August. The order book is a record INR615bn (book-to-bill 2.1x). Against that, Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 3-6% and fair value to Rs2,750 (REDUCE), saying recovery depends on a sharp 2H ramp-up, while Nomura kept its Buy and INR3,750 TP. (Nomura, Kotak)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 27% y-y and came in 9% above Bloomberg consensus (INR60.7bn) and Nomura's forecast. Domestic and exports business rose 34%/29% y-y, with conductors up 30% (volumes +9%, realisations +19%) and cables up 35%. (Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 8% y-y to INR5.0bn, 5% above consensus and 3% above Nomura's estimate. Margin fell 129 bps y-y to 7.5% on a higher mix of lower-margin volumes, higher other expenses (+37% y-y) and employee costs (+46%). Conductor EBITDA/MT was up 8% y-y at INR44,919 on a premium product mix. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 29% y-y and was 4% above Bloomberg consensus (3% above Nomura), led by healthier-than-expected transformer oil (TSO) revenue, up 35% y-y on sharply higher gas-oil realisations. Cables grew 29% and conductors 20% y-y. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was 54% above consensus (48% above Nomura). Margin expanded 263bp y-y to 11.5%, against 7.7% consensus, on TSO outperformance: TSO EBIT margin was 19.5% against 7.7% a year earlier. EBITDA/KL was INR25,482, up 264% y-y. This was despite a INR0.9bn inventory provision and a 14% y-y fall in TSO volumes. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Nomura raises FY27F EBITDA by 10% (margin +64bp) after the 1Q beat and lifts the TP to INR15,400 from INR14,240, with FY28-29F EBITDA largely unchanged. Cables are growing faster than the FY27E guidance of 25%, and the order book is healthy: cables INR19.3bn (+16% y-y) and conductors INR102bn (+31% y-y, exports 57%). US orders are rising and approvals from Meta, Microsoft and Google for data-centre copper cables could lift exports. Risks are lower oil prices causing inventory losses and delayed T&D capex. (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR1.9bn (+30% y-y, as printed; the table rounds to INR bn) is a non-event because ABREL books revenue on project completion, so meaningful recognition starts only from FY29F. Operationally, pre-sales fell 21% y-y to INR3.3bn, below Nomura's INR4bn estimate, after INR0.77bn of terminations at Niyaara and Arika. Collections rose 31% y-y to INR7.1bn. No consensus or P&L estimate is printed (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was a loss of INR0.6bn, against a loss of INR0.4bn a year ago (-29.3% margin vs -27.4%). This reflects completion-method accounting, with low recognised revenue against ongoing costs. PAT from continuing ops was -INR0.7bn (Nomura)

outlook.note: FY27 launch guidance is maintained at INR96bn, with Birla Niyaara Tower C, Worli, Taranya and Evam launches in 3QFY27 and the rest in 4QFY27. Nomura expects sales momentum to improve from 3QFY27. The company is net-debt-free after selling its paper business to ITC for ~INR35bn, and new business development is picking up with two redevelopment deals (Khar West, Vashi) worth ~INR43bn of revenue potential (Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs11.2 bn fell 13% yoy and 23% qoq, 15% below Kotak's estimate. Residential revenue declined 21% yoy to Rs7.1 bn as no new launches took place in the quarter. Leasing revenue rose 9% yoy to Rs3.3 bn and hospitality revenue grew 2% (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.6 bn (+12% yoy, -1% qoq) was 2% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 32.4% vs 25.3% a year ago, helped by residential EBITDA margin improving to 21% (13% in FY2026). Leasing EBITDA grew 3% yoy, while hospitality EBITDA declined 6% on a lower 31% margin (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management reiterated its FY27 pre-sales guidance of Rs90 bn (+20% yoy), backed by 9.4 mn sq. ft of launches (Rs100 bn GDV) planned in FY27. It has also added 4 mn sq. ft of annuity assets to its under-construction pipeline and plans to double hotel inventory over 5-6 years. 1QFY27 pre-sales fell 5% yoy to Rs10.6 bn with no launches, as the Chennai relaunch was held up by a regulatory hurdle. Kotak maintained BUY but cut its fair value to Rs875 from Rs900 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs9.7 bn (+52% yoy, +1% qoq) was in line with Kotak's Rs9.73 bn estimate. The jump comes from the Ecoworld Bengaluru acquisition, which added Rs2.2 bn of NOI, plus blended in-place rentals of Rs104/sq. ft (+7% yoy) (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs7.1 bn (+54% yoy) was about 2% above Kotak's Rs7.03 bn estimate, so in line. NOI of Rs7.5 bn (+50% yoy) was in line, and same-store NOI grew 8% yoy excluding Ecoworld. Occupancy was steady at 93% (89% a year ago). Morgan Stanley calls results versus consensus a modest shortfall, with DPU of Rs5.6/unit (+7% yoy) the weakest growth among Indian office REITs (Kotak, MS).

outlook.note: Management targets 96% occupancy by end-FY2027 with a strong leasing pipeline (1.1 mn sq. ft gross leasing in 1QFY27, 14% re-leasing spread). It is buying a 50% stake in Godrej BKC at an EV of Rs17 bn (7.4% cap rate), which lifts LTV to about 27%. Kotak keeps ADD and raises FV to Rs370 from Rs360. Morgan Stanley stays Equal-weight with a Rs340 target and flags a modest downward revision to consensus EPS, with FY27 DPU growth of 7-8% the weakest among peers (Kotak, MS).

companies.name: DLF
companies.note: There were no new launches during the quarter, with inventory running down to ~Rs173bn (or ~10 months of inventory; JPMe).

1Q27.revNote: Devco revenue of Rs12.8bn (-53% YoY, -29% QoQ) missed Jefferies' estimate. No new launches in the quarter, so recognition stayed low and pre-sales fell 94% YoY to Rs6.6bn. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Devco EBITDA of Rs1.5bn (-59% YoY) was below Jefferies' estimate, with margin at 11.7% vs 13.4% a year ago on the weak revenue base. A strong rentco performance (DCCDL EBITDA +8% YoY) offset this, leaving PAT of Rs7.9bn (+4% YoY) only a small miss. (Jeff)

2Q27.revNote: Reported revenue fell 23% YoY (-2% QoQ) to Rs12.6bn, as revenue recognition remains lumpy and lower than the year-ago quarter. None of the three notes gives a revenue consensus or estimate for the quarter. Morgan Stanley calls reported earnings 'less meaningful'. (MS)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA collapsed 92% YoY to Rs230mn (2% margin vs 17% a year ago). JPMorgan says realised gross margin dropped to 47% (vs 51% in 1Q27 and 48% in 2Q26) and other expenses rose 29% QoQ. MS calls the 2% margin 'too low'. Neither note gives an EBITDA consensus. (MS, JP)

outlook.note: Management is on track for the Rs200bn FY27 pre-sales guidance, but this needs strong execution on Magnolias 2 (Rs80bn), Mumbai (Rs30bn) and Dahlias (~Rs20bn/quarter). FY28 is seen as the revenue-recognition inflection point as Arbour completes. Rental income is Rs68bn annualised against the Rs82bn FY27 exit guidance (MS), and CLSA notes possible short-term construction delays. CLSA keeps its estimates and its Rs810 TP, JP keeps its Rs800 TP and OW, and MS keeps EW with a Rs730 TP. (MS, JP, CLSA)

companies.name: Embassy Office Parks REIT
companies.note: 13% NOI/10% DPU growth guidance is well on track after a strong start to the year. For FY27, Embassy maintained ~Rs27.8/unit (+10% YoY) distribution at midpoint with occupancy range of 92-93

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs12.4bn rose 17% y/y and was 4% above Kotak's estimate. Rental income grew 17% y/y on a larger asset base (43.5 msf vs 40.4 msf), 200bps higher occupancy (90%) and 4% higher in-place rent (Rs96/sf), and solar revenue rose 75% vs the estimate (Kotak). Jefferies calls NOI of Rs10.2bn (+17% y/y) in line with its expectations (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs9.6bn rose 17% y/y and was about 5% above Kotak's estimate, helped by NOI of Rs10.2bn (+17% y/y, +5% q/q) and a steady ~82% NOI margin (Kotak). Higher property tax and interest costs held DPU growth to 9% y/y (Rs6.31), 2% above JPM's estimate (JP).

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of NOI Rs41.5-43.5bn (+13% y/y) and DPU Rs27-28.6 (+10% y/y), with 1Q at 24% and 23% of the range, and leasing remains strong (1.3 msf, 81% from GCCs). Estimates are mixed: JPM raised FY27/28E NOI by 1-2% but cut DPU by 3-4% because of higher interest and cash tax, and said the Four Seasons exit and delayed deliveries could mute FY28. Jefferies kept its estimates, and Kotak and Jefferies raised fair value/TP to Rs485/Rs477 (Kotak, JP, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs5.06bn (+16% YoY, -85% QoQ) was ~31% below Kotak's Rs7.33bn estimate because only one project (Godrej Palm Retreat, Noida, 0.9msf) was delivered in the quarter. Pre-sales of Rs86.5bn (+22% YoY) and collections of Rs43.5bn (+18% YoY) were healthy and in line with JPM's estimates. (Kotak, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA loss of Rs2.85bn compared with Kotak's estimated loss of Rs1.05bn and a loss of Rs2.43bn a year ago, because revenue recognition was low. PAT of Rs3.58bn (-43% YoY) was propped up by other income of Rs8.4bn. Net operating cash flow fell 58% YoY to Rs4.0bn as construction outflows rose 54%, and net debt rose Rs12.2bn QoQ to Rs76.4bn (net debt/equity 0.39x). (Kotak, CLSA)

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 guidance: pre-sales Rs390bn (+14%), collections Rs240bn (+20%), OCF Rs90bn (+15%) and deliveries of 13.5msf. It targets OCF of Rs200-220bn over FY27-28 and positive FCF by FY28, with net debt capped at Rs100bn. Near-term cash flow and margins are weak: BD spend of Rs95bn is ~48% of the Rs200bn guidance, and net debt is rising. CLSA kept its estimates and Rs2,600 TP (Outperform). JPM stays OW with a Rs2,500 TP. Kotak raised its FV to Rs1,930 from Rs1,800 and kept REDUCE. (Kotak, CLSA, JP)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 15% YoY and 4% QoQ to Rs12.4bn. MS's AlphaSignals tag rates the financial results in-line versus consensus. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: NOI rose 15% YoY and 6% QoQ to Rs11.1bn, with NOI margin at 89% (+140bps QoQ). DPU of Rs1.70 was up 5% QoQ, but MS says 1Q DPU is tracking marginally behind its F27e target. NOI and DPU are 23% and 24% of F27e. (MS)

outlook.note: Committed occupancy was 93% (4Q: 92%). Economic occupancy was 88%, which MS expects to reach 91% by 4QF27, against an F27 committed occupancy target of 94-95%. MTM potential is 25%, and LTV of 18% is the lowest among peers. MS sees Bangalore occupancy (87%, largely SEZ) improving over the next 2-3 quarters. 1Q DPU is tracking marginally behind F27e, and the report shows no estimate changes. MS keeps its Overweight rating and Rs127 target. (MS)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs50.0bn (+43% YoY) was ~16% above the Bloomberg consensus of Rs43.1bn. The upside came from revenue recognition on the ~Rs13bn Digital Edge data-centre land sale at Rs425mn/acre. Ex-land-sale revenue was about Rs40bn, up 14% YoY (Jeff, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs19.2bn (+95% YoY) was ~44% above the Rs13.4bn consensus. Margin rose to 38.5%, up ~10pp YoY, because the land sale carried high margins and gross margins improved. Ex-land-sale EBITDA was Rs11.2bn, up 14% YoY (Jeff, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management kept its FY27 pre-sales guidance of Rs240bn. It targets ~40% of that in 1HFY27, with the rest in 2HFY27, which implies Rs193bn over the remaining nine months (+20% YoY). Nomura calls this achievable. Data-centre land earmarked was raised to 660 acres from 400, and ~143 more acres are planned for monetisation at ~Rs600mn/acre (~Rs90bn over 3-4 years). Net debt fell to Rs49.3bn (0.2x gearing). Jefferies flags a 2H-heavy year. JPMorgan expects minimal consensus revisions because weak residential sales (-24% YoY ex-land) offset the land sales, and it stays Neutral (Nomura, Jeff, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 26% YoY and 6.8% QoQ to Rs9.5bn, helped by the Chennai acquisitions and in-place rents up 11% YoY to Rs81/sq ft. Kotak was 2.6% above its own estimate, but MS rates the results in-line with consensus (Kotak, MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 28% YoY to Rs7.2bn. NOI grew 28% (16.2% like-for-like) and the NOI margin improved to 83% from 82%. DPU of Rs6.67 was up 15.2% YoY and was a 'record' per Jefferies (Kotak, Jeff, MS).
1Q27.vsBasis: consensus (MS AlphaSignals: results in-line vs consensus)

outlook.note: Management expects committed occupancy to reach ~97% by FY27 and ~100% at the Chennai assets. It sees ~20% MTM rental upside and targets Rs17-18bn NOI by FY30 (~+60%). The 6.6 mn sq ft pipeline is 69% pre-leased. Jefferies trimmed FY27/28E DPU by 1% each but raised NAV/PT to Rs556. Jefferies also flags a possible REIT tax benefit (Jeff, Kotak, MS).

companies.name: Nexus Select Trust
companies.note: FY27 DPU guidance of Rs9.8–10.0 (~9% growth).

1Q27.revNote: Total revenues (NDCF statement) rose 11% y/y and 4% q/q to Rs6.86bn, led by consumption growth of 17% y/y (Rs38.5bn), Hospitality revenue up 33% y/y and Office up 14% y/y. JPM prints no revenue consensus comparison. (JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 9% y/y and 9% q/q to Rs4.97bn, with the margin at 72.4% (up 277bps q/q, down 163bps y/y). NOI of Rs5.1bn (up 11% y/y) was slightly above JPM/Street estimates, and cost of debt fell 30bps y/y to 7.2%. No EBITDA consensus figure is given. (JP)

outlook.note: Consumption momentum continued into July with early double-digit growth, against FY27 NOI guidance of about 7% at the midpoint (about 8% consumption growth), which looks conservative. Management will review guidance after the 2Q print. The Diamond Plaza acquisition is due to close within 40-45 days, with about 2 more in the next two quarters, and is not in guidance. JPM expects small positive revisions to Street/JPM NOI forecasts. DPU of Rs2.44 is tracking FY27 DPU guidance of Rs9.8-10.0. (JP)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR13.0bn was 24% below Bloomberg consensus of INR17.2bn, even though it rose 32% y-y on a low base. Revenue recognition was slower q-q at Sky City, Eterina and Elysian, and 360 West recognised no revenue. Residential revenue was INR8.9bn (+39% y-y) and annuity revenue was INR3.3bn (+18% y-y) (Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR7.3bn was 30% below consensus of INR10.5bn, with the miss driven by the weak residential revenue. It still rose 41% y-y, and margin expanded to 56.4% from 52.7% a year ago on a strong ~95% annuity margin. PAT of INR5.4bn was 21% below consensus (Nomura, JP).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR16.7bn was 9% below Bloomberg consensus and down 6% y-y, as revenue recognition from 360 West fell to INR1.7bn from INR4.6bn in 2QFY26; residential revenue fell 11% y-y, partly offset by annuity (+17%). (Nomura)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR10.2bn was 1% above consensus and flat y-y, with the margin rising to 61.0% from 57.3% on a richer mix, as annuity EBITDA grew 17% y-y on the Sky City mall ramp-up. (Nomura)

outlook.note: Pre-sales of Rs91.5bn (+604% YoY) beat Nomura's Rs87bn estimate, driven by 360 North in Gurugram. Collections rose 40% YoY to Rs19bn and operating cash flow improved to Rs18bn. Brokers see stronger 2H27 collections and launches in South Mumbai as key drivers; Nomura keeps Buy (TP Rs2,090) and MS keeps Equal-weight (TP Rs2,030), but MS expects FY28/29 earnings growth below 20% YoY with no major completions before the Ritz hotel in 3QFY28. (Nomura, MS)

companies.name: Phoenix Mills
companies.note: Retained guidance of mid teen rental growth over FY27-28. on track to expand retail asset area by ~25% by Mar'28, which should help maintain the mid-teens lease income growth trajectory over the next 3yrs, even as consumption normalizes.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs10.7bn (+13% YoY) was 4% below Street (7% below JPM) as residential revenue recognition collapsed to Rs419mn (-42% YoY) on registration delays, while retail income grew 15% YoY but trailed JPM by 7%. Kotak notes the weak resi/other line (-93% YoY to Rs30mn) distorted growth; adjusted for it, revenue grew 17% YoY (JP, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs6.4bn (+14% YoY) was 3% below Street (7% below JPM) even though margin of 59.7% rose 47bps YoY (-110bps QoQ). Commercial (-600bps YoY) and hospitality (-270bps) margins were dragged by new offices and the Courtyard Agra ramp-up, and residential posted an ~Rs80mn EBITDA loss. Ex-resi EBITDA grew 19% YoY (JP, Kotak, MS).

outlook.note: Consumption growth is strong (+32% YoY to Rs47.3bn) and office occupancy is improving (blended 72%, +200bps QoQ), with management targeting 90% portfolio occupancy. Retail rental growth (17%) still lags consumption as new stores sit on minimum guarantee, and PMC Bangalore/Surat completions have slipped to CY27/28. JPM expects small negative Street revisions and a flat-to-down stock open; Kotak raised FV to Rs1,900 from Rs1,760 but keeps REDUCE on full valuations (23x FY28E EV/EBITDA) (JP, Kotak, MS).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs40.7bn (+167% yoy on a low base) was 19% above Kotak's Rs34.2bn estimate, driven by 1.8 mn sq. ft of residential completions in the quarter. (Kotak, Nomura)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs10.5bn (+93% yoy) was 2% below Kotak's estimate, in line. The margin of 25.7% (35.4% in 4QFY25) was hit by a higher share of lower-margin residential revenue (~19% margin) and higher overheads on strong pre-sales. Nomura flags the margin as below its 37% consensus estimate. (Kotak, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs26.8bn rose 16% YoY but fell 34% QoQ and came in 8% below Kotak's Rs29.1bn estimate. Recognition from the development business was modest, helped by 0.73 mn sq ft of residential completions (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs8.6bn fell 4% YoY and 18% QoQ, 12% below Kotak's estimate. Margin was 32.1% against 38.7% a year ago and 25.7% in 4QFY26. Residential margins were hurt by higher overheads and approval costs ahead of launches (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs5.5 bn was 40% below Kotak's Rs9.2 bn estimate and down 36% yoy, 50% qoq, on lower deliveries during the quarter. It is lagging the run-rate needed for the FY27E guidance of Rs50 bn revenue recognition (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs(-445) mn compared with Rs589 mn estimated and Rs332 mn in 1QFY26. Low revenue recognition drove it, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.3% vs 9.3% in FY26. Adjusted gross margin was 23.7% vs ~30% in the past two years (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management reiterated its FY27E guidance of Rs100 bn pre-sales (20% achieved), Rs50 bn collections (13% achieved) and Rs50 bn revenue recognition (11% achieved). Kotak sees the quarter lagging the required run-rate, with the launch pipeline concentrated in Sector 71, Gurgaon. It cut fair value to Rs940 from Rs1,000 on a lower collections trajectory but kept BUY. Net debt rose to Rs3.9 bn from Rs2 bn in March 2026. Management expects margins to improve gradually as newer, higher-margin mid-housing projects are delivered (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 44% yoy and 5% qoq to Rs5.46 bn, about 3% above Kotak's Rs5.30 bn estimate. Growth came from 25% yoy operational area growth to 10.4 mn sq. ft and a jump in other operating revenue to Rs683 mn from Rs226 mn. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA (before lease payments) of Rs3.46 bn was up 44% yoy and about 1% below Kotak's estimate, so in line. Adjusted EBITDA (after lease payments) of Rs1.07 bn was up 74% yoy and 7% above the estimate. Its margin was 19.6% (+337 bps yoy), even as occupancy slipped to 81% (-200 bps yoy). (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin and a 13 mn sq. ft operational footprint by March 2027. It is adding 2.5-3.0 mn sq. ft annually and has secured supply through FY28 and partly FY29. Kotak expects a 29% adj. EBITDA CAGR over FY26-28E and maintains BUY with an unchanged FV of Rs630. Seat retention fell to 74% and net debt rose to Rs56 mn on elevated capex. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs6.84bn rose 28% YoY on a 18.5% rise in operational area to 9.1 mn sq. ft and 838 bps higher blended occupancy of 84.9%. It was 4% below Kotak's Rs7.09bn estimate and down 2% QoQ, because 4Q had Rs470 mn of one-off customisation revenue against Rs95 mn this quarter; Jefferies calls it in line with its own estimates (Kotak, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj. EBITDA (post lease payments) of Rs1.38bn rose 69% YoY, with margin up 496 bps to 20.2% on higher occupancy. It was 16% below Kotak's Rs1.64bn estimate and down 16% QoQ, on lower customisation and VAS revenue and the drag from new area additions (Kotak, Jeff). Kotak prints no consensus figure, so both calls are against its own estimates.

4Q26.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 29% YoY and 10% QoQ to Rs7.0bn, about 3% above Kotak's estimate. Growth was driven by operational area up 16% YoY to 8.6 mn sq. ft and occupancy up 1,000 bps YoY to 86.9% (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adjusted EBITDA (post lease payments) rose 43% YoY and 22% QoQ to Rs1.65bn, about 12% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 23.7% (+228 bps YoY), helped by higher occupancy and operating leverage. The figure is adjusted, as the table's reported EBITDA is pre-lease (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management has secured 2.9 mn sq. ft of new supply for the next ~18 months and guides to adding ~28k seats (10.3 mn sq. ft) in FY27, with margins above 20% despite the capacity addition. Locked-in revenue is 2.9X locked-in rental cost. Kotak expects 28% adj. EBITDA growth over FY26-28E and raised fair value to Rs800 from Rs780. Jefferies kept its FY27/28 estimates and raised its target to Rs950 from Rs900. Jefferies expects net cash by Mar27 after capex of Rs5-6 bn (Kotak, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 16% YoY to Rs15.8bn but came in ~8% below Visible Alpha consensus. Plumbing revenue rose ~10% YoY to Rs10.5bn on higher PVC-linked realisations despite flat volumes, and chemicals rose ~30% to Rs5.3bn (paints +49%, India adhesives +25%). CLSA and Jefferies call the quarter in line with their own consensus views (MS, CLSA, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.3bn was +25% YoY but -40% QoQ and ~13% below Visible Alpha consensus. Margin was 14.7% (+107bps YoY, -368bps QoQ). Plumbing margin was 18.9% vs ~22.9% in 4Q, and India adhesives margin fell to 12.2% as raw-material prices rose >15-16% against only 6-8% price hikes. CLSA and Jefferies read the print as in line (MS, CLSA, Jeff)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs20.9bn (+24% yoy, +35% qoq) was 1% below consensus and 4% above JPM. Plumbing volumes rose 24% yoy (84,041 vs 67,692), 2% ahead of consensus, and Paint & Adhesives revenue grew 22% yoy, 10% ahead of consensus. (JP)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.8bn (+27% yoy) was 2% below consensus and in line with JPM, with the margin at 18.3% (+38bps yoy). Plumbing EBITDA margin of 22.9% (+252bps yoy) beat expectations, but Adhesives margin fell to 8.7% (-457bps yoy) on a Rs160mn brand-ambassador spend. Excluding that one-off, EBITDA would have been marginally ahead of expectations. (JP)

outlook.note: Management maintained FY27 guidance: double-digit piping volume growth with a 16-18% margin, and adhesives growth of 15-20% with a ~15% margin. July piping volumes were up ~40% YoY after PVC prices stabilised and channels restocked, and August is double-digit so far. Adhesives margins are expected to recover to 15-17% as raw-material costs ease. The 40kt CPVC resin plant is on track for December commissioning. The Pipes/Adhesives demerger has been cancelled. EPS changes are minimal (CLSA -1% to -2%, Jeff <-1%, MS minimal); price targets are Rs1,490 (CLSA), Rs1,650 (Jeff) and Rs1,660 (MS) (CLSA, Jeff, MS)

1Q27.revNote: Standalone net sales fell 15% YoY (-33% QoQ) to Rs 8.8bn. Pipes & fittings volume dropped 27% YoY to 68K MT as the Middle East-led PVC price volatility in Apr26 triggered channel destocking, a revenue-led miss versus Jefferies' estimate (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 14% YoY to Rs 1.07bn with the margin up 309bps to 12.1%, helped by higher realisations, cost control and backward integration into PVC. Raw material costs fell 23% YoY, and gross margin improved to 38.9% from 32.6%. The report does not table an EBITDA estimate, but says PAT missed on weak revenues (Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Net sales rose 12% YoY (+46% QoQ) to Rs13.1bn on better realisations, as pipe volumes were flat YoY (~102k MT) and PVC prices rose sharply in March. The note gives no revenue consensus comparison. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was up 94% YoY to Rs3.3bn, beating both Jefferies' estimate and consensus. The margin expanded to 25.3% (+1,070bps YoY) on ~Rs500mn of inventory gains from the sharp March PVC price rise, plus backward integration and captive PVC resin. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Volumes improved in May-Jun26 as PVC stabilised, July26 demand was healthy and Aug26 has started well. Management targets a core EBITDA margin below 15% in FY27e. Jefferies cut FY27-29e EPS by 6% on lower pipes and fittings volumes and trimmed the target price to Rs210 from Rs220, retaining Buy (Jeff).

companies.name: Supreme Industries
companies.note: Management maintained its FY27 guidance of 12%-13% volume growth and a 14%-14.5% Ebitda margin. This looks demanding, despite recovering PVC prices, given the ask rate for the rest of the year is 20%+ on a high base

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated sales rose 4% YoY to Rs27.2bn, held back by a 14% YoY volume decline (piping -15%) after PVC price falls in April led to channel destocking; realisations improved 13% QoQ (22% YoY) on a richer mix, with value-added products at 42% of sales (Jeff, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs3.98bn (+25% YoY) was in line with Bloomberg consensus; margin expanded 242bps YoY to 14.6% on better business mix and lower raw-material cost share, though employee costs rose 21% (CLSA, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management held its FY27 guidance of 12-13% volume growth (15-17% in piping) and a 14-14.5% EBITDA margin, with recovery expected from Sep-26 quarter as PVC prices stabilise and MIP/duty changes support restocking. Brokers see the volume target as demanding after the 14% Q1 decline: Jeff FY27 volume growth +6-7% and trimmed FY27-29e estimates 1-2%; CLSA cut FY27-29CL PAT 4% to +1% and its target price to Rs3,450 from Rs4,000 on a lower target multiple (Jeff, CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations was 2.8% above Kotak's estimate and up 27.6% YoY. Non-ratings revenue rose 30% on healthy underlying growth and the PriceMetrix acquisition, and ratings revenue rose 22% on strong surveillance and corporate bank credit growth, offsetting a ~25% decline in issuances. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA was 5.6% above Kotak's estimate and up 28.9% YoY, as revenue grew faster than costs (revenue +27% vs expenses +27%, with the beat larger on revenue). Margin was 28.6%, flat YoY and down QoQ from 30.1%. EBIT margin was stable at ~25%, and ratings segment margin expanded ~330 bps YoY to 44.3%. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Kotak upgrades CRISIL to ADD from REDUCE and raises fair value to Rs4,800 from Rs4,700 (~30X June 2028E EPS). It expects PAT to grow 23% in CY2026 and compound at 16-17% over CY2026-28. It stays constructive on the ratings cycle, helped by broad-based credit growth and a potential pickup in corporate capex, and factors in a 17-18% ratings revenue CAGR with ratings margins of 56-57%. Non-ratings revenue CAGR is assumed at ~9% beyond CY2026. The key risk is growth disappointment in non-ratings given limited disclosures. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue from operations rose 31% YoY to Rs1,634 mn, 2% below Kotak's estimate. Ratings revenue grew 13% YoY, backed by 18% bank credit growth, a pickup in bond and CP issuances, and higher working-capital demand. Non-ratings revenue grew 58-59% YoY, largely from the Fintellix acquisition (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 39% YoY to Rs551 mn, 3% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded ~200 bps YoY to 33.7%, with operating expenses up 28% YoY (employee costs +25%, other expenses +40%) against revenue growth of 31%. Ratings segment margin widened ~400 bps to ~35% (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 28% YoY and 7% QoQ to Rs1,749 mn, about 2% below Kotak's estimate. Non-ratings revenue grew 56% YoY, driven by the Fintellix acquisition, while ratings revenue grew 11% YoY (Kotak, 2026/05/22).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs696 mn was 8% above Kotak's estimate (up 18% YoY, 38% QoQ). Operating costs came in 7% lower than expected, though they still rose 37% YoY on acquisition effects, so EBITDA grew slower than revenue (Kotak, 2026/05/22).

outlook.note: Kotak upgrades to BUY with fair value of Rs6,400 (SoTP: ~33x FY2028E earnings for ratings, ~14x for non-ratings). It builds in a 14% ratings revenue CAGR and ~300 bps margin expansion to 42% over FY2027-29E, and expects ~15% overall earnings growth over FY2027-29E. Non-ratings growth should moderate to a ~9% CAGR after the M&A-led jump, with segment margins easing to ~25% by FY2029E (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Sales grew 43% YoY (+33.6% pro forma), 3% above Bloomberg consensus and 4% above CLSA's estimate. India grew 31% pro forma on 23% volume and 6.5% ASP growth, with SSSG of 18.3%. International grew 38% YoY on 37% volume growth (CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 75% YoY to Rs5.9bn, 8% above consensus. Gross margin crossed 70% for the first time (+214bps YoY) on backward integration, and EBITDA margin expanded 394bps YoY to 21.7%. International margins gained 110bps QoQ on gross margin and rent leverage (CLSA).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs25.2bn rose 40.5% yoy and came in 9.1% above Kotak's estimate. India grew 44% on a 23% rise in eyewear units, a 16% rise in ASP and 24% SSSG. International grew 35% on a 29% rise in units and better AOV. Kotak figures are pro forma, including Dealskart and Meller in the base quarter (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.4bn rose 61.6% yoy and was 21.9% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 21.4%, up 278bp yoy, on operating leverage in marketing and other fixed costs. Gross margin was flat yoy at 69.6%, and pre-IndAS India EBITDA margin expanded 622bp (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management reiterates strong demand and the potential for 10k+ stores in India. Brokers raised estimates: CLSA lifted FY27-29CL EPS by 11-18% and its TP to Rs662 from Rs604. JP raised FY27/28E EPS by about 5% and its TP to Rs665 from Rs635, and MS also raised estimates (CLSA, JP, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 14.7% yoy to Rs7.2 bn, slowing from ~20% in 4QFY26 and in line to slightly below expectations. A shift in wedding dates (Adhik Maas) and only 9 net store additions weighed on sales, and SPSF was flat yoy at Rs4,350. (Kotak, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 10.7% yoy to Rs2.1 bn, ~4% below consensus per GS and ~2% below Kotak's estimate. Margin fell 105 bps yoy to 29.8%, since employee and other costs grew ~20% yoy, faster than sales, on talent investment, marketing and new-format occupancy costs. Gross margin rose 15 bps to 59.5%. (Kotak, GS)
1Q27.vsBasis: consensus (GS text: sales growth slightly below, EBITDA 4% below); Kotak's own estimate sh

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 20.3% yoy to Rs7.7 bn, ~4.4% above Kotak's estimate, driven by festive and wedding season demand and the GST rate cut on footwear below Rs2,500. Sales per sq. ft stayed flat yoy at Rs4,750 (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 20.6% yoy to Rs2.4 bn, ~4.7% above Kotak's estimate, with margin up 10 bps yoy to 30.8% on a 30 bps gross margin expansion to 57.8% (Kotak).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 12.2% yoy to Rs7.3bn, about 2.4% below Kotak's estimate; the festive calendar shift (Durga Puja to 3Q) cost 250-350 bps of growth, with ~2%/10% yoy volume/ASP growth and SPSF down 1.2% yoy. GS also calls it below its estimate and consensus (Kotak, GS).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 15.6% yoy to Rs1.97bn, ~2.7% above Kotak's estimate; margin rose 80 bps yoy to 27.0% as gross margin expanded 215 bps to 57.4% (lower EOSS discounts, lower e-commerce mix, price hikes of 2-5%), partly offset by talent, marketing and minimum-wage costs (Kotak, GS).

outlook.note: Management expects 2H growth to improve as the festive shift reverses (October started well; 2H sales growth seen at ~mid-teens by GS) and guides to PAT margin of 13-15%. Offsetting this, frontline staff costs are expected to rise 50-100 bps, Fila EBO scale-up is delayed to FY29, and Clarks EBO launch is in 2HFY27. Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 2-5% and FV to Rs950 from Rs1,000; GS also trimmed estimates and sees 2H margins under pressure (Kotak, GS).

1Q27.revNote: Standalone revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs56.7bn, in line with Bloomberg consensus, as the top line was already known from the earlier business update. Growth came from 27% YoY store expansion, while like-for-like growth stayed low single digit (GS, MS) (GS, 2026/08/07).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA rose 33% YoY and was 10% above consensus. Gross margin expanded 150bps YoY to 46.6% (GS expects Westside drove this), and EBITDA margin rose 210bps to 19.6% against 17.8% expected (GS, MS) (GS, 2026/08/07). Figures are standalone, since the primary report tables only the standalone P&L.

outlook.note: Management flagged rising input costs, with RM inflation expected in 2Q/3Q that it plans to offset through mix and sourcing. LFL growth is expected to stay muted, with ~80% of new stores in tier 2/3 cities where sales throughput is lower. GS raised FY27-29 EPS by up to ~5% after the 1Q gross margin beat, then cut sales estimates (FY27 sales growth 18.2% vs Bloomberg 20.5%) and trimmed its TP to Rs2,960 from Rs3,000, staying Neutral. MS notes store openings are in line with the AGM plan (about 50 Westside, 200-250 Zudio, 25-40 Star a year) (GS, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs8.6 bn (+68% yoy, +57% qoq) came in 34% above Kotak's estimate. BESS commissioning (3.1 GWh) added Rs2.3 bn, and generation revenue rose 24% yoy on higher capacity and CUF (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs7.3 bn (+60% yoy, +53% qoq) was 31% above Kotak's estimate. BESS contributed Rs1.9 bn at an 83% margin, and generation EBITDA grew 20% yoy on 3 GW operational capacity and 30.9% CUF (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management is targeting 10 GWh of BESS commissioning by March 2027 and another 5 GWh the following year. Rs14 bn of FY27 BESS revenue is already locked in via short-term contracts, and PPA-signed under-construction capacity rose to 3.9 GW. Kotak raised fair value to Rs400 from Rs340 and expects a 50% EBITDA CAGR to FY2030E. The key risk is delayed transmission commissioning, which could push back the 1.5/1.1 GW additions planned for FY27/28 (Kotak).

companies.name: Emmvee Photovoltaic Power
companies.note: Orderbook +5% QoQ with strong visibility of revenue/EBITDA over 2HFY27-28.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs 15.6bn (+51% y/y, -11% q/q) was 8% ahead of Jefferies' estimate, driven by module production up 53% y/y to 970MW and cell production up 26% to 454MW, partly offset by lower realization of USc 17/Wp (-10% y/y). The order book rose 5% q/q to 9.9GW. (Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 5.5bn (+56% y/y) was 19% ahead of Jefferies' estimate. Margin rose 240bps q/q on a roughly 3x sequential jump in cell sales, with EBITDA/Wp at USc 6. (Jeff)

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs15.8bn (+39% y/y, +1% q/q) was in line with JEFe (0% variance); module production rose 40% y/y to 952MW and cell production 61% y/y to 513MW, though module volumes were flat q/q (Jeff, Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs5.6bn (+39% y/y, +2% q/q) was marginally above JEFe (+1%) at a 35.3% margin, held flat q/q by a higher cell mix, a DCR mix above 50% of revenue and lower operating costs; lower power cost and automation offset a softer gross margin (Jeff, Kotak).

outlook.note: Order book rose 5% q/q to 10.4GW (record 1.5GW of new orders), giving strong revenue/EBITDA visibility over 2HFY27-28. The 6GW integrated TOPCon facility is on schedule (module line Dec-26, cell line Mar-27), and management guided to the upper end of the Rs22-24bn FY27 EBITDA range (~Rs13bn in 2HFY27). Jefferies broadly kept estimates (PT cut to Rs430 from Rs440, Buy), while Kotak raised FY27E EPS by 11.8% on higher cell output and capitalised interest, with FY28-29 trimmed 2.6%/1.0%. Working capital rose to 138 days from 110 and net debt to Rs7.3bn on capex (Jeff, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR24.6bn (+35%/+10% y-y/q-q) was 2% above consensus and 9% above Nomura's estimate. Modules and cells made up 96% of revenue (module INR17.5bn, cell INR5.9bn), and transformers contributed 4%. The beat against Nomura's estimate came mostly from higher-than-expected transformer revenue. (Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR7.1bn (+30%/+6% y-y/q-q) was 3% above consensus and 9% above Nomura's estimate. Margin of 29.0% was in line with Nomura's estimate and 35bp above consensus. It fell 110bp y-y and 125bp q-q as a flat y-y gross margin was offset by higher employee and other expenses. JPMorgan called margin 60bp below its own estimate. (Nomura, JP)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of INR22.3bn rose 38% y/y and 15% q/q, 3% above consensus. Module revenue grew 69% y/y while cell revenue fell 31% y/y (Nomura).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR6.7bn was up 28% y/y and 7% above consensus. The margin of 30.3% fell 235bp y/y but was 112bp above consensus, even though gross margin fell 142bp y/y on execution mix and higher silver and copper prices (Nomura).

outlook.note: Order book was INR150bn (+74% y-y, +7% q-q), and 1Q order inflow of INR33bn was +67% y-y. Cell utilisation rose to 63% as the new line ramped, and module utilisation is expected to rise in coming quarters. Margin fell 125bp q-q, and JPMorgan expects little change to consensus estimates. Nomura kept Neutral with a TP of INR1,120, and JPMorgan kept Overweight with a TP of INR1,095. (Nomura, JP)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 5.8% yoy, 2.0% above Kotak's estimate. General staffing grew 4.8% despite a 1.6% headcount decline from BFSI regulatory changes, and specialized staffing grew 21% on 11.4% higher headcount. HR services rose 11.7%, 26% ahead of estimate (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs315 mn was 11% below Kotak's estimate of Rs354 mn. Margin was 1.0% against an estimated 1.2%, with both general and specialized staffing margins below estimates. Specialized staffing margin was 6.4% (7.2% in 1QFY26), and HR services margin was -4.0% (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 2.3% yoy to Rs29.2 bn, 1.1% below Kotak's estimate. General staffing headcount fell 1.9% yoy on BFSI regulatory changes, which offset 11.7% yoy growth in specialized staffing (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs457 mn was 2.4% above Kotak's estimate of Rs446 mn, and down 3.9% yoy. Margin was 1.6% against the 1.5% estimate, with both general and specialized staffing margins better than estimated (Kotak).

outlook.note: Kotak cut FY27-29E revenue estimates by 5-7% and EPS by 4-5%, and lowered fair value to Rs1,600 from Rs1,800 on stagnant core staffing headcount. It models a core headcount recovery in 2HFY27 as the BFSI impact normalizes, and management expects the headcount decline to normalize. Specialized staffing is supported by GCC demand, which is 67% of that segment's revenue, and AI, data, cloud and cyber-security hiring (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales grew 15% YoY (19% in 4Q) to Rs187.9bn, 1% above FactSet consensus but 4% below MS's estimate. LFL growth slowed to 5.5% (10.8% in 4Q), the weakest in seven quarters, and revenue per sq ft fell 2% YoY, with older large-metro stores flat. (MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Operating profit of Rs15.0bn (+15% YoY) was 1% below consensus and 3% below MS's estimate, with an 8.0% margin (7.9% in 1QF26) in line. Gross margin rose 50bps YoY to 15.8% on a lower food mix and more private label, offset by staff cost +30% YoY. CLSA's standalone read was a slight beat, with EBITDA 1% above consensus. (MS, CLSA)

2Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales grew 18% YoY (15% in 1Q) and came in about 1.6% above the 193,408 consensus, so in line. The growth was already known from the pre-announced update. LFL growth accelerated to 9.5% (5.5% in 1Q, 6.8% in 2QF26), and bill cuts grew 14% with the implied value per bill up 3%. (MS, CLSA, JP)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated operating profit of Rs13.9bn was about 6% below consensus and 5% below MS's estimate. The margin was 7.1%, 19bps lower YoY. Gross margin slipped on a late-festive, food-heavy mix, and entry-level wage inflation lifted other expenses 18-22% YoY. CLSA's standalone margin was 7.3%, 27bps below consensus. (MS, JP, CLSA)

outlook.note: Mixed. JP expects revenue growth to move into the high teens in 2H FY27 on the festive season and inflation, but sees margins staying range-bound on wage costs. JP cut FY27/28E EBITDA by 2%/1% and EPS by about 5% (PT cut to Rs3,925 from Rs4,100). MS flagged a modest downward revision to consensus EPS. CLSA kept its target price of Rs5,723 and expects store maturity to help margins recover. (JP, MS, CLSA)

companies.name: AWL Agri Business
companies.note: Despite continued volatility in edible oil prices, management remains confident of delivering 5-6% FY27 volume growth, on the back of uptick in volumes with the start of festive from the end of 2Q

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 18% YoY to Rs200.5bn, ahead of Jefferies and consensus estimates. Edible Oil grew 15% on pricing and premiumisation despite volumes up only 2% on channel destocking, while Food & FMCG grew 22% and Industry Essentials 28% (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 90% YoY to Rs6.9bn (margin 3.5%, +131bps), a margin-led beat versus both Jefferies and consensus. Gross margin expanded ~158bps to 11.0%. Edible oil EBITDA/ton rose 30% to Rs5,030 and Foods posted a 6% EBITDA margin (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management is confident of 5-6% FY27 edible oil volume growth as destocking fades and festive demand starts from the end of 2Q, and it kept its medium-term edible oil EBITDA/ton guidance of Rs4,000-4,500. Foods is guided to 18-20% growth in FY27 with ~4% EBITDA margins, and the Madhur acquisition should add Rs7-8bn of annualised revenue. Jefferies raised its revenue estimates by 6% for FY27 and FY28, kept its BUY rating and set a Rs260 price target (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue grew 8.2% YoY (9.5% excluding other operating revenue), in line with consensus (Rs50.0bn vs Rs49.99bn). Growth was driven by rapid e-commerce scale-up and strong general trade, with most key categories improving sequentially and exiting the quarter at mid-teens growth (CLSA, MS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 11% YoY but was 4% below consensus (Rs8.40bn vs Rs8.71bn). Margin was 16.8%, up 43bps YoY and down 127bps QoQ. Gross margin rose 119bps YoY and was 60bps ahead of consensus, but other expenses (advertising, influencer and promotional spend) rose 181bps as a share of revenue (CLSA, MS).

outlook.note: Management said most key categories delivered positive sequential momentum and the quarter exited at mid-teens revenue growth, helped by higher marketing spend, e-commerce and quick commerce. International business is recovering as supply chain constraints ease. Offsetting this, the EBITDA margin missed on higher opex. CLSA kept Hold with a Rs5,569 target; MS said its thesis and direction of consensus EPS were largely unchanged (CLSA, MS, GS).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs6.5 bn grew 11% yoy, ~2.9% above Kotak's estimate, helped by integration of the 'Cello' branded writing-instruments (WI) sales. Writing instruments rose ~64% yoy to Rs1.3 bn (~15% beat) and consumerware 7.2% yoy (~2.6% beat), while molded furniture fell 13.5% (~9% miss) (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,289 mn was ~4.2% above Kotak's estimate, even though it fell 4.6% yoy. Margin of 19.7% (KIE 19.5%) contracted 325 bps yoy as gross margin fell to 46.7% (KIE 50%) on the loss-making branded WI business and higher steelware sourcing costs, offset by lower costs elsewhere (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management guides FY2027E revenue growth of 10-12% and EBITDA margin up 200-250 bps to ~25%, but 1Q27 is expected to be weak (Middle East crisis, cautious channels, volumes hit by 12-20% price hikes). Kotak calls the guidance conservative but cuts FY2027-28E EPS by 2-6% and fair value to Rs550 from Rs640 (Kotak).

companies.name: Colgate-Palmolive (India)
companies.note: While margins continue to be structurally healthy, management is intentionally sacrificing near-term Ebitda expansion to step up brand investments and support long-term growth.

4Q26.revNote: Net sales rose 9% YoY to Rs15.8bn, 4% above consensus, on balanced volume and pricing growth (MSD each) with broad-based gains across core and premium toothpaste, toothbrushes and personal care (CLSA, Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 2.3% YoY to Rs5.1bn, 3% above consensus, though margin fell 210bps YoY to 31.9% on a 75bps gross margin decline and ~160bps drag from the GST inverted duty structure. A&P was stepped up to 12.5% of sales (CLSA, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales grew 12% YoY (highest in 8 quarters) on HSD toothpaste volume growth (8% volume per Kotak), led by premium toothpaste and a favourable base; about 2% above consensus (CLSA, JP, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 6.7% YoY to Rs4.8bn, in line with consensus, because the ~105bps gross margin gain to ~70% was reinvested in A&P (+34% YoY, 15.7% of sales), taking EBITDA margin to 30.1% (-144bps YoY) (CLSA, Kotak, JP).

outlook.note: Management guides to sustainable growth with higher full-year A&P/sales in FY27E, while gross margin could contract 40-50bps on raw-material inflation, managed through cost savings and calibrated pricing. Brokers' FY27-29E EPS changes are small (Kotak 0-3% up, CLSA -1% to +1%), and Kotak sees underlying demand still weak (two-year volume CAGR below 2% for a sixth quarter). CLSA expects the base to get softer next quarter (Kotak, CLSA).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 18.2% YoY to Rs22.6bn, about 3.2% above Kotak's estimate. Electric consumer durables grew 19.2%, lighting 14.3% and Butterfly 15.9%, with price hikes of 14-15% helping and the new categories (solar rooftop, pumps, wires) contributing ~10% of sales (Kotak, CLSA).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 24% YoY to Rs2.0bn, about 8% above Kotak's estimate. Margin expanded 44bps YoY to 9.0% on price hikes, operating leverage and cost savings, which more than offset raw-material inflation and a 260bps YoY fall in lighting EBIT margin from pre-contracted B2B rates. CLSA also called it slightly ahead of its estimate and consensus, while Jefferies saw the quarter as in line (Kotak, CLSA, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs22.35bn, broadly in line (JPMorgan had expected +13%). Growth came from high-single to low-double-digit price hikes with only modest volume growth, and about Rs2bn of sales were lost to supply-chain disruption, mainly in fans (CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 17% YoY to Rs2.2bn, in line with consensus. Margin expanded 45bp YoY to 10.0%, helped by price hikes, cost control and lean working capital, even though about 80% of cost inflation has been passed on and the rest is still to come (CLSA, JP, Jeff).
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA vs consensus (CLSA); revenue vs broker estimate (JPMorgan, +12% actual vs +13% JPMe

outlook.note: Management says it is on track for its FY29 guidance of 13-14% revenue CAGR and an 11-12% exit EBITDA margin, helped by new categories (wires, solar rooftops, pumps). About 80% of the commodity cost inflation has been passed on, with fan price hikes of 17-18%. Estimates moved both ways: Nomura raised revenue by 1.4% but cut EPS 3-5% on margins, CLSA cut FY27-29 PAT 8-9%, and target prices came down (CLSA to Rs300, Nomura to Rs292, Jefferies to Rs305) as rising input costs and a B2C demand slowdown pose risks. Brokers keep Buy/Outperform (CLSA, Nomura, Jeff).

companies.name: Dabur India
companies.note: Mgmt. guided for D/D topline growth in FY27, with pricing > vols; b) Vol. growth is expected to remain under pressure due to higher inflation; c) confident of delivering QoQ improvement in revenue growth in next qt

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 10.6% y/y to Rs37.6bn, ~0.5% above Kotak's estimate. Domestic FMCG grew 9.5% (volume +5%), led by HPC (+12.3%), and international grew 15.5% in INR terms, offset by a drag from beverages and glucose after unseasonal April rains (Kotak, JP, Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 11% y/y to Rs7.4bn, ~0.8% above Kotak's estimate, with margin at 19.7% (+5 bps y/y). Gross margin rose 30 bps to 47.3%, but this was largely offset by A&P spend up 13.6% y/y, so margins were flat (Kotak, JP, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management reaffirmed double-digit consolidated revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion for FY27, and expects sequential acceleration in revenue growth. Brokers see the guide as increasingly price-led, with volumes likely to face pressure from input-cost inflation; the monsoon deficit has narrowed to 14-15%. Estimate changes are small: Jefferies' FY27 EPS is +1% and Kotak's +3%, while JPMorgan cut its target price to Rs485 from Rs525 (Kotak, JP, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales grew 14.9% YoY, 0.8% above GS's estimate of Rs10,307mn. Domestic business grew 22%, with like-to-like domestic revenue up 12% on ~8% volume growth. Subsidiaries, now 18% of domestic revenue, grew 61% like-to-like. International fell 12% on Middle East supply-chain disruption (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 5.6% YoY, 1.1% below GS's estimate of Rs2,288mn. Margin fell ~190bps YoY to 21.8% as gross margin dropped ~360bps on input-cost inflation. The company puts the Middle East conflict's gross-margin hit at ~200bps. Recent price hikes and easing input costs should help margins recover (GS).

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue fell 4% YoY (domestic -3%, international -5%) as unfavourable weather hit the summer portfolio and the West Asia conflict disrupted international shipping; volumes declined 7% (+7% ex. summer portfolio). (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 15% YoY to Rs 1.9bn, 5% below JEFe. Margin contracted c260bps YoY to 20.2% on negative operating leverage and A&P spend up 12%, despite gross margin expanding c250bps to 68.4% on price hikes and cost efficiencies. (Jeff)

outlook.note: Management expects a sequential recovery in international business. It also expects margins to recover as price increases take effect and input costs ease. GS cut FY27/28/29 EPS by ~2% to allow for a higher guided tax rate and cut its target price to Rs625 from Rs655, but kept Buy. GS forecasts FY27 revenue growth of 14.0% and EBITDA growth of 12.7% (GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 15.2% yoy, the fastest in 13 quarters and ~1.5% above Kotak's estimate. High-teens growth in products, with water purifiers up on double-digit volume growth plus 3-12% price hikes, and robotic vacuum cleaners, air purifiers and softeners also strong. Service charges grew only 2.6% as AMC renewals were deferred after the price hikes (Kotak, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs694mn (+12.8% yoy) was 5.6% above Kotak's estimate. Pre-ESOP EBITDA was Rs760mn (+13.3% yoy), ~6.8% ahead, and Nomura says it was ahead of Bloomberg consensus. Gross margin fell 125bps yoy to 58.9% on RM inflation and the pre-ESOP margin slipped 20bps to 10.9%. Higher A&P and in-store investment weighed on margins, though lower service charges as a % of sales helped (Kotak, Nomura).
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA: consensus (Nomura says ahead of Bloomberg consensus); revenue: broker estimate (Ko

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 11.6% yoy to Rs6.8bn, about 2.4% above Kotak's estimate, led by early-teens growth in products. Double-digit growth in water purifiers and strong emerging categories (robotics, air purifiers up 4x), plus double-digit service bookings growth, drove it (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs856mn (+11.0% yoy) was 14.1% above Kotak's estimate. Adjusted (ex-ESOP) EBITDA of Rs905mn grew 14.4% yoy and was ~13.4% above estimate. Tight cost control, with service charges down 105bps yoy to 12.4% of sales, offset a 75bps yoy gross margin decline to 58.9% (Kotak; Nomura also calls the EBITDA ahead of its estimates).

outlook.note: Management expects FY27E growth to step up and holds FY27E EBITDA margin broadly in line with FY26. It reiterated the FY30 ambition of 2x revenue and 3x EBITDA vs FY25. Service growth in 2Q could be similar to 1Q, with softer AMC bookings offset by higher filter/spares sales in 2H. Input costs remain challenging. Kotak cut EPS 2-4% (FY27E EBITDA -1.3%) and held FV at Rs700. Nomura cut EBITDA margin 30/50bps and EPS 4%/6% for FY27/28, and lowered TP to INR572 from INR600 (Kotak, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated sales grew 18.3% y-y (UVG 9%, India volume +7%) vs Bloomberg consensus of +16.2%, about 1.8% above, so in line. India sales rose 11-12% on speedboat categories and soaps, while Africa (+47% INR, +25% CC) and Indonesia (+15%) outperformed. (Nomura, GS, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 15.4% to INR8.0bn vs consensus of c.INR7.9bn (about 1.4% above, in line). Gross margin fell 260bp y-y/400bp q-q to 48.1% on 3x spikes in LPG, kerosene and LABSA, but lower A&P and international margin gains (Africa, Indonesia) offset it, leaving EBITDA margin down 50bp y-y at 19.0%. (Nomura, GS)
