outlook.note: Management sees FY27 India volume growth of ~8% (up from earlier expectations), with sales and EBITDA growth expected to exceed its double-digit guidance. Q2 margins stay hit by high-cost inventory, with recovery expected in 2HFY27, and India EBITDA margin should return to 24-26% for FY27. Nomura raised FY27E revenue to INR173.7bn (from INR168.7bn) with a TP of INR1,300, GS left estimates largely unchanged with a TP of Rs1,330, and JPM raised FY27/28E EPS by 1-3% but trimmed its TP to Rs1,175 from Rs1,200. (Nomura, GS, JP)

companies.name: Hindustan Unilever
companies.note: It expects FY27 to be better than FY26, supported by portfolio and channel transformation.

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 10% YoY, a 13-quarter-high growth rate, split roughly equally between volume (UVG 5%) and price/mix (5%). Home Care grew 14%, Beauty & Wellbeing 12% and Foods 7%. Revenue was in line with Factset consensus (0%) and 1% above MSe. (MS, JP, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 8% YoY, 2% below consensus and MSe. Margin was 23.0%, down 40bps YoY and 73bps QoQ, mainly on gross margin (-70bps YoY, -80bps QoQ) as crude-linked input inflation hit. Home Care margins contracted most, while A&P was 9.6% of sales. (MS, JP, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management reiterated that FY27 should be better than FY26, with stable demand and EBITDA margin kept in the 22.5-23.5% guided range. It is taking further price hikes, with 2-5% sequential inflation expected in 2Q. Only 5% of the 10% raw-material inflation seen in 1Q has been passed on, so inflation is a watch item. Brokers made marginal estimate cuts (Jeff: revenue <-1%, EPS -1%). (Jeff, MS, JP)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs7.56bn (+27% YoY, 32% ex the accounting change) was 3% above consensus (Rs7.37bn) and in line with CLSA's estimate; growth was volume-led (+30.5%). Focus categories grew 35%+, younger brands about 40%, and Mamaearth grew high-teens (CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.10bn was 30% above consensus (Rs845mn) and 30% above CLSA's estimate. Margin of 14.6% was up 688bps YoY and about 310bps above consensus. Drivers were a higher mix of B2B channels, profitable brands (Mamaearth, The Derma Co) and A&P leverage, despite gross margin down 150bps YoY to 69.7%. CLSA puts the one-off-adjusted margin at 12.6%, which is 190bps above its estimate. JP says EBITDA was only marginally ahead of its estimates, with margin broadly in line after one-offs (CLSA, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 23% YoY (28% ex the change in accounting for Flipkart), about 6% ahead of consensus. Growth was volume-led (+30%), with focus categories up 35%, young brands up 28% and Mamaearth up in the mid-teens (CLSA, Kotak, JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs772 mn was about 24% above consensus. The margin rose to 11.8% from 10.0% consensus, helped by A&P optimisation and operating leverage, even though gross margin fell 40bps YoY to 70.3% (CLSA, Kotak).

outlook.note: Management maintained its FY31 guidance of a high-teens revenue CAGR and a roughly 15% EBITDA margin. It expects 100-150bps of margin expansion a year, and Jefferies cites 150-200bps for FY27. CLSA lifted FY27-29CL earnings 6-13% and TP to Rs505 from Rs474; Jefferies raised EPS 8-13% and PT to Rs650; JP raised FY28E EPS about 5% and PT to Rs410. Q2 may see about 50bps of lost summer seasonality and some gross margin pressure from crude-linked RM and packaging costs, which price hikes should largely offset (CLSA, Jeff, JP).

companies.name: ITC
companies.note: The vol. trend should give mgmt. greater confidence to take further price hikes ahead, & expect volumes to stay resilient.

4Q26.revNote: Total gross revenues (incl. excise) rose 17.5% YoY to Rs214.6bn, 10.3% above Kotak's Rs194.6bn estimate, with cigarette gross revenue +31.7% on the Feb-26 tax-structure change and channel stocking. Net operating income (net of excise) fell 6.9% YoY to Rs160.5bn, but the tax change makes it non-comparable. FMCG-others revenue grew 14.7% YoY, 4% ahead of Kotak (CLSA: 2% above its own estimate and 5% above consensus). Agri revenue fell 15.7% on Middle East disruptions. (Kotak, CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 7.3% YoY to Rs64.3bn, 3.2% above Kotak's estimate, and JPM calls it 3% ahead of its estimate. Cigarette EBIT rose 7.2% (CLSA: 15% ahead of consensus), FMCG EBIT margin expanded to 8.3%, and paperboard EBIT rose 21%. Agri EBIT fell 29.8%. (Kotak, JP, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 27.9% YoY to Rs269.4bn, but GS says revenue is not comparable post the tax change: GST cess was earlier netted off revenue, while the excise duty that replaced GST is now booked as a cost. Cigarette net sales fell 23-26% on the sharp tax increase, FMCG grew 12% and paper 9% (GS, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 28% YoY to Rs45.1bn, ~6% below GS estimates, with margin down ~1,300bps to 16.8%. Cigarette EBIT fell 35% as price hikes only partly passed on the tax increase. Paper EBIT rose 38% and FMCG EBIT 21%, which cushioned the decline (GS, JP).

outlook.note: Estimates were cut but a gradual recovery is expected. GS lowers FY27/28/29 EPS ~5% (EPS Rs13.95 for FY27E) and cuts TP to Rs290 from Rs320. JP cuts FY27E/28E EPS 3.1%/3.8% and TP to Rs310 from Rs325. Both expect gradual price hikes to narrow the cigarette EBIT decline from -35% in 1Q, with JP seeing EBIT/stick neutrality by 4Q. Kotak sees the decline easing to 25-27% in 2Q (GS, JP, Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 3% yoy to Rs7.7 bn, 4.6% below Kotak's estimate. The exit of Pril and Fa hurt growth: home care fell 9% yoy, while fabric care grew 14%. Ex-Pril/Fa, volume/value grew 5.3%/8.1%. (Kotak)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 48% yoy to Rs647 mn, 35% below Kotak's estimate, and the margin dropped to 8.4% from 16.5%. Gross margin contracted 950 bps yoy to 38.5% on crude-linked raw material inflation of 15-16% and packaging costs, only partly offset by price hikes. A&P spend was cut 14% yoy to 6.5% of sales. (Kotak)

outlook.note: Management guides FY27 revenue to double-digit growth ex-Pril/Fa and says margin recovery will be gradual. The blended price hike was 4-4.5%, of which about 3% flowed through in 1Q, and high-cost inventory will weigh on 2Q margins. 2H is expected to be substantially better than 1H. Kotak cut FY27-29E EPS by 4-17% and cut fair value to Rs260 from Rs270, but upgraded the stock to BUY from ADD. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 23% YoY to Rs39.6bn, in line with Bloomberg consensus of Rs39.2bn (+1%). Growth was split about equally between price and volume: Parachute rose 23% (volume +10%), VAHO 22%, and foods 43% including acquisitions. India volume growth was 11%. (CLSA, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 25% to Rs8.19bn, 7% above consensus. Margin was 20.7%, 127bps above consensus. Gross margin was 113-116bps ahead of estimates, helped by lower copra prices and better mix, and gross margin rose 34bps YoY and 222bps QoQ. A&P rose 25% but the margin still expanded 36bps YoY. (CLSA, MS)

outlook.note: Management raised FY27 EBITDA growth guidance to high-teens (about 20% by MS's reading, Jefferies cites 17-20%), implying 140-150bps of margin expansion. Revenue growth guidance remains double-digit (>Rs150bn), with Parachute volumes expected to grow mid-single digits and India volumes high-single to double digits. CLSA lifted FY27-29 PAT by 2-8% and its target price from Rs556 to Rs703 but stays Underperform on valuation. MS and Jefferies also raised near-term estimates. (CLSA, MS, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Net sales grew 25.4% YoY, 5.6% above Bloomberg consensus and 4.7% above CLSA's estimate. All segments posted double-digit growth, led by volume, premiumisation, the quick-commerce/e-commerce channel and confectionery. Milk and nutrition improved sequentially (CLSA, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Total EBITDA rose 40% YoY, 14% above consensus, with margin at 24.1% (+253bps YoY, vs 22.5% consensus). Gross margin expanded 219bps YoY to 57.1% and offset a ~40% jump in ad spend; staff costs fell to 9.0% of sales from 10.2% (CLSA, GS).

2Q27.revNote: Sales +20% YoY, in line with Bloomberg consensus (0%) and 2% above MS estimates. Domestic sales rose 20% on double-digit volume growth. Confectionery (KitKat share gains), beverages, prepared dishes (Maggi) and milk products were all strong, and General Trade and quick commerce both grew well (MS, CLSA, JP).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA +31% YoY, 3% above consensus. Margin was 23.8% (+186bps YoY) as gross margin rose 267bps to 56.9% on pricing and mix. That more than absorbed a 46% YoY jump in ad spend (MS, CLSA, JP).

outlook.note: Management flags rising food inflation, with coffee and wheat range-bound, sugar and edible oils elevated, and milk and cocoa volatile. It plans to offset this through productivity and brand investment. JP expects H2 revenue growth to moderate to about 12% on a tougher base (GST-benefit anniversary) and trimmed FY27/28E EPS 0.5-1%. CLSA cut FY27-29CL earnings 0-2% for higher brand spend, and its target went from Rs1,638 to Rs1,628. JP's target went from Rs1,620 to Rs1,480 (JP, CLSA, MS).

1Q27.revNote: Net revenue grew 10.4% YoY to Rs6.59 bn, 1.5% below Kotak's estimate of Rs6.69 bn. Growth was almost entirely pricing, with price/mix up about 10% as spice-cost inflation was passed on. Volume rose only 1.7%, against 8% in 1QFY26. Spices grew 11.5% and Convenience Foods 11.7%. Kerala remained a drag (Kotak, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA grew 0.7% YoY to Rs1.13 bn, 1.9% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was 17.1%, down 165 bps YoY and up 150 bps QoQ. Gross margin fell 125 bps YoY on 33% spice-cost inflation and the absence of PLI benefits. Other income more than doubled, taking PBT and PAT growth to about 9% YoY (Kotak, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 5-6% y/y and was in line with JPM's estimate, led by pricing (~4%) while volume growth was soft at 2.2%. Kerala distribution restructuring and weaker North America (tariff/inventory issues) held back growth, while the GCC grew 11.8% (JP).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs973mn (+2% y/y) missed JPM's expectations, with margin at 15.5% (-40bps y/y; 16.0% ex-PLI incentives). Gross margin expanded 140bps y/y to 45.4% on benign raw material prices, but Middle East freight/surcharges and digital investments weighed on profitability (~200bps impact) (JP).

outlook.note: Management reiterated its ambition of double-digit growth, with demand commentary constructive. Pricing should keep supporting revenue over the next few quarters, and about 10% price/mix growth is expected to continue. Kerala restructuring runs to March 2027 and will take several quarters to mature. Margins face input-cost and Project Bolt investment pressure. Estimates were nudged up: Kotak raised FY27-29E EPS by 0-2% and JP by 6-7% for FY27-28E. JP cut its price target to Rs680 from Rs710 after lowering the target multiple, and Kotak kept fair value at Rs700 (Kotak, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Standalone revenue rose 27% YoY to Rs 113bn, about 20% ahead of Jefferies' estimate. Edible Oils grew 27% on strong mustard oil and rising edible oil prices, and Foods & FMCG grew 28% on higher volumes and pricing actions (Jeff).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Standalone EBITDA rose 69% YoY to Rs 5.4bn, about 35% above Jefferies' estimate. Margin expanded 118bps YoY to 4.8%, helped by stronger edible oil margins (Edible Oils EBIT margin 4.8% vs 1.2%). Lower Foods & FMCG profitability, where segment EBIT margin fell to 5.9% from 8.3% on input cost inflation, partly offset this (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management reiterated guidance of 3-5% volume growth in Edible Oils, 8-10% revenue growth in Foods & FMCG and about 15% growth in HPC. Jefferies expects Foods margins to recover over the coming quarters after input cost inflation, and it kept its FY27-29 estimates unchanged (PAT CAGR of 23% over FY26-29). It also kept its Buy rating with a Rs 560 SOTP target (Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales grew 12% YoY to Rs53.5bn, 1% below consensus and in line with MS's own estimate. India branded growth held at 13% (underlying volume), led by growth businesses +47% (Sampann +58%, RTD +41%), while India tea revenue fell 4% on price cuts and non-branded fell 10% cc on lower coffee prices (MS, JP, CLSA).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 19% YoY to Rs7.2bn, about 2% below consensus (MS -3% vs its own estimate); margin was 13.5%, +84bps YoY but -105bps QoQ. Gross margin expanded 257bps YoY, but the sequential dip came from inflation, higher A&P spend and forex hedge losses (MS, CLSA).

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, ~30% growth in growth businesses and 50-70bps EBITDA margin expansion. Tea inflation of 7-10% is the key watch item; price hikes are planned to protect margins. CLSA tweaked FY27-29 estimates with TP unchanged at Rs1,337, and JP kept its Rs1,340 TP (MS, CLSA, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs7.29bn, in line with CLSA's estimate. Domestic sales grew 14% YoY. Kitchen appliances grew 20% YoY on induction cooktops and electrical cooking appliances, helped by GST cuts on cookware (CLSA).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 30% YoY to Rs669mn, with margin up 127bps YoY to 9.2% (+21bps QoQ) on strategic sourcing and calibrated pricing. CLSA called it a beat on EBITDA margin, though the quarter was in line with its estimates overall (CLSA).

outlook.note: Management flagged margin pressure ahead from about 10% input-cost inflation linked to the Middle East conflict and from high competitive intensity. Price hikes taken in March and April should offset this only gradually through 1HFY27. CLSA cut FY27/28 EBITDA by 9-10% and PAT by 11-13%, raised sales 2%, and cut its target multiple from 35x to 30x, lowering TP to Rs570 (CLSA).

companies.name: Varun Beverages
companies.note: VBL is driving production to newer and more efficient lines, leading to lower costs,while also expanding distribution (4.5m outlet 2026 target versus 4m in 2025).

1Q27.revNote: Net sales of Rs84.5bn (+20.4% YoY) were 3% above Bloomberg consensus (Rs82.3bn) but 3% below CLSA and 6% below MS. India volume growth of 14.4% missed the 20%+ expected, as April was flat. International revenue grew 43% YoY, helped by the Twizza consolidation and 38% volume growth. (CLSA, MS, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs23.4bn (+17.2% YoY) was 4% below Bloomberg consensus, though in line with CLSA. Margin was 27.7%, down 76bps YoY and 180bps below consensus, because the low-margin Twizza business was consolidated and packaging and transport costs rose. India EBITDA margin was up about 40bps YoY to 31.3%. (CLSA, MS, JP)

outlook.note: Management does not expect raw-material inflation to hit India margins, and July India volumes are still growing in the healthy 20s. The 4.5m outlet distribution target for 2026 is on track. Brokers nevertheless trimmed numbers on the volume miss: CLSA cut 26-28CL EPS by 0-4% and its TP from Rs654 to Rs629, and JP expects downward revisions to consensus. (CLSA, JP)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs37.3bn, 1% below consensus (Rs37.6bn) and MSe, so in line. Growth was broad-based across categories at ~19%, with SSSG of 10% and 24 net store additions to 819 stores. (MS, JP)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 19% YoY to Rs5.4bn and was 1% below consensus, so in line. Gross margin expanded 30bps YoY to 28.7%, but a 25% YoY rise in employee costs held the EBITDA margin flat at 14.6%. (MS, JP)

outlook.note: Management said elevated inflation hit demand in 1Q and expects the impact to taper in coming quarters. It expects accelerated small-format store additions, with ~3,000 long-term potential. JP sees marginal earnings revisions after an in-line print and keeps its Rs145 target (FY27E EBITDA Rs22.4bn, +19.1% YoY). The board approved capping foreign ownership at 49.99%. Elevated employee costs from minimum-wage hikes are capping margin expansion. (JP, MS)

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 8.8% YoY to Rs21.8 bn, about 2.2% above Kotak's estimate. Standalone revenue grew 7.4% on share gains in washers and 50%+ growth in RACs, and Elica grew about 32%. Jefferies calls sales broadly in line with its estimate. (Kotak, Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA fell 34% YoY to Rs1.2 bn, about 36% below Kotak's estimate. The margin was 5.6%, down 355 bps YoY against Kotak's 8.9%. Gross margin contracted 380 bps to 30.8%, hit by the BEE table change in ACs and refrigerators with insufficient price hikes, incremental e-waste provisions, raw-material inflation from the Middle East conflict, and a weak INR. Jefferies also reports an EBITDA miss against its estimate. (Kotak, Jeff)

outlook.note: Management called FY27 challenging because of BEE energy-upgrade costs, e-waste provisions and Middle East-driven raw-material, supply-chain and forex pressure. It gave no near-term margin guidance. Kotak cut FY27/28E EPS by about 37%/15% and its fair value to Rs1,050 from Rs1,180, while keeping Buy. Jefferies cut FY27-28E EPS by 3-4%, with AC price hikes of 10-13% YTD partly offsetting, and kept Hold with a Rs850 target. (Kotak, Jeff)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of INR 112.8bn (+10% YoY) was 6% above Visible Alpha consensus (INR 106.4bn) and 14% above GS's estimate, helped by realisation up 11% YoY to INR 183,823/t even as volume fell 7% YoY to 580.8kt on industrial-gas disruption from the West Asia crisis (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of INR 13.3bn (+1% YoY) was 6% above consensus and 1% above GS's estimate; EBITDA/t rose 9% YoY to INR 22,884 on a shift to value-added segments (railways, process, auto) and subsidiaries' EBITDA +15% YoY, offsetting power & fuel cost up 75% YoY (GS, Jeff).

outlook.note: Management reiterated FY29E volume target of 3.5mt (8-10% volume growth), EBITDA/t guidance of INR 18,000-20,000 and FY27E capex of INR 28bn; propane/LPG cost pressure has eased and CR capacity rises to 2.6mt by FY28E. GS cut FY27E EPS 3% on higher power & fuel cost and left FY28E/FY29E EPS broadly unchanged (+0.2%/+0.6%), with TP unchanged at INR 1,000 (GS).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs154.8bn was 10% above both Bloomberg consensus (Rs140.9bn) and GS's estimate. Sales volume rose 17.4% YoY to 2.2mt as the new Angul blast furnace ramped up, and blended realisation rose 7.3% YoY (12% QoQ) to Rs69,427/t on spill-over of higher spot prices from 4QFY26. (GS, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs26.6bn was 6% above consensus (Rs25.1bn) but 3% below GS's estimate. EBITDA/t of Rs11,930 was 6.8% below GS's estimate on higher other expenses (+25% YoY, partly one-off gas costs from the West Asia crisis). Nomura calls it a 7% beat versus consensus on volume strength and resilient realisations despite weak rebar prices. (GS, Nomura)

outlook.note: Both GS and Nomura cut estimates: GS lowered FY27E/28E/29E EBITDA by 7.5%/8.2%/7.4% and its TP to Rs1,240, citing about Rs8,000/t erosion in rebar prices. Nomura cut FY27-29F EBITDA by 5%/8%/11% and FY27F volume by 5%, and forecasts 2QFY27 EBITDA/t of about Rs9,300, down Rs2,700 QoQ. Management guided coking coal costs up USD15/t QoQ in 2QFY27. Kotak is more upbeat, with margins bottoming in 2QFY27 and recovering from 3Q on ramp-ups, long-product price recovery and a FV rise to Rs1,350 on rollover. It sees only 0-1% EBITDA estimate tweaks. (GS, Nomura, Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales rose 10% YoY (not like-for-like because of the BPSL stake sale; about 19% on a BPSL-adjusted basis) on a sharp realisation increase, with volumes up 4% like-for-like and ASP/t up 15% (CLSA). None of the reports prints a revenue consensus.
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs93.8bn was about 5% above CLSA's estimate and 10% above consensus. Nomura had it 16% above its forecast and 12% above Bloomberg consensus, and JPM 13% above consensus. The beat came from higher steel realisations and better profitability at subsidiaries such as JVML, coated products and overseas entities, partly offset by higher coking coal and iron ore costs (CLSA, Nomura, JP).

outlook.note: Management guides to 2Q margin pressure from coking coal up US$12-15/t, back-ended iron ore relief and weaker steel prices (Nomura expects EBITDA/t to fall about Rs180/t QoQ). Cost headwinds are expected to ease from 3Q as iron ore prices fall and steel prices stabilise, with net debt/EBITDA kept below 2.5x and capex of Rs220-240bn in FY27. CLSA upgraded to O-PF, raising FY27-29CL EPS 11-19% and its TP to Rs1,400. JPM raised its TP to Rs1,500 and its FY27-29E EBITDA 1-4%. Nomura kept its TP at Rs1,400 but cut its FY27F EBITDA 5% (CLSA, Nomura, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs54.6bn (+23% YoY, +4% QoQ) was 1% above Visible Alpha consensus and 1% below GS's estimate. Realisation rose YoY across all product categories, and CR coil and pig iron volumes ramped up (+52% and +138% YoY) as new capacity came on stream (GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs7.7bn (+32% YoY) was 8% above consensus and 3% above GS's estimate. Margin of 14.1% rose 92bps YoY, helped by higher prices and a better product mix, with EBITDA/t up across the major products (GS).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 27% YoY and 19% QoQ to Rs52.4bn, led by 18% YoY growth in steel-equivalent volumes (1,316kt) from ramp-up in pig iron, cold-rolled steel and iron pellets. Jefferies does not give a quarterly revenue comparison against estimates. (Jeff)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs7.3bn was up 41% YoY and 49% QoQ, 18% above Jefferies' estimate, on sharp margin expansion across segments. Blended EBITDA/t rose 42% QoQ to Rs5.5K, a 15-quarter high. (Jeff)

outlook.note: GS says growth is driven by the ramp-up of new capacity, including the 18ktpa aluminium foil plant in Odisha, with the 60ktpa flat rolled products plant likely to be commissioned in 2QFY27. July 2026 revenue was up 27.4% YoY, and implied 4MFY27 revenue growth of 25.6% compares with GS's FY27 estimate of 18%. GS kept its Buy rating and Rs1,120 target price (GS). Jefferies noted plans to raise up to Rs45bn through an equity issue (Jeff).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs308bn (+6% YoY, +13% QoQ) was 5% below JPM's estimate. Volumes were flat YoY at 5.3MT, 4% below JPM's estimate, while ASP rose 6% YoY to Rs57,811/t (JPM).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: Adj EBITDA of Rs44.1bn (+38% YoY) was 11% ahead of JPM/BBG consensus on lower-than-expected staff costs (employee count reduction) and raw material costs. EBITDA/t rose 38% YoY to Rs8,266 against JPM's Rs7,155 (JPM).
4Q26.vsBasis: EBITDA vs consensus (JPM/BBG); revenue vs broker estimate (JPM)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs265.5bn (+3% YoY) was 11% below JPMe because volumes of 4.16mt (-9% YoY, -22% QoQ) missed the 4.8mt forecast on advanced maintenance shutdowns, only partly offset by ASP of Rs63.8K/t (+10% QoQ, 4% above JPMe). Kotak's table shows revenue in line with its own estimate (JP, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Adj EBITDA of Rs44.6bn (+72% YoY) was 17% ahead of BBG consensus (Rs38bn) and 3% below JPMe. Better ASPs and lower-cost inventory lifted EBITDA/t to Rs10.7K (JPMe Rs9.5K/t, 4Q Rs8.3K/t). Kotak also called it a beat on higher realisations, partly offset by lower volumes and higher costs (JP, Kotak).
1Q27.vsBasis: EBITDA vs consensus (BBG Rs38bn); revenue vs broker estimate (JPMorgan)

outlook.note: Management kept FY27 volume guidance at ~22mt and capex guidance at Rs150bn/200bn/250bn for FY27/28/29. Kotak expects 2Q27 blended NSR to fall ~Rs1,500/t, offset by ~Rs1,500/t lower coal costs, and says seasonal headwinds should stay mild. It trimmed FY27-29E EBITDA by 0-2% on lower volumes, with leverage set to rise as the ~Rs360bn IISCO expansion starts. JPM expects little change to consensus because rebar prices have corrected sharply (Kotak, JP).

companies.name: Tata Steel
companies.note: TATA's focus has shifted from primary steel expansion to downstream; the next 5mtpa plant will start in FY31, limiting volume growth post FY27. TATA expects India realizations to fall by Rs1.5K QoQ in 2Q, which along with $5 higher coking coal, may drive lower margin in 2Q. The Netherlands facility continues to face regulatory challenges with closures of coke ovens and direct sheet plant impacting profitability

4Q26.revNote: Total operating income rose 13% YoY and 11% QoQ to Rs633bn. Standalone volumes were up 11% YoY to 6.2mt, and ASP was up 5% QoQ. (Jeff, CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 20% QoQ and 50% YoY to Rs98bn, 6% above Jefferies' estimate, on better performance across all businesses. Standalone EBITDA/t expanded 20% QoQ to Rs15,303 on higher realisations, and UK losses narrowed. CLSA called the quarter in line with its own estimate. (Jeff, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated net sales of Rs608bn (+14% YoY, -4% QoQ) were ~3% above Kotak's estimate. Higher India volumes (+8.8% YoY to 5.2mn t) and realisations (+14.9% QoQ) drove the growth, partly offset by weaker Europe. [Kotak, CLSA]
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA of Rs92.6bn (+25% YoY, -6% QoQ) was in line with Kotak's estimate. India EBITDA/t of Rs17,762 (+16% QoQ) was in line, as higher realisations offset higher costs. Europe posted a US$17/t EBITDA loss, better than Kotak's US$17/t loss estimate. CLSA also called it in line. [Kotak, CLSA]

outlook.note: Management guides to India NSR ~Rs1,500/t lower QoQ in 2QFY27 and ~US$5/t higher coking coal costs, so margins compress, partly offset by higher volumes. The board approved the 4.8mtpa NINL expansion (capex Rs339bn). Netherlands regulatory uncertainty persists. Kotak trims FY27/28 EBITDA by 3%/1.3% and cuts fair value to Rs180 (from Rs185) with SELL. Nomura expects Netherlands EBITDA to recover in 2Q and keeps Buy with a TP of INR240, but cuts FY27 EBITDA by 7%. [Kotak, Nomura]

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue was up 6% QoQ and 18% YoY, 3% above consensus (4% above CLSA's estimate). India mobile revenue rose 4% QoQ and 9% YoY, helped by ARPU up 3% QoQ to Rs264 and a 3.3m subscriber add. Africa revenue rose 10% QoQ and 45% YoY (CLSA, JP).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA was up 6% QoQ and 20% YoY, 3% above consensus (2% above JPM's estimate; 4% above CLSA's). The margin was flat QoQ at 56.9% and up 61bps YoY. India mobile EBITDA margin rose 137bps YoY to 60.8% (CLSA, JP).

outlook.note: CLSA lifted its FY27-29CL forecasts by 3-6% and raised its target price from Rs2,310 to Rs2,330, citing strong India and Africa growth, 1QFY27 FCF of Rs165bn after leases, and gearing of only 1.2x EBITDA. JPM expects 10-15% tariff hikes over CY26/28E, deleveraging and higher dividends, but flags that homes net adds slowed to 473K from 1,135K in 4Q26 (CLSA, JP).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs25.1bn was up 4% QoQ/11% YoY and 1.8% above consensus, 1.1% above JPM's estimate. Wireless ARPU rose 3% QoQ to Rs259 (JPM est. Rs255) on international roaming and feature-phone-to-smartphone upgrades, but mobile net adds of 210k were below JPM's 360k. Broadband revenue rose 8% QoQ/61% YoY but is only ~5% of the total. (JP, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs13.2bn was up 4% QoQ/14% YoY and 1.6% above consensus. Margin was 53%, up 18bps QoQ and 139bps YoY, helped by S&M expense 30% below JPM's estimate. PBT was 13% below consensus on higher depreciation (D&A 21% above JPM's estimate). (JP, CLSA)

outlook.note: JPM expects only minor consensus earnings upgrades after the revenue and EBITDA beat, and expects a positive stock reaction on the ARPU beat. Home broadband additions slowed to 75K versus an average of 141K over the last two quarters, and mobile subscriber adds missed. CLSA retains its forecasts, Hold rating and Rs1,610 target price, with the stock at a ~40% premium to Bharti Airtel consolidated. (JP, CLSA)

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs84.3bn (+5% YoY, +4% QoQ) was 1% above consensus and 2% above JPMorgan's estimate, helped by energy revenues (+10% QoQ) while rental revenue grew 1% QoQ. Jefferies called it a revenue miss on its own estimates, but tenancy additions of 4.2k were the weak spot. (JP, Jeff)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs45.2bn (+3% YoY, +1% QoQ) was in line with consensus (Rs45.3bn). Margin fell 140bps QoQ to 53.7% on higher power and fuel costs, with energy spreads at -4.6%. Kotak also called the quarter in line. (JP, Kotak)

outlook.note: Management expects faster tower rollouts over the next 3-4 quarters, as supply-chain disruptions have eased and the order book is strong, and the African entry is on track for 2HFY27. Tenancy growth depends on Vi's Rs250-350bn debt raise. Kotak trimmed FY27-29E EBITDA estimates by 0-1% and cut FV to Rs480 (from Rs500) on the dividend payout. Jefferies trimmed EPS estimates by 1% and sees dividends capped below Rs15/share. (Kotak, Jeff)

companies.name: Tata Communications
companies.note: Led by Ebitda growth PAT jumped 86% YoY. With an encouraging 2QFY27 and TCom CEO commentary strong we retain our forecasts which seea 15% consolidatedEbitda Cagr tillFY29CL

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs65.8bn (+10.5% YoY, +0.4% QoQ) was in line with Kotak's estimate (-0.3%). Data revenue of Rs57bn grew 11.3% YoY, led by core connectivity growth of 5.7% YoY, a multi-quarter high. Voice revenue fell 3.2% YoY. CLSA put revenue 1% above its estimate. (Kotak, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs12.8bn (+12.7% YoY, flat QoQ) was 3.0% below Kotak's estimate on higher network and employee costs, partly offset by lower other costs. The figure is the adjusted/normalised EBITDA, which includes Rs510mn of one-offs; the reported figure is about Rs12.3bn. Margin was 19.5%, stable QoQ. CLSA called normalised EBITDA in line with its estimate. (Kotak, CLSA)

2Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs66.9bn (+10% YoY, +2% QoQ) was 1% above CLSA's estimate, led by data revenue (87% of the total), which grew 12% YoY. Digital services grew 19% YoY, while voice revenue fell 9% YoY. (CLSA)
2Q27.ebitdaNote: Reported EBITDA of Rs14.2bn (+21% YoY, +16% QoQ) was 10% ahead of CLSA's estimate. The margin expanded to 21.3% (+2ppt YoY, +2.6ppt QoQ) as digital losses halved from the previous quarter. 1QFY27 normalised EBITDA was Rs12.8bn, and the reported 1Q figure here is Rs12.3bn. (CLSA)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue rose 9% YoY and 6% QoQ to Rs65.55bn, led by data services (+12% YoY) and the digital portfolio (+19% YoY, +9% QoQ), with collaboration/CPaaS up 31% YoY. Voice (+4% YoY) and subsidiaries (-9% YoY) were weaker. The note gives no consensus or estimate for the quarter. (CLSA)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 14% YoY and 5% QoQ to Rs12.83bn. Margin was 19.6%, up 84bps YoY and down 25bps QoQ, helped by data services EBITDA +18% YoY at an 18.4% margin. The note gives no consensus or estimate for the quarter. (CLSA)

outlook.note: The CEO reiterated double-digit data EBITDA growth (1HFY27 EBITDA up 15% YoY), with 19% YoY digital growth and losses narrowing; net debt/EBITDA is a comfortable 2.2x. CLSA keeps its forecasts unchanged, which imply a 15% consolidated EBITDA CAGR to FY29 and 9-15% data revenue growth (CLSA).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs116.9bn was up 3.2% QoQ and 6.0% YoY, 1.7% above consensus and 2.0% above JPMe. ARPU rose 1.7% QoQ to Rs177 and net subscribers grew 0.3mn, the first positive net adds since the 2018 merger. (JP, Nomura, CLSA)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs50.3bn was up 3.0% QoQ and 9.1% YoY, 1.5% above consensus. Margin was flat QoQ at about 43%, so the beat came from revenue and not from margin. (JP, Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs113.3bn (+2.9% YoY, +0.1% QoQ) was 1.2% above Kotak's estimate, on higher blended ARPU of Rs174 (+6.1% YoY, +1.2% QoQ) and lower subscriber attrition; CLSA and Nomura also called it in line (Kotak, CLSA, Nomura).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs48.9bn (+4.9% YoY) was 3.4% above Kotak's estimate on lower subscriber losses and better ARPU, with margin at 43.1% (+91bps YoY). CLSA and Nomura saw it as in line (Kotak, CLSA, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management is confident of raising debt for the planned Rs450bn three-year capex programme, but the raise is still pending and bank funding remains the key trigger. Capex was Rs19.3bn, down 16% QoQ, below JPMe's Rs23bn, though orders worth Rs90bn have already been placed. Net debt fell 20.5% QoQ to Rs1.5tn after part of the warrant proceeds arrived. JP expects minor consensus upgrades, while CLSA kept its forecasts unchanged and Nomura kept its TP at Rs12.6. (JP, CLSA, Nomura)

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs 2,435 cr (-8% YoY, +8% QoQ) was about 2% above Axis's estimate of Rs 2,398 cr. Global retail demand stayed soft amid tariff uncertainty, while the domestic consumer business grew 29.2% YoY and the Welspun brand grew 44% (Axis).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 249 cr beat Axis's Rs 187 cr by 33%. Margin was 10.2% against the 7.8% estimate, helped by cost optimisation and lower employee costs (Rs 273 cr vs Rs 300 cr est.), though it fell 171 bps YoY from 11.9% (Axis).

outlook.note: Management targets double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion into the teens in FY27, with core capacity utilisation above 86%, net-debt-zero and ROCE back to 15%+. Early signs of export demand stabilisation were noted, and capex of Rs 400-500 cr is earmarked. Axis cut FY27E/FY28E revenue and EBITDA by 2% each and FY27E PAT by 6%, but raised its target price to Rs 180 from Rs 165 (Axis).

companies.name: Kajaria Ceramics
companies.note: Management has guided for double-digit volume growth for the balance 9MFY27 and EBITDA margins in the range of 18-19% for FY27. Management reaffirmed its goal to become the leading integrated peptide CDMO, leveraging backward integration to enhance supply security, speed and costs.

1Q27.revNote: Net sales rose 20% YoY to Rs13.3bn on ~6% volume growth and a 12-13% effective price increase to pass through the gas-cost surge; sanitaryware grew +33%. Tiles revenue was only ~2% ahead of consensus (MS), so broadly in line. (Jeff, MS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.6bn (+39% YoY) was ~16% above consensus (MS, GS); the OPM of 19.6% (+270bps YoY) was helped by lower employee costs, price hikes and better gas sourcing, which offset the fuel surge. (Jeff, MS, GS)

outlook.note: Management guides to double-digit volume growth for the remaining 9M of FY27 (~11% YoY, MS), 18-19% EBITDA margin and Rs10bn+ EBITDA, and capex of ~Rs4bn including new Gailpur and Srikalahasti capacity. The price gap to Morbi players has narrowed to <20% from 25-30%, which helps share gains. Estimates rose: Jeff FY27e EPS +4%, MS FY28-29 EPS +3%, GS TP to Rs1,350 (from Rs1,330). Gas price volatility and Morbi competition are the key watch-points (Jeff, MS, GS).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue of Rs5.6 bn (+7% yoy, -4% qoq) was 2.3% below Kotak's estimate of Rs5.7 bn. Residential contribution was limited and occupancy fell to 68% (-780 bps yoy) on West Asia tensions, new supply in Bengaluru and Khandala, and renovation work in MMR. Hospitality revenue grew 3% yoy to Rs4.7 bn, and annuity revenue grew 37% yoy. (Kotak)
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.66 bn (+10% yoy, flat qoq) was 1.6% above Kotak's estimate, with the margin at 48% against Kotak's 46%. Lower operating supplies and other expenses supported the margin despite weaker occupancy, and annuity EBITDA rose 42% yoy. (Kotak)

1Q27.revNote: Core revenue rose 10.9% YoY to Rs5.05bn: hospitality +8.5% (ARR +9%, but occupancy down 120bps and RevPAR only +6%) and rental & annuity +18.2% on new area leased at Cignus Powai Tower. Nomura calls it in line with consensus. Mumbai (MMR) hotels lagged on Powai tower construction, Vashi renovations and weaker foreign arrivals. (Jeff, Nomura)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Core EBITDA rose 18.3% YoY to Rs2.30bn. Margin expanded 285bps to 45.5%, with hospitality EBITDA +10.9% (margin 42.6%, +92bps) and rentals +20.9% (margin 85%). Nomura calls it in line with consensus; Jefferies had Rs2.2bn. (Jeff, Nomura)
1Q27.vsBasis: consensus (Nomura: revenue/EBITDA ex-residential in line with consensus; Jefferies EBITDA

outlook.note: Management sees Mumbai recovery in 2H as the Vashi renovations finish (Aug-26) and the Powai commercial tower completes in 4Q; August RevPAR is positive, with Pune at high-double-digit growth. Delhi Airport Taj opens 70 rooms in 4QFY27 and rentals are guided to Rs300-320mn/month. Jefferies cut FY27/28 EBITDA ~2% but raised its target price to Rs965 from Rs910 (Buy); Nomura trimmed FY27F revenue to Rs28.7bn (EBITDA +2%) and raised its target price to Rs910 from Rs890 (Neutral). (Jeff, Nomura)

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 14.6% YoY to Rs23.4bn against Jefferies' estimate of +13.6% YoY, about 1% above, so in line on the 2% rule. Jefferies called it a beat. Standalone revenue rose 18% YoY on 14% domestic like-for-like RevPAR growth, with Growth Businesses up 22%. TajSATS was weak at +4% YoY. GS also saw standalone revenue growth of 18% above consensus of ~14-15%, with RevPAR +14% vs GS's 9% (Jeff, GS).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: Consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to Rs6.7bn, which Jefferies described as ahead of its estimate. Margin was 28.8% vs 28.2% a year ago. Standalone EBITDA rose 31% with margin up 400bps to 38.7%. PAT was 6% above Jefferies' estimate. TajSATS EBITDA fell 6% YoY (Jeff).

outlook.note: Management maintained double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27. July RevPAR growth is trending above 1Q, 2Q has a low base from Delhi renovations, and the BRICS summit in Delhi in Sep-26 should help. GS now expects low-double-digit FY27 RevPAR growth, up from high-single-digit. Jefferies sees upside risk to estimates if double-digit RevPAR growth holds. Pipeline is 263 hotels, with 20 signings in the quarter (GS, Jeff).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY, with hotel revenue/EBITDA up 10%/15% YoY excluding Sri Lanka residences. Management fees rose 35% YoY and consolidated RevPAR rose 8% (standalone +7%), trailing the industry on a high base. GS flagged hotel-segment revenue growth of 10% against a consensus 13%. (Jeff, GS)
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs2.92bn was in line with Jefferies' estimate of Rs2.9bn, up 19% YoY, and the margin rose 130bps YoY to 31.3%. Hotels EBITDA grew 15% YoY, partly offset by weaker residence sales in Sri Lanka (Rs377mn, -70% QoQ). GS called the quarter a miss against expectations. (Jeff, GS)

4Q26.revNote: Consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to Rs12.5bn, but the growth is flattered by Sri Lanka real-estate income. Ex-RE revenue grew only 6% YoY, on 3% RevPAR growth for owned rooms, as March was hit by weaker South India assets and the FTA impact (Jeff).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs4.67bn was up 13% YoY but about 5% below Jefferies' estimate, mainly on weaker standalone EBITDA. Ex-RE EBITDA grew just 2% YoY, and consolidated margin fell 168bps YoY to 37.2% on negative operating leverage (Jeff).

outlook.note: Jefferies raised EBITDA estimates by about 2-3% on stronger hotel performance and expects growth to improve from 2Q; GS raised FY27-29 EBITDA by 2-4% on higher management fees and expects low-double-digit RevPAR growth to persist through the year. Industry RevPAR grew about 18% YoY in July, and Jefferies lifted its FY27 RevPAR growth forecast to 8-10% (from 7%). Management targets 250 hotels by 2031 and is acquiring a 130-key Welcomhotel Ahmedabad. (Jeff, GS)

companies.name: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts
companies.note: F2H27 outlook was strong. The company is seeing high-teens RevPAR growth in Q3 and added that its earlier guidance of "mid to high teens FY27 EBITDA growth" has upside risks.

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3.5 bn was +28% YoY and ~11% above consensus, driven by 17% RevPAR growth (occupancy +390 bps to 67.5%, ARR +10%), the acquired 71-key Coorg resort, 25% F&B growth and 86% growth in management fees to Rs262-293 mn (JP, Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.43 bn was +41% YoY and ~19% above consensus; margin expanded ~380 bps YoY to 40.7% on higher room rates, operating leverage and contained costs, with management fees the main upside driver (JP, Kotak).

2Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs4,119m (+33% YoY) was 9% above Bloomberg consensus and 5% above JPMe, driven by 30% YoY ARR growth to Rs25,046 on a stable ~68.8% occupancy, a richer suite mix and the BRICS Summit in Delhi. The Coorg resort ramp-up, 21% higher F&B revenue and 76% higher management fees added to growth (JP, Kotak).
2Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1,877m (+36% YoY) was 10% above consensus and 5% above JPMe; margin expanded 118bps YoY to 45.6% (43bps above consensus) on operating leverage, despite higher employee costs and ESOP expense and Coorg ramp-up costs. PAT beat was larger (+19% vs consensus) on a lower tax rate (JP, Kotak).

outlook.note: Mgmt raised FY27 guidance and now expects high-teens EBITDA growth in H2, implying mid-20s% EBITDA growth for FY27, with demand robust into Q3/Q4 on domestic leisure, MICE and a recovery in international travel. Jefferies raised FY27 EBITDA/PAT estimates by 3-7% and its PT to Rs735 from Rs675; Kotak raised EBITDA estimates 5.2%/2.4% for FY27E/28E and its FV to Rs670 from Rs575; JPM expects consensus upgrades (Jeff, Kotak, JP).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 10% yoy to Rs4,164 mn, led by a 6% yoy ARR rise to Rs7,457/day and occupancy up 78 bps to 78.5%, but came in 3% below Kotak's Rs4,284 mn estimate. Management fees grew 29% yoy on a 34% larger managed base of 6,013 keys (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose only 5% yoy to Rs2,153 mn, 4% below Kotak's estimate. Margin fell 223 bps yoy to 51.7%, as renovation, technology and the loss of GST input tax credit (about 1% of revenue) pushed operating expenses up 29% yoy (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue of Rs3.1 bn (+12% yoy) was 4% above Kotak's estimate, driven by 9.6% same-store RevPAR growth, with occupancy up 484 bps yoy to 79% and ARR up 3% yoy, plus 378 new keys opened in the last 15 months. Room revenue grew 14% yoy while F&B grew only ~4% on lower spending by international travellers (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs982 mn (+12% yoy) was 9% above Kotak's estimate. Margin was flat yoy at 32.2% because the loss of GST input tax credit (Rs92 mn, ~400 bps) and higher operating costs offset the revenue gains (Kotak).

4Q26.revNote: Revenue grew 8% yoy to Rs3.4 bn but came in about 2% below Kotak's estimate of Rs3.5 bn. Growth was driven by ARR of Rs7,865 (+5% yoy), flat yoy occupancy of ~75%, and 378 net new keys in FY26. The West Asia conflict and the GST change weighed on the quarter (Kotak).
4Q26.ebitdaNote: EBITDA fell 8% yoy to Rs1.1 bn, about 15% below Kotak's estimate. Margin contracted 575 bps yoy to 32.4%, with other expenses up 17% yoy. Kotak attributes the decline to the West Asia conflict and the removal of the GST input tax credit (Kotak).

outlook.note: Management expects EBITDA margins to improve over the next few quarters. Drivers are the annualisation of the GST input-tax-credit impact, ramp-up of new hotels, and a recovery in international travel and MICE demand. Demand continued to improve through July, and 1,669 keys are in the pipeline. The board approved an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs7.5 bn, and net debt is 3.8X EBITDA. Kotak kept BUY with an unchanged FV of Rs240 (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs5.4 bn (+7% yoy) was 1.2% above Kotak's estimate, led by hospitality revenue of Rs4.2 bn (+9% yoy) from the full-quarter Hilton Goa and Sol de Goa contribution, Raaya consolidation and blended RevPAR growth of 14% yoy to Rs13,154/day; annuity revenue rose 3% yoy (Kotak).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs1.9 bn (-7% yoy) was 11% below Kotak's estimate, with margin at 35.6% versus 40.9% a year ago. Higher diesel cost in Maldives (+Rs255 mn) on West Asia-driven energy prices hit hospitality EBITDA (-4.4% yoy to Rs1.1 bn), while annuity EBITDA was flat at Rs1.1 bn (Kotak).

outlook.note: Kotak cut fair value to Rs720 from Rs770, lowering near-term estimates for weaker earnings and delayed asset commissioning, and rolling forward to June 2028E. Maldives is hit by travel disruption (international hospitality occupancy -190 bps yoy to 52%) and higher fuel costs from the West Asia crisis, while India RevPAR is strong (+20% yoy). The pipeline expanded with the 80-key Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Sahyadri Hills, taking owned keys to 587; rating stays ADD, with EBITDA seen growing at a 13% CAGR over FY2026-30E (Kotak).

1Q27.revNote: Consolidated revenue of Rs 74.0bn (+13% YoY) was in line with JPM's forecast but about 2% below Bloomberg consensus, and Nomura puts it 3% below consensus. India revenue grew 15.6% YoY (about 12 points volume-led), while EU revenue was flat YoY (JP, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA of Rs 8.7bn (flat YoY) was 1% below JPM's estimate but 10% above consensus. The margin of 11.7% was down 149bps YoY and 284bps QoQ. India margin of 12.0% beat JPM's 11.3% estimate, but Europe's margin was weaker than expected. Nomura calls EBITDA in line with consensus, with the margin ahead of consensus (11.7% vs 11.4%) (JP, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management says India demand stays strong and July was good. Price hikes of ~7-9% in 1Q trailed the ~11-12% needed against ~17% RM cost inflation, and a further ~1-2% hike was announced in July with another expected in August. RM costs are expected to rise ~8% QoQ in 2Q, and Europe should improve from 2HFY27 as restructuring benefits start. Capex is high and the company will be a net borrower in FY27. JPM cut FY27E EBITDA by 3% and raised FY28E by 3% (EPS -3%/+6%). Nomura trimmed FY27/28 EBITDA margins to 12.4%/13.5% (EPS -6%/+3%). Both kept Neutral (JP, Nomura).

1Q27.revNote: Revenue rose 24% yoy, about 10-11% above both Nomura's estimate and consensus. Volumes grew 16% yoy (India +32%, Europe/RoW +15-16%, Americas -16%) and ASPs rose 6% on price hikes and a richer OHT/on-highway mix (Kotak, Nomura).
1Q27.ebitdaNote: EBITDA rose 6.9% yoy and was 7.5% above Kotak's estimate (5% above Nomura, 9% above consensus), helped by volume, ASPs and better gross margin. Margin was 20.6% (-320bp yoy), below estimates on higher other expenses (24.0% of sales) and employee cost (Kotak, Nomura).

outlook.note: Management sees stable EU demand and a strong India, but RM prices rose over 10% in 1Q with a further 4-5% expected in 2Q, so it has taken 3-5% price hikes and guides FY27E capex of Rs25-30bn. Kotak expects margins below 23% over FY27-28E on margin-dilutive TBR/PCR/2W expansion and raised FY27-29E EPS 1-3% (FV Rs2,125, SELL). Nomura cut FY27F EPS 3% and its TP to INR2,410 (Neutral) as TBR/PCR share rises (Kotak, Nomura).

MS sees a modest upward revision to consensus EPS, rates it Overweight with a Rs275 PT and calls it a Top Pick (Jeff, MS).

Jefferies cut FY27/28E EBITDA by 6%/9% and its PT to Rs170 (from Rs180), and JPMorgan expects consensus to be revised down and keeps Underweight (Jeff, JP, Nomura).

Kotak calls it a 'better earnings performance'; Bernstein calls it in line with its expectation (Kotak, Bern).
